repos.name: openai/codex
repos.description: Lightweight coding agent that runs in your terminal

commits.message:
Apply model catalog overrides to history, notes, and context tools (#56313)

## What changed

- Read optional tool descriptions and parameter schemas for `history`, `notes`, `new_context`, and `get_context_remaining` from the acting model's catalog messages.
- Support catalog namespace descriptions for history and notes, preserving explicit empty and whitespace descriptions.
- Share catalog override handling across native tools and MCP resource helpers. Keep bundled schemas when overrides are invalid, preserve encrypted parameters, and leave tool identity and transport fields unchanged.

## Testing

Add coverage for sparse catalog serialization, schema fallback and encryption preservation, per-step tool definitions, and context tool updates when switching models. Extend outgoing-request tests to verify history and notes overrides while retaining history image attachments.

GitOrigin-RevId: 1adac8b5009f95c91adba491f20a4e2e2dc91475

Track accepted conversation history in rollout traces (#56312)

## Why

Model output alone does not establish that an item entered conversation history. Treating every response item as accepted can include discarded attempts, while relying on a later request misses accepted final output when a turn ends or is interrupted.

## What changed

- Record `HistoryItemAccepted` events and retain Responses item IDs, generating missing IDs consistently across item events.
- Build thread conversation history from request inputs, compaction checkpoints, and explicit acceptance. Keep unaccepted output accessible through its inference call.
- Preserve inference provenance across retries and late response records without overwriting newer request or compaction snapshots.
- Mark turns with errors as failed. Bump trace schemas to version 2 and reject incompatible bundles and event schemas during replay.

## Testing

Add reducer coverage for discarded attempts with identical text, late responses, compaction, inherited context, and legacy bundle rejection. Add CLI integration tests that run `debug trace-reduce` after success, stream failure, and interruption followed by shutdown, including responses without provider item IDs.

GitOrigin-RevId: 8e387a91d9b3f704df82847d630e6f0b08f998b3

Support model-specific writable-root permission wording (#56309)

## What changed

Add optional `writable_root` and `writable_roots` templates to model-catalog permission messages. Select the template by the number of displayed roots and substitute exactly one `{{ roots }}` placeholder with the existing formatted path list.

Fall back to the bundled sentence for missing, empty, invalid, or oversized templates. Preserve path contents, permission-path limits, and denied-read instructions. Update the permission wording when the selected model changes.

## Testing

Add coverage for template validation and size limits, singular/plural selection after path truncation, path preservation, sparse serialization, and model switches that append changed permissions once while preserving request history.

GitOrigin-RevId: 4dcfb7ff70b91db3dba3dda684b355b920e07974

Separate directory and repository scopes in the TUI (#56308)

## Why

The `Cwd` session filter included sessions from linked worktrees, leaving no way to restrict the picker to the current directory. Project grouping also combined tasks across linked worktrees.

## What changed

- Keep `Cwd` filtering and directory-scoped `resume --last` and `fork --last` lookups limited to the current directory.
- Add an explicit `Repo` picker filter when multiple local worktrees are available, including sessions from corresponding directories across linked worktrees. Cycle between `Cwd`, `Repo`, and `All` in either direction.
- Add `Directory` grouping to the agent command center alongside `Project`, `Status`, and `Model`. Keep this choice in memory without writing a configuration value older clients cannot read.

## Testing

Extend coverage for directory and repository filtering, pagination scope, linked-worktree grouping, directory aliases, grouping persistence, and adjacent selection after task removal. Update picker and command center snapshots.

GitOrigin-RevId: 59603c9c5136db43124102b3277d1d1dab36bb87

Add support for environment-scoped managed hooks (#56304)

## What changed

- Add discovery and listing APIs for environment-owned required hooks, with command and MCP execution routed to the owning environment.
- Use each environment's working directory in hook input, withhold controller transcript paths, and prevent environment hooks from granting permission requests.
- Resolve `command_windows` against the environment's platform and, when hooks are enabled, reject unloadable required hooks before accepting environment configurations at startup or readiness.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for invalid managed hook matchers at startup and readiness, successful readiness after correction, and per-hook working directory and transcript path scoping for `SubagentStop`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 1ac0ab3778ba608c72e5917fcbaebcc1d454887f

Add hook configuration to environment attachments (#56302)

## What changed

- Add `environment_hooks` to `EnvironmentConfig` for hooks from an environment's effective managed requirements. Initialize it empty for inferred thread configurations and report the handler count in debug output.
- Move `HookEventsToml`, `MatcherGroup`, and `HookHandlerConfig` into `codex_protocol::hooks`, with re-exports from `codex_config::hook_config`.
- Validate MCP hook input recursively to reject nulls and integers outside the signed 64-bit range without converting through `toml::Value`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 410506c8e2b89c9519c81d86b44ccd760d751693

Add TLS forwarding tests for MITM SigV4 requests (#56301)

## What changed

Add a test-only MITM CA constructor and local TLS origin fixtures to exercise AWS SigV4 forwarding:

- Check `aoss` payload hashes and credential replacement for GET and POST requests, while preserving unsigned requests and requests using another access key.
- Verify rejection of unsupported HTTP/1.1 framing and signing headers, and check the forwarded body, payload hash, and signed header presence at an HTTP/2 origin.
- Verify that draining signed request bodies releases buffering capacity before response headers arrive, allowing a ninth request to complete while eight responses remain pending.

GitOrigin-RevId: 4da0a77baace31486e77ad97d9581ec9f51bb34e

Mark built-in dummy credentials and strengthen collision checks (#56297)

## What changed

- Add `masked` after the provider prefix in built-in dummy credentials, followed by at least 22 random alphanumeric characters. Stop copying punctuation from the real credential.
- Check built-in dummy candidates against observed credential owners and discoverable configured-provider aliases, and reject overlaps with existing dummy credentials. Allow configured patterns to match a built-in dummy's format when no credential identity collides.

## Testing

Extend regression coverage for short and opaque credentials, fresh dummy values, known and late credential collisions, alias discovery, header injection, and text restoration. Verify that explicit authorization values remain unchanged even when they resemble masked credentials.

GitOrigin-RevId: 5080176f3ecbcdbb18943eab30136e15a4a3985e

Decouple managed configuration loading from ChatGPT authentication (#56295)

## What changed

Introduce a `BundleSource` interface for authentication, cache identity, bundle fetching, and unauthorized-request recovery. Move ChatGPT plan eligibility and credential recovery into `ChatGptSource`, while keeping validation, caching, and retry orchestration in the shared service.

Support source-specific cache namespaces while preserving the existing ChatGPT cache location. Retain one authentication recovery context across all retries of a bundle fetch.

## Testing

Extend the external authentication test to verify that recovery happens only once per bundle fetch, including when an intervening request failure triggers a retry.

GitOrigin-RevId: f5009f72dc4479f96d4ed1da9232f250988444a5

Use fixed-token auth fixtures in Vertex tests (#56293)

## Why

The sequential token fixture rewrites shared files when resolving credentials. Concurrent credential resolution needs a fixture that can return the same token independently for each caller.

## What changed

Add `ProviderAuthCommandFixture::fixed_token`, which reads a token file using `cat` on Unix or `cmd.exe` on Windows without modifying it. Use it in the Vertex command-auth and guardian-request tests.

GitOrigin-RevId: 5bf5134f113b546a643a47012281fb960e885b15

Fix MCP cancellation tests to use the metadata callback (#56292)

Update both `call_tool` invocations in `dropping_tool_call_cancels_remote_request` to pass `|_| Ok(None)`, matching the metadata callback API while continuing to omit metadata.

GitOrigin-RevId: 9d0f3e3108fe81972ce4fd4cca13f4b7febcc616

Lock Python release build tools with uv (#56290)

## Why

Python release jobs installed build tools without a shared lockfile and allowed isolated builds to resolve additional dependencies. Release retries can also build older source revisions, so their tool pins need to come from the running workflow revision.

## What changed

- Add a shared setup action with pinned `uv` and locked `sdk` and `runtime` dependency groups. Apply a seven-day dependency age cutoff, with a two-day exception for `certifi` CA trust updates.
- Use the action for Python SDK and runtime packaging across Linux, macOS, and Windows. Build with `uv build --offline --no-build-isolation` using the prepared environments.
- In the standalone Python build workflows, check out the release tools from `github.workflow_sha` separately from the requested source revision.

GitOrigin-RevId: a9c0344930e5b9870ce9f7754a1fee1a9219305c

Pin Linux artifact signing to Cosign v3.1.4 (#56288)

## Why

Existing release consumers verify v2 signature bundles, so the Cosign upgrade must preserve that format.

## What changed

- Upgrade `sigstore/cosign-installer` to `v4.1.2` and explicitly install Cosign `v3.1.4`.
- Provide a pinned Sigstore trusted root for offline installer verification.
- Check the installed Cosign version before signing and disable the new bundle format and signing configuration.

GitOrigin-RevId: c54578c904ed890d013d79169164e662b57d3ee5

Bump `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` to `1.32.0` (#56286)

GitOrigin-RevId: 9e01a0298c0daa0843e0bed021e19b0a62965783

Scope model catalogs and caches by thread originator (#56284)

## What changed

Select an originator-specific models manager before resolving thread model metadata. Supported originators send their own `originator` header and use separate in-memory catalogs and disk caches, so each thread receives the corresponding model instructions and tools.

Reuse managers for repeated originators and share the API-key model discovery setting across them. Unsupported originators retain the default manager and catalog.

## Testing

Add coverage for originator headers, concurrent catalog isolation, cache reuse across restarts, shared discovery policy, and the instructions and tools sent in actual turns.

GitOrigin-RevId: ae4aa51c8df2813a72fc8aed8978fd630e467069

Group consecutive transcript prompts into one background block (#56280)

## Why

Consecutive user prompts in the rich transcript have extra blank spacing that breaks up their shared background.

## What changed

- Join adjacent visible user prompts into one background block, skipping hidden entries when determining adjacency.
- Keep prompts separated when intervening content becomes visible through detailed mode or search, and restore grouping when it is hidden again.
- Preserve selectable source offsets and joined spacing when text is rewrapped, and reuse cached layouts when checking adjacency.

## Testing

Add regression tests for prompt grouping, layout cache reuse, source offsets across rewrapping, detailed reasoning, and search-driven visibility. Update transcript snapshots to reflect the tighter spacing.

GitOrigin-RevId: faca8001244b0ac883d9d670864c8f7856ac2bad

Add negotiated network policy metadata support for MCP calls (#56278)

## What changed

Add an optional `NetworkPolicyMetadataProvider` to the MCP runtime. Advertise `codex/network-policy-meta` only to trusted ChatGPT origins when a provider is available, and attach policy metadata only when the sending session also advertises support.

Strip caller-supplied policy metadata and derive restrictions from the call's captured permission profile and server environment. Resolve metadata against each session's capabilities, including after recovery, while retaining one policy snapshot per call. Fail the call before sending if policy resolution fails. Existing runtime callers leave the provider unset.

## Testing

Add tests for capability negotiation, trusted-origin restrictions, forged metadata removal, both tool dispatch paths, and policy snapshot reuse. Add HTTP session-recovery coverage for changing capabilities and policy-resolution failures while preserving caller metadata and read-only restrictions.

GitOrigin-RevId: 4b978f986abc0475fc67659be98fc01a2d6ce7cd

Support bounded request bodies in AWS SigV4 signing (#56277)

## Why

The network proxy previously required AWS signing requests to have an empty body or use `UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD`, preventing signing of nonempty payloads.

## What changed

- Buffer and hash request bodies before signing, then forward the original bytes.
- Add `max_body_bytes` with an 8 MiB default and a 16 MiB maximum, plus a 30-second body read timeout.
- Limit concurrent buffering to eight requests with a five-second capacity wait. Retain reservations while forwarded body data remains alive.
- Reject trailers and mismatched content lengths for buffered payloads while preserving streaming for explicitly unsigned payloads.

## Testing

Add coverage for payload hashing and forwarding, body limits and timeouts, fragmented body collection, and buffer reservation lifetimes. Extend signing tests for S3 path and query canonicalization, header replacement, and secret exclusion from trace logs.

GitOrigin-RevId: 48c18442fa90ae3efb1a4a99a168d07e1be2c496

Wait for cloud config refresh cancellation in loader lifetime tests (#56274)

## Why

Aborting a refresh task is asynchronous, so yielding once before checking `is_finished()` does not guarantee cancellation has completed.

## What changed

Return the refresh task's `JoinHandle` from `cloud_config_bundle_loader_for_service` and retain its `AbortHandle` in the loader lifetime. Update `each_loader_owns_refresh_until_its_last_clone_is_dropped` to await each task and assert cancellation after dropping its last loader clone, while still checking that the replacement loader's task remains active.

GitOrigin-RevId: 2eb65211aefc21f9195ff766d8793f4b8f5a74c4

Upgrade Python SDK model generation to datamodel-code-generator 0.64.0 (#56272)

## What changed

- Regenerate protocol models with `datamodel-code-generator==0.64.0`, targeting Python 3.10.
- Preserve discriminator field titles without introducing extra `RootModel` wrappers for literal values or inline unions.
- Keep nullable project and section IDs optional for compatibility with older SDKs, and remove redundant required-nullable field patches.

## Testing

Extend schema annotation coverage to assert that `ReasoningSummary.model_validate("none").root` remains the string `"none"`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 386d07d7e2e368b07d4602b49be6e81a887685fe

Preserve MCP disable reasons across runtime overlays (#56266)

## Why

A requirements denial on a custom `codex_apps` registration could block the trusted hosted Apps replacement. Requirements filtering also lost whether a server had been explicitly disabled, which must remain effective across runtime overlays.

## What changed

- Track explicit disables separately from requirements denials, retaining the requirement source across catalog rebuilds and server materialization.
- Allow trusted host-owned Apps to bypass a previous registration's requirements denial while preserving explicit disables and blocking later custom replacements.
- Preserve combined explicit and requirements disables during repeated filtering, and reject those servers when preparing standalone MCP login HTTP clients.

## Testing

Extend regression coverage for hosted Apps replacements, later custom replacements, cloud catalog refreshes, repeated requirements filtering, and standalone login rejection.

GitOrigin-RevId: 736a13c40fbf7436b4d0682f70c335f33f45962f

Add a built-in Google Cloud Vertex AI provider (#56265)

## What changed

- Support `model_provider = "gcp"` with a Vertex AI endpoint derived from `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION`, defaulting to the `global` location.
- Obtain credentials through `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token` by default, and allow `base_url`, `auth`, and `http_headers` overrides under `model_providers.gcp`.
- Use a static model catalog tailored to Vertex AI, preserve function tools, namespaces, and client-side tool search, and support remote compaction V2. Disable unsupported reasoning summaries, Responses Lite, custom tools, web search, and image generation.
- Expose a `gcp` account type through the app-server protocol and generated clients without resolving credentials during account reads or requiring OpenAI authentication.

## Testing

Add coverage for endpoint resolution, configuration overrides, model catalog filtering, authenticated requests, unsupported request fields, missing credentials, account reporting across provider changes, and automatic remote compaction.

GitOrigin-RevId: 97a3158269e6dbc2605e2cf576998e09817ea12a

Reject backslashes in HTTP(S) marketplace URL userinfo (#56263)

## Why

The URL parser treats backslashes as HTTP(S) path separators, while Git/libcurl does not. This difference can make a marketplace URL appear to match an allowed host pattern while Git connects to a different host.

## What changed

Reject HTTP(S) URLs containing literal backslashes in userinfo when checking marketplace host patterns. Continue allowing encoded backslashes in userinfo and backslashes in paths or query strings.

## Testing

Expand regression coverage to verify that denied URLs never invoke the cloner, create the marketplace install directory, or write configuration. Extend host-pattern tests to cover accepted HTTP(S) URL variants.

GitOrigin-RevId: cfdd29d6e83fb1718b505abaae85d37257317953

Isolate V8 source dependencies and their C++ runtime settings (#56261)

## Why

V8's Abseil and protobuf's shared Abseil can be built for different C++ runtimes. Give V8's copy a distinct inline namespace so both can link into one binary without interposing incompatible functions.

## What changed

- Move pinned V8 dependency imports and BUILD overlays into `third_party/v8`, and inject those repositories into V8 through a module-extension bridge with no fallback downloads.
- Build V8's Abseil with a V8-specific inline namespace while preserving protobuf's shared Abseil namespace.
- Apply V8's C++ runtime settings in the Abseil, Highway, and simdutf overlays, and remove the shared `rules_cc` patch.
- Document source dependency ownership and the version, checksum, and overlay review procedure for V8 upgrades.

GitOrigin-RevId: 2b8e3deed285559f8dd3324647cb4b81089f2f56

Avoid redundant settings checkpoints when resuming threads (#56250)

## Why

Resuming a thread with unchanged settings appended another `ThreadSettingsApplied` event to its rollout.

## What changed

Compare the effective settings with the latest persisted settings for the same thread before writing a checkpoint. Persist settings when they differ or no matching checkpoint exists, even if no turn follows the resume.

## Testing

Add a regression test that restarts the app server, resumes a materialized thread without overrides, and verifies that its persisted settings events remain unchanged.

GitOrigin-RevId: c545791ed3bb4020fa3da6d233607a9ba73e5c8d

Bump uv to 0.13.5 in CI and release workflows (#56248)

## What changed

Update `astral-sh/setup-uv` to `v10.3.2` and pin `uv` to `0.13.5` across the affected build, test, and release workflows. Refresh the checksum used for DotSlash publishing.

Install `uv` in the Python SDK wheel test from a hash-pinned requirements file, requiring a binary distribution and hash verification.

GitOrigin-RevId: 05295f6468f4897ca08672ccf9dc4e9b7d717fa8

Consolidate Rust unit tests under dedicated test modules (#56247)

## What changed

Move inline crate tests into `lib_tests.rs` and nest related test suites under each crate's `tests` module. Update imports, subprocess test filters, logging targets, and snapshot names to match the new module paths.

Keep test helpers accessible where needed and preserve the schema writer's exact test name used by release tooling.

GitOrigin-RevId: de55eaae66dce4941abb33dd0b2f170093daa8f9

Bump Bazelisk to 1.30.0 in the Bazel CI setup action (#56246)

GitOrigin-RevId: 08284d3342d4dcb13160511b29951fbfadde180a

Make the code mode yield/resume test yield explicitly between phases (#56236)

Add `yield_control()` after phase 2 in
`code_mode_can_yield_and_resume_with_wait` so the intermediate output is
returned explicitly. Increase both `wait` calls' `yield_time_ms` from 1,000
to 10,000 to allow more time for each phase to produce its output.

GitOrigin-RevId: 3626a64ae0269c22ad634ec2e3fd5e27942f649f

Emit prompt telemetry only after hooks accept input (#56234)

## Why

Prompt telemetry can include full user text. Emitting it before hook acceptance logs prompts that `UserPromptSubmit` hooks subsequently block.

## What changed

Move prompt telemetry from input submission to hook acceptance, including queued and steered input. Preserve telemetry for accepted Guardian review prompts that are converted to response items during finalization.

## Testing

Extend hook regression tests to assert that blocked prompts are absent from telemetry and rollouts, while accepted queued prompts are logged exactly once. Extend Guardian review coverage to assert exactly one prompt event across inspection steps.

GitOrigin-RevId: aa71f98de2356dd08f62ff492e897ab3a43b54c9

Make Opus encoder test timestamps follow sample time (#56233)

Timestamp synthetic frames in `real_encoder_produces_twenty_millisecond_opus_packets`
from a single start time using each block's sample offset and input rate. This
keeps the test audio contiguous even when the test thread is descheduled.

GitOrigin-RevId: e66440fcc3b3c965a7b1b22b61246c2a622a9cc9

Reuse current model context across paginated resume config loading (#56224)

## Why

Resuming a paginated thread rechecks stored history after loading configuration. Unchanged model context can be reused instead of loading it again.

## What changed

Retain the prepared model context across configuration loading and reuse it when the thread ID, rollout path, and history revision still match. Add `ThreadStore::is_model_context_current` to validate revisions, with a fresh read when validation fails or is unavailable.

## Testing

Add coverage for revision invalidation after history is appended or removed. Extend resume tests to cover paginated history, concurrent metadata and lifecycle changes, workspace-root changes, and preservation of saved user messages in model requests.

GitOrigin-RevId: bad2ca0caddb63523264ac530ffb801db3961f2b

Consolidate Bazel CI setup into `prepare-bazel-ci` (#56222)

## What changed

Move the Bazel installation, repository cache configuration, and Windows MSVC environment setup directly into `prepare-bazel-ci`, and remove the `setup-bazel-ci` action. Wire the repository cache output and restore step to the inlined configuration step.

Update the Windows PATH script documentation and remove the deleted action from V8 canary path matching.

GitOrigin-RevId: 2472372478e1618cd03e98a1536f862f47352659

Use cargo_bin in the Windows sandbox manifest test (#56220)

Resolve `codex-windows-sandbox-setup` with `codex_utils_cargo_bin::cargo_bin` so the manifest test supports both Cargo binary paths and Bazel runfiles.

GitOrigin-RevId: 23e62800cdd5994eb18fa47fcc1479f4ce10c42e

Remove the `u64` cast from WSL DrvFS detection (#56214)

GitOrigin-RevId: 9298584c88089222fe61209b76641fa970555e1f

Default fresh memory profiles to v2 (#56211)

## Why

Profiles without a v1 memory workspace have no legacy context to preserve or consolidate before using v2.

## What changed

- Select v2 when memories are enabled and the `memories` directory is absent. Preserve explicit `memories.version` settings, the `memories.dual_write = false` opt-out, and the v1 default for existing workspaces or filesystem check errors.
- Report `v2_ready` immediately for profiles without a v1 workspace. Keep the consolidation count and valid-summary requirements for profiles with a v1 workspace.
- Make resetting an absent memory workspace a no-op so it does not create an unused v1 directory.

## Testing

Extend coverage for default and explicit version selection, opt-outs, version-specific memory reads, fresh-profile readiness and reset behavior, and running only the v2 pipeline for fresh profiles.

GitOrigin-RevId: a8fb0844962ae9266ffbe88af97e8dc4a99ac15f

Stabilize the marketplace staging cleanup test (#56210)

## Why

A concurrent fork can retain locks from a previous cleanup pass until exec,
causing the next pass to skip cleanup and fail the test's assertions.

## What changed

Wait for and explicitly release both staging locks before each cleanup pass in
`cleanup_reclaims_unpublished_and_aged_legacy_clones`. Run the existing age
scenarios in a loop and report the age when legacy directory assertions fail.

GitOrigin-RevId: 115d887e6b74159f22a2f675237e3b3356ab0308

Add AWS SigV4 signing to network proxy MITM hooks (#56182)

## Why

Allow workloads to make AWS requests with placeholder credentials while keeping real AWS credentials in the trusted proxy process.

## What changed

- Add an `aws_sigv4` hook action with a placeholder access key ID, region, service, HTTPS port, and credential sources from proxy environment variables or files.
- Re-sign matching requests after network and hook authorization and header transformations, using the configured credentials and optional session token.
- Support empty payloads and explicitly unsigned payloads, including streaming unsigned S3 uploads. Reject selected requests with incompatible credential scopes, presigned URLs, unsupported streaming signatures, or ambiguous framing through the hook denial path.
- Mark generated credential headers as sensitive and suppress signing SDK trace events that could expose credentials.

## Testing

Add tests for the published AWS IAM signature vector, unsigned S3 uploads with a session token, and rejection of invalid transport, credential scopes, signing inputs, and unsupported bodies.

GitOrigin-RevId: ab4fbbc00ba40a5bb309add521fea6ee2ff6e79e

Enable reasoning effort overrides by default (#56163)

## What changed

Promote `reasoning_effort_override` to stable and enable it by default, allowing supported models to receive reasoning effort changes through configuration updates in conversation history.

Update request-history snapshots to include the configuration updates, and remove explicit feature enablement from the reasoning effort override test builder so the suite exercises the default.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6ce16d7f985c33f008e5230fc9bae09cdaf141d5

Add managed network review domains before allow rules (#56154)

## Why

Managed network policies need to require approval for selected hosts even when an exact or wildcard allow rule matches them.

## What changed

- Add `experimental_network.review_domains` to managed requirements and route matching hosts through the existing network approval flow. Explicit denials retain precedence, and approved connections still undergo DNS and local-address checks.
- Preserve review patterns across environment policy attachments and remote proxy configuration. Reject execution on an exec-server that lacks the `networkProxyReviewDomains` capability when review patterns are present.
- Expose `reviewDomains` through the app-server requirements API and generated schemas, and show `review_domains` in debug configuration output.
- Update approval reasons to say that network access requires approval rather than assuming the host is absent from the allowlist.

## Testing

Extend coverage for review precedence over exact and wildcard allows, explicit denials, DNS checks after local and remote approvals, approval hooks, policy merging, remote configuration round trips, and requirements API serialization.

GitOrigin-RevId: 4a861061a0ed80b3537d3b72f2caecb0db2a4f0b

Preserve safe enterprise MCP authentication error details (#56153)

## Why

Enterprise MCP token exchange and sign-in failures can collapse into generic errors, hiding useful diagnostics such as an OAuth `invalid_scope` rejection or a cancelled sign-in.

## What changed

Introduce `EmaErrorDetail` to carry static operation messages and sanitized SDK diagnostics through token-source errors and enterprise login completion. Exchange failures can report the stage, HTTP status, and allowlisted OAuth error code, such as `IdentityProvider: HTTP 400: invalid_scope`, without retaining arbitrary provider text or raw error chains.

Preserve specific discovery, credential storage, cancellation, and account/configuration mismatch errors instead of replacing them with generic failure messages.

## Testing

Extend tests to cover `invalid_scope` diagnostics, specific sign-in completion errors, and exclusion of credentials from diagnostics even when an outer error context contains sensitive text.

GitOrigin-RevId: e9280a5db3565ea91da0810bab528da5ee088d64

Fix the MCP auth status test's IdP OAuth configuration (#56139)

Initialize `client_secret` and `token_endpoint_auth_method` to `None` in
`ema_auth_statuses_do_not_wait_for_account_refresh` to match
`McpServerIdpOAuthConfig`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0c800b4f60d2468d7c2cb0b8d83bbdb4b3998574

Defer agent mail after empty final answers (#56133)

## Why

An explicit `final_answer` with empty or whitespace-only text could allow queued agent mail to restart the turn instead of leaving it queued for the next turn.

## What changed

Treat explicit `final_answer` messages as terminal regardless of visible text in both completed-item handling and turn-item finalization. Untagged messages still require visible text to defer mailbox delivery; `commentary` and `partial_answer` messages do not defer it.

## Testing

Extend regression coverage for empty and whitespace-only final answers, delivery of queued agent mail on the next turn, and message board notifications arriving before or after an empty final answer.

GitOrigin-RevId: 466f1a9c613e07d67ce45458858ba32d5d23f11d

Cancel MCP tool requests when response futures are dropped (#56132)

## Why

Dropping a local tool-call future did not notify the MCP server that the request was cancelled, leaving remote work running.

## What changed

- Send a cancellation notification for the request when its response future is dropped, covering both ordinary tool calls and tool-input rounds.
- Preserve write order for stdio and in-process transports so cancellation cannot arrive before its tool request, without waiting for tool responses.

## Testing

Add regression tests for cancellation on drop, request-before-cancellation ordering under reversed send polling and exhausted task budgets, and continued use of the shared connection after cancellation.

GitOrigin-RevId: fab02d546fd82c601756117d9ecbf1017c28ac11

Avoid blocking EMA auth status checks on account refresh (#56127)

## Why

EMA MCP auth status checks acquired an account grant lease, making status inspection wait for account refresh coordination or an existing lease.

## What changed

Add `AuthManager::account_oauth_grant()` to inspect an owner-checked grant without acquiring the refresh lock. Use it for EMA status checks and share a single lazy read across servers, including missing grants and read errors. Keep refresh exclusion for token exchanges through `lease_account_oauth_grant()`.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for status checks across two EMA servers while an account lease is held. Extend account refresh tests to verify inspection completes with a lease held and refresh queued, and returns no grant after logout.

GitOrigin-RevId: 921214dd552eb216c713596f2737460053a07d08

Forward Guardian reviewer events to parent raw-event subscribers (#56124)

## What changed

Add the disabled-by-default `guardian_recorded_items` feature to forward recorded reviewer items and interruptions through the parent's raw-event subscription, preserving reviewer thread and turn IDs without modifying the parent's history or completing its turn.

Emit reviewer items as `rawResponseItem/completed` notifications and interruptions as interrupted `turn/completed` notifications. Mark opted-in reviewer requests with `guardian_recorded_items` metadata.

## Testing

Extend Guardian integration tests to cover reviewer identity, recorded-item metadata replay, concurrent reviewer interruptions, independent parent completion, and behavior without the feature enabled.

GitOrigin-RevId: beb4dbf6c6f2a800a2fbf3cfd11ae174a1382386

Prepare TUI startup to accept multiple backend sessions (#56097)

## What changed

- Add `InitialBackendSessions` to carry the initial session and additional sessions into the TUI event loop. Existing launches continue to supply a single session.
- Shut down all supplied sessions on startup errors, cancellation, and early exits.
- Register the under-development `tui_multi_backend` feature flag, disabled by default, and expose it in the configuration schema.

## Testing

Add a regression test that fails bootstrap and verifies that both initial backends receive shutdown requests. Update multi-source event polling coverage to use the new initialization path.

GitOrigin-RevId: e5db439552de97594e6f13360b90be71256ab2f0

Keep TUI preferences editable when execution settings are invalid (#56091)

## Why

Saving a local preference could succeed but fail to apply live because reloading the full configuration also resolved execution settings. An unknown `model_provider`, for example, prevented the preference from taking effect.

## What changed

Reload config-panel preferences from the configuration layer stack into `LocalSettings` without rebuilding execution settings. Preserve CLI overrides, loader overrides, cloud configuration, and the existing choice of working directory.

## Testing

Extend the offline remote-session preference test with an unknown `model_provider` override, verifying that automatic recap and paste detection preferences still persist and apply live.

GitOrigin-RevId: 2377a01c77f3cb978a7ee6cd67c1fe89361131fb

Honor server approval reviewer defaults on fresh TUI startup (#56090)

## Why

A saved client `approvals_reviewer` setting could override the app server's default when starting a fresh thread.

## What changed

Use explicit invocation overrides for the first thread's approval reviewer, leaving the selection to the server when no override is provided. Typed overrides take precedence over key-value overrides, and repeated key-value overrides use the last value. Explicit profile launches retain their resolved configuration behavior.

## Testing

Extend startup tests to cover server defaults, embedded startup, explicit override precedence, and profile launches. Verify that the first turn uses the reviewer returned by the server.

GitOrigin-RevId: 19d4d75bb8fbe522fb9495bd9c6951513f8ac4d2

Cache decrypted Codex auth and managed secrets (#56081)

## Why

Repeated reads of Codex auth and managed secrets repeat expensive scrypt decryption even when the encrypted file and keyring passphrase are unchanged.

## What changed

Extend the decrypted snapshot cache to `CodexAuth` and `ManagedSecrets`, keeping at most one snapshot per namespace. Reuse snapshots only when the file path, ciphertext, and passphrase match, and invalidate matching snapshots on writes. Every read still checks the file and keyring before reusing plaintext.

## Testing

Extend cache tests to cover concurrent reuse, writes, external file replacement, file removal, key rotation, keyring errors, invalid ciphertext, and isolation across homes and namespaces. Prime the auth cache before verifying fallback when the keyring fails.

GitOrigin-RevId: eaf802ef4cfdbe482b56423807a1fe0fe3def2cd

Require managed configuration from the configured server (#56055)

## Why

Local administrators need to require managed configuration from a specific customer-hosted server before a session can start.

## What changed

- Add a local managed `config_server` requirement with an HTTPS base URL and optional OAuth settings. Validate endpoints and derive the bundle route as `codex/config/bundle` beneath the base URL.
- Replace the entire `config_server` block when a higher-priority requirements layer supplies one, keeping the endpoint and OAuth settings together. Reject this setting in fetched policy.
- Track the applied server through configuration snapshots, role overrides, and refreshes. Reject session startup and managed refreshes when the applied server does not match the requirement; user refreshes retain the session's managed configuration.

## Testing

Add coverage for missing, mismatched, and matching server configuration at session startup, whole-block replacement, rejection of server settings in fetched policy, and preservation across role overrides and refreshes.

GitOrigin-RevId: 51e8a1738dabdb117ae858120f6fb09ae2ff1261

Support configured credential providers in remote execution (#56049)

## Why

Remote credential masking previously fell back to unmasked execution whenever custom credential providers were configured.

## What changed

- Transport configured provider rules to the executor-local network proxy, where credential values and destination context are resolved.
- Advertise `credentialMaskingCustomProviders` and negotiate masking support. Keep the warning and unmasked fallback for executors that support only built-in providers.
- Discard provider rules when masking is disabled and omit their contents from debug output.

## Testing

Extend coverage for capability compatibility, provider configuration round trips, and fallback on older executors. Exercise configured-provider masking in remote request history and verify that masked placeholders are restored to real credentials in upstream request headers.

GitOrigin-RevId: b036f56900b343ddccc17b5293c82bc1f3426237

Enable executor cleanup hooks with V2 capability discovery (#56044)

## Why

Executor hooks depended on V1 discovery snapshots, so plugins discovered through V2 could not run their cleanup hooks.

## What changed

Prepare executor hook sources during step setup from either V1 or V2 discovery and capture them in `StepContext` for stop, interrupt, and memory consolidation hooks. Restrict V2 sources to selected plugin installations while preserving plugin enablement, hook admission, MCP routing, and app tool policy checks.

## Testing

Add unit coverage for V2 hook admission, environment routing, disabled plugins, and failed discovery. Add integration coverage showing that `Stop` and `Interrupt` cleanup hooks run with V2 discovery alone and remain silent when the plugin is disabled.

GitOrigin-RevId: a4c0e9c56bdebcdf22cea63f02f8fb4c5eed358e

Add a channel-backed cloud app-server client (#56037)

## What changed

- Add `CloudClient` and integrate it with `AppServerClient` and `AppServerRequestHandle` for requests, notifications, server-request replies, events, and shutdown.
- Keep retained request and reply handles bound to their cloud backend, with event delivery independent of request completion and a timeout for shutdown.
- Return no platform or Codex home metadata for cloud clients, and reject TUI filesystem operations for this backend.

## Testing

Add tests for backend ownership of retained handles, independent event delivery, errors after the command receiver closes, and shutdown timeouts when the worker does not respond.

GitOrigin-RevId: 4cf308dc0ea6fa6e7b14dd4542d93e8030b0162d

Add request-scoped OAuth credentials and session lifecycle APIs (#56036)

## What changed

- Add `OAuthSessionRequest` to pair access tokens with their authorization identity and retain rejected-token recovery across transient failures and retries. New sign-ins receive an identity that survives token refresh.
- Expose explicit login, logout, and authorization identity lookup, plus a per-manager option to disable automatic browser login while allowing credential reuse and refresh.
- Move serializable `OAuthSessionConfig` into `codex-model-provider-info`, add an optional `device_authorization_url` field, and share endpoint URL validation through `codex-http-client`.
- Distinguish permission failures, transient token endpoint failures, and invalid responses using `io::ErrorKind`.

## Testing

Add coverage for sign-in identity preservation through refresh retries, removal of saved and cached credentials on logout, and suppression of automatic browser login. Extend token endpoint error classification coverage.

GitOrigin-RevId: ae9f72e787171e179fe139a3b840a9f7e1e46506

Enable the Bedrock setup wizard by default (#56033)

## What changed

Promote `bedrock_setup_wizard` to stable and enable it by default for eligible onboarding. Users can still disable it with `features.bedrock_setup_wizard = false`.

## Testing

Update onboarding coverage to check the enabled default and explicit opt-out. Remove the explicit opt-in from daemon startup tests so they exercise the default configuration.

GitOrigin-RevId: 5bd911088681a31d34aa444398e6d3f7d1d87955

Fix entrypoint lookup in package debug-symbol smoke tests (#56032)

## Why

Rust v0 symbols can mention `codex_code_mode_host` as the instantiating crate of a dependency's generic function, so matching the crate name alone can select the wrong function.

## What changed

Demangle `nm` output and match `codex_code_mode_host::main` exactly, preserving spaces within demangled names. Include local symbols in the Linux lookup by removing `--extern-only`.

repos.name: unslothai/unsloth
repos.description: Local UI to run and train LLMs and diffusion models. Supports GGUF, MLX, Qwen3.8, DeepSeek-V4.1, MiniMax-H3, Gemma 4, FLUX and more.

commits.message:
Studio: restore a kept media model's price after a failed replacement (#14826)

With Keep multiple models loaded set to When they fit, `acquire_for`
records the new image or video load's VRAM price as the load starts.
When the background load then failed and the old model stayed loaded,
only the owner account and resident metadata were rolled back. The old
model stayed priced as the smaller model that never loaded, so a later
load could be admitted that does not fit. The arbiter now keeps the
previous price per load start, and each backend's failed-replacement
path puts it back. A load that takes no GPU claim clears it, so a stale
price is never restored. Tests cover the arbiter and the sd.cpp failure
path end to end.

Studio video: keep the stream encode hook out of a compiled VAE decode graph (#14822)

With `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_COMPILE_VAE=1`, Studio compiles `vae.decode`,
and the stream-encode forward hook on `vae.decoder` ran inside that
graph. Its thread start, queue put and CUDA stream context each broke
the graph: 6 breaks and 6 graphs on a tiny Wan VAE, under both the eager
backend and inductor.

The hook is now registered through `torch.compiler.disable`, so it runs
as one eager island: 2 breaks and 3 graphs. The decoder compute stays
compiled, and the streamed mp4 still matches the exported frames and is
still used. Skipping the stream session under a compiled decode would
give 0 breaks but lose the overlapped encode, so streaming is kept.

Tests: a new test compiles the decode the way Studio does
(`fullgraph=False, dynamic=True`) and checks the frames, the stream use
and the break count on CPU and CUDA. On a B200: 2 failed / 11 passed on
main, 13 passed here.

Not measured: the time cost of the 2 remaining breaks under compile.

Studio images: keep the resident GGUF's base repo on Reapply and native reload (#14828)

When the Images page finds a resident GGUF it did not load, it seeds its
reload target from status but left out `base_repo`. Reapply and the
native-engine reload then reused that target as is and sent no
`base_repo`, so the backend fell back to the card's default companions,
or failed on a gated default. The seed now carries `base_repo`, and both
helpers fill a missing base from status while the target is still the
resident model. A test seeds from a status with a custom base and checks
both reload paths keep it.


Not run: tsc, eslint and the production build (the test uses the Node
test runner), and a real GGUF load in a browser.

Studio MCP: drop a queued video's request and caller once it settles (#14825)

A cancelled, failed or submitted record in the MCP video queue kept its
whole request body, including base64 reference images, plus the caller
and its API token, until enqueue eviction past 64 records. Only the
submit path reads them, and only while the item is still queued, so
`_settle()` now clears them. `get_job` and `cancel` answer from the
status fields as before. A test settles a record each way and checks
nothing is retained.

Apply the repo formatter to 26 files merged without it (#14817)

pre-commit.ci fails `ruff-format-with-kwargs` on every open PR (#14806,
#14805, #14803, #14790, #14785, #14781, #14780, #14777, #14776, #14775,
#14774, #14773, #14772, #14770, #14769, #14768, and others): "files were
modified by this hook". pre-commit.ci runs the hooks on all files, and
20 files on main (26 by the time this lands) are not in the formatter's
output, so every PR is reformatted outside its own diff. Where
pre-commit.ci can push, its autofix commit drags those unrelated files
into the PR (for example #14790's touches `tests/test_block_compile.py`,
`tests/test_bnb_integration_compile.py` and `unsloth/models/_utils.py`).

The drift came in with PRs merged today, among them #14702, #14751,
#14759, #14784, #14786, #14787, #14788, #14791 and the FP8 block decode,
GRPO routing replay, 4-bit decode, compiled blocks and MoE LoRA target
changes.

### Change

`python scripts/run_ruff_format.py` (the hook's own entry point,
`ruff==0.6.9` as pinned in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`) applied to those
20 files, plus 6 more from #14739, #14779 and #14806, which merged while
this was open. Formatting only.

### Verification

- Every changed file parses to an identical AST before and after.
- A second run of the hook over the same files changes nothing (fixed
point), and over all tracked Python files on this branch it changes
nothing.
- `ruff check` passes on the changed files;
`tests/test_formatter_fixed_point.py` passes (16).

Open PRs pick this up on their next pre-commit.ci run after merging
main.

Studio tests: skip the two-card fast pin test on ROCm instead of erroring (#14618)

## Summary

On a ROCm host with two or more GPUs,
`test_video_fast_pin.py::test_releasing_a_buffer_on_another_thread_syncs_its_own_card`
errors at setup instead of skipping:

```
Failed: Error evaluating 'skipif' condition
    7.13.99004
         ^
SyntaxError: invalid syntax
```

The condition ends in a bare `torch.version.hip`. On ROCm that is a
string, and pytest treats a string `skipif` condition as Python source
to evaluate, so the HIP version number becomes a SyntaxError. The test
reads CUDA driver primary contexts, so it is meant to skip on ROCm.
One-card ROCm hosts never got that far because `device_count() < 2`
short-circuits first, which is why this only showed up once a second AMD
device was visible.

## Changes

- `studio/backend/tests/test_video_fast_pin.py`: wrap the condition in
`bool(torch.version.hip)` and say in the reason that the test needs
NVIDIA (CUDA driver contexts).
- `studio/backend/tests/test_skipif_version_strings.py` (new): an AST
check over `studio/backend/tests` that no `skipif` / `xfail` condition
ends in a bare `torch.version.hip` or `torch.version.cuda`. CPU only.

Test-only. No product code changes.

## Verification

| check | base (main b2ba86a) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| CPU repro: torch reports a HIP version string and two devices, the
test run directly | ERROR at setup, `SyntaxError: invalid syntax` |
SKIPPED, `needs two NVIDIA CUDA devices` |
| `test_skipif_version_strings.py` (CPU) | fails, names
`test_video_fast_pin.py:167` | passes |
| AMD gfx1151 runner, ROCm 7.13 / torch 2.11.0+rocm7.13.0, two HIP
devices (one spoofed, see below) | ERROR at setup (junit, same
SyntaxError; first run on main 2749eee, whose copy of this file is
identical) | skipped (skip count 10 on base -> 11 on head in the same
job), guard test passes |

On the same runner, base and head ran the diffusion multi-GPU suites
(`test_diffusion_multigpu*.py`, `test_diffusion_cfg_parallel_tier.py`,
`test_diffusion_zimage_cfg_split.py`, the layer split tests,
`test_video_multigpu_wiring.py`, 986 tests in all, the two-card
`*_cuda.py` tests included). Apart from the line above, the failing test
IDs are the same on both sides. Those are GPU selection / llama.cpp
ordering tests that also fail on this runner without the spoof, so they
predate this change and are unrelated to it.
`test_compiled_blocks_under_group_offload_skip_hook_tracing` failed only
on the second state in both runs, including a run where both states were
the same commit, so it is order-dependent there and not caused by this
change.

Tiny end-to-end renders on the same runner, through the real Studio
entry points (`make_selection` -> `install_cfg_parallel` /
`refine_plan_for_multigpu`), were all bit-identical to one card and
engaged on both base and head: CFG-parallel for FLUX.1, Qwen-Image,
compiled FLUX.1 and Wan 2.1 video (4 replica calls each, replica on
`cuda:1`), the Z-Image CFG split pair (6 parallel pairs), the layer
split for FLUX.1 and Wan, and the companion split.

## Limits

Multi-GPU AMD was verified only as wiring, under a device spoof. The
runner has one gfx1151 APU, and the harness's HIP device multiplier
presents it as two devices. In the harness's words:

- **multi_gpu**: needs at least two GPUs; this runner has one
- **discrete_gpu**: needs a discrete GPU; this runner is a
unified-memory APU
- **1 of the 2 devices torch reported is FABRICATED** by the HIP device
multiplier: the real GPU wearing other numbers. Shared memory, shared
compute, no parallelism. Wiring only, never sharding, throughput or
collectives.

A real two-GPU AMD run, covering throughput, per-card memory, peer
copies and parity across two physical cards, is still pending a tester.

Studio tests: compare MLX snapshot paths as paths, not posix strings (#14809)

## Problem

Two tests in `studio/backend/tests/test_mlx_diffusion_backend.py` fail
on the `windows-latest` staging leg on main:

- `test_base_fetch_is_cancellable_between_files`: `assert
'\\hub\\snapshots\\abc' == '/hub/snapshots/abc'`
- `test_online_companions_land_under_one_cache_root`: same mismatch
under `C:\Users\...`

`fetch_base_snapshot` derives the snapshot directory with
`Path(path).parents[...]`, so on Windows it returns native backslash
paths, while the tests compare against `/`-joined strings. The code is
right; the assertions assume POSIX separators.

## Fix

Test-only: both assertions compare `Path` objects, so the same check
passes on POSIX and Windows.

## Tests

- Linux: both tests pass.
- The Windows strings from the failing staging logs compare equal under
`PureWindowsPath` with the new assertions.
- The `windows-latest` staging leg runs on this PR to confirm.

FSDP2 NF4 saves: stage packed bytes on the CPU, restore QuantState on full DCP load (#14739)

## Summary
Two fixes for FSDP2 saves of bitsandbytes 4-bit models (follow-up to
#13895, #14273). Nothing changes without FSDP2 or without 4-bit weights.

1. save_pretrained / push_to_hub of a sharded NF4 model kept every
gathered packed weight on rank 0's accelerator (offload_to_cpu skipped
any parameter with a quant_state), so the whole quantized base had to
fit on one GPU next to its shards. These saves only write the packed
bytes, so the gather now stages them on the CPU together with a CPU copy
of their QuantState (QuantState.to moves in place, so the live one is
copied first and stays where the sharded weight computes). The written
state dict is byte for byte the same. Merged saves still dequantize on
the device and keep the previous placement.
2. A full DCP load dropped the QuantState entries the full state dict
carries, then reported all keys matched: the loaded packed bytes were
paired with whatever scales the live model had (for example a base that
was requantized or initialized differently). The saved entries are now
copied into the live QuantState in place before they are dropped (rank 0
broadcasts them under broadcast_from_rank0), and a QuantState that does
not fit the model (shape, blocksize, quant type, nesting) raises instead
of loading.

## Tests
- tests/test_fsdp2_save_gloo.py:
test_packed_4bit_save_stages_bytes_and_quant_state_on_the_cpu and
test_full_dcp_load_restores_the_saved_quant_state (two gloo CPU ranks,
real bitsandbytes NF4, nested and not, with and without
broadcast_from_rank0). Both fail on main.
- tests/test_fsdp2_save_coverage.py:
test_only_saves_that_write_packed_bytes_stage_4bit_on_the_cpu (only
save_pretrained and push_to_hub request it; merged saves do not). Fails
on main.
- Existing FSDP2 save tests: same results as main.
test_a_slow_writer_does_not_time_out_the_other_ranks fails on main and
here alike under host load (4 s gloo timeout).

Not covered: merged saves still hold the packed base on the writing GPU
(needs per-layer gather and merge); no NCCL or GPU peak-memory run.

Attention: let the SDPA GQA probe trace under torch.compile(dynamic=True) (#14779)

The SDPA GQA routing added in #14158 asks torch which kernel a call
would get. That probe, `_sdpa_gqa_state` (and `_sdpa_backend_state` for
the varlen choice), runs through
`torch.compiler.assume_constant_result`, and dynamo can only pass such a
function Python constants. #14398 handled the boolean arguments. Under
`torch.compile(fullgraph=True, dynamic=True)` the head dim and head
counts are still SymInts, so compilation fails before the forward:

```
torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported: assume_constant_result argument conversion failed
  Cannot convert argument of type SymNodeVariable to a Python constant
```

Repro: `run_attention` plus backward, noncausal GQA on CUDA, Q (2, 8,
32, 64), K/V (2, 2, 32, 64), no mask, SDPA backend. Before #14158 both
static and dynamic fullgraph passed.

Fix: a small `_constant_probe` wrapper replaces the two bare
`assume_constant_result` wraps. It passes integer arguments through
`operator.index` before the call. Under dynamo that specialises the head
sizes, which are fixed per model. Batch and sequence length stay
dynamic. Plain ints pass through unchanged, so eager and static-shape
routing is identical. `functools.wraps` is avoided on purpose:
`assume_constant_result` marks the wrapped function in place, and
copying its `__dict__` would mark the wrapper too.

Tests (`tests/test_attention_dispatch_compiled_block.py`):
- CPU: `_sdpa_gqa_state` and `_torch_varlen_beats_segments` traced
fullgraph, static and `dynamic=True`, match eager with 0 graph breaks
and one graph across batch / length changes.
- CUDA: real `run_attention` forward plus backward in bf16 GQA, compiled
fullgraph static and dynamic with Inductor. Outputs and gradients match
eager, with 0 graph breaks and one graph under `dynamic=True`.

Results on B200, torch 2.13.0 and 2.14.1:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| fullgraph, static | pass | pass |
| fullgraph, dynamic=True | fails before forward | pass, 0 graph breaks
|
| attention dispatch tests (GPU) | 4 failed, 69 passed | 1 failed, 72
passed |

The remaining failure,
`test_plain_causal_attention_traces_with_a_dynamic_length[xformers]`, is
already on main and fails only on a GPU host: the xformers fp32 downcast
gate looks at the host GPU, not at the tensor device. It is left for a
separate change.

Fused LoRA: fall back to PEFT for variants, disabled or merged adapters, trainable bases and autocast dtype mismatches (#14806)

The fused LoRA kernels (apply_lora_qkv, apply_lora_o, apply_lora_mlp_*)
only compute plain LoRA over a
frozen base weight in the input dtype. Routing let four other
configurations through, and #13898 widened
their reach to lora_dropout > 0 and lora_bias configs:

1. PEFT LoRA variants. Routing never checked `lora_variant`, so a
variant adapter (KaSA, MoNTeCLoRA,
   VeLoRA, BD-LoRA, ...) trained as plain LoRA with no error.
2. Disabled or merged adapters. The fused backward dereferenced the
missing LoRA weights and raised
`'NoneType' object has no attribute 'to'` whenever the input required
grad.
3. Trainable base weights. The fused backward returns None for the base
weight, so a base projection
   unfrozen after attaching LoRA silently got no gradient.
4. Autocast dtype other than the input dtype (fp16 input under bf16
autocast, bf16 under fp16, fp32
under fp16). The matmuls return the autocast dtype, but the in-place
LoRA accumulation does not
autocast, so the forward raised `self and mat2 must have the same
dtype`.

All four reproduce on main and, for the default dropout = 0 / no bias
config, on the commit before #13898.

Change: `_lora_dropout_and_bias` now returns None (PEFT's own forward)
for variants, trainable base
weights, and autocast in a dtype other than the input's. Disabled or
merged adapters fall back only when
a gradient is needed (grad enabled and the input or base weight requires
grad). The no-grad DPO / GRPO
reference forward stays on the fused base matmul, bitwise equal to
PEFT's base_layer, including on a
4-bit NF4 base. The added checks are attribute reads and mode queries:
no tensor ops, no syncs, and they
compile with fullgraph=True. The patch summary names a LoRA variant
adapter. Eligible configurations take
the same branches and make the same fused calls with the same arguments
as before.

Tests: tests/test_fused_lora_peft_fallbacks.py checks that no fused
Function runs for each case and that
outputs, input grads and every parameter grad match PEFT bitwise
(float64 on CPU, float32 on CUDA). It
covers o, qkv and mlp, dropout 0 / 0.3, and lora_bias on / off, and
includes a real PEFT KaSA adapter.
On main 110 of these fail; with this change 181 pass and 10 skip
(merging a lora_B bias, which PEFT
refuses). Guards confirm that eligible configs and no-grad disabled /
merged adapters still fuse. The
neighbouring fused LoRA, QLoRA, FSDP and QAT suites go from 366 passed
on main to 547 passed with the new
file, with no new failures.

Studio diffusion: fast whole-component swap for low_vram offload (#14767)

## Summary

The `low_vram` memory mode (whole-component swap through
`enable_model_cpu_offload`) moved FLUX.2-klein-9B's 16.9 GiB transformer
to the GPU at 50 to 180 MiB/s, even though the weights were already in
pinned host chunks and the link does about 50 GiB/s. A steady image took
240 to 640 s on this host. With this PR it takes 1.2 s, and the images
are bit-identical.

Root cause: the swap allocated and freed device memory for every tensor,
on every swap.

- accelerate's `CpuOffload.pre_forward` onloads with
`module.to(execution_device)` (accelerate `hooks.py:763`), so every
weight gets its own fresh device allocation.
- Right before that it calls `clear_device_cache()` after offloading the
previous component (`hooks.py:756`). diffusers'
`enable_model_cpu_offload`, which runs again after every call through
`maybe_free_model_hooks`, calls `empty_device_cache`
(`pipeline_utils.py:1232`). The caching allocator therefore starts every
swap empty.
- Studio's kept-host-weights wrapper (`diffusion_memory.py:139` and
`:487` on main) already re-points offloaded weights at pinned host
views, so no bytes were copied back. The onload, however, still went
through the stock per-tensor path.

The result was about 360 `cudaMalloc` per image on the way up and the
matching `cudaFree` inside `empty_cache` on the way down. Under host
load those driver calls are the whole cost. In a microbenchmark on the
same host, 2 GiB as 256 tensors uploaded at 0.06 GiB/s into an emptied
cache and at 40 GiB/s into a warm one, and freeing the 256 blocks took
between 0.07 s and 193 s depending on driver contention.

## Changes

`studio/backend/core/inference/diffusion_memory.py`, whole-module
offload path only:

- `_pin_host_weights` records the chunk layout it already builds (which
weight sits at which offset of which pinned chunk).
- New `_upload_pinned_chunks`: onloads a component with one device
allocation and one `non_blocking` copy per pinned chunk, then re-points
every weight and buffer at its slice. It uses the same bytes and strides
as before. Weights that were replaced or reassigned since pinning are
matched by address and skipped, so the stock `module.to` still moves
them as before. Any failure (OOM, or a device whose tensors cannot back
a host Parameter such as `meta`) restores the host views and falls
through to the stock copy.
- The wrapped `pre_forward` offloads the previous component through its
kept hook itself. The stock hook then finds it already on the host and
skips its `empty_cache`. During the stock call, `module.to` is shadowed
for that one call so the chunk upload runs first.
- The wrapped `enable_model_cpu_offload` skips diffusers'
`empty_device_cache` for the duration of the re-enable, but only once
some component uploads through chunks. The original is restored in a
`finally`.
- `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_OFFLOAD_FAST_UPLOAD=0` restores the previous
behaviour exactly.

Behaviour change: the caching allocator keeps the swap chunks between
generations. At rest, reserved VRAM stays at the run's peak (17.9 GiB
for klein-9B) instead of dropping to about 0.1 GiB. Peak allocated and
peak reserved are unchanged. The allocator still releases cached blocks
and retries if an allocation in this process would otherwise OOM. The
planner and its tier choices are not touched.

New tests in
`studio/backend/tests/test_diffusion_offload_fast_upload.py`:

- On CPU: the layout is recorded, the switch is parsed, the diffusers
cache patch engages only after pinning and is restored even when the
call raises, and `meta` falls back to the stock copy.
- On CUDA: output is bit-identical to stock under both `no_grad` and
`inference_mode`, onloaded weights share one storage per chunk, and
repeated renders cause no new `cudaMalloc` (`num_device_alloc`). Also
checked: the kill switch brings back per-tensor storages, a replaced
weight takes the stock copy, and a weight written on the device is still
copied back.

## Testing

FLUX.2-klein-9B, `memory_mode="low_vram"`, `speed_mode="off"`, bf16,
1024x1024, 4 steps, emulated 24 GiB card (`mem_get_info` reports 24 GiB,
and `set_per_process_memory_fraction` enforces it). Three fixed-seed
prompts per process. One shared B200 lease ran base (merge base
`870f37741f`), head, base, head, so each side has an A/A repeat. Steady
means images 2 and 3 of each process. The host load average was 300 to
750 on 192 cores throughout, so ratios matter more than absolute times.

| arm | steady s/image (4 images) | median | DiT upload GiB/s (median) |
cudaMalloc per steady image | peak alloc GiB | peak reserved GiB | peak
host RSS GiB | images |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base r1 / r2 | 603.0, 639.5 / 364.0, 242.4 | 483.5 | 0.08 | 360 to 361
| 17.74 | 17.88 to 17.90 | 52.9 / 52.4 | reference |
| head r1 / r2 | 1.23, 1.20 / 1.97, 1.21 | 1.22 | 50.1 | 0 | 17.74 |
17.88 | 52.9 / 52.9 | identical sha256, all 6 |

- Steady image: about 400x faster, median against median. The worst head
image (1.97 s) against the best base image (242 s) is still 123x. The
A/A spread is 2.6x on base and 1.6x on head, far smaller than the gap.
- DiT upload: 49 to 52 GiB/s on head (one image at 29), which matches
the pinned link (51 GiB/s measured earlier on this card type). Base ran
at 0.06 to 0.18 GiB/s.
- Peak VRAM and peak host RSS are unchanged. All 12 images (3 prompts x
4 processes) match per prompt by sha256 across base and head. They also
match the earlier `low_vram` bench images for the same seeds.
- First image of each process: 94 to 182 s on head against 483 to 1260 s

- Small-scale probe (2 GiB DiT + 1 GiB text encoder of bf16 linears, 128

`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_OFFLOAD_FAST_UPLOAD=0`, head reproduces base (96

- `tests/test_diffusion_offload_fast_upload.py` and
`tests/test_diffusion_offload_keep_cpu.py` on CUDA: 48 passed, 3

Not covered: Qwen-Image at 48 GiB (not rerun), an idle host (cudaMalloc

## Compatibility

The fast path shadows `module.to` for the one onload call inside
accelerate's `CpuOffload` hook and skips diffusers' `empty_device_cache`
during the per-call re-enable. It was exercised with accelerate 1.15.0
and diffusers 0.41.0. Any weight replaced since pinning, a missing hook
attribute or any error falls back to the stock per-tensor copy, and
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_OFFLOAD_FAST_UPLOAD=0` restores the old behaviour
exactly.

Reserved VRAM now stays at the run's peak between generations (17.9 GiB
for klein-9B) instead of dropping to about 0.1 GiB; the allocator still
frees cached blocks and retries before this process runs out of memory,
but other processes on the same card see less free memory.

Studio: cap Pillow below 13 for the MLX image engine (#14802)

## Problem

Pillow 13.0.0 breaks the opt-in MLX image engine (mflux) on every Python
it currently runs on.

- `PIL/_typing.py` in Pillow 13.0.0 does `from numbers import
_IntegralLike as IntegralLike`. CPython 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14 have
no `numbers._IntegralLike`, so `import PIL._typing` raises
`ImportError`. `PIL.Image`, `ImageOps` and the other public modules
import it only for type checking, so they still work.
- mflux 0.22.0 imports `from PIL._typing import StrOrBytesPath` in
`mflux/utils/exif_orientation.py` and `mflux/utils/image_util.py`. Every
mflux import goes through one of them, so the engine cannot load.
- The no-torch path pins `pillow==12.3.0` in
`requirements/no-torch-runtime.txt`, but the torch path that macOS uses
(MPS) leaves Pillow unpinned. A fresh Mac install can therefore resolve
13.0.0. Pillow 13 declares `requires-python >=3.11`, so pip will pick it
on Python 3.12.

Checked on CPython 3.12.13, 3.13.12 and 3.14.3 with the Pillow 13.0.0
wheel: `import PIL._typing` fails on all three, and `from PIL import
Image, ImageOps` passes.

## Fix

- `install_python_stack.py`: the MLX engine install adds
`pillow>=12.3.0,<13` to its `--no-deps` set (12.3.0 is mflux's own
floor). `_mlx_diffusion_engine_is_current` already checks every entry in
that list, so an existing install that drifted to Pillow 13 is
reinstalled on the next update.
- `diffusion_engine_router.py`: `_MLX_RUNTIME_REQUIREMENTS` gains the
same range. A Pillow 13 environment now falls back to the diffusers
engine at selection time, with `the MLX engine needs pillow>=12.3.0,<13
(found 13.0.0)` as the fallback reason, rather than failing when the
model loads.

The existing test that keeps the installer list and the router list in
sync covers both edits.

## Tests

- `test_diffusion_mlx_engine_router.py`: new case `{"pillow": "13.0.0"}`
in `test_an_incompatible_installed_runtime_falls_back`.
- `tests/studio/install/test_mlx_install.py`: the engine's package set
now includes `pillow`.
- Result: `tests/studio/install/test_mlx_install.py` and
`test_install_manifest.py` pass, 121 passed. The backend MLX test files
fail on the same 34 test IDs at the merge base as at this head; those
failures come from a dependency (`fastmcp`) missing on this host and are
unrelated to this change.

## Not covered

No real Mac ran this. The change only narrows which versions are
accepted, and the import failure was reproduced with the Linux wheels of
the same Pillow release.

Studio MLX images: plan text encoder and dense bits from the Metal working set (#14793)

## Summary

The opt-in MLX image engine (`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_MLX=1`, Z-Image GGUFs)
picked its on-load quantization from total RAM alone: on every Mac with
16 GB or less it quantized the Qwen3-4B text encoder to 4 bits and
re-quantized the GGUF's own BF16 tensors to 4 bits. 16 GB is the most
common Apple Silicon config, and the 4-bit text encoder is the one
setting in that stack that measurably hurts images.

This PR sizes the load and picks the most accurate build that fits
Metal's recommended working set:

| rung | text encoder | GGUF BF16 tensors |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8-bit | as stored |
| 2 | 8-bit | 8-bit |
| 3 | 8-bit | 4-bit |
| 4 | 4-bit | as stored |
| 5 | 4-bit | 8-bit |
| 6 | 4-bit | 4-bit (smallest; also used when nothing fits) |

- The converted transformer size is exact: `planned_output_bytes` runs
the converter's own planner over the GGUF header, no tensor data read.
- The text encoder and VAE sizes come from their safetensors headers;
the 8 / 4-bit text encoder size adds the group-64 scale and bias.
- Decode headroom follows the decode path the runtime actually has.
Measured on Metal (Apple M1, mflux 0.22.0), a 1024x1024 denoise step
peaks 0.8 GiB above the weights, a tiled 1024x1024 VAE decode peaks 2.0
GiB and the untiled decode 6.64 GiB. When the runtime can tile
(`vae_tiled()`, added by the companion VAE tiling PR #14796) and
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_MLX_VAE_TILING` is not forced off, 2 GiB is reserved;
otherwise 6.64 GiB.
- The budget is `max_recommended_working_set_size` (the same helper the
hardware probe uses), else two thirds of RAM.
- `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_MLX_TE_BITS` / `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_MLX_DENSE_BITS`
still pin their axis. Any unreadable input falls back to the old RAM
rule, so a load never fails because of the plan.
- The chosen plan, its planned bytes and the budget are reported under
`status()["mlx"]["timings"]["quant_plan"]`.

What a Mac gets for `unsloth/Z-Image-Turbo-GGUF` with #14796 also merged
(sizes from the real files, header only):

| Mac | Q4_0 before | Q4_0 after | Q8_0 before | Q8_0 after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 GB | TE 4 / dense 4 | TE 4 / dense 4 | TE 4 / dense 4 | TE 4 / dense
4 |
| 16 GB | TE 4 / dense 4 | TE 8 / as stored | TE 4 / dense 4 | TE 4 /
dense 4 |
| 24 GB and up | TE 8 / as stored | TE 8 / as stored | TE 8 / as stored
| TE 8 / as stored |

Without #14796 the runtime only decodes untiled, so the plan reserves
6.64 GiB: a 16 GB Mac then stays on TE 4 / dense 4 for both quants (same
as before), and a 24 GB Mac with Q8_0 takes TE 4 / as stored, because TE
8 / as stored plus the untiled decode (about 17.9 GiB) is over its 16
GiB working set. These rows are why this PR is meant to land together
with #14796.

A BF16 Z-Image GGUF on a 24 GB Mac now drops its dense tensors to 8 bits
instead of loading about 15.6 GiB of weights, plus the headroom, into a
16 GiB working set.

## Why the order

Z-Image-Turbo, 8 prompts x 2 seeds at 1024x1024, 9 steps, LPIPS against
the all-bf16 MLX render, paired bootstrap over the 16 images (mflux
0.22.0):

| change | mean LPIPS delta | 95% CI | images worse |
|---|---|---|---|
| text encoder 4-bit vs 8-bit (Q4_0 transformer) | +0.029 | [+0.010,
+0.047] | 13 / 16 |
| text encoder 4-bit vs bf16 (mflux 4-bit transformer) | +0.043 |
[+0.024, +0.064] | 15 / 16 |
| text encoder 8-bit vs bf16 (Q4_0 transformer) | +0.002 | [-0.004,
+0.009] | 10 / 16 |
| text encoder 8-bit vs bf16 (8-bit transformer) | +0.011 | [-0.007,
+0.025] | 11 / 16 |
| GGUF BF16 tensors at 4-bit vs as stored | +0.008 | [-0.002, +0.018] |
9 / 16 |

Only the 4-bit text encoder is outside noise, so it is the last rung.
mflux's own README uses `-q 8`, and its Qwen-Image definition never
quantizes the text encoder for the same reason.

## Tests

- `test_quant_plan_takes_the_most_accurate_build_that_fits`: every rung,
using the real Z-Image Q4_0 sizes and the 32 / 16 / 8 GB working sets.
- `test_quant_plan_shrinks_monotonically_with_the_budget` and
`test_quant_plan_env_pins_one_axis`.
- `test_a_16gb_mac_loads_z_image_q4_0_with_an_8bit_text_encoder`: end to
end through `begin_load`, with the plan in status.
- `test_an_unreadable_gguf_keeps_the_ram_rule` and
`test_working_set_falls_back_to_two_thirds_of_ram`.
- `test_planned_output_bytes_is_the_converted_size`: the planned size
equals the bytes the converter writes, for each dense bits value.
- `test_planned_output_bytes_refuses_what_conversion_refuses`.
- `test_mflux_loads_a_mixed_4_and_8_bit_conversion_at_each_layers_bits`:
runs on real MLX. It loads a Q4_0 + Q8_0 + 8-bit-dense conversion
through mflux's stored-layer predicate, checks each layer's bits, and
compares its matmul with a numpy dequantization.

All 17 new tests fail on main. On Linux with MLX's CPU build (mlx
0.32.4, mflux 0.22.0), `test_mlx_diffusion_backend.py`,
`test_mlx_diffusion_convert.py` and
`test_diffusion_mlx_engine_router.py` pass: 272 tests.

Measured on the GitHub `macos-15` runner (Apple M1 Virtual, 7 GB,
Metal), on a truncated real Z-Image-Turbo: the embedders, both refiners,
4 main blocks and the final layer, with real weights. That truncation
over-weights the BF16 refiner / embedder tensors. Against a torch fp32
run of the same weights, re-quantizing the GGUF's BF16 tensors to 4 bits
(main's default on 16 GB and smaller Macs):
- raised the error from LPIPS 0.0026 to 0.034 for Q8_0, and from 0.0096
to 0.040 for Q4_0;
- did not change the speed (1.44 vs 1.44 s/step).

## Not covered

- The headroom covers 1024x1024 with a tiled decode. Without the tiling
change, main's untiled decode at 1024 needs 6.64 GiB on any rung,
including main's own. 2048x2048 is not planned for.
- I have not run the 16 GB rung on a physical 16 GB Mac. The GitHub
macOS runner has 7 GB, which lands on the bottom rung, same as before.

Studio MLX images: convert Q4_K / Q5_K / Q6_K and Q5_0 / Q5_1 GGUFs (#14794)

## Summary

The opt-in MLX image engine (`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_MLX=1`) converted only
Q4_0 / Q4_1 / Q8_0 / BF16 / F16 GGUFs. Every K-quant was refused, and so
were Q5_0 / Q5_1. That ruled out the files most people download from
`unsloth/Z-Image-Turbo-GGUF`: Q4_K_M, Q4_K_S, Q5_K_M, Q5_K_S and Q6_K.

This PR maps them onto MLX's affine quantized layers:

| GGUF type | MLX layer | how |
|---|---|---|
| Q4_K | 4-bit, group 32 | Every 32-wide sub-block is affine: scale `d *
sc`, bias `-dmin * m`. The 4-bit codes are copied unchanged. |
| Q5_K | 5-bit, group 32 | Same as Q4_K; the fifth bit comes from `qh`.
|
| Q5_0 / Q5_1 | 5-bit, group 32 | Scale `d`, bias `-16d` (Q5_0) or `m`
(Q5_1); the fifth bit comes from the block's `qh` word. |
| Q6_K | 8-bit, group 32 | Q6_K uses 16-wide groups, which MLX does not
have. Its exact dequantized values are re-quantized to 8 bits over 32,
so the step is at most a quarter of Q6_K's own. |
| Q2_K / Q3_K | refused, as before | 16-wide groups at 2-3 bits:
re-quantizing would cost accuracy. |

- `_pack` / `_unpack` now write MLX's little-endian bit stream for any
width; 4 and 8 bits are unchanged.
- The test checks the packing bit for bit against `mx.quantize` at 3, 4,
5, 6 and 8 bits.
- mflux 0.22.0 reads each layer's bits and group size from the stored
shapes (`weight_applier.py`), so a file mixing 4, 5 and 8-bit layers
loads without changes on that side.
- `quant_convertible` accepts the Q4_K_S/M, Q5_K_S/M, Q6_K, Q5_0 and
Q5_1 file names (with or without `UD-`). UD-Q4_K_XL and the Q2 / Q3
names stay refused. The per-tensor type check at conversion time still
has the final say.

## Accuracy

Studio's converter run on the real `z-image-turbo-Q4_K_M.gguf` and
`Q4_K_S.gguf`. Every converted tensor was read back with `mx.dequantize`
and compared with gguf-py's own dequantization:

| type | tensors | worst rel. L2 vs gguf-py | worst max error / max
weight |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q4_K | 112 (+187 in Q4_K_S) | 0.60% | 0.83% |
| Q5_K | 92 (+53) | 0.63% | 0.69% |
| Q6_K | 36 | 0.55% | 0.52% |
| Q8_0 (already supported, for reference) | 240 | 0.17% | 0.39% |

All of that is the bf16 rounding of the scale and bias, which the
existing Q4_0 / Q8_0 path does too. To put it in proportion, here are
the same weights against the original bf16 Z-Image-Turbo transformer (24
tensors):

| type | GGUF vs bf16 | MLX conversion vs bf16 |
|---|---|---|
| Q4_K | 7.1-7.4% | 7.1-7.4% (+0.02 points) |
| Q5_K | 3.5-4.2% | 3.5-4.3% (+0.04 points) |
| Q6_K | 1.9-2.1% | 2.0-2.2% (+0.07 points) |

## Tests

- `test_kquant_codes_and_scales_reproduce_gguf_dequantize_exactly`
(Q4_K, Q5_K): codes and fp32 scales reproduce gguf-py's dequantization
bit for bit. The fp16 store stays within the per-group rounding bound.
- `test_q6_k_requantizes_to_8_bits_within_a_quarter_of_its_own_step`.
- `test_affine_matches_gguf_dequantize_exactly` and the bf16-scale bound
test now also cover Q5_0 / Q5_1.
- `test_pack_matches_mlx_layout_bit_for_bit` (3/4/5/6/8 bits, real MLX).
- `test_a_q4_k_m_mixture_converts_and_mlx_reads_every_layer`: a Q4_K +
Q5_K + Q6_K + Q5_0 + Q4_0 + Q8_0 + BF16 file, read back through MLX.
- The refusal tests now use Q3_K_M / Q2_K. The router's
predict-vs-select matrix covers a Q4_K_M pick on the MLX side and a
Q3_K_M pick on the refusal side.

On Linux with MLX's CPU build (mlx 0.32.4, mflux 0.22.0),
`test_mlx_diffusion_convert.py`, `test_mlx_diffusion_backend.py` and
`test_diffusion_mlx_engine_router.py` pass, 299 tests. The same files on
the macOS runner, on real Metal: 298 passed, 1 skipped.

## Not covered

- The end-to-end evidence is one render. Through Studio's engine,
together with the other Mac MLX changes, on a GitHub `macos-15` runner
(Apple M1 Virtual, 7 GB, Metal), the real Z-Image-Turbo Q4_K_M converted
in 129 s, loaded, and rendered a coherent image at 512 and at 1024. On

was not scored on the Mac; the tensor-level comparison above is the
