FP8 block decode: weight-only GEMV where it beats the block GEMM, fused small-M called directly (#14813)

## Summary

Follow-up to #14792 (block-FP8 small M: fused `act_quant` + narrow-N
w8a8 kernel), which is merged on main. This adds a weight-only block-FP8
GEMV for decode and fixes the order in which the two decode kernels are
tried.

**GEMV** (decode: one token per sequence, no grad, sm89+ CUDA): reads
the fp8 weight once and applies the block scale to unquantized bf16 /
fp16 activations with fp32 accumulation. `M` is not specialized. It only
takes shapes where it is faster than main's `act_quant` + block GEMM in
both timing modes (L2 flushed, and CUDA graph replay with the weight hot
in L2):

- narrow outputs only (2N <= K: k / v, o, down);
- on parts with fewer than 100 SMs: weights up to 16M elements, at most
8 decode rows, and at most 2 rows on weights over 8M elements (L2 hot,
its 16-row tile becomes compute bound: on L4, 2048x6144 at 4 / 8 / 16
rows took 1.06x / 1.46x / 1.98x main's time before this cap);
- on parts with 100+ SMs: up to 16 rows.

A weight's eligibility (including its row cap) is decided once per scale
tensor. Prefill, training, pre-sm89 and ROCm keep the block path.
`UNSLOTH_FP8_BLOCK_GEMV=0` disables it.

**Order between the two kernels**, fixed at import:

| devices | eager decode | compiled regions |
|---|---|---|
| any CUDA device with fewer than 100 SMs (L4) | GEMV where it applies,
else the fused small-M kernel | GEMV where it applies, else the block
GEMM |
| all CUDA devices with 100+ SMs (RTX PRO 6000, B200), Triton block GEMM
| fused small-M kernel, called directly; the GEMV only where the fused
kernel does not apply | GEMV where it applies, else the block GEMM (the
fused kernel is eager only) |
| FBGEMM / torchao block GEMM | GEMV, else that GEMM | same |

With the GEMV tried first everywhere, the combined path was 3% to 4%
faster than #14792 alone on L4 but 2% to 3% slower on RTX PRO 6000
(Qwen3-1.7B / 8B FP8, batch 1 / 4 / 8, A/A at most 3.2%), which is why
big parts try the fused kernel first.

## End to end decode

Greedy decode, 64 new tokens, torch 2.14.1. Main, #14792 and this PR run
from separate checkouts in separate processes, interleaved main, PR, PR,
main, 3 rounds (the two PRs alternate order); tok/s is the median, A/A
is the largest main vs main gap within a round.

| GPU | model | batch | main tok/s | #14792 / main | this PR / main |
this PR / #14792 | A/A |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L4 | Qwen3-1.7B-FP8 | 1 | 14.1 | 1.276 | 1.323 | 1.036 | 1.9% |
| L4 | Qwen3-1.7B-FP8 | 4 | 56.8 | 1.273 | 1.314 | 1.033 | 1.9% |
| L4 | Qwen3-1.7B-FP8 | 8 | 113.4 | 1.266 | 1.310 | 1.035 | 2.2% |
| L4 | Qwen3-8B-FP8 | 1 | 10.8 | 1.231 | 1.302 | 1.058 | 1.8% |
| L4 | Qwen3-8B-FP8 | 4 | 43.2 | 1.245 | 1.312 | 1.053 | 1.9% |
| L4 | Qwen3-8B-FP8 | 8 | 86.3 | 1.238 | 1.309 | 1.057 | 2.1% |
| RTX PRO 6000 | Qwen3-1.7B-FP8 | 1 | 55.5 | 1.150 | 1.206 | 1.049 |
2.0% |
| RTX PRO 6000 | Qwen3-1.7B-FP8 | 4 | 219.8 | 1.153 | 1.201 | 1.042 |
0.6% |
| RTX PRO 6000 | Qwen3-1.7B-FP8 | 8 | 438.5 | 1.151 | 1.198 | 1.041 |
2.0% |
| RTX PRO 6000 | Qwen3-8B-FP8 | 1 | 42.7 | 1.145 | 1.190 | 1.039 | 1.0%
|
| RTX PRO 6000 | Qwen3-8B-FP8 | 4 | 170.3 | 1.154 | 1.192 | 1.033 | 1.3%
|
| RTX PRO 6000 | Qwen3-8B-FP8 | 8 | 339.2 | 1.153 | 1.191 | 1.032 | 1.4%
|

Engagement per 64-token generate: on L4, Qwen3-1.7B runs 5292 GEMV calls
at batch 1 (k, v, down) and 3528 at batch 4 / 8 (k, v; down is past its
2-row cap), the rest on the fused kernel. On RTX PRO 6000 every decode
projection runs the fused kernel and the GEMV runs 0 times in eager; the
gain over #14792 there is host time, since the fused kernel is called
directly instead of through `FP8BlockQuantLinear.forward`.

## Kernel timing, both modes

Every shape and row count the GEMV takes, out of 20 swept projection
shapes (Qwen3 0.6B to 8B, Llama 8B) at M = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, bf16. GEMV
time / main's `act_quant` + block GEMM time, 3 interleaved rounds,
medians:

| GPU | N x K | rows taken | L2 flushed device time | CUDA graph replay,
L2 hot |

QAT: fake quantize Gemma embeddings on the float32 and Accelerate-hooked paths (#14702)

QAT restores Embedding subclasses such as Gemma3TextScaledWordEmbedding
on top of torchao's FakeQuantizedEmbedding (#14376). Two paths still
skipped the weight fake quantizer, so training saw the unquantized
embedding that export later quantizes.

1. Float32 Gemma. With UNSLOTH_FORCE_FLOAT32, unsloth_zoo replaces the
Gemma3 / Gemma4 embedding forward with one that calls
F.embedding(self.weight) directly. The restored class only fake
quantized through super().forward(), so the quantizer never ran.
2. Accelerate hooks. _copy_embedding_subclass_state copied the instance
forward that add_hook_to_module installs. That forward is a partial
bound to the old module, so the replacement ran the old, unquantized
embedding.

Fix:
- The restored class runs the original forward on the fake quantized
weight (scoped reparametrization). A plain lookup sits behind super(),
so the upstream path is still quantized exactly once.
- The instance forward is no longer copied. The Accelerate hook is
re-attached to the replacement (offload hooks excluded).

Tiny Gemma3 on CPU, int8-int4, fake quantizer calls per embedding
forward:

| Path | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| upstream forward | 1 | 1 |
| UNSLOTH_FORCE_FLOAT32 forward | 0 (output equals unquantized) | 1 |
| AlignDevicesHook on the embedding | 0 (output equals unquantized) | 1
|

Tests: new cases in tests/test_qat_phone_deployment.py cover the
direct-weight forward, the hooked embedding and fullgraph tracing. The
direct-weight and hooked cases fail before this change. The QAT test
files pass on CPU (85 passed, 7 CUDA-only skips).


## Scope of the embedding swap (later commits)

- An offloaded embedding (one Accelerate `AlignDevicesHook`, also inside
a `SequentialHook`) keeps its hook on the fake quantized replacement; at
save time its weight and buffers are loaded from `weights_map` on CPU
before conversion or stripping.
- An embedding with any other instance `forward` override or forward
hooks is left out of QAT with a one-time warning and is trained and
saved unquantized, with its override and hooks untouched. Previously it
was swapped and the hooks were silently dropped.

Studio MLX images: tile the VAE decode when the untiled one would not fit (#14796)

## Summary

The opt-in MLX image engine (`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_MLX=1`, Z-Image) always
ran mflux's VAE decode untiled. Measured through Metal on an Apple M1,
the mflux Z-Image VAE decode in bf16 needs this much on top of its
weights:

| decode | working set above the weights | time |
|---|---|---|
| 512x512, untiled | 1.99 GiB | 1.49 s |
| 1024x1024, untiled | 6.64 GiB | 14.5 s |
| 1024x1024, tiled (mflux's 512 px tiles, 64 px overlap) | 2.00 GiB |
8.2 s |

1024x1024 is Z-Image's default size. Take a 16 GB Mac, whose Metal
working set is 10.67 GiB, holding Z-Image Q4_0 with an 8-bit text
encoder (8.65 GiB). It has about 2 GiB left, so the untiled decode goes
4.6 GiB over and pages.

This PR decides before each generation whether to tile, and sets mflux's
`TilingConfig` only when needed:

- **Estimate.** The untiled decode is estimated at 0.44 GiB plus 6.35 KB
per output pixel, fitted to the two measurements above. It is compared
with Metal's recommended working set minus what MLX holds live at that
moment (the resident model).
- **Tile only when it does not fit.** ComfyUI also tiles only after an
out-of-memory decode. Unified memory pages instead of failing, so the
check has to come first.
- **Room to spare keeps the old result.** A Mac with enough free working
set keeps the untiled decode, bit for bit what main produces. A 512x512
image is a single tile either way.
- **Decoders mflux marks as unsafe are left alone.** Only decoders mflux
allows to tile implicitly (`TilingConfig.may_tile_implicitly`; the
FLUX.2 VAE opts out) are tiled. mflux's own `--low-ram` mode tiles the
same way.
- **Override.** `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_MLX_VAE_TILING=1` / `0` forces tiling
on or off.
- **Reporting.** The decision appears in each image's timings
(`vae_tiled`) and in `status()["vae_tiling"]`.

## Accuracy

These are VAE-only decodes of the same seeded random-normal latents on
the runner, scored against a torch fp32 decode of the same VAE:

| decode | LPIPS vs fp32 | PSNR vs fp32 |
|---|---|---|
| 512, untiled | 0.00156 | 43.70 dB |
| 512, tiled | 0.00156 (identical, one tile) | 43.70 dB |
| 1024, untiled | 0.00145 | 43.85 dB |
| 1024, tiled | 0.00166 | 43.27 dB |

At 1024 the tiled and untiled images differ from each other by LPIPS
0.0029 (41.0 dB). In both, the mflux bf16 VAE's own difference from fp32
is about 0.0015.

## Tests

- `test_vae_tiling_engages_only_when_the_untiled_decode_does_not_fit`:
16 GB and 64 GB budgets at 512, 1024 and 2048.
- `test_vae_tiling_env_and_unknown_budget`: an unreadable budget never
tiles.
- `test_untiled_decode_estimate_matches_the_metal_measurements`.
- `test_the_runtime_sets_mfluxs_tiling_config_per_generation`: runs on
real mflux. It checks that `TilingConfig` is set when the decode does
not fit and left unset when it fits, and that a VAE which opts out is
never tiled.

All of them fail on main. Run on Linux with MLX's CPU build (mlx 0.32.4,
mflux 0.22.0): `test_mlx_diffusion_backend.py`,
`test_mlx_diffusion_convert.py` and
`test_diffusion_mlx_engine_router.py` pass, 264 tests.

0.32.4, mflux 0.22.0.

Studio video: stream-encode Wan clips under the ROCm bf16 VAE decode (#14653)

## Problem

On ROCm gfx11 / gfx12 (Strix Halo, RDNA3, RDNA4), Studio decodes the Wan
VAE in bf16 by default (`install_rocm_vae_bf16_decode`, 6x faster per
clip than fp32 on gfx1151). The wrapper runs the decoder in bf16 and
hands the pipeline the fp32 widening of its output, so diffusers'
postprocess runs in fp32.

The overlapped video encode (#14405) converts each decoder chunk to
uint8 inside a forward hook, from the raw chunk. On this path the raw
chunk is bf16, so the hook postprocessed in bf16 while the exported
frames were postprocessed in fp32. The rounding differed, `_matches`
never passed, and every clip did all of the streamed work and then
encoded again. A gfx1151 default Wan render logs:

```
video.stream_encode: fallback (frames differ)
```

on every clip.

## Change

`StreamEncode` checks whether the VAE carries the ROCm bf16 decode
(`vae._unsloth_bf16_decode_mode`, set by the installer, so it survives
the untiled-when-fits layer Studio puts on top). When it is, the hook
widens each chunk to fp32 before the clamp and postprocess, which is
what the pipeline does with the widened output. Unpatchify and clamp are
exact in either dtype, so the chunks now equal the exported frames bit
for bit.

Paths left as they are:

- NVIDIA's fp16 decode returns fp16, so its postprocess already runs in
fp16 and its chunks already match.
- A plain fp32 decoder is unaffected (the widen is a no-op there).

## Results

AMD CI, Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), Linux, torch 2.11.0+rocm7.13.0. Base and
head ran in the same job on the same machine, run
[39753304821](https://github.com/oobabooga/unsloth/actions/runs/39753304821):

- base = main `7fd4988b11`;
- head = base plus this diff;
- Wan2.2-TI2V-5B, all defaults, 832x480, 49 frames, 6 steps, family CFG,
2 prompts;
- `wan_stream_off` sets `UNSLOTH_STUDIO_VIDEO_STREAM_ENCODE=0`, and
every arm ran twice in fresh processes (A/A).

| cell | base: encode | head: encode | base steady s/clip | head steady
s/clip |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wan_auto` | fallback (frames differ) | streamed (49 frames) | 42.20 |
42.43 |
| `wan_auto_repeat` | fallback (frames differ) | streamed (49 frames) |
42.53 | 42.15 |
| `wan_stream_off` | off | off | 42.51 | 42.31 |
| `wan_stream_off_repeat` | off | off | 42.27 | 42.08 |

Verdict CONFIRMED: the base reproduces the fallback, and the head
streams on every default clip.

- **Pixels:** the exported frames have the same sha256 in every arm and
at both states.
- **Peak memory:** unchanged (26.08 GiB).
- **Speed:** at this clip size, the wall-clock difference between
streaming and not is inside the A/A spread (0.3-0.7%). Encoding 49
frames at 832x480 is well under a second of a 42 s render, so the change
removes duplicated work (a full streamed encode thrown away, then a
second encode) rather than buying a measurable speedup here. The saving
scales with encode time (longer or larger clips).

The first version of this change keyed the widen on the outermost
`vae.decode`. Its gfx1151 run
([39743742573](https://github.com/oobabooga/unsloth/actions/runs/39743742573))
still fell back, because Studio's untiled-when-fits decode wraps the
bf16 decode from outside. The final version reads the mode the bf16
install records on the VAE.

Studio diffusion: seed dense fp16 denoisers on the default and max tiers from measured peaks (#14720)

## Summary

On a T4 (and any pre-Ampere card: V100, Turing), Studio placed
FLUX.2-klein-4B as if one 1024x1024 render needed 8 GiB of activation
memory on top of the weights. Measured on a real T4, the peak above the
resident weights is 2.5 GiB on the first render and 1.4 GiB after that.
Because of that estimate the 7.4 GiB DiT streamed from host memory every
step, even though it fits the card.

The cause is not the attention check. On a Kaggle T4 (sm75, torch 2.13)
the SDPA probe runs the memory-efficient kernel, so
`sdpa_subquadratic_confirmed` is True. The real cause:

- Pre-Ampere cards load the denoiser dense in fp16, so
`measured_image_runtime_mib` takes its dense branch.
- That branch only had a seed for the eager tier
(`_MEASURED_DENSE_SPEED_MODES = ("off",)`).
- On Studio's default tier, and on max, it returned None.
`refine_plan_from_loaded_weights` then kept the flat plan (`8192 MiB x
pixels`, 0.85 for turbo models).
- Every multi-GPU fit that reads `measured_runtime_headroom_mib` fell
back to the same flat number.

Ampere and newer cards load bf16, which has no static seed (learned
peaks only), so they never take this branch. That is why only small
cards were affected.

## Change

`studio/backend/core/inference/diffusion_memory.py`, `_dense_seed_mib`:

- **Eager tier:** unchanged (the dense table).
- **Default / max tiers:** for a family the dense table measured at the
loaded DiT size, the seed is now the larger of:
  - the dense eager peak;
- the tier's worst phase in the existing per-phase table
(`_MEASURED_IMAGE_ACTIVATION_MIB`: encoder, denoise, untiled decode).

The result is then multiplied by the usual 1.15 margin and rounded up to
256 MiB. For FLUX.2-klein-4B that is `max(2455, 2645) x 1.15` = 3072 MiB
on default, and 3328 MiB on max.

What it never touches:

- A family the dense table lacks (Z-Image, SDXL, ...), a larger DiT than
the table covers (klein-9B), bf16, GGUF and torchao loads all keep
exactly the old answer.
- The default / max seeds apply only on a target the phase table was
measured on: NVIDIA CUDA where the SDPA probe saw a sub-quadratic kernel
run (`diffusion._measured_target`, recorded on the pipeline as
`_unsloth_dense_tier_seeds`). ROCm, math-only attention, MPS or a probe
that raises keep the flat estimate, since math attention needs far more
than the measured reserve. The Kaggle T4 runs below had the
memory-efficient kernel, so they take the seed.
- Learned peaks still only raise a seed, never lower it.
- The per-request guard (`measured_request_extra_mib`) reads the same
seed, scaled by pixels and batch. A 2048x2048 request asks for 12288 MiB
and streams resident groups again, so the OOM ladder stays a backstop.

Kill switch: `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_MEASURED_ACTIVATION_DENSE_TIERS=0`
restores the flat estimate. The existing
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_MEASURED_ACTIVATION(_DENSE)=0` switches still apply.

This follows ComfyUI in spirit. ComfyUI prices inference memory per
pixel per model (`memory_usage_factor`, plus `minimum_inference_memory`
= 0.8 GiB + `EXTRA_RESERVED_VRAM`), not as a flat amount. Here the
per-model number is a measurement rather than a factor, and the margin
is above what ComfyUI keeps.

Z-Image is deliberately left out. An earlier version also seeded it from
the phase table (no dense entry). On a T4 that kept its 11.5 GiB DiT
partly resident, and that ran slower than streaming it whole: 3.8 to 4.4
s/step against 3.2 to 3.6 on main. Z-Image keeps the flat plan until
partial residency of a dense DiT is faster than streaming.

## Results, Kaggle T4 (15 GB, fp16, torch 2.13)

Each arm is a fresh process with an empty Studio home (no learned

## Summary

Under group offload (Studio's default int8 plan on 12-16 GB cards),
every int8 Linear in Z-Image's fused attention processor hit a Dynamo
graph break at `importlib.import_module`.
`diffusion_int8_fused.install()` returns before `_finalize` when
`offload_active` is set, and `_finalize` itself returns before it caches
`_INTMM_MODULE` when the weights are on no CUDA card. The patched

fused QKV when present) through `int8_linear`, so each `_int_mm` fell

resolve + cache). `install()` calls it right after the kill switch,

first, before the device checks; it still returns 0 when no home is
found, and the device probes, act-quant probe and per-card checks run
exactly as before.
- `diffusion_zimage_fused.py`, `diffusion_qwenimage21_fused.py`: the
processor factories that bind `int8_linear` also resolve it eagerly, so
the result does not depend on install order.
- `_int_mm` keeps its eager fallback for direct calls (tests).

`install(..., offload_active=True)` and after `_finalize` on a model
with no CUDA weights. Both fail on main (1 break each) and pass here.

kernel is probed only for resident cards.

MXFP4 packed Linear: bound the below-sm_80 weight decode by free memory (#14784)

## MXFP4 packed Linear: bound the below-sm_80 weight decode by free
memory

Since unsloth-zoo #1899 the fused MXFP4 tile GEMM is off below sm_80. A
T4 forward through `Mxfp4PackedLinear` (compressed-tensors
`mxfp4-pack-quantized`) with up to 64 rows therefore decodes the whole
16-bit weight and calls cuBLAS. That is about 8 to 24x faster there. But
it holds the full weight: 112 MiB for a 14336 x 4096 fp16 weight, where
the tile kernel needed 28 KiB. With less free memory than one
dequantized weight, the forward now runs out of memory.

### Change
Below sm_80, when the tile kernel passed its self-check but is
arch-gated (`mxfp4_grouped_gemv_available` and not
`mxfp4_gemm_available`), `mxfp4_packed_matmul` now:
1. Allocates the whole 16-bit weight first, decodes into it and makes
one cuBLAS call. This is the current behaviour, same kernels and same
output.
2. If that allocation fails, it decodes row chunks of the packed `[out,
in / 2]` weight into one reused buffer and writes `y[..., r0:r1]`. Each
output column comes from one chunk, so nothing is summed across chunks.
The chunk size is half of what the allocator can still hand out: driver
free memory, capped by `set_per_process_memory_fraction`, plus cached
free blocks. It is measured once after the failed allocation and kept
per GPU, and the whole weight is retried after 1024 calls.
3. If not even 128 rows fit, it runs the tile kernel, which needs only
its output.

The memory queries cost about 100 us, so they run only after an
allocation has failed. A forward that fits pays nothing extra. Under
`torch.compile` this path is a custom op
(`unsloth::mxfp4_bounded_dense_matmul`, with a fake impl). The
allocation fallbacks therefore run at call time instead of being traced
once, with no new graph break. sm_80+ and ROCm (tile kernel), dX, and
inputs over 64 rows are unchanged. With an older unsloth-zoo that has no
sm_80 floor, the new branch is never reached.

### Validation
New `tests/test_mxfp4_packed_low_memory.py`. The sm_75 policy is applied
on any GPU, kernels are real, and the allocator is capped to allocated +
N MiB.

OOM (112 MiB) | pass, peak under 64 MiB, no second OOM |

(`fullgraph=True`, then 64 MiB headroom) | OOM | pass, 0 graph breaks |
| `test_row_chunks_match_the_single_shot_decode` (24 cases: fp16 / bf16,
1 / 7 / 64 rows, bias, 2D / 3D, `out=`) | pass (no chunking) | pass,
within 1 ulp of the single-shot output |

- A grid is capped at 64 cells. Past that, the panel says how many cells
the axes make, and Generate grid is disabled.
- **Progress**: the generation overlay reads `Cell 3/9: Steps: 20,
Sampler: Euler`, and the panel counts finished cells.
- **Result**:
  - A dialog shows each grid with a Download PNG button.
- The PNG carries an A1111-style `parameters` chunk: the shared recipe
plus `Script: X/Y/Z plot, X Type, X Values, ...`.
- Every cell is also saved to the gallery with its own recipe, so any
cell can be restored or reused.

## How

- **Each cell is one request through the existing generate endpoint,
sent from the page's own Generate loop.** `handleGenerate` reads the run
from a ref, so a grid keeps the same behaviour as a normal Generate:
Stop, live progress, the lost-response recovery, the gallery merge and
the error toasts. The only edits inside the loop are:
  - the run count
  - wrapping the request body in `compareRequest(...)`
  - one `onImages` callback
- **No backend batch endpoint.** A grid cell is a full denoise taking
seconds, against a few ms of JSON round trip. Batching seeds or prompts
through `seeds` / `prompts` would change the denoiser's batch size,
which costs a compile and a graph capture per distinct size. The other
axes (steps, CFG, sampler, shift) cannot share a batch anyway.
- **Cells run at batch size 1 with one shared seed** (A1111 `fix_seed`).
The prompt enhancer is off for every cell, so a per-cell rewrite cannot
confound the comparison.
- **Run order**: A1111 nests z, y, x, and moves costly axes to the outer
loop (`AxisOption.cost`). On top of that, values of a costly axis run
grouped by shape class:
  - CFG on vs off, i.e. whether the unconditional pass runs
  - LoRA weight 0 vs above 0
  - each Prompt S/R text

So the denoiser changes shape at most once per class, and no cell needs
a model reload. Cells are placed in the grid by index, so the run order
does not affect the layout.
- **Code layout and startup bundle**: the new code lives in
`src/features/images/compare/` (values parser, axes / plan, run object,
grid layout and drawing, panel). The Images page imports it statically,
and the page is already its own lazy chunk, so none of it is on the
startup path. `bundle:check` is unchanged from main: 6,718.1 KB raw /
2,023.3 KB transfer, 97 chunks. A nested `import()` of the panel was
measured too: rolldown split startup-shared modules out of their chunks,
giving +3 startup chunks and putting the budget over by 1.2 KB transfer.

Fused preference loss: fall back when lm_head has module backward hooks (#14788)

With UNSLOTH_FUSED_PREFERENCE_LOSS=1, DPO / ORPO / CPO score completions
from
head.weight through the chunked kernel and never call the output head
module.
`_output_head` already declined heads with forward hooks, but it
accepted heads
with module backward hooks. Those hooks then never ran, so a hook that
rewrites
grad_input (gradient scaling, masking, some PEFT/analysis tooling)
silently gave
different gradients than TRL's own forward.

Repro (tiny float64 Llama, ORPO, CPU):

| hook on lm_head | hook calls stock / fused | max grad diff |
|---|---|---|
| none | 0 / 0 | 5.6e-17 |
| full backward hook zeroing grad_input | 1 / 0 | 2.38 |
| full backward pre hook, grad_output x3 | 1 / 0 | 4.77 |

`_backward_hooks` (full or legacy), `_backward_pre_hooks`, or a global
module
backward (pre) hook is registered. Weight tensor hooks and
AccumulateGrad hooks
are left alone: the kernel returns dW through autograd, so they already
fire
and match the stock gradients (covered by a new test).

The no-hook path is unchanged; the existing TRL parity cases pass as
before.

MoE dW accumulation: fall back when autograd Node hooks can rewrite dW (#14759)

Follow-up to #14480.

The in-place dW path adds the expert weight gradient straight into
`param.grad` and returns `None` for W. Tensor hooks and
post-accumulate-grad hooks on W were already detected, but hooks
registered on autograd Nodes were not:

- `register_prehook` on the weight's `AccumulateGrad` node
- `register_hook` on the `GroupedGemmBackward` node

Both received `None` instead of dW, so a hook that scales or replaces
the gradient was silently ignored. `UNSLOTH_MOE_DW_ACCUMULATE=0` was the
only workaround.

Nodes cannot list their hooks, but every Python hook of one kind on a
Node lives in one shared dict, and the handle of a new registration
points at it. `_dW_accumulate_target` now registers a no-op on both
nodes, checks whether anything else is in the dict, and removes the
no-op. If a hook is present, that weight uses the returned-gradient
path. The probe runs last, only for weights that are otherwise eligible,
and never under `torch.compile`.

No-hook behaviour is unchanged: same kernel call, same `param.grad`
bytes, in-place path still taken. Host overhead is a few microseconds
per eligible dW call.

Tests: `tests/test_moe_dw_accumulate_node_hooks.py` runs the real
autograd wrapper on CPU with the Triton GEMMs replaced by dense matmuls.
It checks that hooked weights match `UNSLOTH_MOE_DW_ACCUMULATE=0`
bitwise, and that unhooked or unhooked-after-removal weights still
accumulate in place. The two Node hook cases fail before this change.

GRPO routing replay: prime router formulas before compile and score the PEFT reference without replay (#14756)

Two problems with MoE routing replay (UNSLOTH_GRPO_ROUTING_REPLAY=1) as
installed by the GRPO trainer.

Cold fullgraph compile
The unsloth_zoo replay hook picks each router's weight formula on its
first replayed call by reading tensor values (.item(), torch.allclose,
data dependent branches). A router compiled with fullgraph=True and no
eager warm-up failed to trace. The existing compile test warms up
eagerly, so it did not catch this. Right after the hooks are installed,
each hooked router now runs once eagerly on a small synthetic input with
a natural-routing replay. The zoo's own selection picks and caches the
formula, and the zoo state is restored afterwards.

PEFT reference scoring
TRL scores the PEFT reference on the policy model inside
disable_adapter(). The replay hooks stayed attached there, so the
reference log-probabilities used the rollout's routes, while a separate
reference model routes naturally (verl also disables replay for the
reference). The trainer now wraps self.model.disable_adapter so the
replay hooks are detached inside it and restored in their original order
afterwards.

Nothing changes when UNSLOTH_GRPO_ROUTING_REPLAY is unset.

Tests
tests/test_grpo_routing_replay_trainer_hooks.py runs the exact post-init
code rl.py generates:
- a cold router compiled with fullgraph=True replays the forced experts
with correct weights and gradients;
- inside disable_adapter() the reference logits equal the base model's
natural routing, the hooks are back afterwards, and the policy forward
replays again;
- with replay off, nothing is installed or wrapped.
The first two fail on main. The rl.py related CPU suites pass (381
passed, 17 skipped).

Studio: size auto-quantised text encoders at the hosted file in the image picker (#14735)

## Summary

The Images model picker sized every dense row with its text encoder at
bf16, even for families whose automatic load swaps the encoder for a
hosted pre-quantised file (`te_quant_auto` in `diffusion_families.py`,
resolved by `diffusion_te_prequant.te_prequant_sources`). The row
therefore looked several GB bigger than what the backend actually keeps
resident, and the router fell through to the slower GGUF row on cards
where the dense DiT plus the quantised encoder fits.

This PR gives each affected row the size of the encoder file the backend
really loads, and feeds it into `residentSizeGb`, so the fit badge, the
"Fits on device" filter and the default-artifact router all use it. On
the backend, an automatic int8 encoder pick is now budgeted at the int8
ConvRot file's own fraction instead of the fp8 files' 0.65 ceiling,
since that pick never opens the fp8 file. That brings the backend and
the picker into agreement.

Rows whose encoder stays bf16 on an automatic load are unchanged. That
covers families with no `te_quant_auto` (the ComfyUI template keeps the
encoder bf16: Z-Image, FLUX.1 schnell / dev / Krea, FLUX.2 klein,
Lumina, HiDream) and families whose automatic int8 file is not hosted,
so the backend loads the dense encoder (Qwen-Image, Qwen-Image 2512,
Qwen-Image-Edit, HunyuanImage 2.1, Krea 2).

Studio diffusion: Automatic multi-GPU placement fixes and a placement decision in status (#14657)

## Summary

Automatic GPU placement (no GPU picked in the UI) is meant to follow
three rules on a multi-GPU host:

1. If the model fits one GPU, use one GPU.
2. If it does not, and there are two GPUs, use both.
3. If the diffusion model fits GPU 0 and the text model fits GPU 1, put
them there.

On current main the order is already right (one card resident, then the
companion split, then the layer split, then
one-card offload), and Automatic never arms CFG-parallel (a second copy
of the denoiser), so rule 1 holds. But the
budgets that gate rule 3 were stricter than the one-card plan they
replace, so on common hosts the text encoder kept
streaming from host RAM next to an idle second card. Status also did not
say what was chosen or why.

This PR:

- Records the decision. `status()["multi_gpu"]["decision"]` now has the
chosen placement, a one-line summary with the
  sizes, and every rejected candidate with its reason, for example:
`placement: layer split: denoiser blocks across cuda:0, cuda:1 (denoiser
7.2 GiB does not fit one card with its
working memory)`, rejected `one_card` (everything resident on cuda:0
needs 24.9 GiB, 12.5 GiB free after the
reserve), `companion_split` (text_encoder on cuda:1: cuda:0 still needs
17.4 GiB of 10.6 GiB), `cfg_parallel`
(denoiser is split across cards). That is the real FLUX.2-klein-base-4B
record on Kaggle 2x T4. A split that fails at placement reports its
one-card fallback. Nothing is recorded
without a multi-card selection, so one-card hosts and
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_MULTIGPU=0` see the same status as before.
- Fixes the companion split budget on the primary. When the one-card
plan already keeps the denoiser resident
(only the text encoders stream), the split is priced against the same
full budget that plan used, not 85% of it.
The split leaves the primary lighter than the plan it replaces, so it
was being refused for no reason.
- Prices a second card that only runs text encoders like an encoder
card: weights plus 1 GiB of encoder room against
its free memory minus ComfyUI's per-card floor (1.2 GiB on Linux, 1.5
GiB on Windows), the rule the layer split
already uses for cards that only run blocks. Before, it was weights + 1
GiB + 2 GiB base overhead against 85% of
(free - reserve), so a 15 GB T4 could not take Wan's 10.6 GiB umt5-xxl.
The more permissive of the two prices wins,
  so nothing the old rule accepted is refused.
- Caps the discrete VRAM reserve at 4 GiB: `max(2 GiB, min(10% of total,
4 GiB))`. It was 10% of the total, 17.8 GiB
on a 178 GiB card, which forced offload (and refused every split) on a
partly used big card with 20-30 GiB free.
Cards up to 40 GiB are unchanged (every consumer card, T4, L4, A100 40
GB). The load's own activations are still
priced separately, so this stays above ComfyUI's fixed ~1.2 GiB. The
ROCm APU pool keeps the uncapped 10% (it is
  shared with the CPU).
- The layer split's decline reason now reports the shortfall with the
text encoders streamed (they always can be)
and the primary's activation share, instead of counting the encoders
against the cards.

## Summary

On a CPU-only or no-usable-GPU host, a Krea 2 GGUF load fell back to
diffusers: the `krea-2` family had no `sd_cpp_vae` /
`sd_cpp_text_encoders`, so `family_sd_cpp_supported` was false and the
router recorded "family 'krea-2' has no native sd.cpp asset mapping".
Low-end hosts should run stable-diffusion.cpp, which has supported Krea
2 since master-721 (leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp#1705, commit 8caa3f9).

This adds the native mapping and a capability gate:

- **VAE**: `unsloth/Krea-2-Turbo`
`vae/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors`, Krea's own
`AutoencoderKLQwenImage` (Wan 2.1 layout) from the ungated mirror. Raw
and Turbo ship it byte-identical (same LFS sha256).
- **Text encoder**: `unsloth/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct-GGUF`
`Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct-Q8_0.gguf` through `--llm`. Krea's `text_encoder`

RMSNorm kernels: do not specialize on the row count and row stride (#14786)

## What was wrong

The RMSNorm Triton kernels take the row count as a plain runtime
integer. Triton specializes integer arguments on `== 1` and on
divisibility by 16, so every new token count class can compile another
copy of the same kernel. In a training run with variable-length batches
and then decode (one row), the backward kernel ends up compiled several
times for identical code. The affected arguments are row counts or
derived counts that only drive loops and masks:

- `_rms_layernorm_backward`: `n_rows`, `rows_per_program`
- `_rms_layernorm_forward_rows`: `n_rows`
- `_rms_layernorm_backward_rows`: `n_rows`, `blocks_per_program`
- `_rms_sum_dw_partials`: `n_programs`

## Change

Mark those arguments `do_not_specialize` (names checked against the
kernel signatures). Strides and `n_cols` are left alone, so the inner
loads keep their vectorization hints.

## Validation

B200, torch 2.14 + Triton 3.8, shared GPU. Compiled variants counted
from `JITFunction.device_caches`, bf16, Gemma and non-Gemma, 31 row
counts (1 to 19, 31, 32, 33, 100, 511, 512, 1000, 2048, 3001, 4096,
8192):

| kernel | width | base | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_rms_layernorm_backward` | 2048 | 10 | 2 (Gemma / non-Gemma) |
| `_rms_layernorm_forward_rows` | 128 (multi-row path) | 6 | 2 |
| `_rms_layernorm_backward_rows` | 128 | 10 | 4 |
| `_rms_sum_dw_partials` | 128 | 3 | 1 |
| `_rms_layernorm_forward`, `_gemma_rms_layernorm_forward` | 2048 | 1, 1
| 1, 1 |

Outputs are bitwise identical to base for Y, dX and dW in 36 cases: bf16
and fp16, Gemma and non-Gemma, widths 128 / 1024 / 4096, rows 1 / 17 /
4096.

New `tests/test_triton_variant_budget.py` fails on base and passes here.

Tests (`-o addopts= -m "not server and not native_mxc"`): the new test
plus the RMSNorm / norm test files (multirow, multirow settings, fast
launch, gradient layout, save output, weight grad, grad alias,
`test_rms_rope_compile.py`, fused add inference): 1052 passed, 16
skipped on torch 2.10 + Triton 3.6 and on torch 2.14 + Triton 3.8.

## Not covered

- No exclusive-GPU timing. `do_not_specialize` drops the `== 1` / `% 16`
hints for these arguments only; they feed loop bounds and row masks, not
the per-element address math, and the bitwise checks above show no
numeric change.
- ROCm and Triton below 3.6 (multi-row path is off there) were not run.

FP8 block decode: fused act_quant and narrow-N GEMM for 1 to 16 tokens (#14792)

## Summary

Block-FP8 decode (M <= 16 rows) launched `act_quant` and then the 16 x
128 tile w8a8 GEMM, which runs only N / 128 programs (32 for a 4096 wide
projection). This fuses the activation quantization into a narrow-N w8a8
kernel, one launch per linear:

- Quantizes the activation tile in-kernel with the same max / 448 scale
and e4m3 cast as `act_quant`.
- N tile and an optional deterministic split K are sized from the SM
count; `M` is not specialized, so batch 1 and batch 16 share one
compiled variant per shape.
- Without a grad to compute, `FP8BlockQuantLinear.forward` is called
directly, skipping the `autograd.Function` host cost.
- Larger M, the torchao / FBGEMM block routes, pre-sm89 devices and
`torch.compile` regions keep the previous path.
`UNSLOTH_FP8_BLOCK_SMALL_M=0` restores it.

## End to end decode

Greedy decode, 64 new tokens, torch 2.14.1. Main and this PR run from
separate checkouts in separate processes, interleaved main, PR, main, 3
rounds; tok/s is the median, A/A is the largest main vs main gap within
a round.

/ 1.15x / 1.15x | 0.3% / 0.7% / 0.7% |

A second RTX PRO 6000 session reproduced 1.15x to 1.16x. The fused
kernel ran 12348 times per 64-token Qwen3-1.7B generate (all 196

FP8 rowwise decode: one multi-row GEMV launch for 2 to 16 tokens (#14791)

## Summary

Per-channel (rowwise) FP8 weights with 2 to 16 decode rows (batched
`generate`, GRPO HF rollouts) went to `fbgemm_fp8_linear`, whose
`scaled_mm` backend dequantizes the whole weight to 16 bits on every
call below 64 rows. This adds a multi-row variant of the existing
rowwise GEMV that reads each fp8 weight tile once for all rows: exact
upcast, fp32 dot accumulate, per-channel scale applied after the sum,
split K only where K is long or N narrow (deterministic two-pass reduce,
no atomics).

- `M` is `do_not_specialize`, so one compiled kernel serves every batch
size from 2 to 16.
- Reached from the same callers as the 1-row GEMV: the
compressed-tensors FP8 forward
(`UNSLOTH_COMPRESSED_TENSORS_FP8_KERNELS=1`) and `fast_linear_forward`.

GEMV 2, reduce 0 |

The rows kernel's variant count is the same after batch 2 as after batch
16. Fewer Dynamo graphs because the 2 to 16 row calls no longer go
through the compiled `fbgemm_fp8_linear` path.

## Not proven

was dropped. The kernel correctness sweep from the branch work ran on

main's only `fp8.py` change in between (#14677) is in the fp16
per-tensor / per-row `weight_dequant`, off the decode paths timed here.

perf(studio): prefill MLX loads in the planned step while experts are on disk (#14466)

Stacked on #14326 (MLX PLE and expert offload in Unsloth Studio). Only
the last four commits are new here. It uses unslothai/unsloth-zoo#1918
(batch prefill step) and unslothai/unsloth-zoo#1919 (layer-at-a-time
prefill); with an unsloth_zoo that lacks them, each path keeps its
current step and grid.

## Summary

With MoE experts read from disk, every prefill step re-reads the
offloaded experts, so a larger step reads them fewer times per prompt.
unsloth_zoo's offload planner already chooses that step (up to 8192, by
the offloaded bytes re-read per prompt token), but Unsloth Studio pinned
the planner to its own 2048 chunk, dropped the result and generated at
2048. Loads with experts on disk now prefill in the planned step, while
prompt-cache reuse stays exact on mlx-vlm's 2048 grid.

## What changed

- **Planned step:**
- An auto offload plan lets the planner choose the step when experts may
go to disk, pricing each candidate step as a load prefilling in it, and
returns it.
- When the load puts experts on disk, every generation path prefills in
that step: mlx-lm single and batch, mlx-vlm single and audio input, and
unsloth_zoo's batch generation when it takes a step. The memory
estimate, the post-load context fit and the drafter fit price the same
step.
- Loads with resident experts, hand-set offload fractions and loads
Unsloth Studio does not price keep the runtime's own step.
- **Prefix reuse stays on mlx-vlm's grid:**
- When unsloth_zoo runs every layer of a window as mlx-vlm-step
sub-calls (`wide_prefill_step`), a session snapshots on mlx-vlm's step:
boundaries inside a window are copied by the layers as they pass them
(`capture_prefill_rows`), all-or-nothing over the cache entries.
- A prefix-reuse session prefills in the planned window only where that
holds and KV runtime quantization is off. Otherwise it prefills in
mlx-vlm's step, so reuse never falls back to a coarser 8192 grid.
- mlx-vlm prefills every prompt row but the last in chunks, so a resumed
turn answers exactly as an unreused one when both chunk on the same
grid.
- **Under a KV window,** the planned window stays off for prefix-reuse
sessions. Past a rotating window, mlx-vlm's Qwen3-VL derives position
ids from the cache's write index once per forward, so a planned-window
forward and mlx-vlm's steps would see different positions. Hybrid
families build caches without a limit and keep the planned window.

## Performance

Paired A/Bs on the same documents, 8K prompt, step 2048 vs the planned
8192 (with unslothai/unsloth-zoo#1919):

| model | machine | time to first token | decode | peak memory | greedy
tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-4bit, PLE + 75% of experts on disk | M5 Pro 48 GB |
41.2 -> 20.0 s (×0.49, se 0.005) | ×1.02 | 25.1 -> 26.8 GiB (priced by
the estimate) | identical 4/4 |
| Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B 3bit, experts offloaded | M3 Max 128 GB | 13.9 -> 7.6
s (×0.57) | ×1.00 | 5.7 -> 6.3 GiB | identical 4/4 |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 8bit, experts offloaded | M3 Max 128 GB | 16.0 -> 6.8
s (×0.51) | ×1.07 | 13.4 -> 14.1 GiB | identical 4/4 |

Prefix reuse on Flash-Next, a 1K-token follow-up turn after a 9.7-15.7K
first turn: resuming from in-window snapshots on the 2048 grid instead
of the 8192 grid cuts time to first token from 17.7 s to 14.1 s
(re-prefilled rows 5.5K -> 2.4K).

## Validation

```bash
cd studio/backend
python -m pytest tests/test_memory_estimate.py tests/test_mlx_inference_backend.py tests/test_mlx_vlm_prompt_cache.py -q
```

854 passed. The same 16 tests fail on the head of #14326 without these
commits (local environment and checkpoint pricing), and none fail newly.
New tests cover:

- the planner's step choice on the route the load takes;
- the step reaching each generation path;
- snapshot capture inside a window, all-or-nothing;
- the window being refused under KV runtime quantization or a KV window.

Studio: build the CFG-parallel replica outside inference mode and catch in-place edits of inference weights (#14626)

## Summary

Two CFG-parallel defects found after #14564 landed.

**1. The replica never builds on quantised weights, so CFG-parallel
never engages on the default tier.** The router builds the second-card
replica lazily on the first guided step, which runs inside the render's
`torch.inference_mode()`. There, `param.detach().to(device)` on a
torchao weight subclass created outside inference mode raises `Cannot
set version_counter for inference tensor`, and the router disables
itself. On a B200 the default tier picks an int8 transformer, so a
two-card Qwen-Image render ran entirely on one card (`steps_parallel` 0,
second card 0 GiB).

Repro matrix on two B200s (int8, fp8, NVFP4, MXFP8, bf16 x weights
loaded inside / outside inference mode x build inside / outside):
- Weights loaded outside inference mode, built inside it (the Studio
path): every quantised scheme raised; bf16 built.
- Weights loaded inside inference mode: no error, but the quantised
replica weights silently stayed on cuda:0 (replica devices `{cuda:0,
cuda:1}`), so the "replica" shared the primary's weights across cards.

**2. A stale replica after an in-place weight edit.**
`weights_fingerprint` reads each tensor's version counter, which
inference tensors do not have, so an in-place edit left the fingerprint
unchanged and the replica kept the old weights (probe: primary 3.0,
replica 1.0, 0 rebuilds).

## Change

- `build_replica` copies under `torch.inference_mode(False)` +
`torch.no_grad()`, and raises (CFG-parallel declines) if any replica
weight lands on a CUDA card other than the target.
- `weights_probe()` samples 64 evenly spaced bytes of each
inference-tensor weight (torchao inner tensors included) with one host
sync, at replica build and once per render, never per step, outside any
CUDA graph capture. When every weight has a version counter it reads
nothing, so the normal path costs nothing.
- LoRA load / unload / `set_adapters` paths in `_apply_loras` /
`_adjust_baked_loras` now drop the replica explicitly, next to where
they already reset the graphs.

## Testing

| Suite | this PR | main |
|---|---|---|
| CPU: multigpu, cfg_parallel_tier, zimage_cfg_split, static_skip | 221
passed | 218 passed, 3 failed (the new tests) |
| CUDA `test_diffusion_multigpu_cuda.py` on two cards | 7 passed | 4
passed, 3 failed (version_counter error; replica split across cards) |
| `test_a_lora_change_drops_the_cfg_parallel_replica` | pass | fail |

Real two-card run, Qwen/Qwen-Image through `DiffusionBackend` at the
default tier (int8, compiled, CUDA graphs): replica built on cuda:1,
`steps_parallel` 133 over 7 renders (19 guided steps each),
`predicted_hits` 126, not disabled. On main the same run disabled
CFG-parallel with the version_counter error.

Small int8 model, 8 steps: main disables (or, with weights loaded under
inference mode, runs on a replica split across both cards); this PR runs
7 parallel steps with the replica entirely on cuda:1 and output equal to
the single-card render. All 20 matrix cells build on cuda:1 with replica
output bitwise equal to the primary.

Not covered: no timing (shared, oversubscribed host); an in-place edit
that misses every sampled byte of a tensor is not caught (whole-tensor
edits are); GGUF on CUDA and NVFP4 in a full pipeline were not run
(GGUFParameter builds on CPU on both sides).

Studio diffusion: change baked LoRA subsets and weights without recompiling or recapturing (#14692)

## Summary

A torchao int8/fp8 load in Studio bakes its LoRA adapters before
quantize and compile. Since #14312, a later prompt can drop one of the
baked adapters (it runs at weight 0) or change a weight without a
reload. That change only moves the PEFT scale, but the scale is a Python
float read inside the LoRA forward:

- `torch.compile` guards on it (`self.scaling['lora_b'] == 1.0`), so
each new weight vector compiles the denoiser again.
- A CUDA graph records it as a kernel argument, so `_adjust_baked_loras`
calls `cuda_graph.reset_all` and the next prompt captures every graph
again. This also happens when you go back to a selection that was
already compiled.

The adapters and their shapes never change on a baked load, so neither
cost is needed.

## Change

- `_pin_baked_lora_scales`: once the denoiser is placed, and before
anything compiles or captures, each baked `scaling[adapter]` is stored
as a 0-d float32 tensor on the device of its LoRA weights. Compiled code
takes that tensor as a graph input, not as a guarded constant, and a
captured graph reads it from memory when it replays.
- `_adjust_baked_loras` writes the new weights into those tensors in
place (`fill_`) for a subset change, a weight change or turning
everything off. It skips `set_adapters` and the graph reset.
- In these cases the old `set_adapters` + `reset_all` path is still
used:
- an offloaded denoiser (hooks move the LoRA weights off the scale's
device)
  - LoRA weights that are not on the target device type
  - a scale that something has written back as a float
- CFG-parallel replica: `build_replica` copies the pinned tensors to the
replica's card. `weights_fingerprint` now reads their identity and
version counter rather than `repr`, so a write still rebuilds the
replica, and there is no device read on each call.

## Evidence

Tiny FLUX.2 klein (`Flux2Transformer2DModel`, random weights) loaded
through `DiffusionBackend.begin_load` with `transformer_quant="int8"`,
`speed_mode="max"` (compiled + CUDA graph), and two random rank-4 LoRAs
baked on every attention / FF Linear. 256x256, 4 steps, same seed.
Counts are per prompt.

| Prompt | main: new Dynamo graphs | main: graph captures | this PR: new
Dynamo graphs | this PR: graph captures |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 A+B (first) | 2 | 1 | 2 | 1 |
| P2 A+B (repeat) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| P3 A only (subset) | 2 (recompile) | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| P4 A+B (back) | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| P5 A only (again) | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| P6 A=0.5, B=1 | 2 (recompile) | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| P7 A+B (back) | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| P8 all off | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| P9 A+B (back) | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 |

On main, the recompile reason is the guard on `result = result +
lora_B(lora_A(dropout(x))) * scaling`. Every changed prompt captures the
graph again, even for a selection that was already compiled. With this
change, nothing recompiles or recaptures after the first prompt. On both
arms the images match: P2, P4 and P9 equal P1, P5 equals P3, and P3 and
P6 differ from P1.

Unit test
`test_baked_lora_subset_and_weight_changes_keep_compiled_graphs` uses a
real PEFT `lora.Linear` with two adapters under `torch.compile` and goes
through the real `_apply_loras`. It fails on main (`frame_count` 3,
expected 1) and passes with this change. On CPU with the change,
`tests/test_diffusion_lora.py` plus the multi-GPU wiring suites give 147
passed, 4 skipped.

## Not covered

- Offloaded (model / group / sequential) loads keep the previous
behaviour by design.
- CFG-parallel on two cards and layer-split were not run on GPUs, only
the replica fingerprint unit test.
- If diffusers' `scale_lora_layers` is called with a non-1
`attention_kwargs["scale"]`, it would scale the pinned tensor in place
and then unscale it. Studio does not pass that kwarg.

Studio Images: Hires fix and ESRGAN model upscalers (#14651)

Refs #10695

Adds the two top items from the Images settings survey: a one-click
**Hires fix** (render, upscale, refine in one request) and **model
upscalers** (ESRGAN family through `spandrel`) for Hires fix and the
existing Upscale workflow.

## What it does

**Hires fix** (Create only, off by default, shown only where the loaded
model has an image-to-image path, the same gating as the sampler
picker):

1. The base pass is the unchanged text-to-image call.
2. The result is enlarged with the chosen upscaler.
3. The family's img2img pipeline (the one the Upscale workflow already
uses) redraws it at the chosen denoise, with the same seed.

All three steps run inside one generation slot, so no other render can
land between them, and Stop works in every step.

| Setting | Default | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Upscale by | 1.5 | ComfyUI 2-pass example
(`hiresfix_latent_workflow.png`: 768 to 1152) and `LatentUpscaleBy`
default |
| Denoise | 0.5 | Same example, second KSampler `denoise: 0.5` |
| Hires steps | empty = the base Steps | The refine pass runs exactly
this many steps, like ComfyUI's KSampler (`new_steps = int(steps /
denoise)`, last `steps` sigmas) and A1111
(`steps=self.hr_second_pass_steps or self.steps` into
`setup_img2img_steps`) |
| Upscaler | Latent (nearest-exact) on SDXL, Lanczos elsewhere | ComfyUI
`LatentUpscale` nearest-exact in the example; latent only where the
img2img pipe takes 4-channel latents |
| Hires CFG | empty = the base guidance | Forge `hr_cfg` |

ComfyUI example:
https://comfyanonymous.github.io/ComfyUI_examples/2_pass_txt2img/

- Exact step count: diffusers img2img pipes run `int(N * strength)`
(SDXL) or `N - int(N - N * strength)` (FLUX.1, Qwen-Image, Z-Image)
steps, so the request is converted to the `num_inference_steps` that
runs exactly the requested count. ComfyUI's own count is tried first, so
14 steps at 0.5 is the same 28-step grid as the example.
- Supported where `img2img_pipeline_class` is set: SDXL, FLUX.1,
Qwen-Image and Z-Image. Every other family hides the control.
- Size: `round(side * scale / 16) * 16`, capped at a 2048 longest side
(the Upscale workflow's rule), and checked against the family's output
limits before anything runs.
- Denoise 0 means upscale only (no refine pass). The latent upscaler
needs a refine pass, so it refuses 0.
- Batch size and Runs work. Each image is refined with its own seed.
- Not combinable with a source image, a mask, references, ControlNet or
Upscale. Those requests are refused with a 400.

**Model upscalers**:

- New `core/inference/diffusion_upscalers.py`. Ids resolve against a
fixed catalog and a drop-in folder (`<workspace>/upscale_models`, `.pth`
/ `.pt` / `.safetensors`). A request never carries a path. Unknown ids,
path-like ids and names that are not in the folder are refused.
- Catalog: `R-ESRGAN 4x+` (RealESRGAN_x4plus) and `R-ESRGAN 4x+ Anime6B`
(RealESRGAN_x4plus_anime_6B). Both are release assets of
[xinntao/Real-ESRGAN](https://github.com/xinntao/Real-ESRGAN), which is
[BSD-3-Clause](https://github.com/xinntao/Real-ESRGAN/blob/master/LICENSE).
The GitHub API also reports `spdx_id: BSD-3-Clause` for the repo. The
model zoo (`docs/model_zoo.md`) links these exact URLs, and A1111
downloads the same files (`modules/realesrgan_model.py`). They are
downloaded on first use from the GitHub release URL and pinned by size
and SHA-256. A bad download is deleted, and offline mode refuses before
trying. Anything with an unclear or non-commercial licence (for example
4x-UltraSharp, CC BY-NC-SA) stays user-supplied in the drop-in folder.
- Loaded with `spandrel` (MIT), the loader ComfyUI and InvokeAI use.
`.pth` files go through `torch.load(weights_only=True)`.
- Inference runs in fp16 where the architecture supports it
(`supports_half`), else bf16, else fp32. Input tiles are 512 px with a
32 px overlap and linear feathering. The result is resized to the target
on the device instead of moving a 16 MP image through PIL.
- The upscaler stays resident on a load that does not offload. On a load
that offloads, it is freed right after use. Unloading the model always
drops it.
- `spandrel==0.4.2` is added to `extras-no-deps.txt`. Its dependencies
(torch, torchvision, safetensors, numpy, einops) are already installed.
Without spandrel the model upscalers are not listed, and Lanczos and
latent keep working.
- Upscale workflow: an `Upscaler` select next to Scale. The default
stays Lanczos, which is today's behaviour.

**stable-diffusion.cpp engine**: sd-server takes a `hires` object on
`/sdcpp/v1/img_gen` (`examples/common/common.cpp`, `SDGenerationParams`
JSON parser). Studio now sends it with an explicit target size, so both
engines render the same size. The upscaler is `Latent (nearest-exact)`,
`Lanczos`, or a model file linked into the server's
`--hires-upscalers-dir` for the request and removed afterwards. sd.cpp
runs ESRGAN itself, so spandrel is not needed there. An older sd-server
ignores an unknown JSON key, so the control is shown only when the
binary's `--help` lists `--hires-denoising-strength` (cached per binary
path and mtime). When the binary lacks it, or the load uses one-shot
sd-cli, the control is hidden and a reason is shown. sd.cpp has no
separate hires CFG and no denoise 0, so both are refused there. The
native engine has no img2img Upscale workflow, so `upscale_models` is
empty there.

**Metadata**: the gallery record stores `hires_scale`, `hires_denoise`,
`hires_steps`, `hires_upscaler`, `hires_guidance`, `hires_base_width` /
`hires_base_height` and `upscale_model`. `width` / `height` stay the
real output size. The infotext is written the way A1111 writes it
(`modules/processing.py`):

```
Steps: 25, CFG scale: 7.0, Seed: 1234, Size: 832x1216, Model: stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0, Denoising strength: 0.5, Hires upscale: 1.5, Hires upscaler: Latent (nearest-exact), Version: ...
```

- `Size` is the base pass (A1111 `"Size": f"{p.width}x{p.height}"`).
- `Hires steps` is written only when set. A1111 omits it at 0, which
means the same as the base steps.
- `Hires CFG Scale` (Forge's key) is written only when overridden.
- Paste and image import map these keys back into Hires fix. Upscaler
names match by id or A1111 label, and any `Latent*` maps to the latent
upscaler. An upscaler the model does not offer is named as not applied.
`Hires resize`, `Hires sampler` and `Hires prompt` stay reported as not
applied, as before. Restore puts the base size back into Width / Height.

## Graphs and memory

- The base pass is the plain txt2img call, so its compiled graphs and
CUDA graphs are the ones every plain render uses.
- The refine pass runs the img2img pipe, which shares the denoiser, at a
new input shape. That shape records once under the existing size policy
(one CUDA graph per input shape, `MAX_GRAPHS_PER_MODULE`, plus the
compile cache's per-shape registration).
- The next hires render at that size, and the plain renders after it,
record nothing new (numbers below).
- If a background compile is pending, the base pass leaves the kick
until after the refine pass, so the refine pass does not wait on it. The
refine pass does not add bg-compile samples, and a hires request counts
as one generation for the deferred speed profile.
- Memory: before the base pass denoises, the activation guard is also
asked about the refine size. A request whose refine pass cannot fit is
refused up front with the guard's own reason ("Hires fix: the refine
pass at WxH does not fit where the base pass at WxH does. ..."), and
"Generate anyway" still applies. The refine pass then runs its normal
guard, which engages VAE tiling when only that fits.

## Measurements

base steps).

Follow-up to #14611.
`test_decode_rope_on_another_device_orders_with_the_copy` compared the
fused decode RoPE output with the unfused ops at `atol = 0.05`. The
fused kernel rounds once and the unfused ops round several times, so
valid bf16 results differ by one ulp, which is 0.0625 for |x| >= 8. With
the test's `3 * randn` inputs that happens on most seeds, so the test
fails on a two-GPU runner without anything being wrong.

## Change

- The copy is compared bitwise with the same kernel run on the same
inputs with its own device current. That is the property the test exists
for: a copy racing the rotation would see unrotated values, which a
bitwise check catches and a 0.05 tolerance could hide.

`test_decode_rope_inplace_matches_unfused` in the same file.

tensors): max fused vs unfused difference 0.0625, the old `atol = 0.05`
check fails 367 of 400, the 2 ulp bound holds on all 400, and the fused
kernel is bitwise deterministic run to run.

skips on single-GPU runners.

4-bit decode: no recompile from the eager setup, one output dtype under autocast, refresh the cached LoRA cast (#14754)

Three fixes in `fast_linear_forward` (4-bit decode): a recompile from
the bitsandbytes 4-bit GEMM gate added in #14386, the output dtype under
a different autocast dtype, and the cached LoRA weight cast.

## 1. No recompile when an eager call sets the gate up

`fast_linear_forward` read the lazily set global `_BNB_GEMM_4BIT` before
`_bnb_gemm_4bit_ok` checked `_is_compiling()`. Reading the global while
tracing makes Dynamo guard on its value. A graph captured while it was
still `None` is invalidated as soon as any eager call sets it to `True`
or `False`, so every compiled region that goes through
`fast_linear_forward` recompiles once.

The fix checks `not _is_compiling()` first, so the global is never read
while tracing. Under compile the gate already returned `False`, so
compiled code takes the same path as before; only the guard goes away.

## 2. One output dtype under a different autocast dtype

`bitsandbytes` `gemm_4bit` returns `X.dtype`, while the `torch.matmul`
paths (dequantize fallback, dense) return the autocast dtype when called
under a different one (fp16 activations under bf16 autocast, or the
reverse). The output dtype therefore depended on the batch size and
quant path, and with a LoRA adapter the in-place `addmv_` / `addmm_`
update failed: its `torch.mv` / `torch.mm` operand follows autocast
while the base output and LoRA factors do not (`mat1 and mat2 must have
the same dtype`). On main this fails on both the fused GEMM and the
fallback path.

Now the base result is cast back to `X.dtype` when it differs, and the
LoRA `mv` / `mm` result is cast to `X.dtype` before the in-place update,
so every path returns `X.dtype` (the activation dtype every decode
caller allocates its buffers in). Without autocast, or with a matching
autocast dtype, nothing changes.

## 3. The cached LoRA cast follows weight updates

`fast_linear_forward` cast the LoRA factors to the activation dtype once
and stored the copy on the weight as `_fast_lora`, never refreshing it.
When the dtypes differ, which is the default for float16 models (LoRA
kept in float32 for mixed precision, so T4), every later decode reused
the factors from the first decode: after more training steps (GRPO
generation without vLLM, or SFT then generate then more SFT) decode ran
with stale adapters. The cache is now keyed on both weights' `_version`
and `data_ptr()` and the dtype, so an optimizer step or a replaced
tensor recasts. Matching dtypes skip the cache entirely (the cast is a
no-op). Inference tensors (a LoRA model built under
`torch.inference_mode()`) have no version counter, so for them the key
is the storage and dtype only. While tracing, the cast is done inline
instead of setting an attribute, which was the second source of a guard
on the eager setup.

## Tests

`tests/test_bnb_integration_compile.py`:
- `test_fast_linear_forward_eager_setup_does_not_recompile`: compile
cold, run eager once, call the compiled function again, assert one frame
compiled (`torch._dynamo.testing.CompileCounter`) and identical outputs.
- `test_fast_linear_forward_sees_lora_updates`: float32 adapters,
float16 decode, update `lora_B` in place, the next decode must match a
freshly cast one bitwise.
-
`test_fast_linear_forward_lora_under_a_different_autocast_dtype[True|False]`:

GEMM (calls counted) and the dequantize fallback; output must be fp16
and match the no-autocast result.
- `test_fast_linear_forward_lora_cast_with_inference_tensors`: LoRA
model built under `torch.inference_mode()`, float32 adapters, fp16
decode twice.

Compiled blocks: packed GatedDeltaNet op, flex main kernel in training blocks, PrefixGrouper calls skip the block (0 graph breaks) (#14782)

## Summary

A graph-break and recompile sweep of current main (Llama-3.2-1B,
Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3.5-0.8B, gemma-3-270m, tiny Qwen3-MoE and gpt-oss; LoRA
SFT 4-bit and 16-bit, full finetune, GRPO with HF generation, plain
decode; torch 2.10 and 2.14) found three compile problems in the block
compile path. Each is fixed in its own commit:

1. **GatedDeltaNet opaque op: take packed (cu_seqlens) batches too.**
Padding-free SFT, the default, passes `cu_seqlens` to fla's
`chunk_gated_delta_rule`. The block adapter only routed unpacked calls
to `torch.ops.unsloth.qwen3_5_gdn_chunk`, so every packed GatedDeltaNet
call fell back to fla's `torch.compiler.disable`d function: one graph
break per GDN layer per forward and recompute, plus frames Dynamo
skipped whole. The op now takes an optional `cu_seqlens` (and builds
fla's `chunk_indices` when fla's fwd / bwd take them). A second
self-check runs the op on a packed batch with uneven documents against
fla's own Function (outputs, fake metas and grads bit-equal); packed
calls (B = 1) route to the op only when it passed.
2. **Block compile: run flex_attention's main kernel inside training
blocks.** Inductor lowers a flex_attention query shorter than 128 tokens
to the flex decoding kernel. For GQA with head_dim 256 (Qwen3.5) that
kernel does not lower: torch 2.14 rejects BLOCK_M 512 against
SPARSE_Q_BLOCK_SIZE 128, torch 2.10 runs out of shared memory. GRPO
batches are that short, so the first training forward demoted every
Qwen3.5 block to flex outside, failed again, and kept the stock forward.
Blocks only run training forwards, so the block's flex hook now passes
`kernel_options = {"FORCE_USE_FLEX_ATTENTION": True}` (merged into a
caller's options; a caller's explicit choice is kept). Calls outside a
block are unchanged.
3. **Block compile: keep GRPO PrefixGrouper calls on the stock
forward.** Compiled Unsloth decoder-layer forwards (Llama, Qwen3, ...)
guarded on the PrefixGrouper segment table (`prefix_seg_info.T == 80`)
and on the size of its block-mask cache, so the block recompiled at
every new completion length. Those calls now take the stock forward, the
same route `packed_seq_lengths` already takes.

## Summary

Three NVFP4 gaps on the diffusion side, found while re-verifying every
hosted NVFP4 build on current main:

1. **Wan2.2-T2V-A14B: auto picked NVFP4 with no accuracy-gate record.**
The image families only lead auto with nvfp4 once a passing gate record
covers the base and backend. The A14B row skipped that check: its hosted
experts were only ever compared with the FP8 build (LPIPS 0.386), never
with bf16. The row is now `gated = True`, so auto takes the ladder
(int8) there. Explicit `nvfp4` still loads.
2. **HunyuanVideo-1.5 (480p, 720p) and Wan2.2-TI2V-5B measured above the
gate bar, yet still offered nvfp4.** Both now deny nvfp4 the way an
ungated image base does, and the hosted-scheme list no longer offers a
scheme the family denies.
3. **The gate never compared the installed flashinfer with the version a
record was measured on.** Every record says 0.6.18.post1, and Studio
pins and installs 0.6.6. The gate now reads the installed version from
package metadata (falling back to an already imported module's
`__version__`), which keeps the gate module torch-free. On a flashinfer
the record does not cover, or one whose version cannot be read, auto
drops the gated nvfp4 head. An explicit load still runs, and logs one
warning at the point where layers actually move onto flashinfer

Studio sd.cpp: one CPU thread per usable physical core on Linux (#14694)

## Problem

On a host without a usable GPU, Studio runs images (and MiniMax-H3
video) on the CPU build of stable-diffusion.cpp and passes `--threads
os.cpu_count() // 2`. That is one thread per core only on a 2-way SMT
machine that may use every CPU:

- **No SMT** (SMT off in firmware, most Arm servers, many cloud VMs):
half the cores sit idle. On a 6-core VM pinned to one thread per core,
Z-Image Turbo Q4_K_M at 256x256, 4 steps, takes 112.44 s [112.28,
112.76] with 3 threads and 58.63 s [58.61, 58.81] with 6 (1.92x),
pixel-identical.
- **taskset / container cpusets**: `os.cpu_count()` counts the whole
machine, so a container limited to 4 CPUs on a 192-CPU host is handed 96
threads, and the count depends on the host instead of on what the
process may use.

The H3 video path leaves the count to sd.cpp, whose own default has the
same problem (it reads a sysfs path with a typo and always halves
`hardware_concurrency()`; fixed in unslothai/stable-diffusion.cpp, but
the pinned build still has it).

## Change

- `_linux_physical_cores()`: the number of distinct
`thread_siblings_list` sets over `os.sched_getaffinity(0)`, i.e. the
physical cores this process may run on; None when the mask or the
topology is unreadable.
- `_default_threads()` uses it on Linux in place of `cpu_count() // 2`;
the cgroup `cpu.max` cap, `UNSLOTH_CPU_THREADS` and the macOS P-core
count are unchanged, and the old estimate is still the fallback. On an
ordinary SMT host with every CPU available the result is the same number
as before.
- `_explicit_threads()` (H3 video) now passes that count whenever it
differs from what sd.cpp would pick by itself (half the logical CPUs
above 4), so hosts without SMT and cpusets get the right count from the
current pin too; otherwise it still leaves sd.cpp's default alone.

Windows and macOS behaviour is unchanged.

## Tests

`studio/backend/tests/test_sd_cpp_cpu_defaults.py`: 46 passed (28 of
them fail on `main`). New cases cover a fake sysfs with 2-way SMT, no
SMT, partial affinity masks (one thread of each core, both threads of
one core), missing / empty topology, an unavailable `sched_getaffinity`,
the Linux default for no-SMT / cpuset / SMT hosts with and without a
quota, Windows never reading the topology, and `_explicit_threads()`
passing the count only when sd.cpp would choose another. The existing
tests now pin `_linux_physical_cores` so they do not depend on the CI
runner's topology. The thread-related tests in `test_sd_cpp_install.py`
pass too (70 passed with the file above).

## Measurements

Colab A100 VM used as a CPU box (Intel Xeon @ 2.2 GHz, 6 cores / 12
threads), published sd.cpp bundle `master-982-0518b34-ud331c66`,
`taskset` to the CPU sets below, interleaved, 3 repeats, seconds:

| CPU set | threads | Z-Image 256, 4 steps, generate |
|---|---|---|
| 6 CPUs, one per core (a 6-core host without SMT) | 3 (`cpu_count() //
2` there) | 112.44 [112.28, 112.76] |
| same | 6 (this PR) | 58.63 [58.61, 58.81] |

| 4 CPUs = both threads of 2 cores (a cpuset) | 2 (this PR: one per
core, as on an unrestricted host) | 168.89 (1 run) |
| same | 4 | 152.46 (1 run) |
| same | 24 (what an oversubscribed count does) | 158.66 (1 run) |

Images are pixel-identical across thread counts.

The cpuset row is the one place this is not a speedup: inside a cpuset
that holds both threads of each core, the count drops to one per core,
which is what Studio already does on every unrestricted SMT host, and on
this Intel VM that leaves the SMT gain (here 10%) on the table, as it
does unrestricted (6 vs 12 threads: 59.0 vs 55.4 s). A cpuset of
distinct cores (the usual `--cpuset-cpus=0-7`, since Linux numbers SMT
siblings apart) gets every CPU in it.

Block compile: let an enclosing torch.compile own wrapped decoder layers (#14704)

When a user wraps the model or a training step in their own
torch.compile, the per-layer block
compile wrapper (installed on the FastLanguageModel LoRA path since
#14398) is inlined into the
outer trace. It then calls torch._dynamo.maybe_mark_dynamic, which
dynamo forbids while tracing,
and its own compiled callable. fullgraph=True always fails with
"Attempt to trace forbidden callable maybe_mark_dynamic"; with
suppress_errors the outer graph
falls back and splits (5 graphs instead of 1 on a tiny Llama).

Fix: if torch.compiler.is_compiling(), the wrapper runs the stock
forward so the outer graph
owns the layer. Outside an enclosing compile nothing changes (same
graphs, same recompile count,
same loss on a tiny Llama).

Tests:
- New tests/test_block_compile.py::test_outer_compile_owns_the_block
(fullgraph, default,
suppress_errors): fails on main, passes here. Checks grads vs the stock
forward, no nested
  compiled call, no graph breaks, one graph.
- Block compile suites on CPU: 60 passed, 4 skipped (CUDA only) on torch
2.13.0 and 2.14.1.

Studio diffusion: replay a model-offloaded denoiser's CUDA graph across renders and pin torchao int8 host weights (#14666)

## Summary

Under `memory_mode=low_vram` (whole-module CPU offload) on a compiled
speed tier, the denoiser step now runs as a CUDA graph on every render,
recorded once on render 1, and the int8 weights the compiled tier stores
stop being copied back and forth through pageable host memory on every
render.

Four commits:

1. **Stable device range for a model-offloaded denoiser**
(`diffusion_stable_arena.py`). The denoiser's onloads land in one CUDA
virtual address range reserved for the load (driver VMM:
`cuMemAddressReserve` once, then `cuMemCreate` + `cuMemMap` on every
onload and `cuMemUnmap` + `cuMemRelease` on every offload). The weights
get the same addresses on every render, so render 1's step graph replays
on renders 2+ with no new capture. The physical memory is still released
at every offload, so the text encoder and VAE phases get the VRAM back
as they do today. This is the same idea as ComfyUI's `comfy_aimdo`
`model_vbar`. #14497 kept this placement eager because the stock onload
moved the weights on every render. `offload_placement()` now arms the
graph only when the range attaches;
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_MODEL_OFFLOAD_ARENA=0` brings back #14497's eager
step.
2. **Keep and pin torchao int8 / fp8 host weights under model offload**
(`diffusion_memory.py`). The keep-host-weights offload skipped torchao
wrapper weights (`Int8Tensor`). Every render then copied them
device-to-host into fresh pageable memory and uploaded them again from
there. On FLUX.2-klein 4B only 0.5 of 4 GiB of the denoiser was pinned.
Wrapper weights whose inner tensors are plain are now kept: the offload
swaps the parameter back onto its kept host tensors (no copy), and their
inner tensors are pinned on the first onload.
3. **Int8 / fp8 weights in the stable range.** Each inner tensor is
placed in the range, and the weight is rebuilt over the placed tensors
and swapped in, the same way `Module.to` moves it.
4. **Survive diffusers re-hooking.** accelerate's
`remove_hook_from_module` pops instance `to` overrides
(`_accelerate_added_attributes`), and diffusers re-hooks model offload
before every render. Without this commit the range served only render 1.
A forward pre-hook now puts the override back before the hook's
pre-forward onloads the module.

The existing offload speed check still judges each recorded key. A
replay has to be at least 1% faster than the eager step, or the graph is
dropped for the load. That covers the devices where a replay does not
pay.

NVFP4 QAT: require in_features divisible by 32 (#14703)

qat_scheme = "nvfp4" selected Linear layers whose in_features and
out_features are multiples of the 16-element scale block. The NVFP4
matmul needs more than that on K. torchao packs two FP4 values per byte
and passes the packed K / 2 to torch._scaled_mm, which requires that
trailing dimension to be a multiple of 16. So in_features must be a
multiple of 32.

The prepare-time probes did not catch this because they always use
in_features = 64. A layer with K = 16, 48, 80, ... was converted and
then failed at its first forward:

RuntimeError: Expected trailing dimension of mat1 to be divisible by 16
but got mat1 shape: (16x24).

This includes rank-16 LoRA B projections when
UNSLOTH_QAT_FAKE_QUANTIZE_LORA=1.

B200, torch 2.13, torchao 0.18, NVFP4FakeQuantizedLinear forward +
backward:

| in_features | Before: admitted / runs | After: admitted |
|---|---|---|
| 16 | yes / fails | no (stays bf16) |
| 32 | yes / runs | yes |
| 48 | yes / fails | no |
| 64 | yes / runs | yes |
| 80 | yes / fails | no |
| 96 | yes / runs | yes |

Fix: the NVFP4 filter now requires in_features % 32 == 0 (out_features %
16 unchanged). Other layers stay in full precision with the existing
warning. MXFP8 and the other schemes are unchanged.

Tests: a CPU test for the admitted widths and the rank-16 LoRA B case,
plus a Blackwell-only test that prepares and runs forward/backward on
every width. Both fail before this change and pass after it on a B200.
The QAT test files pass on CPU.

## Studio: keep the bf16 sd.cpp text encoders for FLUX.2 klein and
Z-Image

#14008 moved the sd.cpp (native / CPU / Vulkan / Mac) LLM text encoders
off the bf16 single-file repacks onto unsloth GGUFs, and in the same
step dropped their precision:

| Family | Released build | After #14008 | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FLUX.2 klein 4B | bf16 `qwen_3_4b` | `Qwen3-4B-Q8_0.gguf` |
`Qwen3-4B-BF16.gguf` |
| Z-Image | bf16 `qwen_3_4b` | `Qwen3-4B-Q8_0.gguf` |
`Qwen3-4B-BF16.gguf` |
| FLUX.2 klein 9B | bf16 `qwen_3_8b` | `Qwen3-8B-Q4_K_M.gguf` |
`Qwen3-8B-BF16.gguf` |
| FLUX.2-dev | bf16 Mistral 24B repack (36 GB) |
`Mistral-...-Q4_K_M.gguf` | `Mistral-...-Q8_0.gguf` |

An existing native config therefore changed encoder precision on upgrade
without anyone asking for it, and the renders moved. The BF16 GGUFs are
the same weights as the released encoders and render pixel-identical to
them, so this keeps the move to unsloth repos and restores the
precision.

### Measurements

sd-cli CUDA build `master-968-8cd731e`, 512x512, 4 steps, cfg 1.0,
euler, seed 42 with batch count 2, 3 prompts for klein 4B and 2 for
klein 9B, same denoiser GGUF and the same FLUX.2 VAE in every arm. LPIPS
(alex) against the released bf16 safetensors encoder:

| Family | Arm | LPIPS mean / max | Pixel-identical |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| klein 4B | A/A (released encoder, second process) | 0 / 0 | 6/6 |
| klein 4B | BF16 GGUF | 0 / 0 | 6/6 |
| klein 4B | Q8_0 | 0.061 / 0.113 | 0/6 |
| klein 9B | A/A (Q4_K_M, second process) | 0 / 0 | 2/2 (byte-identical
PNGs) |
| klein 9B | Q8_0 | 0.026 / 0.040 | 0/4 |
| klein 9B | Q4_K_M | 0.041 / 0.049 | 0/4 |

sd-cli is bitwise deterministic across processes here, so the noise
floor is exactly zero and any non-zero number is the encoder. The worst
klein 4B Q8_0 case is a visibly different poster: letter shapes and the
storefronts change, it is not just noise. The #14008 measurements at
768px agree: klein 4B Q8_0 0.060 / 0.097 and Q4_K_M 0.149 / 0.210, klein
9B BF16 GGUF pixel-identical.

ComfyUI's own templates (Comfy-Org/workflow_templates) load the bf16
`qwen_3_4b.safetensors` for klein 4B
(`image_flux2_klein_text_to_image.json`) and Z-Image
(`image_z_image_turbo.json`), `qwen_3_8b_fp8mixed.safetensors` for klein
9B (`image_flux2_text_to_image_9b.json`), and
`mistral_3_small_flux2_bf16.safetensors` for FLUX.2-dev
(`image_flux2.json`, with an fp8 variant in `image_flux2_fp8.json`).
Q4_K_M sat below all of them.

### FLUX.2-dev

The 0.155 LPIPS shift #14008 saw with the lossless BF16 GGUF is not
quantisation. sd.cpp runs the Mistral encoder with
`GGML_ROPE_TYPE_NORMAL` (interleaved pairs) and loads both formats
through the same name mapping, with no q/k reordering. The GGUF's
`blk.0.attn_q.weight` is exactly the llama.cpp permutation of the HF
`q_proj` (checked tensor for tensor), while the old bf16 safetensors is
in HF rotate-half order. So the old route paired the wrong RoPE
dimensions, and the GGUF route is the one that matches the encoder. The
BF16 GGUF is 47 GB, so this PR picks Q8_0 (25 GB): it is at least as
precise as ComfyUI's fp8 template and matches the int8 encoder the
diffusers route already uses for FLUX.2-dev.

### Low-RAM hosts

`UNSLOTH_SD_CPP_TEXT_ENCODER_QUANT=bf16|q8_0|q4_k_m` picks another
precision of the same unsloth GGUF for the Qwen3 and Mistral encoders.
Every one of those repos ships all three files. CLIP, T5, the Qwen-Image
VL encoder and the vision projectors are not touched. The delete guard
(`sd_cpp_text_encoder_candidates`) names every precision, so an encoder
fetched under another setting stays protected.

### Cost

A host that already fetched the Q8_0 / Q4_K_M encoder downloads the BF16
file once (Qwen3-4B 8.0 GB, Qwen3-8B 16.4 GB, Mistral Q8_0 25 GB).
Released builds read bf16 encoders of the same size, so peak RAM is back
where it was before #14008, not above it.

### Tests

New `tests/test_sd_cpp_text_encoder_precision.py`: the per-family
defaults, the env override (valid, invalid, empty), that only the LLM
GGUFs follow it, and the delete-guard candidates. 9 of its 10 cases fail
