Windows UI lane: retry the permission suite's auth wipe while the stopped server releases auth.db (#14658)

The Windows Unsloth UI CI "Chat UI Tests" job sometimes fails on lane
`extra` even though every suite in it passed:

```
[banner] 2155 checks, 0 failed
rm: cannot remove 'D:\a\unsloth\unsloth/.studio-lane-extra/auth/auth.db': Device or resource busy
rm: cannot remove 'D:\a\unsloth\unsloth/.studio-lane-extra/auth/auth.db-shm': Device or resource busy
rm: cannot remove 'D:\a\unsloth\unsloth/.studio-lane-extra/auth/auth.db-wal': Device or resource busy
##[error]Windows UI lane extra failed (exit 1)
```

Seen on run 39669502772 and again on a staging replica of #14647 (a
test-only change unrelated to the lane).

### Cause

`run-studio-ui-lane.sh` (lane `extra`) stops its own server with `kill`
plus a 2 second sleep, then calls `run-studio-permission-browser.sh` on
the same `UNSLOTH_STUDIO_HOME`. That script wipes `$studio_home/auth`
before booting a fresh server. On Windows the killed server can still
hold `auth.db` open past the sleep, so the `rm -rf` fails and `set -euo
pipefail` ends the lane with exit 1.

### Change

- The wipe is now `wipe_auth`, which retries `rm -rf
"$studio_home/auth"` quietly once a second for up to 30 tries
(`STUDIO_AUTH_WIPE_TRIES`), then makes one last attempt that shows
`rm`'s own error. If that attempt succeeds the wipe succeeds; if not, it
prints an `::error::` naming the held directory and fails. A server that
never exits still fails the lane, now with a message that says so.
- The fix is in the step that needs the lock released rather than in the
lane's `stop()`, so it covers any caller that hands this script a home
whose server just went away.

### Verification

`tests/studio/test_permission_browser_auth_wipe.py` (new, collected by
the Backend CI `studio` shard) runs the script's own `wipe_auth` body in
bash against an `rm` shim that reports "Device or resource busy" for its
first calls:

- held for 4 calls: wiped on the 5th, exit 0
- released exactly on the final attempt (5 tries): wiped, exit 0
- held throughout (5 tries): exits non-zero after 6 calls, with the
`still held open` error and `rm`'s message
- no bare `rm -rf "$studio_home/auth"` remains outside the helper, and
the wipe runs before `unsloth studio` boots

Sabotage: main's script fails all of them; a `wipe_auth` with the retry
loop removed fails 2 of 3 of the original tests; the previous head of
this PR (which returned 1 after a successful final attempt) fails the
final-attempt test. `test_ui_scripts_report_signals.py` and
`test_windows_ui_lanes_are_isolated.py` still pass.

Not proven here: the timing on a real Windows runner. This PR's own
Windows UI CI run exercises the path; the failure is intermittent, so
one green run is consistent with the fix rather than proof of it.

Unsloth Studio: serve an MLX model through the library that loaded it (#14612)

## Summary

unsloth-zoo now loads a vision checkpoint that mlx-vlm cannot build but
mlx-lm can (mlx-lm 0.32's Muse Spark) through mlx-lm, even when Unsloth
Studio asks for mlx-vlm with `text_only=False`
(unslothai/unsloth-zoo#1949). Unsloth Studio asks for that for every
vision config, and also for speculation, TurboQuant and quantized-KV
batching. It then marked the load as an mlx-vlm model and drove mlx-vlm
generation paths with an mlx-lm model, which fails in generation:

```text
AttributeError: 'RecordingModel' object has no attribute 'config'
```

## Change

After `FastMLXModel.from_pretrained`, when Unsloth Studio requested
mlx-vlm but the loaded model reports `_is_vlm_model is False`, it serves
the model through the mlx-lm text paths it loaded for:

- speculation and TurboQuant fall back exactly as they do when an
mlx-vlm load fails, without loading the model a second time;
- an image model (`_unsloth_supports_images`) keeps `is_vision` when the
installed unsloth-zoo can prefill its images, and Unsloth Studio serves
those images on the text paths:
- the chat template renders the image marker (Muse Spark's template
turns an image part into `<|patch|>`), so `renders_image` follows the
tokenizer;
- sequential: the rendered prompt goes through unsloth-zoo's
`image_prompt_embeddings` (mlx-lm's processor expands each marker,
`embed_inputs` splices the image rows), then
`mlx_lm.stream_generate(..., input_embeddings=...)`, which is how mlx-lm
serves its own image requests;
- batched: mlx-lm's `BatchGenerator` takes token ids only, so
`_TextBatchSession` admits an image row through unsloth-zoo's
`prefill_image_prompt`. The row's embeddings fill its own cache, the row
joins the batch at its last token, and an unset `max_tokens` is budgeted
from the expanded prompt;
- image prompts bypass the token-keyed prefix cache, neither reusing nor
banking it: two images of one size expand to the same patch ids, so a
cached prefix could answer about the wrong picture;
- with an older unsloth-zoo, an image model is served as text with
vision off, and the worker publishes the backend's resolved `is_vision`
so the parent stops offering image input.

Only an explicit `_is_vlm_model is False` triggers this. unsloth-zoo
sets the flag on every load, and a loader that does not set it keeps
today's behaviour. Every mlx-vlm and plain text model keeps its serving
path.

## Validation

- New tests: the load branch (an image model served through mlx-lm keeps
vision only with an unsloth-zoo that prefills images, and downgrades
TurboQuant either way; a model built by mlx-vlm keeps its path); an
image turn feeding `input_embeddings` outside the prompt cache; an image
batch row joining at its last token with its prefilled cache and an
expanded-prompt budget. Each change was checked to fail its test when
reverted (12 mutants).
- `studio/backend/tests/test_mlx_inference_backend.py` passes, as do the
image, multi-image, MCP-image and vision-tools route tests.
- `MLXInferenceBackend` with unslothai/unsloth-zoo#1949 on a shrunken
real Muse Spark checkpoint loaded as a vision config: it reports vision
with `renders_image` and multiple images, a different image changes the
reply, and a three-row batch (image, text, another image) produces
exactly the sequential replies.

```bash
python -m pytest tests/test_mlx_inference_backend.py
python -m pytest tests/test_pr7699_worker_audio_mirror.py
```

RMSNorm: enable the narrow-row kernels on ROCm with the DPP reduction order (#14637)

The narrow-row RMSNorm kernels (several rows per program for widths
33..128, the QK-norm head
dims) were gated off on ROCm because their reduction replay did not
match the one-row kernel
there. The cause is the reduction order, not the wavefront width: on
RDNA3+ and CDNA2+ Triton
lowers tl.sum to DPP, which reduces each 16-lane row with row_shr 8, 4,
2, 1 and then joins the
rows (permlanex16 on RDNA, row_bcast 15 / 31 on CDNA), while CUDA
shuffles xor 16, 8, 4, 2, 1.

This replays the DPP order on HIP (lanes per wavefront read from the
Triton target, so 32 on
RDNA and 64 on CDNA), keeps the per-(device, dtype, width, eps, gemma)
bitwise self-check that
gates every use, and removes the ROCm gate. Arches where Triton uses the
generic butterfly
(RDNA1/2, CDNA1) fail the self-check and stay one-row. CUDA keeps the
same settings and the same
generated PTX.

Results on gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S, torch 2.11 ROCm 7.13, Triton 3.6),
base vs head in one job:
- multi-row engaged through fast_rms_layernorm: base no, head yes
- bitwise vs the one-row kernel (Y, rstd, dX): 40/40 cells (bf16 / fp16
/ fp32, fp32 weights,
gemma on and off, widths 64 / 80 / 96 / 128, rows 1 / 3 / 31 / 4097 /
65537)
- tests/test_rms_layernorm_multirow.py now runs on ROCm: 599 passed, 3
skipped (two-GPU)
- norm op, bf16, graph replay, median of 7:

| width | rows | fwd one-row / multi-row (us) | bwd one-row / multi-row
(us) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 4096 | 7.66 / 3.46 | 7.44 / 3.80 |
| 64 | 65536 | 119.06 / 30.99 | 158.80 / 40.09 |
| 128 | 4096 | 8.07 / 4.83 | 8.67 / 7.68 |
| 128 | 65536 | 172.38 / 56.54 | 298.42 / 229.26 |

On NVIDIA (B200, Triton 3.7.1) the PTX of every RMSNorm kernel is
identical before and after
(108 specialisations) and outputs are bitwise equal. A CPU test pins the
CUDA settings, the CUDA
replay body and the compile-time backend switch.

Not run on hardware: CDNA (MI2xx / MI3xx, 64-lane wavefronts) and RDNA4.
If the replay does not match there, the self-check keeps those devices
on the one-row kernel.

Fix save_pretrained_torchao for full finetuning QAT on transformers 5 (#14639)

Full finetuning with any `qat_scheme` followed by
`save_pretrained_torchao` fails on transformers 5 with
`RuntimeError: Attempted to access the data pointer on an invalid python

The full finetuning branch converts the model in place with `quantize_`
and then calls `save_pretrained`
with no `hf_quantizer` attached. transformers only flattens torchao

safetensors metadata) through the quantizer, so it treats them as plain
tensors. On 4.x this worked
because `safe_serialization=False` pickled the subclasses; 5.x has no
such path.

This attaches a torchao `HfQuantizer` built from the
`quantization_config` that `_convert_torchao_model`
already sets, for the duration of the save only, and only on
transformers 5 (4.x keeps its current path).

mxfp8 and nvfp4 QAT: the checkpoint
now reloads with `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained` and every
quantized weight dequantizes bit-equal
to the in-process model. New CPU test
`test_full_finetune_qat_save_reloads_quantized` fails on main and
passes here; the QAT and torchao save tests pass on transformers 5.17
and 4.57.6.

Studio: load GGUF models faster by skipping the vocabulary read (#14573)

Before starting llama-server, Studio opens the GGUF to work out how much
memory the model needs. It used gguf's full reader for this, which
unpacks every vocabulary entry into its own object even though the
sizing only needs a few numbers and the list of tensors. For models with
large vocabularies this cost several seconds on every load, on Macs and

Studio: stop long MLX chats from re-reading the whole chat every turn (#14574)

With an MLX model on a Mac, a chat that grows past the prompt cache
budget (about 25k tokens for Qwen3-0.6B on a 24 GB Mac) is no longer
cached between turns. Every new message then re-reads the whole
conversation before replying, so a 29k-token chat waited 7 to 13 seconds
per turn instead of under one. A chat that crosses the line partway
loses reuse for everything after that point.

That one long chat now keeps its cache in a separate slot that is handed
back to its next turn without copying, so later turns of a 29k-token
chat start in about 0.6 s. Regenerating, editing the last message and
continuing after a stop reuse it as well. The slot is released as soon
as another chat sends a message, so other chats keep their cache, peak
memory is unchanged, and chats under the budget behave as before.

NVFP4 fused GEMM: honor autocast dtype and check K alignment for dX (#14625)

## Problem

Two issues in the NVFP4 fused decode GEMM added in #13840 (gate refined
in #14122 and #14536).

1. **Fused forward ignores autocast.** The dense path it replaced is
`torch.matmul(X, W.t())`, which autocast runs in the autocast dtype. The
fused Triton GEMM allocates its output in `X.dtype` and never looks at
autocast. With fp16 activations under bf16 autocast, the result comes
back as fp16 and overflows where the dense path returned finite bf16.
bf16 activations under fp16 autocast flip the other way.

Repro: fp16 `X` of shape `[4, 128]` filled with 1000, packed weights
`0x22` (every decoded weight is 1), unit scales, `torch.autocast("cuda",
dtype=torch.bfloat16)`:

   | | before #13840 (dense) | main (fused) | this PR (fused) |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | output dtype | bf16 | fp16 | bf16 |
   | output value | 128000 | inf | 128000 |
   | loss | 1.6384e10 | inf | 1.6384e10 |
   | grad X finite | yes | no | yes |

The same happens through a PEFT LoRA wrapper (LoRA B grad non finite on
main, finite before #13840 and with this PR). The bf16 input / fp16
autocast case now also matches the dense result exactly (fp16 output, as
dense gives).

2. **Fused dX skips the K alignment check.** `_fused_ok` checks `inner %
64` and `N % 64`. In the forward pass `inner` is K, but in dX it is N,
so K was never checked. A weight with N=4096, K=4112 was refused fused
forward but accepted for fused dX on sm80, sm89 and sm120, the shape
class #13840 measured as up to 2.8x slower than dense in dX.

## Change

- `NVFP4Linear_matmul.forward` casts `X` to the active CUDA autocast
dtype before calling the matmul op, outside the opaque `torch.library`
op. The fused path, the dense path and the fake impl then all return the
autocast dtype, and `grad_X` is still returned in `X.dtype` as before.
Without autocast nothing changes. Autocast state is already a dynamo
guard, so no new graph breaks or recompiles.
- `_fused_ok` checks N and K alignment directly (`packed.shape[0] % 64`
and `packed.shape[1] % 32`) in both directions. `UNSLOTH_NVFP4_FUSED=1`
still forces the fused path past the check.

## Validation

B200 (fused path forced with `UNSLOTH_NVFP4_FUSED=1`, as the existing
tests do; dispatch for sm80 / sm89 / sm120 checked by monkeypatching the
capability).

- New tests, failing on main and passing here:
- `test_autocast_dtype_matches_dense` (fp16 under bf16 and bf16 under
fp16): fused output and grad equal the dense path bit for bit, dtype
included. 2 of 2 fail on main.
- `test_autocast_random_weights_match_dense_and_oracle` (fp16 / bf16 /
fp32 inputs): fused vs dense vs fp64 oracle, forward and dX. 3 of 3 fail
on main (the fp32 case because main never runs fused for fp32 inputs;
under autocast they now take the bf16 fused kernel, like the dense path
computes in bf16).
- `test_autocast_fullgraph_compile_has_no_graph_break`: 0 graph breaks,
compiled output bf16 and equal to eager. Fails on main (compiled output
fp16).
- `test_unaligned_k_stays_dense_in_both_directions` (sm80, sm89, sm120,
forward and dX): the 3 dX cases fail on main.
- NVFP4 test files (`tests/test_nvfp4*.py`, GPU tests included):
- torch 2.14.1 / Triton 3.8.0: 166 passed, 5 skipped, 1 failed. The
failure,
`test_nvfp4_loader.py::test_peft_merge_dequantizes_the_routed_base[nvfp4-True]`,
fails the same way on main (pre-existing, not touched here).
  - torch 2.10.0 / Triton 3.6.0: 111 passed, 4 skipped.
- torch.compile (forward + backward, rows 16 / 32 / 48 / 64 / 64,
dynamic): 0 graph breaks, 2 graphs, 0 recompiles on main and here, with
and without bf16 autocast, on both torch versions. Under autocast the
compiled output is fp16 on main and bf16 here.
- Existing fp64 oracle tests for the non autocast path pass unchanged.
- Speed, no autocast (bf16, 4096 x 4096 weight, forced fused, eager, 7
interleaved repeats of 500 calls, median per call): M=1 117.6 us vs
118.2 us on main, M=16 107.6 us vs 107.8 us. Same within noise.

## Not covered

- No A100 / L4 / RTX PRO 6000 run, so the dX slowdown on unaligned K
that the gate now avoids is #13840's measurement, not re measured here.
- Backward run inside an autocast region (not recommended by PyTorch)
still computes fused dX in the grad dtype; with the forward fix, the
grad dtype is already the autocast dtype in the normal flow.
- Non CUDA devices are unchanged (the fused path is CUDA only).
- With a bias, the output is still cast back to `X.dtype` after the bias
add, exactly as before #13840 (dense and fused alike). Only the
bias-free path changes dtype under autocast.

unsloth start: hard-link only auth.json into the Codex parent overlay (follow-up to #14591) (#14635)

Follow-up to #14591.

## What broke

#14591 fixed a real Codex login problem under `unsloth start codex
--as-subagent` on Windows: where symlinks are denied (no Developer Mode,
no admin), the overlay copied `auth.json`, so a token refresh in the
overlay left the user's real `~/.codex/auth.json` with a refresh token
that had already been used. The fix replaced the copy with a hard link.

The hard link was applied to every file in the user's Codex home, not
only `auth.json`. Codex keeps its WAL-mode SQLite databases in
`CODEX_HOME` (`state_5.sqlite`, `queue_1.sqlite`,
`thread_history_1.sqlite`, the logs db, plus any `-wal` / `-shm`
sidecars; `sqlite_home` defaults to `codex_home` in
`codex-rs/core/src/config/mod.rs`). Hard-linking those gives the live
database a second name. SQLite derives the `-wal` and `-shm` paths from
the name it was opened under, so the overlay Codex and a plain `codex`
(or the Codex app) running at the same time use different WAL and
shared-memory files for one database. SQLite documents this as a
corruption path: [How To Corrupt An SQLite Database File, 2.6 Multiple
links to the same file](https://www.sqlite.org/howtocorrupt.html).
Before #14591 those files were copied into the overlay, so the user's
real databases were never touched.

## What changed

- `write_codex_parent_overlay` hard-links only `auth.json` when symlinks
are denied. Every other file is copied, as before #14591. Symlinks,
junctions and the first-login dangling `auth.json` link are unchanged.
- Regression test: with symlinks denied, `state_5.sqlite`, its `-wal`
and `history.jsonl` land in the overlay as copies (not the same inode),
while the existing test still shows a rotated `auth.json` refresh token
reaching the user's home. The new test fails on current `main` and
passes with this change.

The rest of #14591 was audited and left as is: discovery, loopback proxy
bypass, task-tagged model filtering, Hermes provider rename and
`threshold_tokens`, Claude exec-form hooks (`args` landed in Claude Code
2.1.139), `apiKeyHelper` blanking, merged `--settings`, the dsh profile
shorthand, JSONC splicing and the Pi Node warning (`legacy-node20` tag
confirmed on npm).

## Verification

- `unsloth_cli` suites for start, start_app, the Claude plan gate,
inference_chat, mcp, and the Codex and Claude subagent bridges: 1206
passed, 2 skipped.
- `ruff check` and the repo's ruff format on the changed files.

## Not tested here

- Windows itself (NTFS hard links, symlink privilege denied). The test
simulates the denied symlink the same way the #14591 tests do.

Studio: name an untitled chat's fork after its first reply (follow-up to #14587) (#14636)

#14587 changed a fork of an untitled chat to stay "New Chat" instead of

an untitled chat stayed "New Chat" for good, and several of them now
read the same in the sidebar where they used to be numbered.

When a run ends in a regular thread still titled "New Chat", the
autosave reads the stored row, and if it is a fork asks the thread list
item for its title once per page. That goes through the same adapter
`generateTitle` a new chat uses, so the result follows the auto-title
setting and the "only once" check it already has. Brand-new chats,
titled forks and chats that are not forks are left alone.

![Before: the fork of an untitled chat is still "New Chat" after a
reply. After: the reply names
it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shimmyshimmer/unsloth-staging-4/pr-media/pr/14636/fork_title_pair_q-2f4a1b5bb77a.png)

### Verification

- Live Studio (isolated install, Qwen3-0.6B GGUF on CPU, Playwright):
- Before: an untitled chat forked through the API, one reply sent in the
fork, title polled for 30 s: still "New Chat".
- After: same steps, the fork is named "What is weight quantization?"
from its inherited first message, and the sidebar updates.
  - A brand-new chat is still titled once after its first reply.

runtime wiring, and a check on the shipped assistant-ui that it still
only titles `new` threads.
- Frontend: `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (13,467 tests, 0 failures),
`npm run build`.
- Backend fork tests (`test_chat_history_storage.py`,
`test_rag_thread_document_cleanup.py`, `-k fork`): 51 passed.

Studio: keep folder identity lookups inside the scan budget (follow-up to #14588) (#14638)

## Follow-up to #14588: a hung folder could still stall the model lists

#14588 gave every custom folder scan a 10 s budget so a folder on a
stalled network mount can no longer hold the model lists. Two calls that
run before that budget starts were left outside it. Both take a
`realpath` of every registered folder to build the request dedupe key,
and `realpath` stats each path component, which blocks in the kernel on
a hung mount.

### What was still broken

- **`/api/models/local` froze the whole server.**
`_shared_compat_local_inventory_scan` computed
`_compat_inventory_path_identity` (a `realpath`) for every custom folder
on the event loop. One hung folder blocked every request, not just this
one. The Training page and the chat API client still call this route.
The #14588 body lists this as fixed, but only the source probes were
moved off the loop.
- **`/api/hub/local` still hung past the UI timeout.** #14588 moved the
same `realpath` into `asyncio.to_thread`, so the loop stayed free, but
the listing still waited on it with no budget. It never reached the
bounded scans, so the folder was never marked slow. Each new listing
parked one more thread of the shared default executor that inference
also uses, which is what the budget was meant to prevent.

### Fix

- New `custom_folder_identities()` in `local_inventory.py` computes each
identity through the same per-folder budget runner the scans use. If it
does not finish in time, the key falls back to the raw path.
- Because it uses the same runner, a hung folder is marked slow ("This
folder is taking too long to scan") after one budget. The scans of that
listing then skip it at once. Later listings do not start a second
thread on the mount.
- `/api/models/local` now computes these identities off the loop. The
identity only feeds the in-flight dedupe key, so the raw-path fallback
changes at most which concurrent requests share a scan.

### Verification

- Two new tests in `tests/test_scan_folder_scan_budget.py` block
`realpath` for one folder:
- `/api/hub/local`'s folder load returns within the budget and marks the
folder slow.
- `/api/models/local`'s shared scan returns, and the event loop keeps
ticking while it runs.
- Both tests fail on current `main` (the listing hangs) and pass with
this change.
- 93 backend test files that touch the inventory, scan folders or
`routes/models.py`: 5720 pass. The 15 failures and 46 errors are
identical on unmodified `main` (`test_gguf_cache_switch_resolution`
fixture errors, `test_sandbox_files_and_storage_roots`,
`test_account_path_hardening` (2), `test_openai_auto_switch`,
`test_export_reap`, `test_startup_defers_torch`).
- `ruff check` and `scripts/run_ruff_format.py` are clean on the changed
files.

### Not tested here

- A real hung network mount. The tests block `realpath` in a worker
thread to stand in for one.
- No frontend change.

Studio: keep Projects page renames and deletes from waiting out a streaming reply (#14634)

Follow-up to #14586.

## What broke

#14586 gave the Projects page a 2 s reload debounce for streamed chunk
saves (300 ms for structural changes), so expanded project rows stop
reloading on every chunk of a slow CPU reply. Both kinds of event shared
one timer, and every event cleared it. So a structural change during a
stream (renaming, moving or deleting a chat from the Projects page, or
the same change arriving from another tab) set a 300 ms reload, and the
next chunk save reset it to 2 s. Chunk saves keep arriving faster than 2
s, so the reload waited for the whole reply to finish. Until then the
expanded project kept showing the old title or the deleted chat. Before
#14586, chunks spaced more than 300 ms apart did not hide the change
this way.

The codebase already treats this as a bug elsewhere.
`chat-history-revision.test.ts` says "Sharing one timer leaves a delete
unannounced for a whole generation". The search index's
`shouldPostponeSearchRebuild` documents the rule: "Once a structural
refresh has a deadline, stream chunks may join it but must not keep
moving it."

## Fix

`createHistoryRefreshDebounce` in `chat-history-revision.ts` keeps both
delays, but a chunk save that arrives while a structural reload is
pending joins it instead of postponing it. Chunk saves that come after
that reload still wait for their 2 s lull. The Projects page uses it in
place of the inline timer.

## Audit of the rest of #14586

Everything else in #14586 checked out against the code it changed:

- **Sources panel subscription.** The panel's own subscription was
removed, but `useRagDocuments` still refetches on the same event for
project scopes.
- **Indexing poll.** The 4 s poll that runs while a document is indexing
is unchanged.
- **Linked-folder idle poll.** It matches `FOLDER_SYNC_INTERVAL_S` (30
s). `activeJobId` only names pending or running jobs, so a finished sync
does not keep the fast poll running.
- **Workspace backfill.** The project list backfills only rows without a
root. Every other caller (`get_project`, `patch_project`, tools,
gallery) still calls `ensure_chat_project_workspace`.
- **Export.** "Export All Projects" now uses one list request, and it
filters to the same non-archived projects as before.

## Verification

- New `tests/history-refresh-debounce.test.ts` (mock timers):
  - a stream refreshes once, on its lull;
  - a structural change mid-stream refreshes on its 300 ms deadline;
  - cancel drops a pending refresh.
- The structural case fails against the previous timer.
- Updated the source-shape assertions in `projects-page-rows.test.ts`
and `projects-activity-and-polling.test.ts`.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (full suite, 13466 tests), `npm run
build`.

## Not tested here

- Not exercised in a running Studio with a streaming model. This host is
CPU only and shared, so the timing is covered by the unit tests only.

NF4 bitsandbytes GEMM gate: return before its lazy setup under torch.compile (#14608)

#14386 added `_bnb_gemm_4bit_ok`, the gate that sends 4-bit decode with
2 to 16 rows to bitsandbytes' GEMM on T4. On the first call its lazy
setup runs `torch.cuda.device_count()` and the capability checks, and
only then checks `_is_compiling()`. Dynamo cannot trace
`torch.cuda.device_count()`, so a cold compiled decode call fails with
`fullgraph=True`:

```
torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported: torch.* op returned non-Tensor
```

Without fullgraph it becomes a graph break. This happens on every GPU,
not only T4, because the setup runs before the arch check. The existing
compile test warms the function up eagerly first, which sets the gate up
outside tracing and hides the failure.

Repro (fresh process):

```python
import unsloth
import torch, bitsandbytes as bnb
from unsloth.kernels.utils import fast_linear_forward

p = bnb.nn.Linear4bit(256, 128, bias=False, compute_dtype=torch.float16, quant_type="nf4").half().cuda()
x = torch.randn(8, 1, 256, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
with torch.no_grad():
    torch.compile(lambda a: fast_linear_forward(p, a), fullgraph=True, backend="aot_eager")(x)
```

## Change
- `_bnb_gemm_4bit_ok` now returns False under `torch.compile` or with
grad enabled before the lazy setup.
- The same two checks are dropped from the end of the condition, where
they no longer did anything.
- Compiled and training calls take the same path as before #14386. Eager
no-grad decode is unchanged.

## Validation
- New `test_fast_linear_forward_cold_compile_fullgraph` (bsz 8 and 16)
compiles `fast_linear_forward` with `fullgraph=True` from the gate's
cold state, with no eager warmup, and compares the result with eager.
  - Without this change: 2 failed (the error above).
  - With it: 2 passed.
- `tests/test_bnb_integration_compile.py` +
`tests/test_nf4_triton_gemv.py`: 401 passed on torch 2.14.1 and on torch
2.10.0 (B200), incl. the eager bitsandbytes GEMM routing tests.

Not covered: T4 hardware (the routing tests fake the arch); torch 2.11
to 2.13 (the change only moves existing Python checks).

Studio Images: SDXL prompt weighting, CLIP skip, CFG rescale and variation seeds (#14562)

## Summary

Refs #10695

Four generation controls for SDXL checkpoints on the diffusers engine.
Most of these requests come from people bringing Civitai SDXL models
over from AUTOMATIC1111 / Forge:

1. Prompt weighting with AUTOMATIC1111 syntax: `(word:1.2)`, `(word)`,
`[word]`, `\(` `\)` `\[` `\]` `\\` escapes, and `BREAK`. Prompts past 75
CLIP tokens are now encoded in 75-token chunks instead of being cut off
at 77.
2. CLIP skip, using AUTOMATIC1111 numbering.
3. CFG rescale (`cfg_rescale`), which passes through as diffusers
`guidance_rescale`.
4. Variation seed and variation strength (AUTOMATIC1111 subseeds), plus
a Vary button.

All four are off by default, and off sends exactly the pipeline call
that runs today, with one intended exception: a prompt longer than 75
CLIP tokens is now chunked instead of silently truncated. They only show
up when the loaded model supports them.

## Behaviour

### Prompt weighting

- The parser follows `modules/prompt_parser.py` `parse_prompt_attention`
in stable-diffusion-webui (commit 82a973c). That repo is AGPL-3.0, the
same licence as Studio, but the code here is a rewrite, not a copy.
- Tokenization and chunking follow `modules/sd_hijack_clip.py`
`tokenize_line` / `process_tokens`:
  - each chunk is `<bos>` + 75 tokens + `<eos>`;
- when a chunk fills up, the tokens after a comma in its last 20 tokens
move to the next chunk;
- everything after the first `<eos>` uses the tokenizer's pad id, which
for SDXL's OpenCLIP tokenizer is `!`, as in webui.
- Emphasis is webui's default `Original` from `modules/sd_emphasis.py`:
each token's output is scaled by its weight, then the chunk is rescaled
back to its unweighted mean. The pooled embedding comes from the first
chunk, unweighted.
- If either side uses CFG, positive and negative are padded to the same
chunk count with empty-prompt chunks (webui `pad_cond_uncond`), because
diffusers runs both branches in one batch.
- An empty negative prompt still gives zero negatives
(`force_zeros_for_empty_prompt`), the same as the pipeline today.
- It engages only when parsing changes the text (brackets, escapes,
`BREAK`) or the prompt is longer than 75 CLIP tokens (counted after
`maybe_convert_prompt`, as `encode_prompt` tokenizes). A shorter plain
prompt never reaches the new code and goes through the pipeline's own
`encode_prompt`, so it renders bit-identically.
- Layer selection is diffusers' own indexing, so `(fox:1.0)` renders
bit-identically to `fox`.
- `prompt_weighting: false` reads brackets as literal text; a long
prompt still chunks (webui's "None" emphasis).
- A malformed weight such as `(cat:1.2.3)` stays literal text,
parentheses included (webui raises on it).
- Encoding stops at 32 chunks (2400 tokens) and logs a warning; webui
and ComfyUI have no limit, so this only bounds what one request can make
the encoder do. Tokenizing and chunking stop at the cap too, and at most
76800 characters of a prompt are read, so a huge API prompt costs no
more than one at the cap.
- Textual inversion tokens are expanded per fragment with the pipeline's
`maybe_convert_prompt`.

### CLIP skip

The UI and API use AUTOMATIC1111 numbering, where 1 means the model's
own layer.

- diffusers: `StableDiffusionXLPipeline.encode_prompt` reads
`hidden_states[-(clip_skip + 2)]` ("SDXL always indexes from the
penultimate layer"). `StableDiffusionPipeline.encode_prompt` reads
`hidden_states[-(clip_skip + 1)]` and then applies `final_layer_norm`.
- webui-forge reads `hidden_states[-max(N, minimal_clip_skip)]`, with
`minimal_clip_skip=2` for SDXL (`backend/diffusion_engine/sdxl.py`) and
1 for SD 1.x. AUTOMATIC1111 keeps SDXL on the penultimate layer unless
`sdxl_clip_l_skip` is set.
- On SDXL the skip moves CLIP-L and OpenCLIP-G together. This matches
ComfyUI's `CLIPSetLastLayer`: `comfy/sdxl_clip.py`
`SDXLClipModel.set_clip_options` passes the layer to both `clip_l` and
`clip_g`. Forge does the same (`StableDiffusionXL.set_clip_skip` sets
both text engines), and so does diffusers'
`encode_prompt(clip_skip=...)`. AUTOMATIC1111's `sdxl_clip_l_skip`
option, off by default, skips CLIP-L only.
- So AUTOMATIC1111 N maps to diffusers `max(N, 2) - 2` on SDXL (None for
1 and 2) and `N - 1` on SD 1.x. On SDXL, "Clip skip 2" (common on Pony /
Illustrious cards) is the default, and 1 and 2 render the same. A naive
`N - 1` would change every Pony / Illustrious render.
- Values above 2 on SDXL go through the same encoder as prompt
weighting, not through the pipeline's `clip_skip` argument. diffusers'
SDXL `encode_prompt` applies `clip_skip` to the positive prompt only: a
non-empty negative is always read at `hidden_states[-2]`. AUTOMATIC1111
and Forge apply the skip to the prompt and the negative alike.
- The maximum is capped at the shallower text encoder's depth, which the
status reports.

### CFG rescale

- Passed through as `guidance_rescale` to
`StableDiffusionXLPipeline.__call__`, which applies `rescale_noise_cfg`
(arXiv 2305.08891, section 3.4) after the guided combination.
- The default is 0. For v-prediction checkpoints, the hint shows 0.7,
the paper's value, but nothing defaults to it: the NoobAI-XL V-Pred 1.0
and 0.75s cards recommend CFG 4 to 5 and Euler, and neither names a
rescale value.
- Workflows whose pipeline has no `guidance_rescale` (ControlNet) refuse
a non-zero value. On the Images page, Create with a ControlNet engaged
does not send it, and the CFG rescale slider is disabled with the
reason.

### Variation seed

- Follows `modules/rng.py` `ImageRNG.first` and `slerp` in
stable-diffusion-webui: the seed's noise is slerped toward the variation
seed's noise by the strength, per image, using webui's formula including
its nearly-parallel branch.
- The base noise is still drawn by the pipeline's own `prepare_latents`
from the request's generator, so the generator advances exactly as
before and ancestral samplers get the same per-step noise. Only the
initial latent changes.
- Strength 0 is today's render. Strength 1 is exactly the render of the
variation seed.
- In a batch, every image keeps the seed and image i uses
`variation_seed + i` (webui `all_subseeds`), so a batch gives variations
of one image.
- Text to image and ControlNet only. Img2img and inpaint take their
noise from the source image, so they refuse it. The Images page shows
the variation controls and sends their fields only on Create.
- Vary restores the selected image's settings (the exact caption it ran
with, size, guidance, LoRAs and these controls) and re-runs its seed
with a fresh variation seed at strength 0.15, so the result keeps that
image's composition even when the form held something else. It is
offered for a text-to-image image made with the loaded model, and
disabled with the reason when the current load cannot apply part of that
recipe (its LoRAs on a load without LoRA support, or a recorded CLIP
skip, CFG rescale or prompt weighting off the load does not offer). It
is also disabled for an image that already used a variation seed: its
noise was a blend of two seeds, which a fresh variation of its base seed
would not keep. It also needs the image to come off the exact loaded
build: the engine, model kind, checkpoint file, transformer and
text-encoder quants, attention backend, step cache and the LoRAs baked
in at load time (compared as a set) recorded with it must match the
current load, since a different build turns the same seed into a
different picture. An image whose record predates those fields (no
engine recorded) cannot be checked, so Vary stays disabled for it with
that reason; gallery records now include the recorded `engine` for this.
AUTOMATIC1111 users typically use 0.05 to 0.3. Fooocus' Vary buttons are
img2img at denoise 0.5 / 0.85, which is a different mechanism.

## Gating and API

- `/api/inference/images/status` reports `sd_controls`:
`prompt_weighting`, `clip_skip {min, max, default,
same_as_default_through}`, `cfg_rescale {min, max, default,
recommended}`, `variation_seed`, `vary_strength` and `prediction_type`.
It is null for every non-SDXL family and for the native and MLX engines.
Status also reports `baked_loras`, the adapter ids baked into the
transformer at load time (as the gallery record names them), empty when
none were baked.
- The Images page shows the controls in the Advanced section only when
`sd_controls` is present. Each control has a tooltip, and the Vary
button shows only on Create with a selected text-to-image image from the
loaded model.
- `POST /api/inference/images/generate` takes the optional fields
`prompt_weighting`, `clip_skip` (1 to 12, AUTOMATIC1111 numbering),
`cfg_rescale` (0 to 1), `variation_seed` (0 to 2^32 - 1) and
`variation_strength` (0 to 1). Omitting them all is today's request.
- A FLUX, Qwen or other non-SDXL load returns a 400 that names the
controls. Weight syntax there is still literal text. The native and MLX
engines also return a 400 for a non-default value.
- The recipe, gallery record and PNG `parameters` record what ran, using
webui infotext names: `Variation seed`, `Variation seed strength`, `Clip
skip`, plus `CFG rescale`. Restore brings the values back. The record's
`prompt_weighting` is true when weight syntax was applied and false when
the request turned weighting off, so restoring a literal-prompt image
keeps Prompt weighting off. On the native sd.cpp engine, which always
reads `(word:1.2)` syntax, restoring or importing such an image names
"prompt weighting off" as not applied. Restoring a gallery image onto a
load that lacks a recorded CLIP skip, CFG rescale or variation seed (for
example the same SDXL repo on the native engine), or would clamp it,
names those too instead of reporting a full restore. A literal-prompt
run also writes `Emphasis: None` into `parameters`, so A1111 and Forge
replay it unweighted.

## How this fits with #14508

#14508 (paste generation parameters) already parses A1111 / Forge `Clip
skip`, `CFG Rescale` (and `RescaleCFG`, Forge's
`latent_modifier_rescale_cfg_phi`), `Variation seed` and `Variation seed
strength`, and listed them under "Not applied" because no request field
existed yet. This branch is merged with main after it and fills that
gap:

- Pasting a parameters block, dropping an image, or loading a recipe now
sets CLIP skip, CFG rescale, the variation seed and its strength in the

one restore path (`applyImportedRecipe` into `restoreSettings`); the
duplicate parser branch this PR had is gone.

to restored keys. `importNotApplied` now takes the loaded model's
`sd_controls`. It names only what that model lacks, a Clip skip above
the model's maximum (as clamped), a CFG rescale outside [0, 1] or above
the model's maximum (as clamped), a variation seed for img2img or
inpaint (the backend refuses it there, so the import also clears it),
and a variation seed or strength outside the request bounds (not 32-bit,
or strength above 1), which is named and left off instead of becoming a
random seed or a clamped strength. On a model without `sd_controls` the
toast is the same as on main.

brackets are applied, so they are no longer reported as "passed as plain

Prompt weighting off; on the native sd.cpp engine it is named as not

- The image's own parameters text uses the same key names, so pasting it

- Inpaint mask blur / Only masked (#14508) and these controls sit side
by side in the request, the gallery record and `generate()`. A variation
run keeps one base seed across runs, and that seed is the one "Reuse
last seed" picks up.

## How this fits with #14563

#14563 (per-generation Shift for flow-matching models, SDXL textual
inversion embeddings) is merged into this branch. The two touch the same
request, status, gallery record and restore code but different fields,
so they combine side by side:

- `DiffusionGenerateRequest` takes `shift` / `base_shift` / `max_shift`
and the four SDXL controls; status carries `shift_control`,
`textual_inversion` and `sd_controls`. Shift applies to flow-matching
models and these controls to SDXL, so one model shows one set or the
other.
- On an SDXL checkpoint, the weighted encoder expands embedding tokens
per fragment with the pipeline's `maybe_convert_prompt`, the same hook
#14563's embeddings rely on, so a weighted prompt can name an embedding.
This pair has not been run end to end on a real embedding file here.
- Recipes record and restore both sets of keys; the import toast lists
Shift values and missing embeddings next to the SDXL controls.
- To keep the startup bundle within budget after the merge, the three
Images-page-only calls (`listDiffusionControlNets`, `moveGalleryImage`,
`addGalleryImageToProject`) moved out of `api.ts` (which the eager chat
chunk carries) into `images-page-api.ts`, as #14563 did with
`embeddings-api.ts`.

## Compile and CUDA graphs

With the compiled U-Net and CUDA graphs on the tiny SDXL pipeline (speed
`default`: channels_last, fused QKV, compiled, CUDA graphs), changing
weights, clip skip, rescale or variation between renders compiled
nothing new.

Prompts 2 to 4 of a probe that alternates weighted and plain prompts
with and without a variation strength had 0 FX graph cache misses and 0
new graphs. Weighting and variation only change tensor values.

A prompt that now chunks to 154 or 231 tokens is a new text length for
the U-Net and compiles once per chunk count. The same is true of any new
text length.

MoE autotune cache: version disk entries and refit loaded configs (#14617)

## What broke

#14578 made disk cache hits in `unsloth/kernels/moe/autotune_cache.py`
live: `get_or_autotune_moe_kernels` rebuilds the cached `KernelConfig*`
objects and returns them straight away. Two things were missing on that
path:

1. The cache key has no schema or Triton identity, so a file written by
the pre-#14578 code (whose loader always returned `None` and deleted it,
so the file was dormant) now loads unchanged.
2. The loaded configs never go through `_fit_configs_to_dims` /
`_fit_configs_to_smem`, which every other config source (heuristic,
default) already uses.

Concrete failure: bf16, E=128, hidden 2048, intermediate 768, top-k 8, a
cached dW tile (BM, BN, BK, warps, stages) = (128, 256, 256, 8, 4). That
tile was valid for the legacy dW kernel (69,632 B shared memory on
sm86), but the per-expert dW kernel from #14550 needs 132,096 B on sm86
(limit 101,376 B) and 263,168 B on sm90 (limit 232,448 B), so the launch
raises `OutOfResources`. A cached entry with N=128, K=64 and
`BLOCK_SIZE_K=128` also loads unchanged and fails `tl.static_assert(K %
BLOCK_SIZE_K == 0)`.

## Change

- `_CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2` plus `triton.__version__` go into the
cache key and into the saved JSON. `load_cached_config` treats an entry
without them, or with different values, as a miss (returns `None`
without deleting; the next save overwrites it). Legacy files sit under
the old key and are never opened.
- On a disk hit, the reconstructed configs run through
`_fit_configs_to_dims(configs, 2 * intermediate_dim, hidden_dim)` and
`_fit_configs_to_smem(configs, dtype, weight_dtype)` before they go into
the in-memory cache. The example dW tile becomes (64, 256, 256, 8, 3),
66,048 B compiled on sm86.

The warm path is still a single dict lookup: fitting runs once per key
per process, on the first disk load. `get_or_autotune_moe_kernels` stays
`@torch.compiler.disable`, so compile behaviour does not change. A
one-time re-tune per model shape happens after upgrading, since old
entries are misses.

## Validation

New `tests/test_moe_autotune_cache_validate.py` (CPU, CUDA capability
and shared memory mocked):

- a legacy unversioned file is ignored and autotuning runs once; the
legacy-key file is left on disk
- an oversized dW tile from disk is fitted to (64, 256, 256, 8, 3) with
zero autotune calls
- a `BLOCK_SIZE_K` larger than K from disk is fitted to divide K and N
- a valid current entry hits unchanged with zero autotune calls, and the
warm call returns the same tuple without reading disk

`tests/test_moe_autotune_cache_hit.py` now pins the mocked shared memory
so its tuned tiles stay as saved.

Flip on main: 3 of the 4 new tests fail (legacy file reused, dW tile
unchanged, BLOCK_SIZE_K unchanged); the valid-hit guard passes on both.
With the fix, the new tests plus the existing MoE cache / fallback /
compile tests (`test_moe_autotune_cache_hit.py`,
`test_moe_fallback_smem.py`, `test_moe_fallback_tile_dims.py`,
`test_grouped_gemm_mixed_tma_device.py`,
`test_moe_autotune_under_compile.py`) give 230 passed on torch 2.10 and
torch 2.14 venvs.

## Not covered

- No GPU launch of a refitted disk config was run in this change; the
shared memory numbers come from the existing estimator and a CPU
cross-compile.
- Device selection is unchanged: lookup and tuning still use the current
CUDA device, and unsloth_zoo passes no operand device. On a mixed-GPU
host where the current device differs from the operand device,
capability and shared memory can be read from the wrong card. Fixing
that needs a device argument threaded from zoo, left for a follow-up.

Studio: OpenAI-compatible fine-tuning jobs API (/v1/files, /v1/fine_tuning/jobs) (#14496)

Fixes https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth/issues/13603

Existing code that uses OpenAI's fine-tuning API can now train on
Unsloth Studio by changing only the base URL and the key:

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8888/v1", api_key="sk-unsloth-...")

f = client.files.create(file=open("train.jsonl", "rb"), purpose="fine-tune")
job = client.fine_tuning.jobs.create(
    model="unsloth/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507",
    training_file=f.id,
    method={"type": "supervised", "supervised": {"hyperparameters": {"n_epochs": 2}}},
    suffix="support-bot",
    extra_body={"lora_r": 16, "max_seq_length": 4096},  # any Studio training setting
)
client.fine_tuning.jobs.retrieve(job.id)          # status, trained_tokens, fine_tuned_model
client.fine_tuning.jobs.list_events(job.id)       # loss per step
client.fine_tuning.jobs.checkpoints.list(job.id)
client.fine_tuning.jobs.cancel(job.id)
```

OpenAI is winding down its own fine-tuning platform (new jobs only until
January 6, 2027), and none of the popular open-source trainers serve
this API today, so this gives people moving off it a local drop-in.

## How it works

A thin translation layer in
`studio/backend/routes/openai_fine_tuning.py`, mounted on `/v1` next to
the existing OpenAI inference routes. It adds no new capability: an API
key can already do all of this through `/api/train`.

| OpenAI route | Studio |
|---|---|
| `POST /v1/files` (purpose `fine-tune`), `GET /v1/files`, `GET
/v1/files/{id}` | The same dataset upload as the Train page, so the file
also shows up in the dataset picker. `file-<id>` is the upload's own id.
|
| `POST /v1/fine_tuning/jobs` | Builds a normal training request and
calls the same handler as `/api/train/start`, so every guard and refusal
applies (one run at a time, busy GPU, gated models, account sandbox).
`n_epochs`, `batch_size`, `seed` and `suffix` map directly,
`validation_file` becomes the eval set (with evaluation on), a `wandb`
integration turns on W&B logging for its project,
`learning_rate_multiplier` scales Studio's default 2e-4, and Studio
settings (`lora_r`, `max_steps`, `load_in_4bit`, `training_type`, ...)
go through `extra_body`. |
| `GET /v1/fine_tuning/jobs`, `GET /v1/fine_tuning/jobs/{id}` | Read
from the training history; a job is a Studio run (`ftjob_<run id>`), so
runs started from the UI are listed too. Status: running, succeeded,
cancelled, failed, plus validating_files / queued before the worker is
up. `fine_tuned_model` is the run folder name Chat and Export show. |
| `GET .../events` | One `metrics` event per logged step (loss, learning
rate, grad norm, eval loss), framed by start and outcome messages. |
| `GET .../checkpoints` | The run's `checkpoint-N` folders with their
step loss. |
| `POST .../cancel` | `/api/train/stop` for that job (saves at the next
safe step). |

API keys never see host paths: a local model path comes back as its
handle and error messages are path-redacted, as on the other routes.
`/v1/files` gets the dataset upload's own body cap instead of the small
JSON cap.

Not supported yet, with a clear 400: `method` `dpo` and `reinforcement`,
and pause / resume. A second job while one is running is refused with
409 rather than queued, which the SDK raises as `ConflictError`.

## No change for existing users

Only new routes. The UI, the Train page flow, `/api/train` and the
existing `/v1` inference routes are untouched.

## Verified end to end

On a Colab T4 with Studio installed from this branch (`studio/setup.sh
--local`), the stock `openai` SDK pointed at `http://127.0.0.1:8888/v1`
with an `sk-unsloth` key:

| Call | Result |
|---|---|
| `files.create(codes.jsonl, purpose="fine-tune")` | `file-b66b...`,
10522 bytes, `processed` |
| `fine_tuning.jobs.create(model="unsloth/Qwen3-0.6B", ...,
extra_body={"max_steps": 12, "save_steps": 6})` | `validating_files`,
then `running`, then `succeeded` after about 100 s |
| `jobs.retrieve` |
`fine_tuned_model="unsloth_Qwen3-0.6B__project-e2e_1792585453"`,
`trained_tokens=1000` |
| `jobs.list_events` | one event per step, loss 4.40 at step 1 down to
1.47 at step 12 |
| `jobs.checkpoints.list` | `checkpoint-12` (loss 1.47) and
`checkpoint-6` (loss 2.86) |
| `jobs.create` while a job is training | 409 `Training is already in
progress. Stop current training before starting a new one.` |
| `jobs.cancel` mid-run | `cancelled`, and stays `cancelled` on retrieve
|

On main the same calls return 404.

## Tests

`studio/backend/tests/test_openai_fine_tuning.py` drives the routes with
the real `openai` SDK: upload then create (checks the exact training
request built), a finished run read back as a succeeded job with events
and checkpoints, a failed run with its host paths redacted for an API
key, cancel, the refusals, and paging through the whole history. The
multi-account route matrix now covers the new object routes (another
account and the owner get 404).

Studio: resize the sliding pill with transforms, so it keeps pace with the move (#14361)

## Summary

Follow-up to #14030. On an Unsloth Studio segmented toggle, the selected
pill could fall out of step with itself while it slid between two tabs
of different widths. It moved on time, but its width lagged behind. Two
things followed:

- Moving to a narrower tab at the edge of the track, the pill ran past
the edge (into the model picker's "All" dropdown) and then snapped back.
- Moving to a wider tab (On Device → Recommended), the pill arrived at
its old width and then grew into place.

Now the move and the width change run together, in every browser.

</details>

## Why it happened

The pill slides with a transform, which every browser runs on the
compositor. Its width changed through a `clip-path` animation, which
Chromium repaints on the main thread. A click that also re-renders a
list keeps the main thread busy, so the clip held the old width while
the transform kept moving. Recommended's model list is one example.

## Changes

`segmented-pill-slide.ts`, `segmented-control.tsx`:
- While the pill changes width, it is drawn as two round caps and a
strip between them. The end cap moves by the width change and the strip
stretches with `scaleX`. Every piece is a transform on the same clock as
the move, so the whole slide runs on the compositor, and a busy main
thread can't pull it apart. The caps keep the ends round, since only the
strip, which has no round ends, is scaled.
- The strip tucks 1px under each cap, so no seam shows and its square
corners never poke out past the curve.
- The pieces hold their last frame (`fill: "forwards"`) and are
cancelled in the same cleanup that hides them, so nothing flashes
between the end of the slide and the cleanup.
- `SegmentedPill` renders its four hidden pieces from one list. This
keeps the startup bundle inside its budget, with no budget change.

## Testing

**Cross-browser** (Playwright Chromium 156, Firefox 157, WebKit 27.2):
- Real model picker, both themes, both directions. The slide was paused
and stepped to fixed times in each engine. The pill shape and position
match in all three engines, the slide ends exactly on the tab, and no
pieces or animations are left behind.
- Test page, four width-changing moves, both themes. Pill edges match
the shipped clip-path version to within 0.23 px at every step. The
pixels match too, with no corners or seams.
- Busy page (main thread held for 250 ms after the click):

Fused decode RoPE: drop the per-layer host drain on split models (#14611)

#14599 (fused decode RoPE) calls `_sync_if_split(Q)` after its Triton
launch in `decode_rope_inplace` and `decode_qk_norm_rope`. On a model
split across GPUs (device_map), that blocks the host once per layer per
decoded token.

The drain is not needed there. Both helpers launch inside
`torch_gpu_device(Q.device)`, so the kernel runs on Q's device and its
current stream. The next layer's `.to(other_device)` is already ordered
after it: PyTorch's device-to-device copy synchronizes with the current
streams of both devices (`aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Copy.cu`). The older
eager RoPE entry points keep their drains. Those were added in #3049 /
#3061 for launches made while another GPU was current, and this PR does
not touch them.

Measured on a random-weight 8-layer Llama (hidden 2048, fp16) split 4 +
4 over two B200s: batch 1, 32 new tokens, 4 interleaved repeats, median
generate time.

| decode RoPE path | median s | tokens/s |
|---|---|---|
| before #14599 | 0.442 | 72.4 |
| main (fused + drain) | 0.723 | 44.3 |
| fused, drain removed (this PR) | 0.444 | 72.0 |

All three arms produced the same tokens. With random weights that is
only a weak correctness check (the output is mostly one repeated token),
so this PR also adds a direct ordering test.

## Change
- Remove `_sync_if_split(Q)` from `decode_rope_inplace` and
`decode_qk_norm_rope`.
- Single-GPU behaviour is unchanged: the drain was a no-op there.

## Validation
- `test_decode_split_sync_and_mixed_devices` now asserts that the decode
helpers make no drain call.
- New `test_decode_rope_on_another_device_orders_with_the_copy`, which
needs two GPUs and skips on one:
  - rotates Q / K on GPU 1 while GPU 0 is current;
  - copies straight to GPU 0 with no host sync;
  - compares the result with the unfused rotation.
- `test_decode_fused_rope`, `test_qk_norm_rope`,
`test_rope_kernel_layouts`, `test_rope_sync_single_device`,
`test_qwen3_decode_offset_rope`, GPU-marked tests included: 414 passed,
1 skipped (the two-GPU test) on torch 2.14.1 and on torch 2.10.0.

Not covered: the two-GPU test was not run here (single-GPU leases). The
timing table comes from a two-GPU run of the same change outside this
PR's CI. ROCm split models were not tested.

Fast LayerNorm backward: no aliased gradient buffers when only one of weight / bias trains (#14609)

#13801 made `fast_layernorm` return weight and bias gradients. When only
one of the two is trainable, the backward passes the dW and dB kernels
two views of the same buffer:
- `partials[0]` / `partials[-1]` into `layernorm_backward_dw`;
- `outs[0]` / `outs[-1]` into `_layernorm_sum_partials`.

In eager mode only the trained one is written, so this is harmless.
Under `torch.compile` (both kernels are user Triton kernels traced by
dynamo) one of the two writes into the aliased buffer is dropped, and
the gradient comes back uninitialised. Measured relative error against
fp64:

| case | eager | compiled (main) |
|---|---|---|
| bias trainable only, fp32 | 7.3e-08 | 4.5e+35 / nan |
| weight trainable only, fp32 | 1.0e-07 | 1.01 / 5.7e+17 |
| weight only, bf16 | 1.7e-03 | 1.01 / 3.8e+17 |

This covers `bias=False` with a trainable weight, which #13801 added,
and the frozen-weight or frozen-bias LoRA setups. When both train, the
views differ and the result is correct, which is the only case the
existing compile test covers.

## Change
- With one gradient, the unused pointer of each launch gets its own
one-element buffer.
- The kernels never touch it: `TRAIN_W` / `TRAIN_B` are constexpr, and
the sum kernel only runs `len(outs)` programs.
- No change when both or neither train.

## Validation
- New `test_layernorm_compiled_single_trainable_matches_eager`:
  - covers only bias, only weight, and no bias, in fp32 and fp16;
- compiles with `fullgraph=True` and requires bitwise equality with
eager for y, dX, dW and dB.
  - Main: 6 failed. This PR: 6 passed.
- The four LayerNorm test files (`test_layernorm_weight_grad`,
`test_layernorm_gradient_layout`,
`test_high_precision_layernorm_coverage`,
`test_layernorm_precision_env_scope`), GPU-marked tests included: 174
passed, 4 skipped on torch 2.14.1 and on torch 2.10.0 (B200).

Exposure: nothing inside unsloth or unsloth-zoo calls `fast_layernorm`
today, so only users calling the public `unsloth.kernels.fast_layernorm`
from their own compiled code were affected.

Not covered: other GPUs and ROCm (the change is host-side buffer
allocation only).

Studio Run settings: restore saved settings on a fresh editor, show save state, group Advanced rows (#14589)

## What changed

**Saved settings now come back when you open Run settings.** The panel
mirrors each model's remembered settings to the server so Desktop, LAN
and tunnel origins share them. On a fresh editor (a new browser, the
Desktop app vs the web UI, or cleared site data) the server row arrived
but was always refused. The guard that protects in-flight edits compared
the config by object identity, and the primed draft is a new object that
is equal to the first render's fallback, so the row was dropped and the
panel opened on defaults with Remember unticked. The guard now compares
by value. Edits made while the request is in flight are still protected
by the existing edited flag and the value comparison.

**The footer shows whether settings are saved.** Under "Remember for
this model" one line now reads: Saved for this model, Unsaved changes
(amber), Not saved yet, Saved settings will be forgotten, Using default
settings, or Not remembered for this model. It compares what Save would
store against the stored record and re-reads that record on every write,
including writes from other tabs. The line is always rendered, so it
never shifts the Load button under the cursor.

**An unticked Load only forgets settings that were remembered.** Before,
every Load with Remember unticked deleted the local record and sent a
server forget. That removed settings the editor had never shown, CLI-set
flags included, in two cases: a compare pane seeded from its own
snapshot opens unticked over a newer saved record, and a failed or
timed-out overrides read lets Load run before the row is read. A forget
now happens only when Remember was on and has been unticked.

**Reopening right after Save or Forget reads the new row.** The
overrides read now waits for that model's queued writes, so a panel
reopened while a Forget was still in flight can no longer read the old
row back and re-save it locally.

**Advanced settings are grouped.** The GGUF list was about 15 rows in
one column. It is now split into Memory (KV cache, GPU memory, Vision),
Speed (speculative decoding, parallel slots, batch sizes, tensor
parallelism), Output (reasoning budget, chat template) and Server
(mmap/mlock, checkpoints, cache RAM, extra arguments). The Server group
stays hidden for diffusion models, as its rows were before.

instead of a literal -1. With -1 in the box, typing a digit produced

memoized), and whole-store platform subscriptions in the page and in

## Summary
Follow-up to #14491 from a post-merge review. Two cases where the FLUX.3
prompt upsampler did less than it could on NVIDIA hosts running the
Vulkan llama.cpp build.

- **Vendor by positive evidence.** Older NVIDIA drivers name Vulkan
devices without the word "NVIDIA" (`Tesla T4`, `Quadro RTX 8000`,
`GeForce GTX 1080 Ti`). The single-card check treated those as another
vendor's GPU and declined the warm start, so the first enhanced prompt
paid a cold start. A Vulkan row now counts as another vendor only when

no vendor at all is not treated as another card.

every prefetch. Each probe can take up to 15 s, and two prefetches
inside the 120 s window used to run four probes; they now run two (the
probe and one retry), and concurrent prefetches share one answer. The
next window can retry again.

Vulkan rows, and a lone row from a plainly different vendor (still
declined).

MoE grouped GEMM: no lock on cached autotuner launches; read the SM count once per card (#14605)

## Summary
Follow-up to #14490 from a post-merge review. #14490 wrapped every
grouped GEMM autotuner launch on a multi-GPU host in a per-GPU-model
lock, so identical cards would tune a new shape once. The lock was also
held on cache hits: every launch paid it (about 0.5 us more per call),
and a cold shape being tuned on one card blocked already-tuned launches
on an identical card until the benchmark finished.

## What changes
- **No lock.** Per-card tuner copies still share one results cache per
GPU model, so a shape tuned on one card is reused by every identical
card. A cached launch never waits on another card. Two identical cards
hitting the same cold shape at the same instant may both tune it, which
is what every multi-GPU host did before #14490.
- **SM count read once per card.** The forward, dX and dW launchers
called `torch.cuda.get_device_properties(...)` on every launch (three
per MoE layer per step); it is now cached per device index, since it
cannot change within a process.

Single-GPU hosts are unchanged (they never used the per-card copies).

## Tests
- `tests/test_grouped_gemm_mixed_tma_device.py`:
`test_identical_cards_launch_concurrently` (two cached launches on
identical cards must be inside `run` at once; main fails with
`BrokenBarrierError` because the lock serializes them) and
`test_sm_count_is_read_once_per_card` (fails on main). The shared-cache,
separate-model and configs-follow tests still pass.
- MoE CPU suites (11 files): main 225 passed / 48 skipped, this branch
226 / 48 (one new test), 0 failures on both.
- B200, base and head interleaved: forward, dX and dW with autotune off
and on give the identical output hash on every run.

unsloth start: fix Studio discovery, proxy, Hermes context, Claude hooks and Codex login (#14591)

## What changed

A sweep of `unsloth start` for bugs a normal user hits. Each fix has a
regression test. Several were reproduced against the real agents: Hermes
0.21.0, Claude Code 2.1.307, dsh 0.2.1-rc.2 and PowerShell 7.6.

### Server discovery and HTTP
- **Finds your own Studio when another one holds 8888.** If 8888 belongs
to another OS user's or another install's Studio, `unsloth studio` moves
to the next free port. `unsloth start` then failed with "Couldn't verify
that http://127.0.0.1:8888 is your Unsloth". Discovery now uses the
server this install recorded whenever the default port's server can't
prove it belongs to this install. `unsloth chat` and `unsloth mcp` share
this code, so they get the fix too.
- **Loopback requests skip `http_proxy`.** urllib proxies 127.0.0.1
unless `no_proxy` lists it. With a proxy exported, discovery failed, the
health poll ran to the 900 s timeout, and the minted `sk-unsloth-` key
went to the proxy in plain text. Loopback requests now skip the proxy,
which `unsloth studio` already does. Remote URLs still use it.

### Model selection
- **No-model attach skips speech and separation models.** These entries
carry a `task` tag in the loaded-models listing. Before, Claude or Codex
could be pointed at an Orpheus TTS model. If only such a model is
loaded, the error now says so.
- **Relative paths are resolved for a running server.** `--model
./foo.gguf` is now sent as an absolute path, because a running server
resolves paths against its own working directory.
- **Conflicting variants now warn.** `--model repo:Q8_0 --gguf-variant
Q4_K_M` used to drop the inline variant silently. It still prefers the
flag, and now prints a warning.
- **Clearer `--no-launch` error.** With no server running, `--no-launch
--model X` now says that `--no-launch` never starts one.

### Hermes
- **Small-context models work again, and context pins apply.** The
provider is now registered as `unsloth-studio` instead of `unsloth`.
Hermes strips a `<provider>/` prefix from model ids, which turned
`unsloth/Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF` into `Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF`. The id then no longer
matched `model.default`, so Hermes ignored the pinned `context_length`.
Models under 64K were refused outright ("below the minimum 64,000"), and
larger ones lost the pin. An earlier `providers.unsloth` entry written
by Unsloth is removed, both in the session home and with `--app`. A
user's own entry is left alone.
- **Compaction fits the real window.** Hermes raises any threshold below
0.75, so a 40K model compacted at 55,705 tokens, past its real window.
`compression.threshold_tokens` now caps compaction at 90% of the real
window (36,864 for 40,960).
- **No leftover pins under `--persist`.** A home kept with `--persist`
no longer carries small-window settings into a later run with a larger
window.

### Claude Code
- **Hooks work on Windows without Git Bash.** Hooks now use exec form
(`command` + `args`, Claude Code 2.1.139+), so no shell parses them.
Without Git Bash, Claude Code runs shell-form hooks in PowerShell, which
can't parse `"python.exe" -c ...`. Since 2.1.299 a failing guard blocks
the call, so `--as-subagent` could never call `unsloth_agent`. Older
builds keep the shell string.
- **`apiKeyHelper` no longer runs.** The session overlay now blanks
`apiKeyHelper`. Before, the user's helper ran on every launch and its
cloud key was sent to Unsloth as `x-api-key`.
- **Forwarded `--settings` is kept.** Claude keeps only the last
`--settings`, so a user's forwarded one used to be dropped. It is now
merged into the overlay, and Unsloth's pins win where the two conflict.

### Codex
- **`--as-subagent` no longer breaks Codex login on Windows.** Where
symlinks are denied, `auth.json` is now hard-linked rather than copied.
Before, a token refresh in the overlay left the real
`~/.codex/auth.json` with a refresh token that had already been used, so
the next plain `codex` run couldn't refresh it.
- **A first login is kept.** A first sign-in under `--as-subagent` now
goes to the user's Codex home instead of the overlay, which is deleted
on exit.
- **Recovery hint for `--app`.** The `--app` message now says how the
app is switched back if the command is killed.

### Other agents
- **dsh profile shorthand passes through.** `unsloth start dsh headless
"task"` now reaches dsh as its own profile shorthand, instead of
becoming `dsh web ... headless "task"`, which dsh rejects.
- **`--app` keeps comments in JSON configs.** OpenCode and OpenClaw
configs keep their `//` and `/* */` comments: only the touched member is
rewritten. The parsed result is checked, and the old full rewrite is the
fallback.
- **Pi warns about an old Node.** Pi needs Node.js 22.19+, while Unsloth
accepts Node 20.19. Pi now warns and names the `legacy-node20` package
when `node` is older.
- **Docs.** Help text and the README table now list VS Code and Mistral
Vibe.

## Verification
- `unsloth_cli` suites for start, start_app, plan gate, the subagent
bridges, inference_chat and mcp: all pass. In the full
`unsloth_cli/tests` run, the only failures are in studio update and
training tests that touch none of the changed code; they fail locally
because torch and GPU are absent.
- End to end on macOS (CPU) with an isolated Studio on its own port,
while another Studio held 8888:
- `unsloth start hermes unsloth/Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF:Q4_K_M --no-launch`
downloaded and loaded the model and found the right server.
- A one-shot `hermes chat` initialized against the 40,960-token model
and compacted at 36,864. Before this change it refused the model.
- `unsloth start claude -p ...` with Claude Code 2.1.307 sent its
requests to the local model.
- The PowerShell hook repro: the shell-form string fails with
`ParserError: Unexpected token '-c'`, and the exec form returns the deny
decision.

## Not tested here
- Windows and WSL themselves (NTFS hard links, a Claude Code session
without Git Bash). These rest on the upstream sources cited above plus
the pwsh repro.
- Node 20 at runtime for Pi.
- The OpenCode and OpenClaw desktop apps.
- Not changed, noted for follow-up: a trusted project
`.codex/config.toml` can override the Codex model, and TOML table
splitting doesn't account for `[` lines inside multi-line strings
(`--app` refuses those files instead of corrupting them).

torchao's MXFakeQuantizedLinear returns bfloat16 from the MX GEMM and
asserts the
output dtype equals the input dtype. Full finetuning runs under autocast
with
float32 hidden states, so any MX QAT config (including a hand built
TorchAOConfig)
failed at the first forward with an AssertionError in
torchao/prototype/qat/mx.py.

autocast,
  the same thing autocast does for nn.Linear.

float8_e4m3fn
activations and weights, 32 element blocks, output head kept in full
precision.
- Prepare-time checks shared with "nvfp4": bfloat16 layers only (the MX
GEMM always
returns bfloat16), a GEMM probe per layer placement that refuses GPUs
without MX
support (use fp8-fp8 there), narrow widths that fail the probe and
biased layers
(torchao's MX QAT backward returns no bias gradient) stay in full
precision.

### Tests
- tests/test_qat_microscaling_schemes.py: 7 new or parametrized cases
fail on main,
  all 22 pass; the other QAT suites pass (77 total).
- B200, tiny Qwen3 / Llama: LoRA (FastLanguageModel, FastModel) and full
finetuning
train with dynamic sequence lengths, merged 16 bit save reloads, and the
torchao
export reloads as MXTensor weights within MXFP8 rounding of the merged
weights.

Known, not changed here: a FastModel LoRA model trained without
model.train()
runs its decoder layers through the per-function compiled path, where
torchao MX
QAT hits a SymInt error in the backward with
allow_unspec_int_on_nn_module = True
and dynamic = True. The HF Trainer calls model.train().

Studio: Projects recency by chat activity, less polling behind projects and sources (#14586)

## What changes for the user

- **Projects page and switchers order projects by last use.** Previously
the Projects page, the header project switcher ("recent 6") and the
composer's quick project list sorted by the project's own `updatedAt`.
That value only moves on a rename or an instructions edit. So a project
you chatted in today could show "Sep 10" and sink to the bottom, while
the sidebar showed it first. All of these now use `max(lastActivityAt,
updatedAt)`, the value the sidebar already uses. The backend already
returns it.
- **Deleting a project from the Projects page cleans up like the sidebar
delete.** It now notifies chat history, so the deleted project's chats
leave the sidebar and Recents straight away. It also clears the
runtime's active project, so "Chat" does not reopen a project that no
longer exists.
- **Import defaults to Recents.** "Import chats…" used to preselect
`projects[0]`, which is whichever project the server listed first. It
now preselects Recents.
- **Unread chats are visible on the Projects page.** Expanded project
rows now show the unread dot. Before this, "Mark as unread" on that page
had no visible effect.
- **Search UX on the Projects page.** Escape clears the search, and an
empty result offers "Clear search". The empty page now says what a
project is for.

## Performance and lag

- **Idle chat page polls less.** On every chat open with no model
loaded, the page waits up to a minute for a CLI-started load and polled
`/api/inference/status` every 500 ms (~120 requests). It now polls at
500 ms for the first 5 s (or while a load is in progress), then every 2
s.
- **Linked folders.** They were polled every 4 s forever, including from
hidden tabs and with nothing syncing. They now poll every 4 s only while
a folder is syncing, every 30 s otherwise (the backend's scan interval),
skip polls while the tab is hidden, and refresh when the tab is shown
again.
- **Sources panel.** Each linked-folder change triggered three full
document-list fetches in the panel: the announce, a panel subscription
duplicating the hook's own listener, and an explicit refresh. It now
triggers one.
- **Document list merge.** The merge was O(n²) (`prev.find` per row).
With a 10k-file linked folder, that ran about 10^8 comparisons on the
main thread every 4 s, per instance. It now uses a Map, keeps unchanged
rows by identity, and returns the previous array when nothing changed,
so an idle poll re-renders nothing.
- **Fewer refetches of the project list.** `useChatProjects`
force-refetched the project list on every mount, and gallery tiles each
mount it. A mount now reuses a list loaded in the last 5 s.
- **Projects page reloads.** Expanded project rows reloaded 300 ms after
each streamed chunk save, which on a slow CPU model is nearly every
chunk. Chunk saves now wait for a 2 s lull. Structural changes keep 300
ms.
- **"Export All Projects" lists chats once.** It used to send one
request per project.
- **`GET /api/chat/projects`.** This endpoint ran
`ensure_chat_project_workspace` for every row: several SQLite
connections plus mkdirs per project, per call. It now only backfills
rows with no recorded root. Workspaces are still ensured where they are
used (project open, tools, gallery).

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm test` (full suite).
- New `tests/projects-activity-and-polling.test.ts`. Updated the
source-shape tests the change moved.
- Backend: new `test_project_list_workspace.py`. Existing project tests
pass (`test_project_working_folder.py`,
`test_project_workspace_location.py`, `test_chat_sidebar_rows.py`,
`test_gallery_projects.py`,
`test_account_private_directory_project_root.py`).
- Isolated Studio on CPU, with seeded projects, checked in the browser:
- A project edited 40 days ago with a chat today lists first, reading
"Today".
  - The unread dot appears.
  - Escape and Clear search work.
- Deleting a project with chats from the Projects page removes its rows
from the sidebar.
- The Sources tab issues 2 linked-folder requests in 20 s instead of
about 6.
- Idle `/api/inference/status` drops to about one request every 2 s
after the first 5 s.

## Not testable here

- Desktop-only linked-folder sync (native folder leases) was not run.
The polling change was exercised only with zero folders.
- Large-folder timing is reasoned from the code, not measured.

## Chat fork fixes and clearer fork affordances

### What users see

called "New Chat" used to produce "New Chat (1)". The frontend only
auto-titles a chat named exactly "New Chat", so the fork never got a
title. Now the fork stays "New Chat", and its first reply names it. Once
a chat has a title, its forks are numbered as before.
- **Later uploads stay behind.** Forking at message 2 used to copy every
document in the chat, including a PDF uploaded at message 10. Now a fork
only gets uploads made before the source chat moved past the fork point.
Forking at the tip copies everything, as before.
- **Forks are easier to recognise.**
- Sidebar rows mark forked chats with a grey fork icon at the right edge
of the row. It gives way to the generating spinner and the unread dot,
and to the pin and menu buttons on hover.

![Sidebar with grey fork icons on forked
chats](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shimmyshimmer/unsloth-staging-4/pr-media/pr/14587/sidebar_q-c9ac36a3bdf9.png)

of "Continued from chat".

chats](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shimmyshimmer/unsloth-staging-4/pr-media/pr/14587/fork_q-062e96a46e1a.png)

A bare `assets/plot.png` fails to parse, so harden replaces the image with the blocked indicator. The card's `urlTransform` already resolves relative paths against `.../resolve//`, but it runs after harden, so it never saw these images. Harden's image prefix list is `["*"]` and the backend CSP allows `img-src https:`, so this was not an intentional host block. The fix adds a small rehype pass (`rehypeReadmeUrls`) that runs between sanitize and harden, through the existing `beforeHarden` hook that the chat renderer already uses for sandbox images: - Resolves relative `src` / `href` / `poster` against the repo's `resolve//` base (on the configured HF endpoint, so mirrors keep working). - Rewrites Hugging Face `.../blob//...` media URLs to `.../resolve//...`, since `blob/` is the HTML file viewer and never loads as an image. Links keep `blob/`, and other hosts are left untouched. - Leaves every other scheme alone, so harden still blocks `javascript:`, non-image `data:` and the rest exactly as before. `withLiteralUnknownTags` gains an optional `beforeHarden` argument (default empty, so the other callers are unchanged). ## Verification - New `tests/hub-readme-images.test.ts` renders through the real Streamdown pipeline: a bare relative image is blocked without the pass, resolves with it (raw HTML and Markdown, `assets/`, `./assets/`, root-relative), `blob/` image URLs on huggingface.co become `resolve/`, links and third-party hosts are unchanged, unsafe schemes stay blocked. - `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (all pass), `npm run build`; biome clean on the new files. - Isolated Studio on this branch, Playwright on `/hub?model=unsloth/flint-GGUF`: BEFORE on the merge base, the three repo-relative images show the blocked indicator; AFTER on this branch, they load from `huggingface.co/unsloth/flint-GGUF/resolve/main/assets/...` (all 8 card images report `naturalWidth > 0`, none blocked). ![Flint card before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shimmyshimmer/unsloth-staging-4/pr-media/pr/14602/flint_card_before_after-fd0b5cd373da.png) ## Not tested here Desktop (Tauri) builds were not run from this host; the change is frontend-only and the Desktop shell serves the same bundle.

Fast decode: rotate Q and K in one launch, and fuse Qwen3 q/k norm with RoPE (#14599)

In Unsloth's fast decode path (`LlamaAttention_fast_forward_inference`
and the Qwen3 decode attention), each layer rotates Q and K for the
single new token in eager ops. The path:
- gathers cos / sin at the position;
- builds `rotate_half` copies;
- multiplies and adds.

Qwen3 also runs q_norm and k_norm as separate RMSNorm launches before
that. This costs about 12 launches per layer per decoded token, and at
small GRPO rollout sizes decode is launch-bound. HF generate rollouts
(GRPO without vLLM) spend 95 to 97% of each step decoding, so this is
where the step time goes.

## Change
- `decode_rope_inplace` (`unsloth/kernels/rope_embedding.py`): for
single-token decode, one launch rotates Q and K in place at their
positions. It reuses the existing `_rope_qk` Triton kernel.
- `decode_qk_norm_rope` (`unsloth/kernels/qk_norm_rope.py`): for Qwen3,
one launch runs q_norm + k_norm + RoPE, built on the existing fused
`fast_qk_norm_rope` kernel.
- Both helpers write nothing and return False / None where they do not
apply. The caller then runs the old code unchanged. They do not apply:
  - when the sequence length is not 1;
  - on a non-CUDA device;
  - while `torch.compile` is tracing;
  - when Q, K, cos or sin have different dtypes;
- on non-contiguous tables, odd head dims, or a position count that does
not match the batch.
- `UNSLOTH_DECODE_FUSED_ROPE=0` restores the previous path.
- Training and prefill code paths are unchanged.

## Validation
In-process A/B with the kill switch toggled per rep, arms interleaved, 6
reps:
- setup: batch 4, LoRA r = 32 with non-zero B attached (as GRPO's HF
generate rollout runs it), greedy;
- timing: median `generate` wall time, 128 new tokens.

16-bit |

change otherwise), also for LongRope's short cache copy. Values are
