Studio diffusion: latch failed fused fp16 RoPE and AdaLN launches for the load (#14583)

## Problem

Follow-up to #14566, which made the fused FLUX RoPE in
`diffusion_rocm_fused.py` turn itself off for the rest of the load after
its first failed launch. Two sibling wrappers still retried a failing
launch on every call, so a broken JIT / driver / PTX path paid the
failed launch once per RoPE or AdaLN call for the whole render:

- the fp16-only FLUX.2 RoPE wrapper in `diffusion_flux2_rope.py`
- the opt-in fused AdaLN modulation (`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_FUSED_ADALN=1`)
in `diffusion_rocm_fused.py`

## Fix

Same latch as the fused FLUX RoPE:

- The first launch exception sets a per-path flag; every later call
skips the kernel and runs the stock path (the same stock code the
exception fallback already used, so output is bit-identical).
- One warning is logged when the latch trips. The fused FLUX RoPE latch
now logs the same way.
- `uninstall()` and the next load's install clear the flag, so a new
load tries the kernel again.
- AdaLN eligibility checks moved into `_adaln_eligible` (no behaviour
change) so the latch is testable without a GPU.

## Tests

- `test_a_failed_launch_disables_the_fused_path_for_the_load`
(`test_diffusion_flux2_rope.py`) and
`test_a_failed_adaln_launch_disables_the_fused_path_for_the_load`
(`test_diffusion_rocm_fused.py`): a raising launcher, four calls,
exactly one launch attempt, stock output after the failure, re-armed
after reload. Both fail on main and pass here.
- On a real CUDA GPU with a raising AdaLN launcher: main makes 4 launch
attempts in 4 calls, this branch makes 1; output equals stock in both.
- The related diffusion suites pass on GPU (161 passed).

## Not verified

- No real ROCm / gfx1151 or T4 run with a kernel that actually fails to
JIT; the failure is simulated with a raising launcher.

Studio video: export GIFs with one clip-wide palette (about 3x faster) (#14581)

## Problem

Exporting a generated video as GIF from the gallery Download menu is
slow. `_transcode_gif` decoded each kept frame to a full-resolution PIL
image, resized it with LANCZOS, then quantized it on its own with
`convert("P", palette=ADAPTIVE)` (median cut) before a Pillow
`save_all`.

Profile of a MiniMax-H3 clip (960x544, 124 frames at 24 fps, 62 kept) on
a loaded host:

| Stage | Time |
|---|---|
| Per-frame ADAPTIVE quantize | 5.8 to 10.3 s (80 to 85%) |
| PIL LANCZOS resize | 0.8 to 1.5 s |
| Decode | 0.4 s |
| Pillow save | 0.5 s |
| Total | 8 to 12 s |

The cost grows linearly with clip length and size (up to 300 frames at
720 px), so a longer clip or a slower user CPU waits tens of seconds or
more.

## Fix

The GIF now follows the common ffmpeg palettegen / paletteuse recipe,
through PyAV's filter graph:

- swscale scales each kept frame to rgb24 at the capped size
(`frame.reformat(..., interpolation="LANCZOS")`).
- `palettegen=reserve_transparent=on:transparency_color=ffffff` (default
`stats_mode=full`) builds one palette from all kept frames.
- `paletteuse=dither=sierra2_4a` maps each frame to that palette, and
PyAV's `gif` encoder writes the output with `loop=0` (loop forever).
- The 12 fps target and the `_GIF_MAX_EDGE` / `_GIF_MAX_FRAMES` caps
stay the same. Frames run on the kept-frame clock (`rate / step`), so
delays alternate between 8 and 9 cs and the total matches the clip. The
old fixed 8 cs delay played about 4% fast.
- palettegen has to see every frame before paletteuse can map the first
one. The scaled rgb24 frames are kept in memory when they fit in 160 MB
(about what the old path held as paletted frames at the caps). Larger
clips are decoded twice, so memory stays flat. The second decode is
cheap next to quantization (0.4 s on the clip above).
- If a PyAV build has no `palettegen`, `paletteuse` or `gif` encoder,
export falls back to the Pillow per-frame path, with the same error
messages. Swapping that path to a faster quantizer was not worth it:
FASTOCTREE lost about 2 dB PSNR.

## Results

Base is the merge base. Measurements are CPU only, interleaved
base/head, 3 runs each, on a heavily loaded shared host (load average
about 600 on 192 cores). The base repeats show the noise: their spread
is 5 to 15 s. In each clip, the slowest head run was faster than the
fastest base run. PSNR compares each GIF frame with the same frames
scaled by PIL LANCZOS, which is the old path's input to quantization.

| Clip | Base median (runs) | Head median (runs) | Base size | Head size
| Base PSNR | Head PSNR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H3 960x544, 124 f | 15.7 s (27.8 / 15.7 / 12.9) | 6.6 s (6.6 / 8.5 /
4.0) | 8.5 MB | 10.2 MB | 39.0 dB | 37.7 dB |
| H3 dense 960x544, 124 f | 11.1 s (11.1 / 9.3 / 20.2) | 3.8 s (3.4 /
3.8 / 4.1) | 11.8 MB | 11.7 MB | 43.6 dB | 41.7 dB |
| H3 1344x768, 124 f | 14.9 s (18.2 / 14.9 / 13.4) | 4.6 s (4.4 / 7.1 /
4.6) | 10.5 MB | 11.8 MB | 38.5 dB | 37.3 dB |

Every arm writes 62 frames at 720 px on the long edge. On first-frame
comparisons the two outputs look the same. The lower PSNR comes from the
error-diffusion dither, which trades per-pixel error for smoother
gradients and no banding. With `dither=none` the export takes about 1.9
s at 39.9 dB, but sierra2_4a is the default of the recipe this follows.

## Tests

The new tests in `studio/backend/tests/test_video_gallery.py` read the
GIF block structure directly:
- Global palette path: one palette for the whole clip, so no frame after
the first has a local color table. Tested both with frames held in
memory and with two decode passes. Also checks the NETSCAPE loop count
of 0, 8 or 9 cs delays, a total of about 1 s for 12 frames, and that the
palette path ran and the Pillow path did not.
- Caps on size and frame count on the palette path.
- Fallback to Pillow when `palettegen` / `paletteuse` are removed from
`av.filter.filters_available`.
- The missing-dependency error message is unchanged.

Before this change, the same clip writes a local palette on 11 of 12
frames with a fixed 8 cs delay, so the global-palette test fails. With
the change, all 127 tests in `test_video_gallery.py` and
`test_video_routes.py` pass.

## Not covered

- Timings come from one loaded Linux host, not a quiet machine or a user
CPU. The ratio is consistent, but the absolute numbers are noisy.
- No clip longer than 124 source frames was timed. Cost should scale
linearly with kept frames, but this was not measured.
- No PyAV build that is actually missing the filters was tested. The
fallback is covered only by the monkeypatched test.
- Exports are still not cached on the server, so each click transcodes
again.

## Summary

An audit of every Studio image and video optimization switch (all 144
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_*` / `UNSLOTH_VIDEO_*`
names, the other optimization env vars the diffusion and video modules
read, and the non-env defaults such as the
speed tier, attention backend, step caches and CFG batching) against two
rules: an optimization should be on by
default when it costs no accuracy, and where ComfyUI picks a setting by
default, Studio follows it.

Almost everything already passes. Most switches are kill switches for
optimizations that are already on, and the
rest are on through measured auto gates. Five defaults change here, plus
one follow-up to the bf16 rule, one commit each, so any of them can be
dropped
on its own:

1. **Fused FLUX RoPE now runs on NVIDIA CUDA too** (Linux, WSL
included). Bit-identical, 18.7% faster per eager
FLUX.2-klein-4B step on a B200. ComfyUI runs FLUX RoPE through
comfy-kitchen's fused `apply_rope` by default.
2. **Small DiTs keep bf16 by default while they fit** (FLUX.2-klein 4B,
Z-Image, FLUX.3-klein). FP8 / INT8 on
these sizes measured up to LPIPS 0.129 (klein-4B) and 0.191
(Z-Image-Turbo) against bf16. INT8 is still picked
when bf16 would offload. The rule is scoped by resolved base repo:
FLUX.2-klein 9B and base 9B (an 18.2 GB bf16
transformer, not measured here) keep the quantized default, mirrors
included.
3. **The automatic static step skip is now only on `speed_mode=max`.**
It is lossy (gated at LPIPS <= 0.05 on
`default`, <= 0.10 on `max`, #12652), and ComfyUI skips no steps by
default. Unset and `default` speed no longer
   skip steps, including the deferred "from the third image" path.
4. **CFG batching now also runs for a resident denoiser**, as ComfyUI
does by default (`calc_cond_batch`), behind
the existing per-shape timing gate (on only where one batched step,
timed end to end with its prediction,
merge, snapshot and verification, is at least 8% faster than two plain
calls). An explicit `speed_mode=off`
keeps one branch per call (`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_CFG_BATCH=force`
overrides). The trial now
runs once per shape on step 1 with its outputs discarded, so a render
never mixes paths and the same seed twice
gives the same image. On a compiled denoiser the doubled shape compiles
only inside a shape's first render: 0
   graph breaks and 0 recompiles on follow-up prompts.
5. **On Blackwell, `auto` attention keeps native SDPA where torch
already dispatches cuDNN.** Same kernel, bitwise
identical, without the cuDNN pin's per-call wrapper (0.4% to 22% per
eager SDPA call, equal compiled). ComfyUI also
   defaults to native.

6. **Small DiTs kept bf16 compile from render 1.** With speed unset, the
INT8 default for these models was compiled
from render 1. Keeping them bf16 (change 2) moved them onto the deferred
profile, which compiles on the third
image, a follow-up prompt. They now compile from render 1, as the INT8
load did, so follow-up prompts compile
nothing. The eager reference renders 1-2 are given up for these loads
only. An explicit speed is honoured, and
   every other dense load keeps the deferred profile.

Two switches stay off on purpose: the NVFP4 runtime
(`UNSLOTH_NVFP4_DIFFUSION`, waiting on the hosted NVFP4 repos)
and background compile (`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_BG_COMPILE`, which breaks
same-seed repeatability).

B200), the shape stays plain.

Three fixes go with it:

- **The trial no longer mixes paths inside a render.** It used to time
live steps, so render 1 ran some steps plain
and later ones batched, while render 2 read the verdict and took a
different path. Now steps 1-2 of every render
run plain, and step 2's own pair is timed. If needed, the trial runs
once per shape on step 2's arguments: two
plain pairs interleaved with two batched steps, outputs discarded,
fastest of each compared. A batched sample
times everything the live path does: predicting the second branch,
merging, snapshotting, the doubled call, the
  split and the second-call verification. Steps 3+ of every
  render of a shape take the verdict's path.
- **A slow card pays nothing.** A resident pair of 0.25 s or more is
compute-bound: one doubled call cannot win 8%
there, so the shape stays plain with no extra calls. On Kaggle T4s the
ungated trial added 19 s to the first
FLUX.2-klein-4B render, 17 s on klein-9B and 44 s on Wan2.1, all to
conclude "no gain". B200 winners measure
0.03-0.06 s per pair. Offloaded denoisers are never gated, because they
save an upload per step.
- **One slow sample cannot decide the verdict.** The old gate compared
one plain sample with the faster of two
  batched ones.
- **Compiled denoisers add nothing after warm-up.** A doubled batch is a
new input shape, so it compiles a second
graph per compiled block. A B200 audit of main found this happening,
along with graph breaks traced inside the
  router. The rules are now:
- a resident compiled denoiser stays plain (two calls upload nothing, so
batching would only add a compile);
- an offloaded compiled denoiser batches from its trial render on, so
the batch-2 graph compiles inside the same
    first-render warm-up;
- a shape judged before a later compile (the deferred profile, or
#14528's compile below the offload hooks)
    stays plain after it;
- a doubled call that still compiles a graph on a follow-up render ends
batching for the load after that render;
- a router reached while Dynamo traces passes straight through, so none
of its own code enters a graph.
  This is checked at install and at the start of every render.
- **Model offload stays declined**, as before. diffusers rebuilds the
model-offload hooks around the denoiser between
renders, which takes the router out of the forward slot after render 1.
On Wan2.1-1.3B `low_vram` a first version
  of this change batched render 1 only.
- Rebased onto main, which now has #14420's stride-safe byte compare for
Wan's `t.expand(batch)` timestep. Before
  that, every batched Wan step counted as a miss.

## What stays off, and why

- **Decided off:**
- the NVFP4 runtime (`UNSLOTH_NVFP4_DIFFUSION`), until the hosted NVFP4
repos are public;
- `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_BG_COMPILE=1`. Render 1 runs eager and render 2
compiled, so the same seed no longer repeats.
- **Lossy, or a tolerance class instead of exact:**
  - fused AdaLN (LPIPS 0.004, no speed);
  - int8 MiniMax-H3 VAE;
- explicit static-skip knobs, and the auto static skip below `max`
(change 3);
  - NVFP4 protect steps (must be measured per model);
- torchao's own inductor config (renders differ between processes, and
TF32 is process-wide).
- **No gain:**
- per-block CUDA graphs on streamed or model-offloaded denoisers
(copy-bound, extra VRAM);
  - the NVFP4 zero buffer (strictly slower);
  - NVENC export (larger files, slower than libx264 on many-core hosts);
- the on-disk conditioning cache (the in-memory prompt cache is already
on);
- cuDNN attention on eager renders 1-2: 6.4% slower than native on a
B200 at 1024x1024 (53.1 vs 49.9 ms per
    step).
- **Platform, unverifiable here:**
  - MLX engine;
  - MPS fp16 compute for Z-Image;
  - sd.cpp on MPS;
  - sd.cpp text encoder on Metal (ggml-metal can abort an LLM encoder);
  - W8A8 on the native-quant path on ROCm and the Windows torchao stub.

Studio: keep CFG-parallel on the default speed tier and run Z-Image's guidance branches on two cards (#14564)

## Summary

On two selected cards, Studio's CFG-parallel router (conditional branch
on the primary card, unconditional on a replica on the second card) had
two gaps:

1. On the default speed tier it stopped after the 2nd image. On the 3rd
image the deferred speed profile arms a whole-step CUDA graph in the
denoiser's `forward` slot. That replaced the router, and
`drop_displaced_cfg_router` then uninstalled it. Image families arm
whole-step graphs by default, so every guided image family fell back to
one card at that point.
2. It never ran Z-Image in parallel, on any tier. `ZImagePipeline`
batches a guided step into one call. Before #14551 the Z-Image CFG split
declined whenever a router was armed, so the router saw one call per
step; since #14551 the split runs under the router, but the router pairs
branches by the identity of the latent argument, and Z-Image's first
tensor argument is a timestep that is new on every call, so the two
halves still never paired and both ran on the primary card.

With this change, CFG-parallel stays on with the default tier (compile
plus CUDA graphs) and Z-Image runs its branches on two cards. On Kaggle
2xT4 that cuts seconds per step about in half.

## What it does

- `GraphedForward.install` installs the graph under a CFG-parallel
router (`router.inner`) when the router holds the slot. The primary
branch replays the graph. The replica runs the same compiled blocks
without a graph (same kernels). `uninstall` on either side gives the
slot back to the graph.
- `install_cfg_parallel` moves a resident whole-step graph that was
armed at load (non-deferred tier) under the new router. Before this, the
replica was declined as a "root forward override".
- Graph recordings use the global capture mode, which stops the replica
thread from allocating while one is in progress anywhere in the process.
So all CUDA work on the replica thread is held out of recordings:
binding the card at thread start, and each job from submit until it has
finished and dropped its inputs. A capture waits for those holds to
drain, with a 120 s timeout after which it records anyway (a failed
capture already falls back to eager).
- New `CfgParallelRouter.run_pair(primary_call, args, kwargs)`. A caller
that splits a batched guided call queues the second half on the replica
and runs the first half on the source through its normal call (hooks,
graph). The Z-Image split now uses it instead of declining under a
router. If the pair cannot run (router disabled, replica unavailable,
root hooks present, opaque inputs), both halves run on the source as
before. If the replica fails mid-step, that half is recomputed on the
source.
- Counters: `pairs_parallel` in the router stats, `parallel` in the
Z-Image split status.

The rest is unchanged: the guidance-distilled path, decline reasons
(offload, layer split, two experts, whole-module compile), automatic
placement (CFG-parallel still needs several selected cards or
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_CFG_PARALLEL=force`), and video (video families do
not arm whole-step graphs by default).

## Results

Kaggle 2xT4, fp16, 768x768, 10 steps, guidance 4. Each arm is 3 timed
renders after a warm-up. s/step is the median of per-step deltas (step 0
excluded). The A/A row is the same single-card arm run again.

Z-Image (base, `Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image`), final code:

| tier | single card s/step | A/A repeat | CFG-parallel s/step | speedup
| peak VRAM card0 / card1 (GiB) single | parallel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| eager | 2.922 (spread 0.127) | 3.046 | 1.561 (spread 0.017) | 1.87x |
12.02 / 0.00 | 12.02 / 11.84 |
| default (compile + graph) | 2.599 (spread 0.002) | 2.599 | 1.298
(spread 0.019) | 2.00x | 11.95 / 0.01 | 11.77 / 11.74 |

Z-Image-Turbo at guidance 4, same setup: eager 3.206 -> 1.623 s/step
(1.98x, A/A 3.208), default 2.595 -> 1.317 s/step (1.97x, A/A 2.597).

On the default tier, a follow-up prompt (same length bucket) added 0
dynamo graphs and 0 graph captures, and all 10 of its steps ran as
parallel pairs. The first default-tier render (compile, replica
recompile, capture) took 38 s. With the router, the primary graph
records only the conditional branch: 1 graph instead of 2.

Per family, tiny pipelines, one card (replica on the same device). `rc /
sp` = replica calls / parallel steps over 3 renders of 6 steps:

| family | eager tier, base | eager tier, head | default tier, base |
default tier, head |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FLUX.1 (true CFG) | 15 / 15 | 15 / 15 | 0 / 0 (router dropped) | 15 /
15, graph 1 capture, 21 replays |
| FLUX.2-klein base | 15 / 15 | 15 / 15 | 0 / 0 (router dropped) | 15 /
15, graph 1 capture |
| Qwen-Image (true CFG) | 15 / 15 | 15 / 15 | 0 / 0 (router dropped) |
15 / 15, graph 2 captures |
| Z-Image | 0 / 0 (batched call) | 18 / 18 pairs | 0 / 0 (router
dropped) | 18 / 18 pairs, graph 1 capture |

All head rows match single-card output bit for bit.

## Compile on one card while the other runs

Up to torch 2.13 the FX tracing flag that AOTAutograd sets during a
compile is process-wide (torch 2.14 made it thread-local). A first call
on the replica's card, or a new prompt length on either card, compiles
while the other card's thread may be inside a compiled block, and dynamo
then raises "Detected that you are using FX to symbolically trace a
dynamo-optimized function". On Kaggle 2xT4 (torch 2.11) this once sent
the default tier's graph capture to its eager fallback.

- The router now remembers the input shapes, layouts and modes each card
has run. A call new to either card waits for the other card's in-flight
work instead of overlapping it, and a prediction is launched only when
both sides have seen their inputs. Steady-state steps are unchanged; the
cost is one serialized step per new shape.
- Capture warm-ups now also wait for held replica work, not just the
recording itself.
- 4 new tests force the interleaving with a process-wide flag and fail
without the fix. Kaggle 2xT4 rerun: the default-tier arm captures (1
capture, 50 replays, 0 fallbacks), 1.97x over one card, 0 new graphs or
captures on the follow-up prompt.

## Testing

- New `tests/test_diffusion_cfg_parallel_tier.py` (8 tests, CPU): graph
under the router, primary branch through the graph, a graph armed at
load moving under a later router, capture and replica-job exclusion in
both directions, queued jobs holding captures off until their inputs are
dropped, Z-Image pairs (exact) and replica-failure fallback. All 8 fail
on the merge base and pass here.
- `tests/test_diffusion_multigpu_cuda.py`: 2 new two-card tests (graph
under the router with real capture and replay, exact vs single-card
graph, no capture on a follow-up prompt; Z-Image pair on two cards,
exact). On Kaggle 2xT4: head 4 passed, base 2 failed (exactly the 2 new
tests).
- Related suites (multigpu, cuda_graph, zimage_cfg_split, cfg_batch,
block_graph, offload graphs, layer split, step skip, speed, wiring),
base vs head: the only failing test IDs on base are the 8 new ones.
Head: 685 passed, 65 skipped (CUDA-only).

## Not verified

- A family whose speed plan arms an automatic static step skip
(Qwen-Image's default plan does) still renders on one card: the skip
holds the source module, so the replica cannot carry it and the router
steps aside with the reason 'a static step skip wraps the denoiser'. The
graph now installs beneath such a nested router instead of replacing it,
but which of the two levers to keep for those families (step skip on one
card vs both branches on two cards) is left for a follow-up measurement.
The Qwen-Image row above is the tiny pipeline, which arms no skip.

- Bit identity on real Z-Image weights. In fp16 on T4, Z-Image and
Z-Image-Turbo produce NaN latents on a single card too (fp32-encoded
prompts, finite embeddings), so output equality was proven only on tiny
models (two real T4s, and one card).
- Not run here: Wan 2.1, Lumina 2, Chroma, CogView4, Qwen-Image edit /
layered, Krea 2, Ideogram 4, FLUX.3 modular, HunyuanImage. Their
pipelines make two calls on the same latent tensor, which is the path
FLUX and Qwen-Image exercise above. LTX, LTX-2 and HiDream batch both
branches into one call, and Wan 2.2 A14B is declined as two-expert, so
this PR does not change them.
- Studio's full load and generate path on two cards. The measurements
use the router, the Z-Image split, the compile recorder and
`install_cuda_graphs` directly on a diffusers pipeline.
- Cards other than T4, and NVLink hosts.

Studio diffusion: keep fp8 single-file weights stored in fp8 where widening would offload or crowd host RAM (#14549)

## Summary

A ComfyUI fp8_scaled or plain fp8 diffusion single file loaded where no
fp8 GEMM runtime applies (GPUs below sm_89 such as Ampere and T4, fp16 /
fp32 pipelines, e5m2 codes, offloaded plans,
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_COMFY_FP8=0`) is dequantized to the compute dtype at
load. That doubles host RAM and VRAM: the Krea 2 Turbo transformer goes
from a 13.8 GB file to 23.9 GiB resident.

ComfyUI keeps such weights stored as fp8 and widens them one layer at a
time at forward time (`cast_bias_weight` /
`QuantizedTensor.dequantize`). This PR does the same through machinery
Studio already has, the torchao-free `NativeWeightOnlyLinear` (scheme
fp8). It does not add a parallel path.

- `load_comfy_quant_transformer` and `load_original_layout_transformer`
(Krea 2 / HunyuanImage plain fp8) can keep an fp8 Linear as its codes
plus a per-row fp32 scale (unit scale for plain fp8). The forward
rebuilds `(codes.float() * scale).to(dtype)`, which is the formula the
load-time dequant uses, so outputs are bit-identical.
- `NativeWeightOnlyLinear` now also accepts e5m2 codes. The compile
cache keys stored e5m2 layers apart from e4m3fn ones (e4m3fn keys are
unchanged). Under `torch.compile` it decodes the codes with integer ops
plus a bitcast, which match the cast bit for bit on all 256 codes.
Triton has no e4m3fn convert below sm_89, and this keeps the decode
fused into the compiled region on every arch.
- Offloaded renders of a pipe with stored fp8 run under `no_grad`. Under
`inference_mode`, the keep-host offload could not track the moved
buffers, so every offload copied 12 GB back to new host memory.
- A LoRA selected at load keeps the widened path. A LoRA added at
generation time on a stored load is refused, with the reload hint, the
same way as for the nvfp4 / mxfp8 runtime layers. MPS (no float8) and H3
(torchao-only residency path) keep today's behaviour.

### When it engages (default rule)

The per-layer widen slows eager steps. Compiled steps are at parity. So
storage is the default only where the widened load would be worse:

- the planner prices the single file both ways, and stores fp8 when the
widened plan would not keep the denoiser resident (offload or
streaming), or when the widened weights would leave less than 4 GB of
host RAM free; the plan is then re-priced at the stored size. An
offloaded plan is priced with the backends an offloaded load keeps
(torchao fp8 does not survive the offload hooks), so a resident fp8
runtime cannot hide the widened size. When that offloaded price is the
smaller one (the int8 / fp8 twin only an offloaded load runs), the image
load keeps those backends even if the re-made plan fits resident, as the
video path does. Linears in the transformer's `_keep_in_fp32_modules`
are never stored and are priced widened (fp32 on an fp16 load);
- video loads store under an offloaded plan, and when the stored price
is smaller the plan is re-made at it; a load that then fits resident
keeps fp8 storage. A resident video DiT follows the same host RAM rule
as an image single file: it stores fp8 when widening would leave less
than 4 GB of host RAM free;
- FNUZ float8 files (`F8_E4M3FNUZ` / `F8_E5M2FNUZ`) are priced widened
and never stored, since every loader widens them;
- `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_FP8_STORAGE=1` stores on every load that can; `0`
never stores (today's behaviour).

Planner output for the Krea 2 fp8 file on simulated cards (header-only
probe):

| free VRAM | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 24 / 28 / 32 GiB | group offload, transformer streamed every step |
fp8 stored, transformer resident (text encoders streamed once) |
| 40 / 48 GiB | transformer resident | unchanged (widened) |
| 16 GiB | streamed | streamed, half the bytes per step |

### Interaction with the single-file host RAM check (#14510)

The up-front header estimate from #14510 now prices the layers fp8
storage keeps at their stored bytes: the codes stay memory-mapped, plus
the fp32 row scales. It no longer prices them at the widened size. A
load that fits only because of storage is therefore not refused.

- The estimate and the planner's resident size use the same header rule
(`fp8_stored_by_header`, a 2-D float8 weight outside the fp32-kept
modules).
- The stored path charges the row scales it allocates through
`charge_host_ram`.
- Any layer the loader still widens is charged live, as before.
- With `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_FP8_STORAGE=0` the same file is priced widened
and refused when free RAM is below that need.

## Measurements

Krea 2 Turbo fp8_scaled single file, built from the bf16 shards (256
block Linears, per-tensor scale). B200 with the fp8 GEMM disabled
(`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_COMFY_FP8=0`) to force the no-runtime path.
1024x1024 images. s/step = (t(12 steps) - t(4 steps)) / 8, 3 prompts per
arm. Timing comes from one exclusive card with every arm run twice. The
A/A arm is head with `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_FP8_STORAGE=0`.

| arm | host RssAnon peak | transformer | VRAM peak | s/step eager |
s/step compiled |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| widened (base) | 25.6 GiB | 23.9 GiB | 36.4 GiB (compiled 33.8) |
0.165, 0.184 (A/A 0.169) | 0.114, 0.127 |
| fp8 stored | 2.3 GiB | 12.2 GiB | 24.8 GiB (compiled 22.1) | 0.240,
0.272 | 0.127, 0.128 |

With model offload, the stored load pins 13.0 GiB of transformer host
weights instead of 25.0 GiB. VRAM peak drops from 24.6 to 13.6 GiB and
RssAnon from 25.9 to 2.6 GiB. Wall time per 12-step image goes from
about 3.0 s to 3.6 s.

The compiled path has 1 graph, 1 CUDA graph capture, 0 recaptures and 0
graph breaks on prompts 2+, the same as base.

## Parity

- Eager, resident: bit-identical to the widened load on every image, for
both the fp8_scaled and the plain fp8 file.
- Model offload: bit-identical on every image.
- Compiled: bit-identical in 7 of 9 fresh compiles. The other 2 differ
by LPIPS at most 0.0005 (PSNR at least 54 dB). Fresh compiles of the
widened model on main are not bit-reproducible either (1 of 6 differed).

## Tests

New CPU tests fail on main and pass here:
- stored dtype and bytes;
- layer forward parity against the dequant formula (bf16 / fp16 / fp32,
e4m3fn / e5m2, per-tensor / per-row);
- all 256 codes for the integer decode, plus a compiled `fullgraph` with
no graph break;
- plain fp8 Krea 2 storage;
- the default rule, the kill switch, LoRA refusal, offload grad mode,
video backends and plan sizing;
- the host RAM check: with free RAM between the stored and the widened
need, a plain fp8 or fp8_scaled file loads when stored and is refused
with `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_FP8_STORAGE=0`. The same holds for a resident
ComfyUI fp8 video DiT.

Results on the related suites (41 files: every planner / loader / host
RAM test file plus comfy quant / block, native quant, Krea 2, LoRA,
offload, memory, CUDA graph, backend), current main vs this branch: 5926
passed vs 5949 passed, nothing fails on either side.

## Not covered

- No real sm_80 / sm_75 GPU or ROCm card was run. The no-runtime path
was forced on a B200, and the Triton fp8 limit below sm_89 is handled by
the integer decode, but it was not executed on that hardware.
- The resident-on-24-32 GiB result is planner output; it was not
measured on a real card of that size.
- FLUX-style plain fp8 files that go through diffusers
`from_single_file` are still widened by diffusers.
- MPS keeps the widened path.

fix(dotfiles): report a saved enrollment under a symlinked parent instead of failing capture (#14871)

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/986
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A single saved dotfile enrollment that sits under a symlinked parent no
longer stops automatic capture for every other tracked path.

## Problem

`mise dot status` could report "Automatic capture has failed N times in
a row" while all entries showed as tracked. Each capture re-read the
saved enrollment manifest through `Manifest::tracking()`, which returns
an error for the first entry whose path now runs through a symlink, for
example `~/.claude/skills/entire-trails/SKILL.md` enrolled back when
`entire-trails` was a real directory and later replaced by a link to
`~/.agents/skills/entire-trails`:

```
cannot track ~/.claude/skills/entire-trails/SKILL.md through symlinked parent ~/.claude/skills/entire-trails; explicitly track the link itself and its real target instead
```

Saved enrollments are kept until untracked, so the one stale entry
failed every capture, and nothing was saved.

## Fix

Live capture now reads the manifest with `Manifest::tracking_lenient()`.
An entry under a symlinked parent is left out of the capture set and
recorded in `invalid` with the same message, so it shows up as omitted
in the checkpoint coverage and still blocks publishing until it is
untracked. Replay and sync keep the strict `tracking()`.

I reproduced this from reading the code and your report rather than from
a failing machine; the new assertions in
`enrollment_rejects_alias_parents_but_allows_links_and_real_targets`
cover the lenient read.

fix(bootstrap): match only an exact bootstrap task (#14858)

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/979
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise bootstrap` no longer fails when the config has a namespaced task
such as `system:bootstrap` but no task named `bootstrap`.

Before, with this config:

```toml
[tasks."system:bootstrap"]
run = "echo hi"
```

`mise bootstrap` logged ``running `bootstrap` task`` and then failed
with `no task bootstrap found`. The check used a fuzzy task match that
also matches namespaced tasks ending in `:bootstrap`, while the run step
requests the exact name. Now the phase runs only for a task named
exactly `bootstrap` (or aliased to it); otherwise it is skipped and
bootstrap continues to the final hook.

Fixes #14836

I did not change the special task's name or add namespaced lifecycle
tasks, which the issue also suggests.

fix(packslip): stay quiet about an installed version past the release-age cutoff (#14835)

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/970
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

With `minimum_release_age` set, installing a version newer than the
cutoff made every later `mise outdated` and `mise up` warn about
skipping it, even though it was already installed and there was nothing
to upgrade:

```
$ mise outdated
mise WARN  packslip:github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk: skipping 0.81.0: verified release time is after the allowed cutoff
mise All tools are up to date
```

Now mise stays quiet when the version being skipped for the release-age
cutoff is already installed. The version is still skipped, and other
skip reasons (withdrawn release, no artifact for the host) still warn.

Only the packslip backend is changed. No test added: the path needs a
signed manifest and network. Verified with `cargo clippy --lib -- -D
warnings`.

Fixes discussion #14834.

> **Overview**
> When **`minimum_release_age`** excludes a packslip release because its
verified time is past the cutoff, **`mise outdated`** / **`mise up`** no
longer emit **`packslip:… skipping …`** warnings if that version is
**already installed**.

but for an installed version it runs host artifact and requirement
checks first so a cutoff-only skip is distinguishable from other
failures. **`admits`** suppresses the skip warning when the reason is
**`AFTER_CUTOFF`** and the version is installed; other skip reasons
still warn.

**`is_installed_version`** helper.

fix(plugins): grant channel plugin commands their native capabilities (#180968)

Plugin commands typed in Slack, Discord and other channels never received
the command-scoped native subagents (#180173) or scheduled turns
(#180282), although the docs describe authorized channel senders as
eligible. Channel ingress already binds the verified sender's operator
authority, but the native gate also required a Gateway chat.send run id
and user-turn recorder, which channel dispatch never supplies.

For channel ingress only, the host now mints that run id and recorder,
and only for the operator authority host ingress bound to the message's
verified principal. The existing gate is unchanged: command authorization,
the declared capability, the requester's native tool policy, admission
and per-call authority rechecks still decide. Unlinked, unverified,
demoted or unauthorized senders keep seeing no capability.

The committed input uses the message's route-scoped source turn id, so a
continuing agent turn and restart recovery join it, and it stores the
same redacted form the delivered-command transcript mirror records. That
mirror now records only the reply once a native command committed the
input.

feat(vercel): pick the onboarding default from catalog recommendations (#180905)

## What Problem This Solves

Vercel AI Gateway onboarding always set `vercel-ai-gateway/anthropic/claude-opus-4.6` as the default model, a constant that has not changed since the first onboarding wizard. A Vercel Token Pass key cannot call that model, so the first chat after setup failed with HTTP 403. Changing the default also needed an OpenClaw release.

## Fix

Maintainer decision (Ayaan): the onboarding default comes from the hosted catalog's recommended models, filtered to the models the user's key lists.

- **Catalog:** the Vercel manifest maps the provider to models.dev (`vercel`), like Kilo. The publisher now creates a mapped provider entry from its raw manifest declaration when it declares no static rows, so Vercel publishes rows and `recommendedModels` without a static seed row. Vercel's public `/v1/models` is added to the inventories that retire unlisted rows.
- **Onboarding:** a shared SDK helper, `resolveRecommendedStarterModel`, refreshes the hosted catalog, reads the provider's stored recommendations, and returns the first one in the key's own model list. If none match, onboarding sets no default instead of a model the key cannot use.
- **Recommendations after a release:** stored recommendations are read even when the catalog is older than the build. `readRemoteModelCatalogUpdate` keeps its newer-than-build rule for rows and prices.
- The hard-coded default and alias-only `onboard.ts` are removed.

## User Impact

- A Token Pass key gets `vercel-ai-gateway/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` (the highest-ranked recommended model it can use). A regular key gets the top recommendation, currently `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5`.
- Onboarding no longer adds an Opus 4.6 allowlist entry.
- Changing the recommended order or adding models needs a catalog publish, not a release.

## Evidence

- Local publisher run: `vercel-ai-gateway` published with 249 models.dev rows and a `recommendedModels` list; inventory retirement ran with 0 retired.
- Live run with a real Token Pass key on built OpenClaw, catalog served from a localhost mirror of that publish, key added with `models auth paste-api-key` and then `openclaw onboard --non-interactive --auth-choice ai-gateway-api-key`:
  - Before (`main`): primary `vercel-ai-gateway/anthropic/claude-opus-4.6`, allowlist `[anthropic/claude-opus-4.6]`.
  - After: primary `vercel-ai-gateway/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, allowlist only that model. `openclaw models list` adds no Vercel rows; `--provider vercel-ai-gateway --all --refresh` lists the key's 6 models. `openclaw agent --local` replied on the new default.
  - The same run with a build newer than the catalog first set no default; the stored-recommendation reader fixed it.
- Regression tests:
  - publisher hydrates a mapped provider with no static rows (fails on `main`: `expected {} to deeply equal { gateway: … }`);
  - stored recommendations are read when the catalog is older than the build, and not when refresh is disabled;
  - the starter helper picks the first recommendation the key serves and returns nothing when none match.
- Focused suites: 63 tests in `extensions/vercel-ai-gateway/`, the SDK helper, `src/model-catalog/remote-overlay.test.ts` and `test/scripts/publish-model-catalog.test.ts`.
- Upgrade from released `openclaw@2026.10.6` with a real Token Pass key: on 2026.10.6, `models auth paste-api-key`, non-interactive onboarding (writes the old Opus 4.6 default and alias), then `openclaw models set vercel-ai-gateway/zai/glm-5.3` and a successful turn. Then the PR build ran `openclaw doctor --fix` (the update's state migration), `models auth list`, `models list --provider vercel-ai-gateway --refresh` and `openclaw agent --local`:
  - `agents`, `auth` and `models` config sections are byte-identical before and after;
  - profile `vercel-ai-gateway:manual` still loads as `api_key` with no cooldown;
  - primary stays `vercel-ai-gateway/zai/glm-5.3`; the old Opus 4.6 allowlist entry and alias are kept, not rewritten;
  - the turn replied `upgrade ok` on `zai/glm-5.3`.
  The change only runs during new onboarding, writes no stored rows or schema, and does not migrate existing defaults.
- Two `publish-model-catalog-v2` rename-failure tests fail locally on unmodified `main` as well; left to hosted CI.

feat(plugins): keep requester command schedules across Gateway restarts (#180844)

* feat(plugins): keep requester command schedules across Gateway restarts

Requester-admitted scheduled command turns (#180282) ended when the Gateway
restarted. Accepted schedules now survive a restart, within their original
bounds and under the same per-occurrence authority checks.

- A schedule accepted from a plugin whose loaded source has a captured
  digest records a private restart binding in job state: the serving
  Gateway process and plugin instance, plus that source digest. The released
  `pluginCommand` envelope and payload kind are unchanged; no table, column or
  schema version is added.
- After a restart, the scheduler's launch claim re-arms the schedule onto the
  newly loaded instance only if it runs the same code: the same plugin ID,
  source, root and version, the exact captured source digest, and the target
  command still registered. The re-arm, the budget check, the receipt and the
  charge share one state transaction. The Gateway thread supplies the loaded
  instances.
- The deadline, maxRuns and spent attempts carry over. Expired, exhausted,
  disabled, removed and completed schedules are never re-armed. Without a
  matching instance (disabled, uninstalled or changed plugin) the claim
  retires the schedule before running plugin code or spending an attempt.
- Each occurrence still restores the original requester and rechecks the
  operator, parent session, plugin instance and code, command and tool
  ceiling; a demoted or removed requester is refused before the command runs.
- In-process plugin reloads still retire schedules bound to the replaced
  instance. Core-bundled plugins have no captured digest and keep
  restart-scoped schedules.
- The active cap also counts unexpired restartable schedules of the same
  code left by an earlier process.
- `command-scheduled-turns-restart-v1` advertises continuity, and `schedule()`
  returns `survivesRestart` for each accepted schedule.
- Released #180282 readers decode the unchanged envelope, ignore the binding
  and end the schedule at its next occurrence; that ended schedule stays
  ended after upgrading again.

fix(vercel): keep Token Pass keys usable after model-scope errors (#173750)

## What Problem This Solves

A Vercel Token Pass API key works only with Token Pass models. When OpenClaw sends that key to another model, Vercel returns HTTP 403 `no_providers_available`. OpenClaw treated that 403 as an auth failure: the user saw "Couldn't sign in", and the whole key went into an auth cooldown, so the next request to a Token Pass model also failed. Credit exhaustion had the same 403 shape and was also treated as auth.

## Fix

The Vercel plugin classifies the two documented Token Pass 403 messages:

- credit used up → `billing`
- key scoped to Token Pass models → `model_not_found`, a model-scoped cooldown

The generic classifier also lets the provider read the bounded body details, because the native Anthropic transport keeps the response text outside its generic error message. Other 403s keep the current policy, and explicit permanent-auth codes keep precedence.

## User Impact

A request to a model outside the pass now fails only for that model. The same key keeps working for Token Pass models. Credit exhaustion uses billing failover instead of asking the user to sign in again. No config or credential storage changes.

## Evidence

- Error contract: [Vercel Token Pass errors](https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/token-pass/models-and-routing#errors). A live 403 from a Token Pass key to `anthropic/claude-opus-4.6` returned the documented scope message.
- Live run with a real Token Pass key, built OpenClaw, `openclaw agent --local`:
  - Before: `anthropic/claude-opus-4.6` → `failoverReason=auth`, "Couldn't sign in". Next turn on `zai/glm-5.3` → `Provider vercel-ai-gateway has auth issue (skipping all models)`. Profile cooldown reason `auth`.
  - After: `anthropic/claude-opus-4.6` → `failoverReason=model_not_found`. Next turn on `zai/glm-5.3` → replied `ok`.
- Regression tests cover both messages through the native body path and the direct message path, ambiguous 403s that stay `auth`, and permanent-auth precedence. Focused suites: 218 tests passed in `src/agents/failover/` and `extensions/vercel-ai-gateway/`.
- Not proven live: credit exhaustion (cannot be triggered on demand). It is covered by the regression test against the documented message.

Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi <hi@obviy.us>

* fix(config): advance last-known-good after accepted config writes

An accepted write that only removes verbose formatting (BOM, deep

so the new promotion admission kept rejecting it and froze recovery

The writer now advances the health baseline right after any write the
config owner accepted, so the next startup promotes the accepted config
whether the raw-byte reduction came from formatting normalization or an
explicitly permitted size drop. Stub-shaped results (missing meta,
missing gateway mode, update-channel-only root) keep the older baseline,
and external truncations never go through the writer, so they stay

io.write-safety.ts stays within the line-cap ratchet after the rebase.

* fix(config): restore the health baseline when a committed write rolls back

A config write that grows the file beyond twice its size and then fails
runtime activation rolls the file back to the original bytes, but the
accepted-write baseline advance had already persisted the grown candidate
as last-known-good. The next startup then flags the valid restored config
as a size-drop anomaly and the promotion guard refuses it, so the
recovery backup stays frozen at an older config while every start warns
about a truncation that never happened.

The writer now publishes the pre-write baseline alongside the advance and
restoreEffects compensates it after a successful rollback, keeping newer
observations (a baseline or anomaly signature recorded after the advance)
untouched.

Fixes #152509

* test(config): add pre-upgrade health-state compatibility proof

The health-state rows persisted by the previous build keep working after
this change: the config_health_entries schema, the fingerprint JSON shape,
and the permissive read contract are all unchanged. A regression test
seeds the row exactly as the pre-change build wrote it, then drives the
new promotion guard, the accepted-write baseline advance, and the
rolled-back-write restore against that pre-upgrade row.

Also fixes the check-test-types failure (TS2741) by supplying the error
logger required by the rolled-back-write test's config IO deps.

* fix(config): keep baseline persistence off the Gateway thread and safe from intervening reads

Accepted-write baseline advancement and rollback compensation ran the
synchronous health-store reader and writer, executing SQLite reads and
write transactions on the Gateway event loop during ordinary live
config writes, and the compensation read the prior baseline only after
the candidate file was published, so an observed read landing between
the publication and the baseline advance could record the grown
candidate as healthy and freeze promotion of a validly restored
config as a size drop.

The baseline capture, advancement and restore now run on the
worker-backed config health owner, and the writer captures the
pre-publication baseline so the conditional compensation always
retains the pre-write state.

* fix(config): stop concurrent observation from freezing the recovery backup

The three write-owned health transitions (baseline capture, accepted-write
advance, rollback restore) ran on the observer's health-state scope, so an
ordinary observed read landing while they awaited the worker superseded that
scope: the read returned null and the conditional update silently no-op'd.
For an accepted formatting normalization or a permitted size reduction below
half the old baseline, the competing observation recorded a size-drop anomaly
without advancing the baseline, so the next startup promotion kept refusing
the valid edited config and openclaw.json.last-good stayed stale.

Each transition now settles through a shared bounded retry that captures a
fresh scope, re-reads the persisted snapshot and re-applies its guard, so
supersession can neither drop the transition's read nor win a silent
conditional write. Newer valid baselines are still preserved and the
state-database ownership checks are unchanged.

read" interleaves a synchronous observed read into the accepted write's

* fix(config): retain input anomalies after metadata stamping

fix(vercel): list models with the configured API key (#180838)

## What Problem This Solves

The Vercel AI Gateway plugin fetched `/v1/models` without the user's API key. Vercel scopes that list per key, so OpenClaw showed the public list (486 models) even when the key can use only a few. A Vercel Token Pass key can call only Token Pass models, so most models in the picker failed with HTTP 403.

## Fix

The Vercel catalog now resolves the provider credential and sends it on the model-list request, using the existing live catalog helper (same pattern as Hugging Face). The trusted-proxy fetch guard, the strict discovery mode and the static catalog for unauthenticated reads stay as they are. The provider docs gain a short Token Pass note.

## User Impact

`openclaw models list --provider vercel-ai-gateway` and the model picker show the models the configured key can use. New Vercel models still appear without an OpenClaw release, and model details still come from Vercel's live rows.

## Evidence

- Vercel API, Token Pass key: `/v1/models` returns 6 models (`deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `moonshotai/kimi-k3`, `zai/glm-5.3` and their `-fast` variants). Without a key it returns 486.
- Live run with a real Token Pass key on built OpenClaw: `openclaw models list --provider vercel-ai-gateway --all --refresh` lists exactly those 6 models, with Vercel status `ready`. `openclaw agent --local` turns on `zai/glm-5.3` and `moonshotai/kimi-k3` replied as expected.
- Regression test: the catalog run sends `Authorization: Bearer <key>` on the model-list request. It fails on `main` (`expected null to be 'Bearer scoped-key'`) and passes with the fix. All 12 Vercel plugin tests pass.
- Related: #173750 keeps the key usable after a 403 for a model outside the pass.
- Follow-up, not in this PR: onboarding still sets `anthropic/claude-opus-4.6` as the default, which a Token Pass key cannot use.

fix: view_image refuses host images that read can open (#180846)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `view_image` (and `pdf` and media references for generation tools) refuses a local file with "Local media path is not under an allowed directory" even though `read` can open the same file, when the tool policy allows host reads (`tools.fs.workspaceOnly: false`).

## User Impact

User impact: with host file access enabled, the agent can look at a screenshot or image it can already `read`, for example one saved by a browser tool outside the workspace. Workspace-only and sandboxed runs are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Media tools resolve local files against a fixed list of OpenClaw media folders plus the workspace, regardless of the file policy. `read` follows the policy: with `workspaceOnly: false` it opens any host path. The two tools disagreed about the same file.

When the policy explicitly sets `workspaceOnly: false` and the run is not sandboxed, the referenced file's own folder is added to the allowed roots, so the existing containment, symlink and hardlink checks still apply to that folder. Runs without a policy, workspace-only runs and sandboxed runs keep the current roots.

## Evidence

- Production: a scheduled run's `view_image` on a browser screenshot outside the OpenClaw folders failed with the refusal, while `read` on images in the same tree worked in chat on the same install.
- New regression in `media-tool-shared.test.ts`, "admits host files read may open": a real file outside the media folders passes the media access check with `workspaceOnly: false`, and is still refused for workspace-only and no-policy callers. The host-reads case fails on the base with the refusal above.
- Production-path proof (real tool factory, real filesystem, fs.open spied on the image path; temporary harness not committed). Path: `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` → `fsPolicy` (`agent-tools.ts`) → `createOpenClawTools` → `view_image` → `resolveMediaToolReferenceAccess` → `loadWebMedia` → `openLocalMediaFile`. Retained tools were checked on both run-retirement paths: the agent run execution scope and the embedded runner's run abort signal.

fix(scripts): PR wrapper leaks materialized trust-anchor dirs in TMPDIR on failures and interrupts (#180848)

* fix(scripts): retire materialized PR anchors on every exit path

Materialized wrappers were retired only after fully clean supervised exits,
leaking code and dependency links on failures, signals, bootstrap exits,
unsupervised commands, and failed execs.

Keep creator ownership across the Bash and supervisor exec chain. Share
FD/path/PID identity checks, retire drained operations independently of PR
lock decisions, and restore cleanup after Bash 3.2 failed execs. Retain code
for undrained operations and sweep at most four old owned anchors at startup
using creator PIDs in new names.

PID reuse conservatively delays sweeping. Legacy names have no liveness
record and may be reclaimed after 24 hours even during a long operation.
Drained cleanup accepts the same fd-closing escapee residual as clean exits;
missing runtime or ownership evidence remains retain-only.

Cover lifecycle exits, crash-retained recovery fixtures, dependency pinning,
and bounded stale sweeping without changing lock recovery semantics.

* docs(scripts): name the stale-anchor sweep residual

A dead creator PID is the sweep's only evidence that an operation ended. Descendants that outlive a crashed or undrained supervisor by more than 24 hours can lose their anchor; their PR lock stays retained. Also replace the busy loop in the forwarded-SIGTERM supervisor test with sleep.

The capacity blocker in the scheduled-command harness enqueued with maxConcurrent 1,
but every swarm reservation re-applies the configured lane limit (default 32), so the
child's own reservation widened the lane and it launched immediately. Whether it was
still queued when the test acted depended on module-load timing: the first test in a
file was slow enough, later tests were not, so a demotion in a second test landed after
the child had already passed admission.

Pin the configured swarm limit to one in a shared hold helper, assert the child holds a
reservation without launching before acting, and split the queued-child authorization
cases back into separate tests.

feat(cron): pause automations whose parent conversation is gone (#178965)

A job linked to the exact conversation that created it (sourceConversation or
a stored operator source) is now paused by its occurrence admission when that
conversation was removed or archived, or its bound worktree no longer exists.
Nothing runs for that occurrence: no trigger script, payload or session turn.
It is skipped with a notice that names the conversation and the re-enable
command, and the job is disabled so it sends that notice once. It resumes only
when re-enabled, and the next occurrence checks the parent again.

A reset (/new) parent keeps the automation running: that occurrence is built
as an unbound parent and takes the legacy decisions, with nothing carried into
the new incarnation. Command jobs never pause: they still consume the
admitted occurrence and run as before. Jobs without an exact parent link are
unaffected, and a failed read never pauses.

fix(cron): owners cannot change their automation's tools from chat (#180619)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a channel owner cannot change the tools of their own automation from chat. The update fails with "Cannot authorize toolsAllow … Recreate the automation from a fresh authenticated owner turn to capture app authority", and the agent then tells the user to recreate the job or move to the Control UI.

## User Impact

User impact: owners on the native runtime can repair or adjust their own automation's tool list from the conversation that owns it. Jobs that hold app runtime authority (Codex apps) still refuse an edit that would drop it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The owner-edit guard on `cron.update` refused any `toolsAllow` edit from an admin-management turn without a fresh creator-authority capture. Only runtimes with app authority (Codex) can produce that capture, so on the native runtime the exact owner was always refused, while creating the same job from the same conversation worked. The guard exists to stop an edit from silently dropping a job's app authority; a job without app authority has nothing to drop.

The guard now refuses a capture-less owner edit only when the stored job holds runtime authority. The job keeps its account tool policy, so the new list is still capped by the owner's account at run time. Owner, session, account and borrowed-capture checks are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Production: on 2026.10.5 an owner's chat repair of two disabled automations and of a scheduled stock check was refused with this error; the agent then deleted one job and sent the owner to the Control UI.
- New regression in `cron.scheduled-policy-adoption.integration.test.ts`, "lets the owner edit tools on a job without app authority from a native turn": a real `automations` tool call through gateway `cron.update` as the exact owner with no app-authority resolver updates `toolsAllow` and keeps the account policy. It fails on the base with the refusal above.
- The existing "no capture" case (owner, job holding app authority, no capture) still refuses and leaves the store unchanged; other-session, other-account and borrowed-capture cases are unchanged.
- The ownership matrix now expects a manager's own-session cap edit to succeed for jobs without app authority.
- Local: `cron.scheduled-policy-adoption.integration`, `cron.ownership-matrix` and `cron-tool.management` tests pass; oxfmt and oxlint are clean on changed files.

fix: show repository updates instead of waiting during worktree creation (#178526)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a new worktree session shows the generic "Waiting for turn to start…" while the Gateway updates the repository before checkout, including after the chat is reopened during that wait.

## User Impact

Users see **"Updating repository…"** while the default branch is fetched, then the existing checkout, setup and model progress. Pinned retries and explicit base refs resolve locally and go straight to "Creating worktree…". No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The worktree service already reports `checkout` and `setup` progress. It now reports `base` immediately before the default-branch fetch, and `checkout` after the base resolves.
- Session creation maps `base` to the new `preparing_worktree_base` startup phase; the Control UI labels it "Updating repository…".
- Chat history replay uses the existing session-progress predicate, so an accepted run that has not started yet replays its status after a reload.
- Protocol: one additive startup-phase value. Native apps map unknown phases to no label, so released clients ignore it.

## Evidence

- Real browser against a real Gateway and local bare origin, with the fetch held: base showed "Waiting for turn to start…"; this change showed "Updating repository…", kept it across a chat reload, and checked out the newly published default-branch commit after release. Stop cleared the status with no late checkout.
- `base-ref.test.ts`: against a real remote, the default base reports `base` before `fetch` and ends with `checkout`; an explicit `HEAD` ref reports only `checkout`. Fails on the earlier unconditional emit.
- `chat-abort.history-budget.test.ts`: accepted preparation replays before execution and clears on cancellation.
- `chat-gateway.model-wait.test.ts`: label renders, then yields to model-wait states.

### Before

![Before: generic waiting text during the real repository fetch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7ad7fbf2-9d66-48fb-9b2b-658c6f17405f)

### After

![After: Updating repository status during the real repository fetch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b3d54ae8-dea6-4694-a9a4-2ca201a75e24)

* refactor(cron): admit each scheduled occurrence once

executeJobCore now admits every occurrence once, after the cheap skips and
before trigger evaluation or any payload branch: it reads the parent row,
runs the requester's owner check and holds the parent generation until the
occurrence settles. Trigger, script, isolated, session (including `main`)
and command executors take the admitted occurrence as a required field, and
each admitted run, including scheduled plugin-command turns, mints its
context from it instead of reading the parent again.
prepareCronRunAdmission refuses a run without one. Hook and join-intro
turns admit with trigger "event".

`main` jobs now get an in-session context on the agent's main session, like
session:<key>.

No consumer reads the context, so behavior is unchanged. A harness without
an admitter gets fail contexts.

* fix(cron): admit event occurrences outside the isolated-agent facade

Hook and join-intro turns reached admitScheduledOccurrence through the isolated-agent facade, so suites that isolate that facade lost the export and hook runs failed before the agent runner. admitEventOccurrence now lazy-loads admission on its own, and the facade keeps only the runner.

feat(cron): add the scheduled-run execution context (no behavior change) (#178933)

* feat(cron): add pure scheduled execution context builder

buildScheduledExecutionContext derives one occurrence's principal, placement,
authority, tool policy, resource scopes and inference account from stored job
fields plus caller-read facts (parent row, requester check). No consumer reads
it yet; admission minting follows in openclaw-0d5.2.

Jobs with sourceConversation or operatorSource become children of that exact
parent and pause when it is removed, archived or reset, or its worktree is
gone. Key-only parent links stay on their legacy decisions. A parent-linked
job without a recorded requester gets no owner authority.

The admission-source rule moves unchanged into src/cron/admission-source.ts
so the timer and the builder share one owner.

* feat(cron): mint the scheduled execution context at run admission

Each prompt-executor attempt reads the parent session row (for jobs with an
exact parent link), rechecks the requester, builds the context and binds it to
the admitted run. A parent-linked context holds the parent's session generation
so assertCurrent fails once the parent is reset or removed; the lease is
released when the admission closes. Nothing reads the context yet, and minting
errors become a fail result instead of failing the run.

The prompt executor's scheduled tool policy setup moves into the same module so
the executor stays under its line cap.

* test(cron): add execution context replay and stored-shape fixtures

execution-context-projection reproduces what the existing scheduled-run code
decides for a stored job and labels where the context differs (equal,
gain-intended, gain-unexpected, loss, retarget, pause). Doctor will reuse it.

scripts/dev/cron-context-replay.mts is a development script: it copies a
Gateway's state and agent session databases with SQLite's online backup into a
private temp directory, replays every stored job against the copies, prints the
labels and can emit anonymized job shapes. The fixture test pins the builder and
projection results for those shapes.

* fix(cron): align the context's parent read with principal resolution

Read the parent row with the same precedence the builder uses (operator source
first, then the creating conversation). Expose the minted context through the
admission owner until a consumer reads it, use typed rank lookups, keep real
exports in test mocks, and register the replay script as a Knip script entry.

* fix(cron): keep replay fixtures faithful to runtime admission

Replay now reads the parent row with the admission's parent precedence
(operator source first) and resolves each job's agent through the cron
owner resolver, reporting jobs with no resolvable owner instead of
replaying them as main. Fixture anonymization keeps operator sources,
channel requesters, lifecycle-revision changes and worktree existence,
so emitted fixtures replay to the same outcome as the recorded jobs.

Drops two tests that restated existing assertions and comments that
named future work.

* fix(cron): release the minted context when admission preparation throws

The parent-generation lease taken while minting was released only by a closed admission or the missing-fence path. Any other preparation error left it held. The prompt executor now releases it whenever preparation throws, and admission keeps releasing it on close.

* fix(cron): sanitize every replay fixture payload and keep tool-cap inputs

Script and system-event payloads were exported unchanged, so --emit-fixtures could write private script bodies into anonymized fixtures. Trigger and runtime-authority markers were dropped, letting resolveCronRunToolsAllow widen a restricted automatic cap in the fixture.

* fix(cron): hold the observed parent generation for revisionless links

A parent link stored without a lifecycle revision leased generation null, which the generation owner rejects against the row's revision, so a valid parent-linked occurrence minted a fail result. Admission now leases the revision of the parent row the builder validated. Also replaces the anonymizer's switch with returns that satisfy consistent-return.

feat(plugins): let requester commands schedule bounded follow-up turns (#180282)

* feat(plugins): let requester commands schedule bounded follow-up turns

Authenticated requester commands that opt into `scheduledTurns` can schedule
bounded follow-up turns of the same command. Each occurrence restores the
original requester under current policy, rechecks the exact parent session and
loaded plugin instance, refuses direct model calls, and must route model work
through admitted native subagents.

- Bounds: deadline at most 7 days, maxRuns 1-100, 4 schedules per invocation
  and 8 active schedules per loaded plugin instance and parent session. Only
  enabled schedules of the same instance in the current Gateway process count.
- Retirement: the scheduler disables the job and clears its next run in the
  same transaction that launches the final allowed attempt or finds it
  expired, exhausted, invalid or from a previous process. A replaced plugin
  instance retires the schedule on its first refusal.
- v1 scope: schedules end when the Gateway restarts or the plugin reloads;
  plugins re-enroll from a later requester command.
- Rows persist under a dedicated `pluginCommand` payload kind so hosts without
  this feature quarantine them instead of running a model prompt.
- `command-scheduled-turns-v1` advertises support.
- The session-event route predicates move to `timer-session-route.ts` so a
  scheduled occurrence can never prepare parent notices or prompt the model.

* refactor(plugins): break scheduled command import cycles

Move the stored schedule contract and its reserved message into
`src/cron/plugin-command-schedule.types.ts`, and the native subagent request
source into `src/agents/plugin-native-subagent.types.ts`, so cron types,
creation and storage, and the native subagent runtime and scheduled turns no
longer import each other. No behavior change.

* test(plugins): prove queued scheduled children re-admit their requester

A scheduled occurrence queues a native child, settles, and the child launches
later through the real Gateway instance runtime. While the requester stays
authorized the child passes the agent turn's admission revalidation; after the
requester is demoted (committed and published as `users.setRole` does), the
next queued child is refused at that admission, before any model runner.

* test(plugins): close the agent turn runtime without awaiting a void result

* fix(plugins): keep the native child list helper in command runtimes

The command runtime projected `subagents` to spawn and collect so scheduling
stays outside that object, which dropped the optional `list` helper added by
#180274 for every command. Forward `list` when the native runtime provides
it, and pin the exact helper set through a real command invocation.

perf(control-ui): render cached full-UUID chat routes before sessions.resolve, off the hello window (#179701)

On a warm reload of a full-UUID chat link for a session outside the cached sidebar roster (Peter's sessions on Team), the transcript waited for sessions.resolve before the pane mounted. An earlier attempt (#177153) rendered the cached transcript first but its single mount landed on the WebSocket connect response and was reverted (#177760).

Admit the route from the account/host-scoped prewarmed snapshot only for an exact full-UUID + agent match (scope key and connection revision re-checked after the read), schedule the cached pane mount after the connect request is sent and split it so no task lands in the hello window, and keep sessions.resolve authoritative (deleted, moved or mismatched sessions are replaced). Composer sends and restored queued sends are held until the route is confirmed; other mutations stay server-authorized by session key, ID or view ticket and fail safely on a deleted/moved session (see "Write hold scope" in the PR). Saved agent selection is restored after roster hydration so a fresh shell reopening the canonical global session lands on the selected agent (regression test; the old head reproduced the failure, 0/30 on the final head and base).

Evidence (AWS c7a.4xlarge, 11 interleaved triplets): transcript paint 1,112 -> 860 ms (11/11), final rows 1,279 -> 1,119 ms, LoAF 240 -> 208 ms, FCP flat. Accepted tradeoff: hello handling +15.6 ms paired, which does not cascade (final rows improve in the same runs). Live rule: revert if Team's live final rows or hello regress materially.

Runtime +163 LOC; startup gzip 325,800 -> 325,703 B. 179 unit and 34 focused e2e tests; full UI 842 passed (QA-lab failure reproduces on base; two intermittent color assertions - a sidebar hover reference captured mid-transition and a theme-change color read - did not differ meaningfully between head and base in paired replays and passed in CI); exact-head CI green.

fix(auth): rate-limited profiles stay locked out for hours after repeated 429s (#180280)

* fix(auth): time rate-limit cooldowns only from the provider

Remove the escalating rate_limit failure counter (30s doubling to 24h, from
how long to wait, and exactly that long; without timing it stays available
and the turn still fails over.

- Record lastRateLimitAt instead of failureCounts.rate_limit; session
  recovery to an earlier auth.order profile keys on it.
- Release legacy rate-limit cooldowns and counters on read.
- Pass provider timing from every rate-limit failure writer.
- Prefer an explicit Retry-After over exhausted-bucket resets; read
  Anthropic reset headers and Google RetryInfo.
- Same-model rate-limit retries wait exactly the provider's time.
- Stop WHAM probes and the fallback probe heuristic from adding local delay.

* fix(auth): let explicit retry text outrank bucket resets; read full RetryInfo

An exhausted-bucket reset (x-ratelimit-reset-*, anthropic-ratelimit-*-reset)
is the full-refill time and must apply only when the provider gave no
explicit retry time. Retry prose such as OpenAI's "Please try again in 6s"
previously lost to that reset (max), so the usual TPM 429 cooled for the
whole refill.

- Keep explicit and reset header timing apart (parseRetryAfter*Timing).
- Decide on the raw thrown error before projection adds its own
  Retry-After suffix; drop the reset when prose timing is present.
- Read google.rpc.RetryInfo in any key order from the untruncated body
  (Gemini puts it after ~1KB of QuotaFailure details), with a fixed number
  of getter-free reads; accept Gemini's "Please retry in 32s" prose.

* fix(auth): suppress a bucket reset only for retry text that parses

hasExplicitRetryText accepted any digit-leading value, so "try again in 6
attempts" dropped the exhausted-bucket reset even though the failover parser
rejects that unit, leaving no timing at all. Share one retry-text duration
grammar (parseRetryAfterTextSeconds) between the reset check and the
failover path.
