fix(agents): stop model-catalog worker from discarding incrementally-loaded plugins on scope growth (#162226)

* fix(agents): stop model-catalog worker discarding incrementally-loaded plugins on scope growth

The prepared-model-catalog worker's plugin registry reuse check required an
exact match between the previously-loaded plugin-id set and each new
request's set. Any request needing a plugin beyond what was already loaded
(e.g. runtime provider discovery proving a new provider is needed) was
treated as a full cache miss, discarding and rebuilding the entire registry
-- including every other already-loaded plugin that hadn't changed.

loadOpenClawPluginsCore already has a correct per-plugin incremental-reuse
mechanism via a previousRegistry option; it was simply never threaded
through for this call path. Fix: thread it through unconditionally for
model-catalog requests, and remove the unsafe direct-return fast path that
could otherwise skip the loader's own signature validation entirely.

Also: resolveWorkerGenerationBasePluginIds carries previously-proven
scope-expansion plugin ids forward so a later fingerprint-miss rebuild
doesn't regress below what discovery already established; the worker now
threads its previous generation through on a fingerprint miss so the
reuse mechanism above actually has something to reuse against.

Also: markPreparedModelRuntimeSnapshotsStale/refreshPreparedModelRuntimeSnapshots
gained a resetPluginGeneration opt-out (default true, preserving existing
behavior) so refreshes with no plugin-relevant change (secrets reload,
chat-metadata polling, per-agent database startup reusing an already-captured
metadata snapshot) stop forcing an unrelated full plugin rebuild -- a second,
smaller contributing cause to the same CPU/memory/disk symptom.

Also: recordPreparedPluginRegistrySuccessor ensures a registry promoted as
a generation's successor is excluded from its predecessor's disposal, since
retained plugin instances are now shared across generations more often.

Tested: real (unmocked) plugin-load regression test proving the actual
benefit -- load A+B once, request A+B+C, only C's load path re-executes.
60+ targeted tests passing across all touched files, no regressions.

* fix(agents): resolve disposal-successor exclusion lazily at release time

Prior attempt (this commit, before amendment) added registrySuccessors-aware
exclusion inside retainPreparedPluginRegistry's inspection-owned branch, but
placed it as an EAGER check evaluated at retain-time (when the function first
runs and returns a release closure). That branch is also unreachable for the
model-catalog worker's real registries in the first place: those registries
are always registered through PreparedModelRuntimeBuildResources.load(), which
wraps them in a PreparedRegistryResources instance keyed into
retainPreparedModelRuntimeSnapshotResources's backing map BEFORE
retainPreparedPluginRegistry ever runs its own inspection lookup -- so the
earlier `if (prepared) return prepared.release` branch always wins first for
that path (ClawSweeper's finding on 8f7b6bfb303).

But fixing only the early-return order is not sufficient either: both of the
worker's call sites capture a predecessor's release closure from an EARLIER
call to retainPreparedPluginRegistry, then call
recordPreparedPluginRegistrySuccessor(previous, next) only once the successor
exists -- strictly AFTER retainPreparedPluginRegistry already returned for the
predecessor. So even moving the registrySuccessors.get() lookup to the top of
the function, unconditional of branch, still resolves it too early: the
successor is never recorded yet at that point, for any owner shape.

Fix: resolve the registrySuccessors lookup lazily, inside the returned release
closure itself, at the moment it is actually invoked -- by which point the
successor has been recorded. Every real owner shape (PreparedRegistryResources
-wrapped, bare PluginRegistryInspectionResources-owned, and the
createLifetime-owned fallback, which already did this correctly via its own
lazy accessor) now applies the same registrySuccessors-aware exclusion right
before triggering its real release, regardless of which branch is active.

Also adds a regression test that goes through the worker's actual
PreparedModelRuntimeBuildResources.load() + retainPreparedPluginRegistry flow
(not a bare PluginRegistryInspectionResources construction), confirming it
fails against the pre-amendment code and passes with this fix.

* fix(agents): transfer disposal custody for previousRegistry-retained plugin instances

Both P1 findings on the model-catalog worker's scope-growth promotion
(A -> A+B) traced to the same root cause: resolvePluginInstanceOwner's
owner.registry is set once per PluginRecord and never reassigned, so a
record retained forward into a successor via previousRegistry reuse
still reports its ORIGINAL (predecessor) registry as its disposal
custodian. Every consumer that gates disposal/liveness on
owner.registry (the inspection retire filter in loader-runtime-load.ts,
getPluginRecordRegistry, isPluginRecordActive) therefore still lets the
retiring predecessor revoke/dispose an instance the successor is
actively relying on (finding 1), and nothing ever disposes it once the
predecessor stops being considered its owner (finding 2, a leak).

Investigated whether #161267's lender/borrower borrowRegistry
mechanism (merged on main the same day) could cover this directly:
resolveLendingGatewayRegistry explicitly excludes purpose ===
model-catalog from borrowRegistry, and more fundamentally the
model-catalog worker's own generations are always loaded through
acquirePluginRegistryForInspection with activate: false, so
runtimeSideEffects is always false for them -- they never set
/record a borrowSignature on their own plugins, so they could
never act as a borrowRegistry lender for their own successor even if
wired up manually. The borrow/view-fencing model is for a lender that
stays alive and serves many concurrent short-lived borrowers; the
worker's generations are a strict linear hand-off instead, so the
right fix is to move custody forward, not to add fencing.

Fix: add transferPluginInstanceOwner(record, registry) and call it in
loader-runtime-core.ts's resolvePluginRecordRetention retention branch
whenever a record is retained from previousRegistry (never for
borrowRegistry, which keeps the lender's permanent custody as-is).
This makes the existing generic owner.registry === registry custody
check correct for the whole chain with no extra bookkeeping: the
predecessor naturally excludes a transferred instance from its own
retire filter, and the successor naturally includes it in its own
eventual retire filter, guaranteeing disposal exactly once wherever the
chain actually terminates.

With the root cause fixed, the registrySuccessors/
recordPreparedPluginRegistrySuccessor/retainInstancesFor machinery
added across this branch's prior two commits is now dead weight: it
only ever suppressed a predecessor's premature disposal (finding 1)
and never transferred custody anywhere (finding 2, still a leak even
with that machinery in place). Removed it from
prepared-model-runtime.plugin-lifetime.ts,
prepared-model-catalog.worker.ts, and
registry-inspection-resources.ts.

Replaced the three removed tests (disposal-successor,
inspection-successor, build-resources-successor -- all asserted
behavior of the now-deleted recordPreparedPluginRegistrySuccessor) with
prepared-model-runtime.plugin-lifetime.generation-handoff.test.ts,
covering the real worker path end to end:
- PreparedModelRuntimeBuildResources + retainPreparedPluginRegistry
  (the exact prepareWorkerGeneration flow): predecessor release
  survives, a real successor-side call through
  instance.runInRegistry(successorRegistry, ...) succeeds, and the
  shared instance disposes exactly once once the successor itself
  later retires.
- The same ownership transfer through the plain
  acquirePluginRegistryForInspection(previousRegistry) path.
- A disabled-plugin-between-generations case and a no-successor
  terminal-retirement case both still correctly reject a stale

incorrectly disposes/revokes the predecessor's shared instance.

2. Attempts successor build that throws
3. Disposes failed successor resources FIRST
4. IMMEDIATELY verifies predecessor still has custody (instance not disposing,

2. prepared-model-catalog.worker.ts's runCatalogRequest failure paths (fixed earlier)

The bug manifested as the test 'failed worker handoff (generation build throws after transfer) restores predecessor custody via real worker path' failing because:
- acquireAgentRuntimePluginRegistry transfers instance ownership to the successor registry
- The onPrimaryRegistry callback throws (simulating a worker generation build failure)
- Without rollback execution, the transfer remains in effect
- When the failed successor disposes, it incorrectly disposes/revokes the predecessor's shared instance

fix(plugins): tolerate ctime-only stat drift in native companion admission (#179949)

* fix(plugins): tolerate ctime-only stat drift in native companion admission

Native plugin admission re-checks a dev:ino:mode:size:mtimeNs:ctimeNs identity
after reading each companion to digest it. On Windows Endpoint DLP (and Code
Integrity) the first read stamps an extended attribute that advances only ctime,
so the strict !== in finishPluginNativeNamespace and the re-capture digest made
admission invalidate itself and native plugins could never load.

Use the module's existing pluginSourceIdentityChangedOnlyByCtime helper at all
three cited comparisons (and drop the managed||previous gate on the copy pass) so
metadata-only stamps are tolerated while a real size/mtime/inode/content change
is still rejected. Same principle as merged #164823 and #165982.

Adds plugin-native-namespace.test.ts covering ctime-only tolerance and
real-change rejection.

* fix(plugins): verify native companion bytes across metadata stamps

Reconcile first-read ctime drift without retaining stale mutable-source copies, and record verified identities for warm reuse. Cover all three admission phases and timestamp-preserving edits.

Prep v2.33.0 release: release notes, install docs

Move the unreleased server notes to v2.33.0 (released October 23, 2026) with a short intro, and bump install.md to 2.33.0.

Merge pull request #2085 from binwiederhier/db-pool-metrics

Export PostgreSQL connection pool metrics
Pool metrics collector: one table of metrics instead of six fields
Pool roles as constants
One field per line in struct literals

Merge pull request #2086 from binwiederhier/go-1273

Build with Go 1.27.3

Build with Go 1.27.3

Go 1.27.2 and 1.27.3 are security releases; 1.27.3 makes crypto/x509
reject chains through the eight compromised eMudhra intermediate CAs.
ntfy's outbound TLS (Firebase, web push, Stripe, Twilio, S3, upstream)
only gets that by being rebuilt.

The bump was held at 1.27.1 because staticcheck v0.8.1 could not read
Go 1.27.2's export data; staticcheck 2026.2.2 (v0.8.2) can, and is
clean. text/template is unchanged, so only GENERATED_FROM moves.

Export PostgreSQL connection pool metrics

ntfy_db_pool_connections_{max,open,in_use,idle}, ntfy_db_pool_waits_total and
ntfy_db_pool_wait_seconds_total, one series per pool (role primary or
replica, host). Read from database/sql's pool stats at scrape time, so a
burst that exhausts a pool between two scrapes still shows up as waits.

Needed to size pool_max_conns for several active cluster nodes: the
managed database allows 97 connections, and the open count alone says
nothing, since the pool rotates through all its connections.

commits.message:
feat(connectors): no guest on page open, connector sign-in offer (#143248)

* feat(connectors): list hosted apps without creating a guest identity

Opening the desktop Connectors page used to create a Nous guest identity:
connectors.list, connectors.catalog, connectors.accounts and
connectors.policy.get each created one before answering, because the
Portal's catalog route needs a token. A user who only looked at the page
got an identity anyway.

While there is no identity yet (and one may still be created), those four
reads now answer without one: the catalog from a snapshot that ships with
Hermes, an empty connector list, no accounts and no rules. Connecting an
app still creates the identity, as before.

scripts/refresh_connector_catalog.py rewrites the snapshot from a
signed-in install. It leaves logos out: no client draws them.

* feat(free-tier): sign-in offer for guests who connected apps

Every free-tier sign-in offer keyed on the welcome trial, so a user on
their own model key who connected apps through a guest identity never saw
one.

The offer record now tracks two offers on the same schedule. `trial` is
unchanged. `connector` is for a guest without the trial that has connected
an app: each app that finishes connecting sets `has_connected_app` on the
guest state (so it dies with the guest) and counts as a finished task.
free_tier.status (still a pure local read) adds connector_nudge_due_in, and
free_tier.claim_nudge takes a `kind`.

The desktop reads the connector offer whether or not the trial is
available, re-reads the status after a turn or a page connect, and shows
connector copy instead of the free-allowance copy. After a page connect
settles it also re-reads the catalog and rules, so the bundled catalog
from before the identity existed is replaced by the account's own.

* fix(connectors): point the sign-in hint at `hermes auth upgrade`

`hermes connectors` told users to run `hermes login`, which no longer
exists. Both hints now say "Run `hermes auth upgrade` to sign in."

* feat(connectors): read the public catalog with no token; one guest rule per entry point

The bundled catalog snapshot listed apps a new guest cannot connect and
went stale whenever the catalog changed. With no token, the Connectors
page now reads the Nous Portal's public catalog route
(GET /api/v1/connectors/catalog/public), sent with no Authorization and
parsed with the existing catalog model. Once a token exists the page reads
the signed-in route, as before.

Whether an entry point may create the guest identity is now declared once
per entry point instead of checked inside handlers:
- managed_client(creates_guest=...) is required: connect (page, agent,
  card retry) and the explicit lists (CLI `hermes connectors list`, agent
  manage_connections status/display) pass True, unchanged.
- account RPCs declare creates_guest on _account_method: catalog,
  accounts and policy.get never create one; tools and the account writes
  still do.
- the page's connectors.list never creates one; connect does.

With no token the page reads give true answers: public catalog, empty
connected list, no accounts. The invented "unrestricted" policy is gone:
the desktop asks for rules only once the list has rows, which needs a
token, and policy.get without one refuses with sign-in-required.

Deleted: the bundled snapshot, its refresh script, and the no-identity
stubs.

* fix(connectors): CI and review round: older backends, outside connects, link connects, guest opt-out

- CI: test_legacy_fallback_ticket_profile_verbs faked managed_client with
  no arguments and gave the secondary profile no token, so the page list
  (now token-gated, creates_guest=False) never reached it. The fake takes
  the new keyword and the profile holds a token.
- Older backends: a trial claim sends free_tier.claim_nudge with no
  params again. An older backend rejects the unknown `kind` key and would
  have dropped the trial offer; the new backend defaults to the trial.
  Only the connector claim sends `kind`.
- Outside connects: while the page's list is empty (no identity), every
  finished turn or connect re-reads the list and catalog. An agent connect
  in a chat then moves the page to the signed-in routes and its rules.
- Link connects: an agent status read that sees a connected app on a
  guest without the flag arms the connector offer, so messaging and
  one-shot connects (no operation watcher) count too.
- Opt-out: the connector offer requires nous.guest to be allowed.

* fix(connectors): the Connectors page list arms the connector offer too

A guest whose apps were connected by an older Hermes has no has_connected_app flag, and only the operation watcher or the agent's status read set it. The page's connectors.list now passes its rows to note_connected_apps_seen, which owns the any-connected check for both list reads.

* fix(connectors): review round 3: accounts after an outside connect, retryable offer record

- An identity created outside the page (an agent connect in a chat) now also re-reads the accounts cached while there was none, so the new account row, rename and remove show up.
- note_app_connected records the connector task before it sets has_connected_app. The flag ends list-read sightings, so a failed schedule write no longer leaves the offer unarmed for good.

feat(desktop): sign-in result shows who signed in and what moved (#143236)

* feat(desktop): sign-in dialog shows who signed in and what moved

The free-tier sign-in dialog now reads "Finish in your browser" with the
device code shown small ("Do not share it.") and an "Open page again"
button. Once the browser approves, the result screen sets the account
email large under "Signed in as", then says what the replaced free
tier's apps did, in the same lines every other sign-in surface prints.
A Reconnect button opens the app that has to be reconnected; a move
still retrying is a small note that updates itself.

- The sign-in poll is a long-poll (`?wait=`): the backend answers once
  the session leaves pending, capped at 25 s. The desktop never asks
  again sooner than 2 s, so an older backend that answers at once is
  not hammered. The onboarding picker uses the same loop, and a Nous
  sign-in there that moved apps opens the same result screen.
- The poll reports `handoff_status`: the handoff record as fields plus
  its copy (`guest_handoff.wire_status`).
- New `GET /api/providers/oauth/nous/handoff?since=&wait=`
  (token-protected, profile-scoped) long-polls the handoff record so a
  retrying move is followed until it settles or the dialog closes.
- The copy and failure screens for the retired transfer outcomes
  (declined, superseded, retired) are gone.

* test(auth): sign-in copy check builds Completed with its handoff_status

The every-state copy check builds each SignInState from a placeholder
per dataclass field; Completed gained handoff_status in the parent
commit, so give it a real wire_status value.

* fix(desktop): Greptile round 1 on the sign-in result screen

- Onboarding paints above every dialog, so a result from the onboarding
  provider list now waits until onboarding leaves the screen.
- The result keeps the profile the sign-in ran for, and Reconnect names
  that profile (and connection) in the Connectors link, like a chat's
  connector links do.
- A sign-in whose own run attempted no move (another process held the
  claim, or the budget ran out) reports the replaced free tier's saved
  record instead of no handoff (`guest_handoff.record_status`).
- A failed handoff read retries with backoff (4, 8, 16, 32 s) before the
  result stops following the move.

feat(auth): every Nous sign-in is the plain device login (#143235)

* feat(auth): every Nous sign-in is the plain device-code login

Every Nous sign-in (desktop, CLI and TUI /login, gateway /login,
`hermes auth upgrade`) now runs one plain device-code login,
`anon_sign_in.run_sign_in`: device code, a cancel-aware token poll,
save. The free tier the account replaces hands its apps over in the
existing guest handoff step after the save, and every surface prints
what moved and what to reconnect right after "Signed in as ...".

The promotion intent/status calls, the consent page link and the
`cancel_wins_after_promotion` rule are gone, with the Declined,
Superseded, Retired and Unavailable states. A cancel is now one
`Cancelled` state and always wins: nothing is saved.

- The token poll takes a `cancelled` hook and checks it on a <= 1 s
  tick, so a desktop cancel or a newer /login stops it at once.
- An expired code maps to `TimedOut` (`reason: timeout` on the desktop).
- The account email is read from the access token's `email` claim.
- TLS goes through `_resolve_verify`, so the CA bundle settings apply.
- /login works with no free tier on disk.
- The desktop start route always uses the flow (`replace_account=True`
  keeps "connect another account" working) and the poll route returns
  the handoff lines.
- `hermes model` signs a connector-only free tier in instead of
  refusing; `_login_nous` prints the handoff result too.
- Every sign-in that saves an account settles the config itself once
  its locks are released (`run_sign_in`, `_login_nous`, `hermes auth add
  nous`, the billing step-up, the tool-setup login); the handoff runner
  only moves apps.

* fix(auth): CI round 1 on the plain sign-in

- The docs page wrote "<= 1 s", which MDX parses as a JSX tag; say
  "at least once a second" instead.
- The shared Retry-After parser test still imported the promotion
  status poller's helper, which this PR deletes; drop that leg.

* fix(auth): Greptile round 1 on the plain sign-in

- Read the Portal URL inside the profile scope: with no Nous state on
  disk, a multi-profile backend read the override after the scope had
  exited and signed in against the default Portal.
- An expired_token answer from the token endpoint is TimedOut (the
  desktop's timeout screen), the same as running out the clock.

* fix(auth): Greptile round 2 on the plain sign-in

`hermes auth add nous` and the tool-setup Nous login now capture the
free tier's handoff around their save and print what moved and what to
reconnect, the same as the terminal login does.

* fix(auth): Greptile round 3 on the plain sign-in

- The Portal is resolved through the same rule every other Nous call
  uses: the operator's override wins over a URL saved in the auth store,
  so a staging override no longer signs a desktop "connect another
  account" into production.
- Gateway /login holds its registry lock across the final cancel check
  and the save, so a replacing /login cannot land between them and the
  replaced attempt never saves.

* fix(auth): Greptile round 4 on the plain sign-in

Gateway /login no longer holds its registry lock across the save. The
final cancel check claims the save under the lock, then the save runs
outside it: the event loop takes that lock, and a save can wait on the
auth store. A replacing /login while the save runs is told a sign-in is
finishing instead of cancelling it.

feat(auth): hand the free-tier guest to the account after sign-in (#143234)

* feat(auth): hand the free tier's apps to the account that replaces it

When a Nous account is saved over a free-tier identity, Hermes now moves
that identity's connected apps into the account with one call to the Nous
Portal claim endpoint, authorized by the account's own token. Nothing asks
first; the result (account email, what moved, what needs reconnecting) is
shown afterwards in `hermes auth status nous` and exposed for the desktop.

Sign-in code does not know about it. A hook at the two lowest write seams
(`_store_provider_state`, `_write_shared_nous_state`) writes a pending
record under the existing locks and does no network. The claim runs
outside every lock: after a shared-store write, when a `deferred()` block
exits (the desktop poller and `run_sign_in` save under their own lock),
after a free-tier reconcile, and on each Nous keepalive tick, which
resumes retries from an earlier process.

Records sit beside the shared Nous store, keyed by a hash of the free-tier
credential and bound to the destination account, so profiles sharing one
free-tier identity share one record and one claim. A claim lock spans
read, claim and write. A Claimed record is never reopened; a lost success
followed by an unknown-credential answer reads as "probably moved". The
account token is refreshed after the move only when the cohort carried.
The same path runs `settle_after_upgrade` once per replacement, so every
replacing writer settles the config.

The legacy promotion sign-in already moves the apps on the server, so it
records the handoff as done and sends no claim.

* fix(auth): the free-tier handoff only ever claims into its bound account

Review round 1 on the guest handoff.

P1, Bearer not proven to be the destination: the runner checked the
profile's account against the record's destination, then resolved a
Bearer separately. A sign-in landing between the two could move the apps
into that other account and mark the record Claimed. The Bearer is now
resolved first and its JWT subject is compared to the record's
destination inside the reservation, so only a token proven to belong to
the destination is ever sent.

P1, stale reservation: the destination check and the attempt increment
were separate record reads, so a sibling could rebind the destination in
between. `_reserve` now does one locked read-modify-write: still active,
due (`next_attempt_at`, so a waiting runner honours a Retry-After another
runner saved), under `MAX_ATTEMPTS` (a crash after the last send now
closes the record as Failed instead of sending again), and bound to the
Bearer's subject. A record without a destination subject is never written.

P2, config completion in the runner: `drain` no longer runs
`settle_after_upgrade`. Settling stays with the sign-in that saved the
account (run_sign_in, the desktop poller), as before this PR. This
deletes the thread-local queue and the batch's settle fallback.

P2, keepalive: a handoff failure is logged and token renewal carries on.
An unparseable records file is moved aside to .corrupt on the next write
instead of blocking every Nous account save.

P2, budget: the remaining sync budget is checked before each record,
token resolve and request, and is passed as their timeout, so a refusal
at the edge starts no refresh or second claim.

P2, status: an active move bound to an account the profile no longer
holds reads as paused, with copy that says so.

* fix(auth): free-tier handoff retries reach every profile and every long-lived process

Review round 2 on the guest handoff.

P1, queued moves had no worker: retries rode the token keepalive, which
does not start in a process that boots with a guest (a Desktop backend
before sign-in). A move left by a CLI sign-in during an outage then
waited for a restart. Retries now run on a dedicated worker that
`start_nous_auth_keepalive` starts in every long-lived Nous process,
guest or not; the keepalive tick no longer drains.

P1, named profiles never retried: the keepalive drained only the launch
profile's records. Each worker tick now runs every due record under its
owning profile's home and secret scope (the way the cron ticker binds a
profile), so a named profile's move retries from a process launched as
another profile. The bound-account check and the Bearer proof in the
reservation still decide whether anything is sent.

P2, cached guest token: the resolver's 5 s memo could still hold the
guest's token from a connector call just before the save; the
reservation then refused its subject and the move waited for a later
run. The handoff now drops that memo before reading the account token.

P2, budget through locks: the token read waited the resolver's own
15 s floors for the auth and shared locks. The handoff now takes both
locks itself within the remaining budget (same order), which makes the
resolver's acquisitions reentrant, and re-checks the budget before
reserving or sending.

* fix(auth): free-tier handoff never gives up on a transient failure before the reap

Compatibility audit, items B1, B4 and B5.

B1: a handoff that reached Failed was never retried, so the free tier's
apps were lost when the idle free-tier identity was reaped after 14
days. Transient failures (5xx, the 503 breaker with no Retry-After,
timeouts, busy, unknown codes) became final after 8 attempts, about 81
minutes. Now only codes no later attempt can change are final
(client_not_allowed, account_locked, invalid_request). Every other
outcome retries, the slowest rung (1 h) repeating, until 13 days after
the record was made. The attempt reservation then closes it as Failed
`retry_window_ended`. One predicate (`_retryable`) picks the work for
every run, so a record an older build failed on a transient code re-arms
on the next sign-in, `hermes auth status nous`, `hermes auth upgrade`, or
retry-worker tick, with no new state. The attempt cap is deleted.

B4: failure copy printed raw server codes. Final codes map to a plain
sentence, and anything else shows only the generic sentence.

B5: a claim answer without a `connectors` field (an older service) read
as "There were no free-tier apps to move", and so did Gone on a first
attempt, which follows a released ticket that already moved the apps.
The first now reads as unknown with neutral copy, and the second as
"Nothing left to move from the free tier."

* fix(auth): a free tier with no apps reads as nothing moved after sign-in

A free tier that only read its connectors gets a vendor id row on the
service, so the claim answers kind `moved` (or `swapped`) with an empty
`moved_toolkits`. The status copy keyed on the kind and printed "Your
apps moved to <email>." for an account that received nothing.

One rule: an empty moved list reads as nothing moved, for moved and
swapped alike. The service now refuses a move it could not read, so an
empty list is the truth. The promotion sign-in's record, which reports
no list at all, now carries kind `unknown` and keeps its neutral copy
instead of falling under the rule.

fix(launchers): every publication collects retired launcher copies

Review follow-up: the sweep of `hermes.exe.<pid>.deleteme` copies ran only
when the publication fell back to a .cmd launcher, so a later publication
with distlib available (an .exe) left the aside copy behind forever. The
sweep now runs on every successful publication. The running-launcher test
bounds its readiness wait, keeps the child's whole lifetime inside the
try/finally (kill + reap on a stuck shutdown), and republishes with distlib
restored to pin the collection.

fix(launchers): a Python repin retires the running Windows launcher

On Windows without distlib in the runtime environment, a repin of PM's Python
republishes the source launcher as a .cmd and must retire the old hermes.exe
so it cannot shadow it. stage_launcher deleted it, but the exe it has to
retire is usually the one running `hermes update` (or the launch retrying
the owed step), and Windows refuses to delete a mapped image. The publication
failed, the update owed 'launchers', so the install stamp and bootstrap
receipt were withheld at the old commit and the old exe kept booting the old
interpreter. Every retry ran from that same exe and failed the same way.

Windows does allow renaming a running image, so retire it by renaming it
aside when the delete fails (distlib's .deleteme move), and collect the aside
copy on a later publication once its process has exited.

test(desktop-e2e): a reloaded document's sockets stop counting as live

The transcript oracle's "live sockets to the one host backend" check
intermittently saw two native_dial sockets on two ports: the current
socket through the test's loopback proxy, plus the direct socket the
renderer held BEFORE the `reload` step.

Root cause: Playwright forgets a page's WebSockets when a new main-frame
document commits (frameManager._clearWebSockets) without emitting their
'close', so recordWebSockets kept the pre-reload socket at closed=false
whenever its close event lost the race against the reload's commit.
The renderer held one socket; the recorder held a dead one.

recordWebSockets now retires every recorded socket at a new-document
commit (a main-frame navigation request followed by framenavigated).
Hash navigations issue no navigation request, so they never retire a
live socket, and any socket the new document dials (a real duplicate to
the host backend, #120006) is still counted.

Evidence: a standalone Playwright 1.62.1 + Electron 44.9.3 probe (page
with one WebSocket, 10 reloads with a hash navigation between each)
left 9/10 pre-reload sockets "live" in the old recorder while the server
saw exactly one open; the retire-on-commit recorder reported 1 live on
10/10. Local run of the full spec was not possible on this host
(electron.launch of the app dies on connect here).

test(desktop-update-e2e): find the packaged app by its install dir, not its environment

Electron 44's Chromium zeroes /proc/<pid>/environ in the browser process
and every child it execs right after start (Electron 40.10.2 kept it
readable: same headless probe, PROBE_MARK=1 on 40, 0 on 44.9.3). The
update suite's install census matched processes by HERMES_HOME in that
environment, so after the Electron 44 upgrade (#142727) it stopped seeing
the installed Desktop app at all:

- app-update: "the app to relaunch itself" picked a short-lived process
  instead of the relaunched app, the SIGTERM missed the app, the
  "quits cleanly" poll passed on an empty census, and the next launch hit
  "another Hermes Desktop instance holds the single-instance lock".
- build-fail and app-update: session.close() SIGKILLs installProcesses();
  the relaunched app survived it with live connections to the spec's
  provider/edge servers, and the Playwright worker hung 300 s on stop.

The app itself is fine: the relaunched Electron 44 app quits within 1 s
of SIGTERM at every point of its boot (0.2 s to 10 s, source build).

installProcesses now adds every process whose /proc/<pid>/exe lies under
the install's release dir (install-specific, readable whatever the
environment shows), and desktopMainProcesses reads that set directly,
dropping a candidate whose parent is a candidate (a child between fork
and exec still shows the main's exe and argv).

refactor(delegation): the first-use default loads through the shared plugin loader

_load_bundled imported plugins/delegation/<name> with its own importlib
spec under its own module name. It now goes through
plugins.plugin_loader.load_plugin_module like the other bundled provider
categories (cron, memory, context engine). That loader serializes
concurrent loads of one module, reuses an already-loaded module, and
returns None rather than raising when the plugin fails to import, so the
backend then reports itself unavailable. The first-use fallback and the
plugins.disabled check are unchanged (Greptile on #142564).

test(delegation): the hosted-backend test loads the bundled default strategy

With default a bundled plugin, the hosted test's empty bundled dir left no default
to switch a session to; point it at plugins/delegation like the other backend tests.

fix(delegation): an unavailable replacement default falls back to the bundled strategy

A provider registered as "default" that reported unavailable made _usable()
return None without trying the enabled bundled strategy, so with
delegation.backend unset every task was refused with a message claiming
delegation/default is disabled (Greptile). The bundled strategy is now tried
whenever the registered provider is missing or unavailable.

fix(delegation): a first-use default never outlives plugins.disabled

The first-use loader for a bundled strategy registered it straight into the
global provider registry, outside the plugin manager's registration lifecycle.
Once loaded that way, disabling delegation/default and rediscovering left the
entry alive, and _usable() returned it before plugins.disabled was consulted
(Greptile on #142564).

The first-use provider is now kept in its own cache, outside the registry the
manager owns, and plugins.disabled is checked on every call, so a later
disable refuses delegation without a restart. Adds a test that a replacement
provider registered as "default" gets the full route contract (tier checked
and applied, label reported), pinning the name-free rules from da5fec8dc6e.

refactor(delegation): the default delegation strategy is a bundled plugin

Move today's delegation routing (every child follows the delegation section,
else the parent's route) out of core into plugins/delegation/default, a bundled
kind: backend plugin that registers through ctx.register_delegation_provider
like any other strategy. Core keeps only the name 'default' as the fallback
selection; no built-in provider class and no reserved name remain.

The registry loads a bundled strategy on first use when the plugin sweep never
registered it (runtimes that pinned discovery with zero plugins), so
delegate_task never depends on the sweep; plugins.disabled still wins and a
disabled default is a clear refusal. Config names are validated before they
become a path.
fix(contributors): add ebrearly to contributors map

Merge origin/main into window-plans

Resolves hermes_cli/auth_model_picker.py against 7a8569baa9a (the picker
takes a title, public as prompt_model_selection): keeps this branch's
description_lines()/menu_title() split, with menu_title(title=...) and the
title= parameter on _prompt_model_selection carried over from main.

fix(delegation): the undeclared-parameter refusal names the saved backend

`/new` starts on the saved backend (4c4692f25d), so "start a new session with /new for a tool that
matches '<session backend>'" sent the user back to the saved mode. The fix in the message is now
"`/delegation <session backend> --global` then `/new`", or "`/delegation <saved backend>`" to switch
the session back. When the session follows config.yaml (it changed mid-session) the fix is just /new.

Review: Greptile on #142563 and the plugin lane (hermes-official-plugins#136).

fix(delegation): refuse a task parameter the session's backend does not declare

The delegate_task schema follows config.yaml for the whole session (the tool list is part of the
cached prompt and is never rebuilt mid-conversation), so after a session-only `/delegation <mode>`
switch the model still sends the previous backend's parameters. _route_one kept only the active
backend's declared names, so e.g. `option: fast` (model_map) under profile_routes was dropped and
the task ran on the profile default / parent model.

Core now refuses, per task and fail-closed like every other routing refusal, a task carrying a
parameter the active backend does not declare (core-owned names excepted). The message names the
session's backend, the parameter, and the fix: `/new` for a tool list that matches, or
`/delegation <backend>` back to the backend that declares it. A name no installed backend declares
is refused too, with "resend it without" as the fix. Siblings in the batch still run.

Review: @unsupportedpastels on hermes-official-plugins#136, finding 2.1.

fix(delegation): a child routed back to the launch profile uses its container

Persistent Docker keys a session-bound container by profile. _container_profile
took the bound home's profile only when that home is a routed (non-launch) one,
else the session's HERMES_SESSION_PROFILE. A coder chat on a default-launched
gateway routing a child to default binds the launch home, which is not routed,
so the child fell back to the parent chat's profile and ran in profile:coder's
container instead of default's (Greptile on #143126, relayed in #142563).

The bound home's profile now decides whenever it differs from the session's
own; a session with no profile name is still the launch profile's, so the
launch home's own turns keep their key. The sibling per-profile keys
(_routed_home_task_key, _qualify_task_key) already key the launch home as the
default profile does and were right.

fix(delegation): /new starts the chat on the saved delegation backend

A /delegation pick is session-scoped like /model, but it lives in
agent.delegation_backends keyed by session_key, and the gateway's route key
survives /new, /reset, /resume, idle/daily auto-reset and the
compression-exhausted reset. Nothing popped it at those boundaries, so the
next conversation in the chat kept overriding config.yaml's delegation.backend
(Greptile on #143126, relayed in #142563).

The conversation-boundary funnel (_clear_conversation_scope), which already
clears the /model override for every one of those boundaries, now drops the
session's backend pick too. Other chats keep theirs.

docs(delegation): is_available() and the config example describe fail-closed backends

Greptile P2 on #142563: the provider table and cli-config.yaml.example still
promised a fallback to default; also name advanced-delegation, route
fallback_providers inheritance and ctx.delegation_backends.

fix(delegation): report an inherited fast tier; refused tasks settle the batch manifest

A backend route that inherits the parent's request settings reports the tier they
carry (service_tier/speed, top level or extra_body) instead of normal. A refused
task's manifest entry is written when the call is accepted, so a background call
whose async units never carry it does not leave it running. Greptile P2 on #142563.

fix(plugins): a settled choice closes the CLI picker; a described choice keeps its plain label

The CLI answering a plugin command's clarify request between turns now tracks the
open request: the gateway's request.cancel (another viewer picked, or its wait
ended) closes the panel, and so does the end of the command's wait. A choice with
a description still accepts its plain label typed back. Greptile P1/P2 on #142563.

fix(delegation): a hosted plugin switches the owner's backends (ctx.delegation_backends)

Under plugins.isolation: host a /delegation handler calling agent.delegation_backends
changed the plugin host's copy of the session overrides, not the one delegate_task
reads, and listed the host's (empty) registry. ctx.delegation_backends exposes the
same API as plain data and is a host remote facade, so the call runs in the Hermes
process. Greptile P1 on #142563.

feat(plugins): the model picker takes a title, public as prompt_model_selection

_prompt_model_selection gains title= (default 'Select default model:'), so a
plugin's route editor can say 'Select the model for this route:'. It is public
for plugins as hermes_cli.auth_model_picker.prompt_model_selection (listed in the
admission lint's public surfaces, with agent.delegation_backends) and documented
in the delegation provider guide.

fix(delegation): a global backend switch is refused on a managed install

set_global_backend raises PermissionError (format_managed_message) when a package
manager owns the install, like every other config writer, and leaves config.yaml
untouched.

feat(plugins): plugin slash commands can ask the user to pick an option

PluginContext.ask_choice(question, choices) -> str | None lets a sync
slash-command handler ask the user who ran it to pick one option and get
the picked value back. Choices are strings or {value, label, description}.
Each surface binds an asker around the handler call
(hermes_cli/plugin_choices.py), and every asker is that surface's
existing clarify prompt. No surface gets a new card type or wire shape:

- messaging chats (gateway/plugin_command_choice.py): adapter.send_clarify
  plus the clarify tool's own delivery (_clarify_send_then_wait, text
  fallback, card retire). Telegram/Discord/Slack show buttons, other
  platforms a numbered list. The typed reply reaches the clarify
  text-intercept while the command still holds the chat.
- local sessions on the gateway (classic CLI, Ink TUI, Desktop): the
  `clarify` server request to the session's viewers. Two fixes make the
  answer arrive while slash.exec is still waiting for the handler:
  * tui_gateway/ws.py: a viewer's answer to an open server request (a
    response frame, `clarify.lock`) is settled at once instead of queuing
    behind that socket's running slash.exec.
  * hermes_cli/gateway_plugin_commands.py: the classic CLI answers the
    session's `clarify` requests with its clarify panel while it waits for
    slash.exec. No turn pump reads the session's frames between turns.
- in-process classic CLI and the legacy `hermes serve` backend: their
  clarify panel / `clarify` server request.

Returns None when nothing can ask (hooks, cron, async handlers on the
event loop), when the user cancels or answers with something that is not a
choice, or when the clarify timeout passes. The handler then prints its
text usage.

feat(delegation): a session can switch its delegation backend

agent/delegation_backends.py is the public API a /delegation command uses,
following the /model convention: list_backends() (name, label, description,
available, reason), get/set_session_backend(session_key, name) for one session,
and set_global_backend(name, session_key=) which writes delegation.backend to the
active profile's config.yaml and drops that session's override. delegate_task
resolves the calling session's key (turn session context, else the parent's
session id) and routes with its override. The delegate_task schema keeps
following config.yaml, since it is part of the cached prompt. Providers gain a
user-facing summary for pickers.

feat(delegation): an unusable backend fails closed, an unroutable task is refused alone

A configured delegation.backend that is not installed or reports unavailable no
longer runs children on the default route: delegate_task returns a tool error
naming the backend and the fix. Within a batch, a task its backend cannot route
(enum miss, DelegationRouteError, unknown reasoning_effort, unoffered tier,
unresolvable credentials or profile) is refused alone: no child is built, its
result entry carries the error and route.refused, and its siblings run; the call
is a tool error only when every task is refused. A non-profile backend route
without its own fallback_providers inherits delegation.fallback_providers. Every
backend-routed result's route names the backend, and fallback_activated shows
when a fallback provider took over.

fix(delegation): ultrafast is checked against the route's own Codex account

The ultrafast entitlement check ran without an access token, so it read the
profile's stored Codex login. A backend route carrying another account's key
could be refused (or allowed) on the wrong account's catalog (Greptile). The
check now gets the route's key, or the inherited parent's on an unpinned route.

fix(delegation): a profile child uses the target profile's persistent container

Persistent Docker keys a session-bound container by HERMES_SESSION_PROFILE,
which delegated_profile_scope leaves on the parent: a child routed to coder
inside a default-profile gateway/TUI session reused the default profile's
cached container, without coder's image, mounts and env (Greptile).

The container profile now follows the bound HERMES_HOME override when there is
one, else the session's profile. HERMES_SESSION_PROFILE itself is untouched: it
is also the delivery identity notifications read, which stays the parent's.
Gateway routed turns bind both to the same profile, so their key is unchanged.

fix(delegation): a profile child reads the starting directory seeded for it

seed_workspace recorded the child's starting directory (the parent's, or its
isolated worktree) in the parent's scope. cwd records are keyed by the active
profile on a multiplexed host, so a profile-routed child, looking its record up
as the target profile, missed it: with worktree isolation its relative commands
could run in the target profile's configured directory although it was told its
terminal starts in the worktree (Greptile). The parent's record is now read in
the parent's scope and the child's written inside child_profile_scope.

fix(delegation): route-field rules follow the route, not the backend's name

resolve_task_routes treated any provider named "default" as the old built-in
strategy: its service_tier was dropped and its results carried no route
report. Once the default strategy is a replaceable plugin (stacked #142564), a
replacement under that name silently loses both (Greptile on #142564).

The rules now follow the route itself:
- the built-in default strategy drops service_tier from its own route (the
  delegation section has no tier key), instead of core special-casing it;
- the reasoning_effort check already skips the delegation section's own value,
  which is all the default route carries;
- the result report sits next to a route's label, as the label alone did
  before: unlabelled routes (default, a backend's dict(config) fallback) keep
  the result shape unchanged.

docs(delegation): document delegation.backend, delegation.backends and route fields

cli-config.yaml.example and the configuration reference now cover
delegation.backend and delegation.backends.<name> (model_map,
profile_routes); the user and plugin guides cover the settings block,
service_tier and reasoning_effort route checks, the per-result route
report, and that listing a profile in delegation.backends.profile_routes
lets this profile's subagents use that profile's credentials, credential
pool, SOUL.md and terminal policy.

Co-authored-by: unsupportedpastels <274530371+unsupportedpastels@users.noreply.github.com>

feat(delegation): results report the route a backend-routed child ran on

A routed task's result carried only the backend's label. It now carries
route = {label, provider, model, reasoning_effort, service_tier}, read off the
built child, so the parent sees what actually ran. Failed and abandoned
entries carry it too. Default-strategy results keep their shape.

Co-authored-by: unsupportedpastels <274530371+unsupportedpastels@users.noreply.github.com>

fix(delegation): an unknown reasoning_effort on a backend route is a tool error

A backend route's effort went through parse_reasoning_effort in
_resolve_child_runtime, where an unknown word only logged a warning and the
child inherited the parent's level. A value a backend returned now refuses
the task, naming the valid levels. The delegation section's own
reasoning_effort (also what a backend returning dict(config) carries) keeps
its warn-and-inherit rule.

Co-authored-by: unsupportedpastels <274530371+unsupportedpastels@users.noreply.github.com>

feat(delegation): service_tier is a route field checked by core

A tier could only reach a routed child through request_overrides, which
skipped the /fast access checks (Codex silently serves another tier to a plan
without ultrafast) and could be overwritten by a custom provider's extra_body
at construction. A backend route may now carry service_tier: core resolves it
against the route with resolve_fast_mode_overrides + ultrafast_offered before
any child is built, refuses the spawn when the route does not offer it, and
re-applies it after the child is built. model_map options get it by listing
the field. The default strategy never reads a tier from the delegation
section, so its route is unchanged.

Ported from #140614 (per-task speed tiers); the per-task route preflight
builds on #107945.

Co-authored-by: unsupportedpastels <274530371+unsupportedpastels@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: KoNit-K <124019182+KoNit-K@users.noreply.github.com>

feat(delegation): a backend's settings live under delegation.backends.<name>

Plugin backend settings no longer share the core delegation namespace:
DelegationProvider.settings(config) returns delegation.backends.<backend
name>, and DEFAULT_CONFIG carries an empty backends map. The selector stays
delegation.backend; config passed to every method is still the delegation
section, so dict(config) remains the default route.

feat(delegation): speed-tier helpers for delegated children

Ported from #140614 (d435a4b2205, 6015c98eb1c): a tier is validated with
the same gates as /fast (resolve_fast_mode_overrides, plus the Codex
account check for ultrafast), clears tier keys at the top level and inside
extra_body, and is re-applied to the built child so a custom provider's
extra_body merge cannot restore another tier. The per-task model fields
from that PR are not part of this port; delegation backends supply the
tier as a route field instead.

fix(delegation): one profile resolves once whatever its label

The route cache key included the display label, so one profile routed under two labels resolved
(and rebuilt its scope from disk) twice. The key now drops the label; each task keeps its own.

fix(delegation): a profile pinned to a missing ACP command refuses at routing

The delegation.provider path refuses a pinned ACP command that is not on PATH (#80450); the
profile route skipped that check. Reuse _require_pinned_command so the spawn fails at routing with
a message naming the profile, before any sibling child is built.

fix(delegation): refuse profile routes inside a managed worker

A managed worker (kanban, safe mode, managed sessions) binds its session config at creation and
every config reader returns that snapshot, so load_config_readonly() under the target profile's
HERMES_HOME override still returned the launch profile's config while secrets came from the
target scope: the child got the launch model with the target profile's keys.

Reading the target profile's config.yaml from disk there would cross the frozen-policy boundary
(the worker never opens profile files; safe-mode workers must not read user config at all), and
there is no reader for another home that bypasses the snapshot by design. Refuse the route with a
clear error instead; a route to the worker's own home is unaffected.

fix(delegation): a profile scope that fails to enter never strands the parent in the child profile

delegated_profile_scope bound the HERMES_HOME override, secret scope, multiplex flag and terminal
scope before its try:, so a later step that raised left the earlier tokens set and the parent ran
on inside the child's profile. Each step now enters an ExitStack, the same discipline as the
gateway's routed-turn scope (_profile_runtime_scope).

fix(delegation): profile routes resolve like the profile's own startup

`_profile_route` read the target profile's raw `model.default`, kept only `rt["provider"]` and
only `agent.reasoning_effort`:
- a `model.default` alias was sent as a model name to the default endpoint (or refused) instead of
  taking the alias's model, endpoint and key; it now goes through `resolve_startup_model_route`,
  the owner CLI/oneshot/TUI startup use;
- a named custom provider collapsed to `custom`, so with two named providers on one URL the child
  leased the first one's pool (wrong account); the name is kept as the identity, as the
  `delegation.provider` branch already does;
- reasoning ignored `agent.reasoning_overrides` and, when unset, fell back to the launching
  profile's `delegation.reasoning_effort` / parent level; it is now the target profile's
  `resolve_reasoning_config` result, carried as a final value (`ResolvedReasoning`).

Review: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/142563#discussion_r4337785472
Review: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/142563#discussion_r4337785483

fix(delegation): a profile child's lease and schema retry run as that profile

The profile scope covered only the child's first conversation. `_run_single_child` leased the
startup credential before entering it (a lease can refresh the profile's OAuth entries, and
`_swap_credential` re-reads TLS material and headers from config) and ran the output_schema retry
turn after leaving it, so both read the launching profile's config, secrets and terminal policy.
One `child_profile_scope(child)` boundary now wraps all three; parent bookkeeping stays outside.

Review: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/142563#discussion_r4337785444

fix(delegation): plugin parameters never overwrite the core task index

`index` is part of the core payload handed to `route_task`, but it was missing from
RESERVED_TASK_PARAMETERS: a provider declaring it as a model-facing parameter let the model's
value replace the real task position before routing. Reserve it with goal/context.

Review: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/142563#discussion_r4337785500

feat(delegation): pluggable delegation providers

delegate_task asks the active delegation provider (delegation.backend, a new
provider category registered with ctx.register_delegation_provider) for each
task's route: model/provider/endpoint/reasoning resolved by the existing
delegation credential resolver, or a Hermes profile the child runs as. A
provider may add enum-checked per-task schema parameters built once with the
tool definitions. Core keeps the whole lifecycle.

- agent/delegation_provider.py + agent/delegation_registry.py: ABC + registry;
  the built-in 'default' strategy is today's behaviour and the fallback for an
  unregistered/unavailable backend.
- tools/delegate_tool_routes.py: per-task routes, parameter validation, and the
  profile scope binding (home override + secret scope + multiplex semantics +
  terminal policy) around a profile child's construction and conversation.
- Host isolation: HOST_OBJECT_BASES row, so providers run under
  plugins.isolation: host.
- delegation.backend in DEFAULT_CONFIG; registrar table moved to
  hermes_cli/plugins_registrars.py to keep plugins.py under its cap.
- Default config: delegate_task schema and every hermes-cli tool definition
  are byte-identical to main.

fix(usage-window): the status bar drops the plan gauge once a reply arrives off a window plan

Greptile: "Old allowance stays visible" (gateway/session_usage.py:101-102).

Both usage builders (gateway/session_usage.py::tui_usage and
tui_gateway/server.py::_get_usage) always send `calls` and send
`plan_gauge` only on a window plan, so a complete usage payload without
the key means the session is off the plan (or the allowance reset).
Desktop merged every payload into the stored usage, which kept the old
gauge forever. The new `mergeUsage` (apps/shared usage-tick) clears it on
complete payloads and keeps it across partial ticks; usageFromTick forwards
a top-level frame's gauge so a canonical counters-only frame is complete
too. The wire stays byte-identical for accounts never on a window plan.
The Ink TUI never reads plan_gauge, so it has no stale copy.

fix(usage-window): a model of unknown tier is never promised the earlier reset

Greptile: "Large models retry too early". With a Large model and both the
daily and Large-model allowances full, an expired (300 s) or cold catalog
made current_model_is_top_tier answer False, so _stop_gauge took the daily
gauge and the refusal text, retry time and pool bench promised the daily
reset while the model stays refused until the later Large reset.

current_model_is_top_tier now returns None when the cached catalog has no
row for the model. The stop gauge (and limit_hit, so the card agrees)
counts a full top-tier allowance for an unknown tier, so of the full
allowances that could stop the model the later reset wins. A model the
catalog marks regular keeps the e3fff39 day reset; that test now stamps
its model as a regular catalog row instead of relying on an empty catalog.

fix(usage-window): never retry another chat from the TUI limit card's model switch

Greptile: "Recovery retries another chat". After accepting the limit
card, the user could open another chat while session.mutate was pending;
switchCanonicalModel skipped /model's stale checks, painted the result
into the newly active chat and called /retry, which reads the current
sid and so rewound and resent the other chat's last prompt.

switchCanonicalModel now reuses /model's guards: the mutation is fenced
on the refused chat's sid (stale after the CAS read and after the reply),
and isSupersededControl (now taking the baseline info) drops a reply an
epoch change or newer turn superseded. A stale reply applies nothing and
does not /retry. The legacy config.set path gets the same sid check.

test(pm): sealing tests see a build-machine .pth to prune

uv 0.13 writes no _virtualenv.pth, so the sealed arms passed even if the build
never called prune_site_pth. The fixture wheels now ship an __editable__ pointer
that only the sealed build removes.

fix(pm): pm update repairs stale installer pins when nothing needs re-pinning

The lock is saved before the fragments regenerate. If that generation failed,
the retry found every pin current and returned before regenerating.

refactor(nix): dev shell takes hermesNpmLib.nodejs instead of a second node+npm pair

hermesNpmLib.nodejs already puts the pinned npm over the pinned node; the
separate npmPinned + pmPackages.node pair relied on PATH order to get the same.

fix(tests): keep the Nix shell's PYTHONPATH through run_tests.sh's env -i

The devShell's HERMES_PYTHON is the lock's interpreter, which finds pytest and
the uv2nix venv only through PYTHONPATH. env -i dropped it, so every file failed
with 'No module named pytest'. Only the unactivated HERMES_PYTHON branch keeps it;
the activated test environment stays hermetic.
fix(deps): update python to 3.14.9
fix(deps): update uv to 0.13.5

feat(nix): dev shell runs the pm-pinned tool set

The dev shell took uv, node, ripgrep and ffmpeg from nixpkgs, so it ran
different versions than pm/lock.json ships (uv 0.11.32 vs 0.13.5, node
26.5.0 vs 26.12.1, ffmpeg 8.1.2 vs 9.0.1). Compose its tool set from
nix/pm-packages.nix instead, and wrap the pinned npm onto the pinned node
so `npm` and `node` are one generation.

pm-packages.nix also shipped every artifact nested under its archive's
versioned directory ($out/node-v26.12.1-linux-x64/bin/node), so no consumer
could reach them through PATH; flatten that and link root-level executables
into $out/bin.

git and openssh stay nixpkgs: the lock carries no Linux artifact for either.

feat(pm): pm update and pm lock --bump regenerate the installers' bootstrap pins

The curl|sh and irm|iex installers bootstrap uv (and, on Windows, git)
before any checkout exists, so they carry those pins as fragments that
scripts/gen-bootstrap-pins.py derives from pm/lock.json. Both re-pin
paths wrote only the lock: `pm update uv` left the installers on the old
uv, and the bootstrap-installer drift check failed until someone ran the
generator by hand.

Run the generator after either path saves the lock. It keys off the
saved lockfile's own checkout, so a fixture lock outside a checkout
regenerates nothing.
fix(deps): update node to 26.12.1
feat(nix): add pm to devshell

fix(usage-window): a managed worker turn keeps the usage-window refusal marker

agent/managed_worker.py::RESULT_FIELDS dropped usage_window_message, so a
window refusal on a managed-worker session reached the owner as a plain
billing failure and the error card fell back to the generic out-of-credits
card. The marker is a bounded scalar like failure_resets_at; usage_limit
(nested lists) still does not cross the worker frame, so that route shows the
window card without the suggested-model buttons.

fix(usage-window): the limit card re-runs the turn only after the model switch applied

Greptile: "Retries run before model confirmation". executeSlash reports nothing: it
renders a refused /model itself and resolves right after opening the guarded-model
confirm dialog, so the card reloaded the refused turn on the old model before the
user answered. The session-tile delegate gains switchSessionModel: the picker's
config.set wire, always --session, with a guarded target asked through the shared
surfaceModelSwitchConfirm and awaited. The card reloads only on true.

The card test that pinned the executeSlash call now pins switchSessionModel with the
same session-scoped arguments.

fix(usage-window): a pinned current model never takes the Recommended heading in the composer menu

Greptile: "Headings mislabel pinned current models". sectionAt assumes picks-first order,
but the composer menu prepends a current model the catalog omits, so with featured A and
pinned custom X, X got "Recommended" and A "Other models". Re-apply the picks-first
order (splitRecommended) after the pin, and state the order contract on sectionAt.

fix(usage-window): Billing says credits cover a used-up Large allowance only when credits_pay

Greptile: "Billing promises access without credits". The exhausted Large-model caption
keyed on keep_going_on_credits alone, so the setting on with a $0 top-up balance still
read "credits cover the rest" while the next request is refused. Use plan_usage.credits_pay
(setting on AND balance left), the same rule the gateway enforces.

fix(usage-window): keep warm Nous model tags across repeated pending model.options replies

Greptile: "Repeated pending replies erase labels". The merged row keeps its pending
flags, so the next pending reply found no warm row and dropped the Large / Free tags
(or locked every model) again. Remember the warm row each merged result was built from.

fix(usage-window): one billing row dismissing its step-up no longer resumes refetches mid-approval

Greptile: "Approval hooks clear others' pauses". $stepUpInFlight is shared by every
useStepUpFlow on the Billing page; dismiss() from an idle instance (the Keep going switch)
cleared it while another row's approval was in flight. Each flow now holds the pause under
its own token and the atom is true while any holder remains.

fix(usage-window): switch the TUI limit card's model via session.mutate on canonical connections

Greptile: "TUI model recovery is rejected". On a canonical connection the
owner's busy_config (gateway/session_busy_controls.py) refuses config.set
key=model with use_session_mutation_model, so the usage-limit card's
"switch to <model>" printed an error and never re-sent.

On canonical connections the card now uses the same revision-fenced,
session-scoped session.mutate operation=model path as /model
(switchCanonicalModel in canonicalSessionControls.ts, sharing
applyModelResult and the guarded-target confirmation). /retry runs only
once the switch committed; a refusal, a declined ask or a pick deferred
behind a running turn does not re-send. Standalone backends keep the
legacy config.set call.

fix(usage-window): carry the plan gauge on the canonical usage feed

Greptile: "Normal Desktop usage omits gauges". plan_gauge was built only in
tui_gateway/server.py::_get_usage (the embedded backend), but a normal local
Desktop session reads its session.usage ticks and message.complete usage from
gateway/session_usage (usage_stats -> tui_usage), so the status-bar allowance
never showed. Move the builder to gateway.session_usage.plan_gauge, use it on
both paths (omitted off a window plan, as before), and type it on the Usage,
SessionStats and session.usage contracts (regenerated).

fix(usage-window): do not /retry a turn that ran while the limit-offer switch resolved

Greptile: "Delayed offers retry newer work". The offer checked the run
generation before _accept_usage_limit_switch, but the switch awaits source
normalisation, model resolution and the commit; a turn that finished during
those awaits was the one /retry rewound. Carry the refused turn's
(session_key, run_generation) into the retry dispatch and re-check it with no
await before the /retry. The switch itself stands.

fix(usage-window): carry the refusal marker through the gateway turn projection

Greptile: "Gateway drops the refusal marker". TurnRunner.run_sync copied
usage_limit but not usage_window_message, so the authority message.complete
built the generic billing card instead of the window card, and the chat
refusal rewording never fired. Add it to _FAILURE_DESCRIPTOR_KEYS.

test(usage-window): pin the 402/403 credits capture by behaviour

Greptile: "Hook test checks source text". The test read
handle_api_error's source with inspect.getsource and matched strings
(banned by tests/AGENTS.md). It now drives the real handle_api_error with
a real AIAgent and a refused request, stopping the turn right after the
hook, and checks the capture runs (marked refused) only for a Nous
402/403 carrying usage-window headers: not for another provider, a
credit-grant account or a 5xx. Mutations of the provider gate, the
window gate or the capture call each turn it red.

fix(usage-window): keep an allowance whose reset is unknown

Greptile: "Unknown resets hide valid gauges". parse_gauges accepts a valid
allowance with an unknown reset, but _bp_window dropped the row because the
reset was not an int; with every reset unknown, build_nous_credits_snapshot
fell back to the dollar view and lost the window plan. The row now keeps
its percent with reset_at=None, which every renderer already shows as no
reset phrase (the same shape other providers' windows use).

fix(usage-window): retry a plan sync the refresh did not fix

Greptile: "Stale snapshots stop future refreshes". After its first refresh a
mismatch was suppressed until the headers and snapshot agreed again, but the
Portal can lag (the refresh returns the same stale gauges) and a failed
fetch is reported as source="error" without raising, so that mismatch was
never refreshed again while cache-only pickers kept the old snapshot. The
guard now expires after a bounded retry interval, and an error result
clears it like a raised failure does.

fix(usage-window): suggest free models from this profile's own Portal

Greptile: "Suggestions use another Portal's cache". _portal_free_models took
the last nonempty entry of the whole recommended-models cache, which is
keyed by (profile, Portal), so a process serving several profiles could
put another profile's free pick on a limit card. Read the caller's own
(profile, Portal) entry, else that Portal's disk copy in this profile's home.

fix(usage-window): name the allowance that stopped this model

Greptile: "Regular models get monthly resets". A full Large-model allowance
won the limit line, retry time and pool bench even when the refused model
is not top tier and its daily allowance is also full, so the line said
"monthly large-model limit · resets in 30 days" while limit_hit (the card)
said "daily". The stop line, window_stop_resets_at_ms and the pool's
reset_at now take the gauge from plan_limits.blocking_gauge with the
model's top-tier mark, the same rule limit_hit reads; a refusal no
all-scope allowance explains still falls back to the top-tier one.

fix(desktop): fresh Windows hosts can unpack Electron 40.10.3+ without the VC++ redist

From 40.10.3 on, every Electron line unpacks its binary with
@electron-internal/extract-zip, an MSVC-built binding that imports
VCRUNTIME140.dll. A Windows host that never installed the VC++
Redistributable has no copy, so install.js dies with ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED.
This is the failure that made bb8280b7537 roll Electron back to 40.10.2.

Our Python ships vcruntime140.dll. source_build_env() passes its path to
the Node builders as HERMES_VC_RUNTIME, and electron-runtime.mjs copies it
beside the extractor's binding right before it runs install.js. Node
loads bindings with LOAD_WITH_ALTERED_SEARCH_PATH (libuv uv_dlopen), so
Windows finds that copy first. This is the same app-local copy
fdea3e92e01 ships beside ARM64 rg.exe.

Clean Windows Sandbox (ARM64, no redist), Node 26.7.0, electron 44.9.3:
- before: install.js exits 1, "Cannot find native binding", ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED
- after: install.js exits 0, dist/electron.exe --version prints v44.9.3

fix(desktop): prepare the locked Electron runtime explicitly before use

Electron 42 dropped the postinstall that unpacked its binary into
node_modules/electron/dist. The binary now appears on the first
require('electron'), so parallel vitest workers race to unpack it
("Text file busy" in #128267's CI), and `hermes desktop --source` finds
no path.txt to launch.

electron-runtime.mjs runs Electron's own install.js once: after npm ci
for the desktop workspace, and in CI before the parallel checks. It first
checks the installed package against the desktop pin and the lockfile,
and does nothing when the runtime is already in place. On the current
40.10.2 pin, whose postinstall still unpacks the binary, it is a no-op.

Salvaged from #137648 (the runtime-preparation subset only).

fix(guardrails): no exact-replay warning on a throttled retry after earlier failures

Review follow-up: when the same call had already failed twice for an ordinary
reason, a later rate-limited result kept the old exact-args count and still drew
the "stop retrying unchanged" warning. A throttled result now never gets that
warning; the per-tool cap still bounds it.

fix(guardrails): retrying a rate-limited call is not counted as a replay

A throttled read retried after its cooldown is the correct move, but the
exact-args failure streak counted it like any identical failure: from the
second attempt the result carried "This looks like a loop; ... change strategy
instead of retrying it unchanged", steering the model away from a valid retry
(seen with Slack MCP rate limits behind an enterprise connector).

A failed result that says it was throttled (a retry_after field, a 429 status,
or rate-limit wording in its error) no longer advances the exact-args streak.
It still counts toward same_tool_failure, so an endpoint that never recovers is
warned at 3 and halted at 8 on unattended platforms, as before.

fix(api_server): a budget-exhausted chat turn reports "length", not "cancelled"

When a turn hits agent.max_turns, Hermes still makes one toolless call and
returns the agent's wrap-up of what it found. /v1/chat/completions mapped that
result (completed=false, not interrupted, no error) through the not-completed
fallback to finish_reason "cancelled" with hermes.error_code "agent_error", a
code reserved for user interrupts (f48d09563b3). An integration that treats
"cancelled" as an abort discards a usable answer.

Budget exits (turn_exit_reason max_iterations_reached(...) / budget_exhausted)
now report finish_reason "length" with hermes.error_code
"iteration_budget_exhausted", streaming and non-streaming. Interrupted turns
keep "cancelled"; real failures keep "error". /v1/responses already reports
status "incomplete" for this case and is unchanged.

The yes/no is a full-screen menu that hid the "Found on this computer: ..." lines printed before it,
so "Import your setup from any of them?" pointed at text the user could not see. prompt_yes_no
takes a description (the menu already rendered one) and the step passes the detection lines.

The plugin install is brief (one catalog line plus the outcome), and the import runs with the
plugin's --from-setup (hermes-official-plugins#159), so it does not tell the user to run
`hermes setup` from inside setup and folds OpenClaw's skipped items into one line.

fix(plugins): no "restart the gateway" after an install when no gateway exists; brief install for setup

`hermes plugins install/enable` printed "Restart the gateway for the plugin to take effect" whenever
no gateway answered the reload, including when none runs or is installed for the profile (every
first-time `hermes setup`): a gateway started later loads the plugin at boot. The hint now needs a
live gateway pid for the profile (or the root serving it) or an installed gateway service.

`cmd_install(brief=True)` is for a caller that already said what it installs and why (setup's
agent-import step): the catalog pin line, prompts, warnings, errors and the outcome still print;
the ~20-line catalog description, the clone line and the default "Installed" panel do not.

fix: python -m hermes_cli.main --profile default no longer lands in the sticky profile

Hermes spawns its own CLI as `python -m hermes_cli.main`. Run that way the
module executes as __main__, and a later `import hermes_cli.main` loads a
second copy whose import-time _apply_profile_override sees the argv the
first one already stripped and HERMES_HOME at the root, so it follows a
sticky active_profile: `--profile default` (setup's import child,
spawn_unmanaged_gateway's root selector) ran in the other profile. The
__main__ module now registers itself as hermes_cli.main before the
override runs, so the later import reuses it.

fix: setup's import runs in the profile it set up, and a refused enable no longer ends setup

The import child got HERMES_HOME but no profile selector, so on the root
home its _apply_profile_override followed a sticky active_profile into
another profile: the import failed there (no plugin) or wrote into the
wrong profile. A root home now passes --profile default, as
spawn_unmanaged_gateway does.

Enabling an installed-but-disabled agent-importers raises AdmissionRefused
when PM cannot admit it; only SystemExit was caught, so the refusal ended
the whole wizard. It is now caught like the install's exit: the import is
skipped with a warning and setup goes on.

fix: `hermes auth import-agent` no longer suggests a nonexistent login command

The agent-importers row used `cli`, the field for a plugin command that
replaces core's `hermes auth <cli>` login, so `hermes auth import-agent`
answered "is now `hermes import-agent login`". `hermes import-agent` is
core's own top-level command kept under its name: that is `command`
(without an `old_command`), which the top-level hint already matches.

fix: a scheduled hermes import-agent --sync installs the plugin on a home nothing migrated

A home with sync sources (import-sync.json) that upgraded without
`hermes update` (a Docker image swap) has no agent-importers plugin, and
when the scheduled `hermes import-agent --sync` is its only Hermes process
no agent or gateway start ever runs the left-core recovery: every run
failed with the moved-command hint. A command a left-core plugin registers
now runs that recovery for the active home before plugin commands are
discovered (same lazy-install policy and backoff), so the install lands and
the command runs in the same invocation.

refactor: OpenClaw migration leaves core too; first-time setup offers the agent-importers plugin

moved into the agent-importers plugin (hermes-official-plugins #140/#141), which
