fix(pm): a plugin whose pyproject installs nothing no longer rebuilds the dependency environment

Enabling or updating a plugin whose pyproject.toml declares `dependencies = []` (the official
agent-importers plugin) ran "Resolving / Installing Python dependencies" and built a new
environment generation although nothing gets installed, and every update of the plugin did it
again.

Workspace membership keyed on "has a pyproject", so such a plugin became a uv workspace member,
and members_stamp hashes a member's whole tree into the venv stamp: enabling it, or any change to
its files, made the recorded environment stale. A plugin is now a member only when it installs
packages (`PythonDeclaration.installs_packages`, the predicate dependency consent already uses
since the sibling fix for the empty consent step), so membership, requires-python checks and the
stamp all follow what the plugin actually puts in the environment.

Test fixtures that used a dep-less pyproject as a cheap stand-in for a member now declare a real
dependency (a local wheel through tool.uv.sources, resolvable offline, or a requirement where no
resolution runs); their assertions are unchanged. New: enabling a `dependencies = []` plugin
through the real admission path keeps the selected generation and recorded stamp, a later change
to its files keeps the venv current, and a plugin with a real dependency still joins.

test(pm): downloader connection-limit tests leave the active count before sending the body

test_fragmented_resume_obeys_connection_limit read `maximum == 2` with
connections=1 (main run 37594754436). The fake server decremented `active` in a
`finally` AFTER wfile.write: once the client has the bytes it opens its next
sequential gap, so a handler thread descheduled between the write and the
decrement overlapped the next request on the counter alone. Decrement right after
the release wait, before the body; a genuinely concurrent request has already
entered while the first sat on the release, so overlap is still caught.

The two-process sibling (test_processes_share_partial_ownership_...) had the same
write-then-decrement shape; fixed the same way.

fix: safe-mode and config-only chats refuse a removed folder instead of parking their queue

Safe-mode and config-only sessions run turns in a managed worker. A
removed folder crashed that worker inside its policy scope; the worker
reported only managed_worker_failed, which the owner treats as a LOST
execution: the admission settled unknown and every later message stayed
queued behind it, even after the folder came back.

The managed ingress route (admit_managed) now checks workspace readiness
before any worker exists and settles the same stamped, never-run failure
the in-process runner does. workspace_ready / workspace_unavailable_result
move to gateway/session_policy.py so policy_scope, TurnRunner and the
managed route share one predicate and one result; execute_managed (the
spawn phase tests drive directly) is unchanged.

Real-gateway test: safe-mode session, folder removed -> terminal/failed
naming the folder with zero model calls; folder restored -> the next
message completes. Red on the previous head with ('unknown', None).
Found by an independent review of #143075.

fix: a refused turn never drives /goal or a /loop --until judge

Live: in a session whose folder is gone, /goal burned its whole 20-turn
budget in ~40 s. Every continuation was refused, yet the classic CLI's
goal hook judged the previous (stale) assistant reply each time and
re-queued, one judge model call per refusal. The gateway hook (Desktop,
TUI on the shared gateway, messaging) would judge the refusal text, since
a failed turn now settles with text. A /loop --until tick likewise graded
stale or refusal text on every tick.

Both hooks now follow the TUI's existing rule (_is_successful_goal_turn):
a failed turn is no evidence. The classic CLI records _last_turn_failed
next to _last_turn_interrupted and skips the goal judge; the gateway reads
the owner's captured result (execution_result) and skips the goal hook.
/loop ticks are still released and rescheduled, with no text, so --until
never grades a refusal and the loop heals by itself once the folder is
back. The goal stays active (0 turns spent) and resumes on the next real
turn.

fix: /compress and /btw name the missing folder too

The workspace refusal now carries field=cwd, detail=<path>, but two
error boundaries dropped it: the classic CLI's /compress printed the bare
GatewayRPCError (only the reason code) and the /btw side-agent worker
published only exc.reason. /compress now goes through refusal_text (the
existing helper that prints field/detail from the RPC error data) and the
side worker appends (field: detail) when the refusal names them.

Live (Ink TUI, folder removed): [btw ...] error: workspace_unavailable
(cwd: <path>). Reported by Greptile on #143075.

fix: a chat whose working folder is gone says so instead of "model request failed"

A local session freezes its working directory; the owner's readiness gate
(policy_scope) refuses any turn whose frozen cwd no longer exists, by design.
But TurnRunner.run_sync let that RuntimeStoreError('workspace_unavailable')
escape as a raw exception into the generic agent-error handler, so every
surface showed an unexplained failure: the classic CLI printed "The model
request failed. Run /model ... / Details: Something went wrong", the
transcript gained a false "Some actions may already have run" row, and the
gateway logged a traceback per message. A classic `hermes -w` session whose
clean tree quit removed (or any folder deleted by hand) became a chat where
every message failed with no hint why.

run_sync now catches only that refusal on scope entry and settles the turn as
a failed, never-run result (api_calls 0) with its own copy naming the missing
folder and the way out (recreate it, `/worktree new` in the CLI, Move to
project in Desktop), stamped failure_reason workspace_unavailable /
failure_retryable false: the same shape the model-resolution failure path
uses. The refusal carries field=cwd, detail=<path> so other paths that
surface it name the folder too. agent/error_surface maps the code to the
gateway layer (no "Switch provider"), and Desktop gets its own error-card
copy with Retry + Start new chat.

Copy lands in all 17 gateway catalogs and the 9 Desktop catalogs carrying
error codes. The over-cap Desktop catalogs offset the growth by moving their
error-card tables into topical siblings (<lang>_error_layers.ts as en already
does, en/ru_error_codes.ts).

feat(desktop): install with +, switch once installed; tier badges on the install dialog (#142708)

* fix(desktop): catalog card actions sit above the card-wide hit area

On compact and hero cards the action slot comes before the title button,
whose ::after stretches over the whole card and painted on top of it, so
clicks on the switch or + opened the details instead.

* feat(desktop): install catalog entries with +, switch only once installed

Install is one-way, so it is now a + button instead of a switch that also
meant enable/disable. Installed entries keep their on/off switch. Featured
cards and the detail spell it out as "+ Install". A plugin's Uninstall
moves from the header trash icon to a labelled row at the bottom of its
detail.

* feat(plugins): badge the install dialog with the catalog tier

The dialog called every catalog pick Verified. It now says Official,
Verified or Community. plugins.catalog.lookup returns the tier so
hermes://plugin/install?catalog= links badge the same as in-app picks.

* refactor(desktop): plugin Uninstall row is its own component

Keeps PackageRow under its code-health complexity cap.

* chore(i18n): regenerate desktop locale keys for catalog.install

* fix(desktop): "Install here" badges the catalog tier too

The third way into the install dialog opened it with a catalog name but no
tier, so a community package still read Verified. Read the tier from the
cached catalog by name; uncached keeps the generic badge. Also note why the
catalog path passes entry.source as the tier.
plugin-catalog: re-pin agent-importers to b5932f1 (setup-run imports read as part of setup; OpenClaw workspace → terminal.cwd)

fix(config): config set/get still recognise terminal.singularity_image

The key left DEFAULT_CONFIG with the backend, but the singularity plugin reads it
and its setup text says `hermes config set terminal.singularity_image <image>`;
set and get now flagged it "not a recognized config key ... Hermes may not read
it". A seeded default would hide the plugin's TERMINAL_SINGULARITY_IMAGE fallback,
so _validate_config_key accepts left_core_migration.LEFT_CORE_TERMINAL_KEYS (the
renamed RETIRED_TERMINAL_ENV_COPIES, which unset already consults) instead.

The wrong-prefix refusal text moves to hermes_cli/config_key_notices.py to keep
config.py under its line cap.

Review: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/142561#pullrequestreview (kshitijk4poor, item 2)

fix(config): config unset terminal.singularity_image still removes its .env copy

While core shipped the backend, `hermes config set terminal.singularity_image`
also wrote TERMINAL_SINGULARITY_IMAGE to .env (TERMINAL_CONFIG_ENV_MAP), and the
plugin still falls back to that copy. Dropping the key from the runtime bridge
also dropped it from `config unset`, so a reset removed only the YAML and the old
image came back instead of the default. left_core_migration.RETIRED_TERMINAL_ENV_COPIES
keeps the cleanup without restoring the bridge.

Review: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/142561#discussion_r4345291204

fix(left-core): singularity_in_use expands dotenv references as load_hermes_dotenv does

load_hermes_dotenv expands ${VAR} / ${VAR:-default} before TERMINAL_ENV picks
the backend, so `HPC_BACKEND=singularity` + `TERMINAL_ENV=${HPC_BACKEND}` runs
Singularity. The predicate compared the raw text, said no, and the non-empty
reference also blocked the startup process-env fallback: update and startup
both skipped the plugin.

env_loader.resolve_home_dotenv returns what load_hermes_dotenv would publish
from a home's dotenv layers (home .env, then managed .env, both override),
read-only, through the same parser and resolution step the loader now shares
(_parse_dotenv_file, _dotenv_lookup_env, _resolve_dotenv_assignments).

Review: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/142561#discussion_r4343427764

fix(dashboard): validate a terminal backend pick inside the target profile's scope

PUT /api/tools/terminal/backend checked the name against the launch home's
plugin backends before config_write_scope switched to the requested profile,
while GET /api/tools/terminal/backends?profile= lists that profile's own. A
backend plugin installed only in a secondary profile (the singularity plugin,
now that the backend left core) was listed there and refused with 400 on
select. The check now runs in the same scope as the write.

Review: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/142561#discussion_r4343427772

fix(left-core): singularity_in_use reads the managed .env, and process env only for the launch home

- The dotenv layer is the home's .env with the administrator-managed .env
  applied last, as load_hermes_dotenv does: a managed TERMINAL_ENV=singularity
  over a home's TERMINAL_ENV=local runs Singularity, so the home needs the plugin.
- TERMINAL_* is process-global (get_secret never scopes it), so the startup
  fallback to the process env counted the launch profile's backend for every
  secondary home the gateway serves. It now applies to the launch home only.

fix(terminal): a plugin backend in the plugin host refuses with the isolation setting

Under plugins.isolation: host a user terminal backend's create_environment()
ran in the host and its environment came back as an Opaque placeholder, so the
first command failed with a backwards 'not available inside the plugin host'
AttributeError and the host was left holding a sandbox nothing could clean up.
Pre-existing for every plugin terminal backend; the Singularity move makes it
reachable for Singularity users who run host isolation.

Creating the environment now refuses before the host starts anything, naming
plugins.isolation: in_process (the Bot Desktop placement refusal's shape).

refactor: move the Singularity terminal backend out of core into the singularity catalog plugin

The Singularity/Apptainer backend (tools/environments/singularity.py) now ships
as the official 'singularity' plugin in NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins,
registered through the terminal-environment provider seam under the same
backend name and config keys (terminal.backend: singularity,
terminal.singularity_image / TERMINAL_SINGULARITY_IMAGE, terminal.container_*).

- 'singularity' leaves BUILTIN_BACKEND_NAMES so the plugin can register it;
  every hardcoded classification set drops it (the provider declares
  is_remote/is_container/supports_streams instead).
- LEFT_CORE gains a singularity row: homes whose terminal.backend (or .env
  TERMINAL_ENV) is singularity get the catalog plugin once, on hermes update
  or agent/gateway start. An unknown-backend error for 'singularity' names
  the install command (new row field terminal_backend).
- A plugin backend receives its per-task '<backend>_image' override; batch
  runs register one for the active backend.
- BaseEnvironment's sudo-probe knob is renamed _passwordless_sudo_probe_supported:
  plugin backends set it, and the old spelling trips the install scanner.
- Core's scratch-dir disk warning and process-exit sweep were Singularity-only
  and move to the plugin; the singularity setup row, dashboard probe/row and
  config defaults/bridges go too. Docs point at the plugin.

fix(dashboard): resolve a channel's platform inside the target profile's scope

PUT /api/messaging/platforms/<id> and POST .../<id>/test looked the platform up
(plus its env-value rules and authz env names) in the launch profile's
platform registry before entering the requested profile's scope, while
GET /api/messaging/platforms?profile= builds the target profile's catalog. A
platform plugin installed only in a secondary profile was listed there and
refused with 404 on edit and test; a plugin only the launch profile has passed
the check and applied its env allowlist to the other profile's .env. The
lookups now run in the target scope, where the catalog build materializes that
profile's entries, so its value rules still apply.

fix(dashboard): validate toolset names inside the target profile's scope

The toolset routes (PUT /api/tools/toolsets/<ts>, GET .../config, PUT
.../provider, PUT .../env, POST .../post-setup) ran _require_known_toolset on
the event loop before entering the requested profile's scope, so the name was
checked against the launch profile's plugin toolsets while
GET /api/tools/toolsets?profile= lists the target profile's own. A plugin
toolset installed only in a secondary profile (spotify, homeassistant, ...)
was listed there and refused with 400 Unknown toolset on every edit. The check
now runs in the same scope as the work; the post-setup route also checks its
key (plugin providers' post_setup keys are per profile) in that scope.

fix(gateway): authority auth-failure cards keep their sign-in / update-key action

Most failed turn results (agent/turn_recovery._failed_turn_result and the
other early exits) name no provider or model, so the descriptor the
authority built for message.complete had no auth_kind / api_key_env and the
Desktop's auth card offered no action. The TUI path reads both from the
agent; the authority now does too.

- run_turn_runner: the projection records the agent's provider beside its
  model (a result that names one still wins).
- managed_worker: the worker's result frame carries the agent's provider and
  model unless the result already names them.

fix(gateway): failed authority turns carry the error_surface the TUI sends

A turn that failed on the session authority completed with status 'error'
and no error_surface, so the Desktop showed the generic card (with a Retry
that fails again against a full free tier) instead of free_tier_at_capacity,
rate_limit with its reset time, auth, and so on.

- run_turn_runner: the projection keeps free_tier, failure_retryable and
  failure_resets_at, the fields build_error_surface_from_result reads.
- session_settlement_recovery.completion_payload: every failed completion
  builds the descriptor from its result; a gateway refusal's prebuilt one
  (session_cron) still wins.
- managed_worker: the worker result frame carries the same fields, with
  free_tier validated like billing_block.

fix(gateway): a Desktop chat saved before the local mark moved still resumes and runs as local work

main stamped desktop_local into a Desktop chat's frozen create request; d838333682 moved the mark to
the policy's own config. For a chat main saved, the Desktop's exact retry after a reconnect (which
never sends the key) was refused as invalid_params, and its turns no longer ran as work for the local
Desktop.

client_request drops desktop_local from the saved request, since the owner stamped it and no client
can send it (CREATE_FIELDS refuses it). local_desktop_turn reads the mark from either place.

fix(gateway): a resume reading history while a fresh launch claims the chat keeps it

attach took a fresh launch's claim back before prepare_history, which yields to a worker thread. A
resume could pass the take-back before any claim existed, pause while the start found the chat
unwatched and claimed it, then join; the claim stood and the settle write deleted the reopened chat.

The take-back now runs after attach's last other await and never yields itself, so the viewer joins
in the same loop step: the start (which claims only on the loop) either claimed first and the claim
is taken back, or sees the viewer and claims nothing. A delete in flight still holds the lock across
its write; the take-back waits for it off the loop and retries, and the re-check answers not_found.

test(tui_gateway): the fresh-launch onboarding tests start as the local Desktop

onboarding.start's claim path refuses (5080) outside the local Desktop since d838333682. These
fixtures never bound serving_local_desktop the way the Desktop's declared socket does, so all three
tests got the refusal. The client fixture now binds it, as test_onboarding_session's does; the gate
is unchanged.
test(gateway): the sidebar-delete test resends on a revision conflict, as the Desktop does

fix(gateway): a window that reopens the old onboarding chat keeps it from the fresh launch's delete

A fresh launch's onboarding.start chose the chats to delete (no live viewer) on the loop, then
deleted them in the settle write. A session.resume finishing during that write attached a viewer
to a chat the stale choice still deleted.

The chosen chats are now claims on the authority. attach takes a claim back before the viewer
joins, and the settle write deletes a chat only while its claim stands; one lock covers the
take-back and the delete, so a resume either keeps the chat (its run ends as replaced) or meets
the committed delete as not_found. The take-back waits off the loop, since a delete in flight
holds the lock across its write.

fix(cron,kanban): a claimed welcome trial runs cron jobs and Kanban workers on a fresh install (review)

The trial's free model was a fallback only ordinary session.create calls reached. A fresh install that claimed the trial has no model.default, so a default cron job refused with "no model configured" and a Kanban worker's launch policy carried an empty model that restore_policy rejected as storage_unavailable.

The trial is now the last rung of model resolution (anon_auth.trial_model): _resolve_gateway_model falls back to it, which covers session.create, Kanban workers and every other gateway reader, and the cron ladder ends on it below HERMES_MODEL. It is never written to config.yaml, so a configured model wins at once. A chat created on the trial model keeps its FOLLOW_ADOPTED mark.

fix(desktop): reconnects keep their chat, trial chats move to a connected provider, a failed boot retries, only the Desktop starts a first run (review)

A Desktop chat's local mark lives in the policy's own config, not the frozen create request: an exact retry from a socket whose declaration has not landed resumes the chat, and launch_request no longer echoes it.
A chat created on the welcome trial's model follows its profile (FOLLOW_ADOPTED), so the provider the user connects later replaces nous/welcome.
A bootstrap that could not record the install or settle the claim is retried on the local Desktop's next connection instead of only after a gateway restart.
onboarding.start's claim path refuses (5080) before writing onboarding.run unless the request serves the local Desktop, on the authority and the sidecar; a rerun from Settings is unchanged.

Merge pull request #142919 from NousResearch/sid/drop-serve-era-desktop-spawn

refactor(desktop): delete what only the Desktop's own hermes serve reached

fix: a failed onboarding turn shows the beat answer once

After an onboarding turn failed, a transcript refresh painted the user's
beat answer twice: once from storage and once in the kept local error
bubble, which still held the setup_beat tool part.

Desktop: a stored assistant sharing a tool call with the local error
bubble is that bubble's stored copy, so the error folds onto it instead of
re-appending the bubble (the hidden opening row left no visible turn to
anchor the existing match on). Hydration no longer merges a failed-turn
boundary row into the tool-call reply it follows, so its error card
survives and its notice is not painted as model text.

Backend: both failed-turn closers (agent/conversation_loop.py and
gateway/run_turn_persistence.py) also close a durable tail that is a tool
row, so a reload carries the error card. OPEN_TURN_TAIL_ROLES in
agent/turn_failure_copy.py names the open tails once for both.

refactor(desktop): read the readiness checks' failure sentences in one place

Keeps interpretRuntimeReadiness under its complexity cap (CI health ratchet).

fix(desktop): no CLI instructions in any readiness reason when nothing is set up (review)

When setup.status reports no provider and no provider was requested,
runtime-readiness now returns the caller's default reason in both the
runtime_check and setup_status branches, instead of the check's own
sentence (hermes model, hermes auth add, the home path). The picker,
the gateway menu, the status-bar tooltip and SDK callers all get it.

That removes the unconfigured flag and the store's override, which
let a stale state.reason (an earlier AuthError sentence) win over the
picker. onboarding.ts is back to its main shape. A requested provider
keeps its cause. The local-endpoint save test now uses the
provider_configured: true a saved custom endpoint actually reports.
chore: drop the comment the reason line already says

fix(desktop): keep terminal instructions off the provider picker

The provider picker showed the backend's "no provider" error word for word
in a banner: `hermes model`, `/login`, `hermes auth add <provider>` and the
user's home path, above a card that already says "connect a provider".

The banner hid that sentence by matching its words
(lib/provider-setup-errors.ts: "No inference provider configured").
23036e20a66 rewrote the backend sentence to "Hermes is not connected to
any AI provider yet. Run `hermes model` ...", the match stopped firing,
and the banner has shown it since.

Decide from what the readiness check reported instead of its wording:
when setup.status says no provider is set up at all, the check's sentence
only restates that, so the picker keeps its default (hidden) reason.
A configured provider that fails still shows its specific cause, and so
do transport failures.

fix(desktop): keep an older Desktop's dashboard fallback starting (review)

An older Desktop whose serve --help probe times out spawns
dashboard --no-open with its per-spawn token; dropping the exemption made
that backend pop its packaged dist and exit. Keep it while such builds can
meet this runtime.

chore: trim comments the code already says across the onboarding stack

Comment and docstring edits only (no code or assertion changes): bug
history in module docstrings, narration, cross-refs and test copies of
the handshake comment go; WHY comments on ordering, locking, the launch
profile scope and the old-backend wire constraint stay.

refactor(desktop): delete what only the Desktop's own `hermes serve` reached

Since the unified gateway (#106742) the local Desktop runs `hermes gateway
ensure` and attaches; it never spawns a local `hermes serve` again. What
only that spawn reached is removed:

Desktop main process
- getBackendArgsForRuntime / backendSupportsServe, backend-serve-support.ts,
  backend-command.ts: the local serve argv and its `serve --help` probe.
- spawnOwnedBackend / claimBackendChild and the claim-only half of
  backend-claim.ts (claimDecision, probeStartMarker, the output tail) and
  parent-process-identity's start-marker resolver. Orphan reaping and the
  ownership ledger readers stay.

Runtime
- The local Desktop is decided only by the connection
  (`process_identity.serving_local_desktop`); the env-token branch of
  is_local_desktop_backend, which only the local spawn satisfied, is gone,
  and with it the serve-boot first-install probe and due-answer boot that it
  gated (the gateway runs that boot when the Desktop first connects).
- The welcome-trial grandfathering for guests minted before the claim
  existed (grandfather_existing_guest, stamp_legacy_guest_claim).
- The `dashboard --no-open` legacy fallback exemption in
  _dashboard_sanitize_desktop_env.

The remote SSH `hermes serve` path (token file on argv) is untouched.

fix(free-tier): once claimed, the welcome trial runs every surface

The claim stays the local Desktop's (a fresh install, once per machine).
After it, cron, side agents, managed workers, the CLI and chats adopted
from older Desktop builds all run on nous/welcome instead of failing with
no provider: free_inference_active no longer asks which surface is
asking.

fix(desktop): run the Desktop's boot work for the launch profile

On a multiplexing gateway a Desktop connection runs in its own profile's
scope, and the boot thread copied it. A first connection for a named
profile built the launch profile's setup record and first-install latch
from that profile's home. The boot now binds the launch profile's scope.

fix(desktop): run the Desktop's boot work when it first connects to the gateway

`hermes serve` did first-launch work at boot when the Desktop spawned it:
record a fresh install (onboarding stays due and the trial stays
reserved when the first launch misses the run), settle a claim a crash
interrupted, build the setup record that setup.status and the claim
refresh read, and work out the due answer. The gateway never boots that
way, so on the unified gateway none of it ran: a new user who closed the
app or chatted before onboarding lost the trial on the next launch, and
refresh_record() after a claim did nothing.

The local Desktop's first accepted `client.capabilities {desktop_local}`
now starts that work, once per process, as work for that Desktop.

fix(desktop): give a fresh install its onboarding and free trial again

Since the unified gateway (#106742) the Desktop attaches to the shared
gateway instead of spawning its own `hermes serve`. Onboarding, the
welcome-trial claim and free inference decide "is this the Desktop app on
this machine?" from HERMES_DESKTOP and the spawn token in the process
environment, which the gateway never has. So `onboarding.state` answered
eligible:false for every new user, who landed on the provider picker with
no free account.

The answer now comes from the connection:

- The Desktop sends `client.capabilities {desktop_local: true}` first on
  every socket, as a call of its own, before the boot's first
  `onboarding.state` (the backend reads frames in order). An older backend
  refuses only that call and keeps the server_requests answer.
- The gateway counts it only on a native-ticket connection, so a remote or
  tunnelled client never gets the trial.
- Requests on that connection run under `serving_local_desktop(True)`, and
  a chat it creates records the declaration in its launch policy, so the
  chat's later turns run the same way (`local_desktop_turn`).
- A trial-only user has no configured model; a canonical chat freezes its
  model at creation, so the chat now freezes the free model
  (`_welcome_trial_model`) instead of refusing.

Live: a --fresh-install sandbox launch minted a guest account, opened the
onboarding chat and the free model answered.

fix(gateway): onboarding claims in the default home, skip takes profile, deleting the chat ends the run (review)

- Start from a secondary profile's host socket runs the default-profile start inside owner_scope(default), so the trial claim, provider check and chat policy read the default home.
- onboarding.skip validates with OnboardingSkipParams, accepting the profile key the Desktop sends.
- The canonical session.mutate delete of the chat holding the live run ends it (deleted) and announces onboarding.ended, via agent.onboarding_record.delete_chat.
- A fresh launch deletes every unfinished chat no window watches (recovered mounts included) under tracked_write, retires it from the authority, and withdraws the card of every replaced chat that survives.
fix(providers): allow external-process plugins to opt into streaming

test(desktop): the mounted group room clears its working indicator on settle

Keep the busy room mounted and flip the next groups.state poll to idle, so
a working line or roster spinner that never clears fails the test.

fix(desktop): gateway group chats show which bot is working again

Group chats moved to the gateway-owned room view with the unified gateway
runtime, and that view dropped the legacy room's "X is thinking..." line:
after sending, nothing said whether any bot had picked the message up.

The room header now marks each member that is answering (spinner) or
queued, and a status line under the log reads "Working: <names>". On a
gateway too old to report members it still says the group is working,
from the existing room-level flag.

fix(gateway): groups.state names the member answering a hosted room

Gateway-owned group rooms only reported a room-wide `working` flag, so a
client had no way to show which bot was busy. `HostedRoomService.status`
now returns `member_activity`: the room's live tasks (queued, running,
stopping) with their member, in admission order. `working` derives from
the same list. The field is optional in the contract, so older gateways
simply omit it.

Fixes #102196.

plugin-catalog: re-pin agent-importers to 2442ec1 (a fresh home no longer blocks the OpenClaw import)

hermes-official-plugins #149: Hermes seeds a default SOUL.md into every new
home, and the OpenClaw import treated it as a conflict and refused the whole
apply. A SOUL.md still holding Hermes' default (or an older seed) is now
replaced by OpenClaw's persona with the usual item backup; a SOUL.md the user
wrote is still a conflict. Only agent-importers/ changed between the pins.

fix(gateway): serve onboarding on the session authority

Run onboarding again (and the launch's first-run onboarding) failed on the unified gateway:
onboarding.start fell through to the old sidecar handler, which built its own live runtime
for the chat (session.resume + prompt.submit in the sidecar), so the window's session.resume
on that chat found it leased by another writer and was refused with
runtime_coordination_required. The greeting painted, the name card closed unanswered and
'Resume failed' toasted on every retry.

onboarding.start and onboarding.skip are now authority handlers (gateway/session_onboarding.py):
the chat is a local Desktop session the authority owns from its first row, the run record is
written before any agent is built, and the hidden opening is admitted through the durable
FIFO. The onboarding chat's per-session pieces move to agent/onboarding_session.py and both
runtimes use them: the onboarding toolset fold-in (on the authority keyed on the record
existing, so a finished run never changes the tool array mid-conversation), the scripted
greeting + name card, and the per-turn note. Skip withdraws the waiting setup_beat card
through the owner's server-request registry. A rerun with no model to run on opens no chat
(5080) instead of committing a session whose launch policy cannot be restored.
Merge branch 'NousResearch:main' into window-plans
PR review comments

fix(pm): judge overrides only against a complete pip-check report

An environment created with an output sink streams uv and keeps only
the last 2,000 characters, so a long `uv pip check` report could lose
its head: the "Found N" total and any unrelated failure printed before
2,000+ characters of override-covered lines. unexpected_incompatibilities
skipped the count check when the total was missing, so the surviving
lines read as fully explained and check() accepted a broken environment.

check() now runs pip check captured (it is a quiet step, so streaming
showed nothing anyway), and override exceptions are accepted only when
uv's "Found N" total is present and matches the lines parsed.

fix(deps): bump Pillow 12.3.0 → 13.0.0 (critical, GHSA-8g5g-8vmr-9782)

Pillow 13.0.0 fixes 28 advisories open against 12.3.0, three critical:
GHSA-8g5g-8vmr-9782 (heap overflow in ImagingJpegDecode),
GHSA-332p-7hrc-92wf (heap overflow saving TIFF to a buffer) and
GHSA-w889-685w-c8fh (Ghostscript argument injection), plus 16 high and
9 medium decoder/encoder memory-safety and DoS fixes. None has a 12.x
backport.

browser-harness 0.1.13, a core dependency and its latest release, pins
pillow==12.3.0 exactly, so the bump needs a uv override. The override
equals the direct pin (the existing contract for direct overrides).
browser-harness only opens, converts, composes, thumbnails and draws
images; its contact-sheet, masked-frame, thumbnail and click-overlay
output is pixel-identical under 12.3.0 and 13.0.0. pillow-heif stays
at 1.6.0 (requires pillow>=11.1.0); its HEIC round trip is identical
too. uv.lock changes only pillow.

An override installs a version the dependent's own metadata rejects, so
PM's install-time `uv pip check` failed every install (activate, pm
install/repair, fresh and bundle builds) with "browser-harness requires
pillow==12.3.0, but 13.0.0 is installed". check() now takes the uv.lock
the environment was installed from. pm/pip_check.py accepts a report
line only when that lock's [manifest] overrides name the dependency and
it is installed at the version the lock resolved. Missing packages,
other mismatches and any report it cannot fully parse still fail.
pm/pip_check.py is stdlib-only (with a tomllib-less fallback) because
the bootstrap runner loads pm.environment on older system pythons.

test_direct_overrides_preserve_the_declared_exact_version compared the
declared spelling (Pillow) with uv.lock's normalized names, so it found
no locked rows for the first capitalised override; it now compares
canonical names.

zephyr-cp: add the MacroPad RP2040
Merge branch 'main' into zephyr-cp-macropad-rp2040

zephyr-cp: MacroPad RP2040: CONSOLE=1 console on the STEMMA QT pins

A CONSOLE=1 or DEBUG=1 build puts the Zephyr console back on uart1, on
the STEMMA QT pins (TX on SDA/GPIO20, RX on SCL/GPIO21), and disables
i2c0, so board.I2C() and board.STEMMA_I2C are not available.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

zephyr-cp: MacroPad RP2040: I2C on the STEMMA QT connector

Upstream puts the Zephyr console on uart1, on GPIO20/21, which are the
STEMMA QT SDA/SCL pins. Remove the console, as the nRF52840 boards do,
and enable i2c0. The zephyr_i2c label makes it board.STEMMA_I2C as well

wifi.Monitor: track deinit per object, not globally

deinited() checked whether promiscuous mode was on, which is global. An
old, deinited Monitor whose __del__ ran while a newer one was live saw
"not deinited", turned promiscuous mode off and passed its NULL queue to
FreeRTOS, which hard faults. packet() and queued() on the old object did
the same.

deinited() now takes self, like every other deinited(), and checks the
object's own queue. deinit() clears the singleton, because the root
pointer outlives the VM heap and would otherwise be read in the next VM.
The rx callback skips packets while there is no singleton, which also
fixes a NULL dereference before the first Monitor is set and a payload
that was malloc'd for a queueless Monitor and never freed.

test(managed-agent): poll ToolTurn producers instead of waiting on onExit() (#15065)

* test(managed-agent): poll ToolTurn producers instead of waiting on onExit()

ProcessHandle.onExit() completes on the common ForkJoinPool, so the
producer wait after Broker shutdown could time out with a bare
TimeoutException for a worker that had already exited whenever the
shared Hosted fork kept that pool busy. The JVM-wide descendants()
snapshot could also pick up processes left by earlier classes in the
same fork, which this Broker never owned.

Snapshot only the descendants this run started, poll liveness instead
of waiting on onExit() (a zombie counts as stopped, as in the sibling
probes), and name the pid, parent, /proc state and command line when a
producer outlives the deadline.

Fixes #15049

* test(managed-agent): pin the producer drain in a unit test

Move the polling wait into a package-private HostedProcessLiveness so
the default surefire lane can exercise it, and take the zombie judgment
from HostedOperatorRecoveryProbe.statRunning rather than a private
/proc parse: a non-ENOENT stat failure on a live process now surfaces
as an IOException instead of a 10 s timeout that reads like #15049.
Without procfs the wait stays on isAlive(). The failure message keeps
its own bounds-guarded state read so a malformed stat cannot replace it.

HostedProcessLivenessTest covers a real unreaped zombie, a process that
outlives the deadline (pid, parent, state and command line named) and
an exited process; a new statRunning case pins the parse against
recorded kernel lines, including a ')' inside the command name.

test(managed-agent): pin the queue_one reachability (FG11d) (#15187)

* test(managed-agent): pin the queue_one reachability (FG11d)

The design record claims the queued-input arm is reachable under queue_one; this
cell is the witness. A second manual fire is admitted at one active run, its run
commits, and no prompt for its occurrence ever appears. The cancel half stays
open: measured here, a task cancel on that queued run is accepted and the run
stays running, because the queue is settled by the turn.

* test(managed-agent): align the queue_one assertions and mark the cancel half ungated (FG11d)

The active-run half of the reachability cell excluded one settled state fewer
than the queued half, so a run that had failed would still read as untouched.
Both halves now exclude the same three settled states.

The design record called the un-gated cancel half "(measured)", which reads as
if a witness exists in the tree. It now says "measured locally, not gated", the
same claim the PR body makes.

* test(managed-agent): observe the queue_one dwell and scope the record to what it proves (FG11d)

The negative rested on a single `isEmpty()` sampled one poll after the run row
committed, so an asynchronous dispatch of the queued input would land after the
assertion had already returned green. It now runs as a bounded dwell through
`waiting()`, keeping the failFast and lock-exception guard.

Both records cited the cell as pinning that no prompt appears, which attributes
the absence to the overlap arm. The first turn is parked, so the wake pump
cannot start the queued input under any policy; the records now say the cell
pins admission (its own run id and a `fired` occurrence) and only observes the
absence over a dwell.

test(managed-agent): keep the FG12d lifecycle cells' writer lease past the close window (#15068)

* test(managed-agent): keep the FG12d lifecycle cells' writer lease past the close window

Once a v2 close is admitted, the store fences ordinary writer renewals,
and the Harness renews under the claim only when the first lifecycle
phase reaches it (#15011). With the class's 3 s writer lease the client
renews every 1.5 s, so a fenced renewal can let the lease lapse before
the close's first claimed renewal, and effects then fails with "The
Managed Session writer grant is stale or unavailable." (about 4% of
close preambles in a repeated-preamble probe).

The two lifecycle cells that keep their Harness now use a 30 s writer
lease; cases that kill the Harness keep 3 s so the replacement can take
over the killed writer.

* test(managed-agent): use one writer lease for the whole FG12d class

Review follow-up. The per-case 30 s lease left
harnessKillDuringReleaseResumesTheOriginalReleaseOnMySql exposed: its
close preamble runs on a live Harness before the kill, so it still met
the #15011 window at 3 s. Give every case a 30 s writer lease, and have
killHarness() expire the dead writer's lease row so the replacement
takes over at once instead of waiting the lease out. This removes the
per-case switch and its misleading constant names.

Rewrite Decision 2 of the R1-1 cell in both design docs for the new
lease: the inactive-writer retry is opportunistic coverage, the
accepted retry codes are the recorded contract, and the exact wire
assertion still binds any unsettled attempt. The writer lease section
now names the route code next to the store message and records the
probe rates on both hosts and the injected-gap result.

* test(managed-agent): scope the FG12d lease expiry to the dead writer and assert it

killHarness() expired every lease row of the tenant and did not check
that it matched anything, so a silently broken UPDATE only showed up as
each Harness-kill case waiting out the 30 s lease. Scope the update to
the killed Harness's writer id and assert that it expired at least one
lease.

Record the second 2.5 s gap measurement (3 of 6) next to the first
(4 of 6) in the FG12d design note.

* test(managed-agent): assert the FG12d dead writer's leases lapsed

killHarness() asserted that its UPDATE matched a lease of the dead
writer, but not that the lease ended up in the past: moving it 30 s
ahead instead still passed, with each Harness-kill case waiting out the
lease. Also assert that no lease of the dead writer is still live.

leaves other writers' leases alone (not other Sessions'), and record

feat(managed-agent): read the Harness credentials from one file (#15063)

* feat(managed-agent): read the Harness credentials from one file

The Hosted Harness and the control plane share a bearer token and a
capability digest, which the reference distribution stored twice, in
harness.env and server.env, so every rotation or hand edit had to change
both files identically.

QWEN_MANAGED_AGENT_HARNESS_CREDENTIALS_FILE now names the Harness's own
environment file. The control plane reads QWEN_SERVER_TOKEN and
QWEN_HOSTED_HARNESS_CAPABILITY_DIGEST from it into its configuration,
never into its process environment, and refuses to start when the file
is combined with a direct token or digest, or lacks either key.
Preflight reports the file's permissions and points credential fixes at
it. The bootstrap, templates, systemd instructions and guide store the
credentials once.

* fix(managed-agent): refuse credential lines the Harness reads differently

The credentials parser accepted a subset of the environment-file grammar
and silently mis-read the rest. A continuation, an escape, an
unterminated quote, text after a closing quote or a `$` expansion gave
the control plane a different value than systemd or a shell gave the
Harness, while preflight passed. Such lines now fail startup, naming
the file and line but never the content.

The file is now read once and only while the Harness is enabled, and an
unreadable file reports its exception type in the validation row.
Preflight shares one secret-file permission policy between the config
and credentials rows. The credentials row also fails an unreadable file
and reports an unusable path instead of aborting, and the harness row
fails the shipped placeholder token.

Tests now pin the run order, values containing `=`, world-readable
files, the file-aware 401 fix and the shipped harness.env.example keys.
The systemd READMEs describe the warning as a warning.

* fix(managed-agent): accept only credential lines both readers take literally

Credential values in the Harness credentials file may now contain only
letters, digits and ._:/+=-, and whitespace around `=` or a carriage
return is refused: a shell runs `KEY = value` as a command and keeps a
trailing \r, so the control plane and the Harness could hold different
digests while every preflight row passed.

When startup refuses the file, the harness row now skips its probe
instead of sending whatever credentials are left bound, and the file is
applied atomically. run() delegates to checks(args) so a test can pin
the credentials row after the harness row.

api.anthropic.com requests carrying two or more tools were rejected with

every native request into a hard failure rather than a cache miss.

feat(core): gate scheduled tasks on a shell command run outside the model (#15069)

* feat(core): gate scheduled tasks on a shell command run outside the model

A scheduled task can carry a `gate`: a shell command the scheduler runs
at each fire before the prompt reaches the session. Silence skips the
fire with no model turn; output delivers the fire with the output
attached as data; a failure is reported once per streak and counted.

The gate runs inside CronScheduler so every fire kind and every consumer
(TUI, ACP, headless, daemon-bound sessions) shares one path. It is
confirmed like a Monitor command when the task is created and checked
again against the session's approval mode and permission rules at fire
time. Durable tasks persist the gate together with a downgrade fuse in
the legacy `condition` field, so an older binary withholds the task
instead of firing it unconditionally every slot.

Also routes cron fires away from the composer's shell mode in the TUI.

Design: docs/design/2026-10-21-scheduled-task-gate.md
Refs #15056

* fix(core): normalize the gate rule hint and refuse a gate on a one-shot task

The rule a blocked fire suggests is now derived from the same normalized
command the cron_create dialog offers and the permission manager matches,
so a wrapper-style gate such as `bash -c "./probe.sh"` names
`Monitor(./probe.sh *)` rather than a `bash *` rule that never matches.

A one-shot task has no next slot, so a quiet gate would consume it with
nothing delivered and no trace; cron_create now refuses `gate` with
`recurring: false` and says why, and the design records the rule.

* fix(core): close the gate's permission, cancellation and lifetime gaps

Review of the gate found seven ways a gated task could run, keep running or
stall when it should not. All seven are closed here.

- An explicit `Monitor(...)`/`Bash(...)` deny rule now blocks the gate in
  every approval mode: the runner evaluates the command before the yolo/auto
  shortcut, the way an ordinary tool call is denied before the mode approves
  it, so a persisted gate stops the moment the rule is saved.
- In auto mode a bare `cron_create` allow rule takes the allow fast path
  around the classifier, so nobody looked at the command. `cron_create` now
  detects that case (a tool-only permission lookup answering `allow`) and
  holds the gate to the default-mode check: a `Monitor(...)`/`Bash(...)` rule
  or the read-only command, else the call is refused.
- A manual run of a gated task has no scheduler in the loop and used to
  dispatch the raw prompt. The daemon's per-run `/run` and the Web Shell's
  "Run now" now send a manual-run prompt that asks the model to run the gate
  itself first and stop when it prints nothing; the task view carries `gate`
  and `gateStatus` so the client can do that for a tool-created task.
- A gate's output goes to the consumer installed when it settles, not when
  it started: ACP re-installs its callback through `start()` after every
  turn, and that used to drop a gate that was mid-run. Only `stop()` ends
  the subscription, and it aborts the gate.
- A tasks-file reload that drops, disables or rewrites a job now aborts its
  running gate, as `delete()` does, instead of letting the command finish
  and discarding the result.
- A quiet final gate no longer pins a headless run: `sessionSize` counts a
  session-only one-shot or final fire until its gate settles, and a new
  `setGateSkippedListener` reports settlements that deliver nothing so the
  hold-open is re-checked.
- A gated catch-up persists its `lastFiredAt` stamp at once but books its run
  only when the gate delivers, as a `catch-up` run, instead of recording a
  run that reached no session and a second one on delivery.

Tests cover each case (runner, tool, scheduler, headless run, daemon route,
run prompt, Web Shell dialog); the design docs and the user guide describe
the new rules.

* fix(core): match the gate's auto-mode lookup to the permission flow and tighten the manual-run text

- In auto mode `cron_create` asked the permission manager about the tool
  name alone to tell whether an allow rule had skipped the classifier. A
  rule scoped to the call's parameters (`cron_create(prompt:…)`) takes the
  same fast path but matched only the real flow's context, so the gate was
  accepted unreviewed. The lookup now evaluates the same context the flow
  built for this call (`buildPermissionCheckContext` with the tool params),
  pinned by a test with a real permission manager.
- The manual-run prompt told the model to follow the task whenever the gate
  printed something, so partial output before a failure counted. It now
  follows the task only on exit 0 with output, reports the gate printed
  nothing on a silent exit 0, and reports the failure and stops on a
  non-zero exit, a timeout or a cancellation — the runner's three outcomes.
  The Web Shell copy, the tests and the docs say the same.

* fix(core): refuse a denied gate at creation and show the gate exactly as it runs

`cron_create` now evaluates the gate as a `monitor` command before any
other check, so an explicit `Monitor(...)`/`Bash(...)` deny refuses the
call in every mode, a confirmed dialog included. The runner already
checks that deny first at each fire, so such a task could only ever be
blocked.

The exec dialog showed Monitor's re-spelled spawn command while the
scheduler persists and runs the trimmed gate. They differed for a gate
whose wrapper script ends in `&` (`bash -c './probe.sh &'`), which the
background check let through: the dialog showed `bash -c './probe.sh'`
and every fire would have detached the probe. That gate is now refused
at validation, and the dialog shows the persisted string itself.

The design doc's approval section said the tool's default permission
followed Monitor's read-only check; it is `ask` unconditionally.

* fix(core): hold headless runs for running gates and close the wrapper-& gap

- Headless: the hold-open also waits for a gate still running, durable
  ones included. A durable catch-up flushed by start() is stamped before
  its gate decides, so stopping the scheduler there aborted the gate and
  lost the slot (`CronScheduler.hasGatesInFlight`).
- Validation: `backgroundsAnyPart` looks for a shell wrapper behind any
  prefix the Monitor parser does not unwrap (`nohup`, `sudo -u ci`,
  `command`, `env FOO=1`) and checks its script, nested scripts too, so
  `nohup bash -c './probe.sh &'` is refused like `bash -c './probe.sh &'`.
- Runner: the 16 KiB cap cuts on a character boundary instead of leaving
  a lone lead byte that decodes to U+FFFD; binary output stops the
  command and fails the fire instead of settling quiet with nothing kept.
- Web Shell: pin the manual-run prompt to the same literal as the daemon
  copy, so the two cannot drift apart; drop the test-only export.

* fix(core): re-check headless completion after a cancelled gate

A delete or disk reload that cancels the last running gate left the
headless run waiting: the cancelled settlement returned before reaching
the gate-skipped listener, so nothing re-checked the hold-open that
hasGatesInFlight() had kept open. The settlement now reports to the
listener (still delivering nothing) unless stop() cancelled it.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* fix(ci): keep a parked lock head's ticket alive under fast priority

A head blocked in `flock --wait` could not touch its ticket, so once a
hold outlasted the 1800s mtime arm another waiter reaped a live head and
the next ticket, whatever its class, parked in the kernel too. With two
classes that lets normal tickets take kernel positions ahead of fast
tickets that arrive later during a long hold. A keepalive now refreshes
the parked head's ticket at the waiters' two-second cadence; it closes
the lock fd and uses `touch -c`, so it can neither hold the lock nor
recreate a removed ticket.

The ordering and promotion cases used a stub whose `--wait` returned
every 200 ms, so they exercised a head that loops, which production never
does. They now park `--wait` until release and assert the reachable
paths: a fast ticket overtaking a normal ticket that is still waiting,
and a promoted waiting normal ticket preceding a later fast ticket.

The comments and design docs no longer claim a fast job waits at most
the hold already running (a parked head still goes first) or cite
#14962/#15032 as fast-behind-full evidence; they state what priority
removes and that a single hold longer than the budget is outside it.

> ### 🚨 Branch strategy — read before opening this PR
>
> The v2 refactor has merged into `main`, so **`main` is the default
branch for active development** (v1 and v2 code currently coexist there
— expect large, breaking changes).
>
> - **Active development** (features, refactors, optimizations, fixes
for the current codebase) → target **`main`** (the default base).
> - **v1 maintenance** (hotfixes and subsequent v1 releases) → branch
from and target **`v1`**, _not_ `main`.
>
> A v1 fix does **not** auto-carry to `main`: if the same bug exists on
`main`, open a separate forward-port PR targeting `main`. Before
touching subsystems being replaced, read `docs/references/data/` and
watch for `@deprecated` markers — they flag code being deleted.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

- The 44px history loading thumbnail showed a few oversized corner
blocks.
- Large painting surfaces created an uncapped, visually dense loading
grid.

After this PR:

- Surfaces up to 64px use a centered 6px compact grid suitable for
history thumbnails.
- Larger surfaces keep 14px loading dots while adaptive spacing caps the
grid at 256 cells.
- Same-topology resizes recenter existing cells without restarting image
sampling or remounting the animation.

fix(chat-layout): isolate list-group expansion state per window (#20848)

Follow-up to #20828 (supersedes its scope for the list-expansion keys),
tracking the same detached-window sharing family as #19778 / #20073.

## Problem

Agent session groups (left rail of the Agent page) and Chat topic groups
store their collapsed-set in cross-window broadcast persist keys:

- `ui.agent.session.expansion.time` / `.agent` / `.workdir` (read in
`Sessions.tsx`, maintenance write in `AgentPage.tsx` when switching the
list position)
- `ui.topic.expansion.time` / `.assistant` (read in `Topics.tsx`,
maintenance write in `HomePage.tsx`)

Every write broadcasts to all windows via `CacheService.setPersist`, so
collapsing group B in one detached window folded group B in every other
window.

## Fix

- Route both readers through `useWindowScopedPersistCache` (persisted in
the main window, renderer-local in detached windows) — same pattern as
#20828.
- Route the two imperative maintenance writes (`setSessionListPosition`
/ `setTopicListPosition`) to the matching tier via the existing
`isWindowFrame`.
- Add the five `ui.window.*` keys to `UseCacheSchema`.
- Bridge the hook's first-frame window value to the schema default:
`useCache`'s raw snapshot is `undefined` until its seeding effect lands,
while `resolveDefaultCollapsedGroupIds` only guards `null` — without
this, a detached window could crash on its first commit.

## Tests

- New `useWindowScopedPersistCache.test.ts`: embedded reads/writes
persist, detached seeds from persist, detached writes stay local, and
detached ignores later persisted broadcasts.
- Sessions mock updated to mirror the real seed-then-override semantics;
AgentPage/HomePage mocks gain the `useCache` export the hook needs.

`pnpm lint` green; related vitest suites (373 tests) green.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

Refreshing a preview recreated its format component and reset reading
state. A Word document at 150% on page 2 returned to its initial view.
Retaining the component alone also exposed stale measurements,
selections and native viewer geometry during reload.

After this PR:

Refreshing the same file reads fresh contents while preserving valid
zoom, reading position, worksheet, display mode and image transforms in
the current portable preview architecture. Different files or formats
reset normally. Shorter content clamps the position; obsolete selections
and failures cannot affect the replacement document. PDF and PowerPoint
also restore after Activity/tab reconnection.

Fixes #20859

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made:

The desktop owns one metadata request per refresh. Its stable request
reader lets the portable source invalidate old operations immediately
and wait for the new metadata before opening. HTML, Markdown and text
share that same request. Metadata completion does not open or read the
file a second time, and Activity reconnection creates a fresh request
even with unchanged props. Selection stamps use the metadata belonging
to the opened document.

Each format owns its reading state and resource cleanup. Format-local
asynchronous completions consume the portable host's existing session
generation, so an obsolete read or worker cannot clear retained content.
PowerPoint restores the slide through its existing viewer and then
applies offsets relative to the slide's new layout.

PDF retains a first-visible-page anchor in PDF coordinates and loads
only the pages covering the restored viewport before applying a native
XYZ destination, including the preceding area when the document end
clamps it. Formerly in-page points are constrained to resized bounds
while legitimate page margins remain intact. Effective numeric zoom and
automatic-fit intent retain their separate native meanings.

The following alternatives were considered:

A persistent cache would duplicate format ownership and add close/reopen
history. Keeping old source operations alive would hide file changes and
violate source lifetimes. Retrying with old metadata, fetching metadata
twice or discarding version errors would leave the request race intact.
Absolute PDF/PPTX document offsets and fixed delays cannot establish
valid geometry after layout changes; loading every PDF page is
unnecessary.

https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/20859 and
https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/pull/20897#discussion_r4336277873

fix(agent-lifecycle): reclaim purged session transcripts immediately (#21582)

### What this PR does

Before this PR: permanently deleting an Agent Session — "Delete" in
Archive, "Empty Archive", hard-deleting an active session, or
hard-deleting an agent with its sessions — removed the rows and the
system workspace, but left the session's Claude Code transcript on disk:
`Data/Agents/.claude/projects/{cwd-slug}/{sessionId}.jsonl` plus the
`{sessionId}/` subagent-transcript directory. Those artifacts were only
reclaimed by the orphan sweep inside `trash.purge`, which runs on the
daily 03:00 schedule (plus a catch-up run) and skips anything modified
within its 5-minute freshness gate (`FRESHNESS_GATE_MS`). A session
archived just before "Empty Archive" therefore always survived, and only
disappeared at a later purge — there is no archive-protection concept in
the code.

After this PR: the purge reclaims the artifacts of exactly the sessions
it just permanently deleted, in the same operation and without any
freshness gate, so deleting from the Archive or emptying the Archive
removes the `.jsonl` and its subagent directory immediately. A project
directory left empty by that reclaim is removed as well.

Fixes #21579

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

Permanently deleting a session is authoritative: the rows are gone and
the runtime has already been drained, so the in-flight window the
sweep's freshness gate protects does not apply.

- The reclaim is keyed by the resume tokens read from the session's
message rows *before* the FK cascade drops them, and only for the
sessions that were actually purged — so it cannot touch an artifact
belonging to a live or trashed session, even when another session shares
the same project directory.
- A token still claimed by a live runtime
(`AgentSessionRuntimeService.listClaimedResumeTokens()`) is skipped and
left to the sweep, rather than risking a running session's transcript.
- Failures are logged, never thrown: the DB deletion has already
committed, and any residue is still picked up by the existing orphan
sweep.
- The new `reclaimPurgedSessions` capability is optional on runtime
drivers and takes no freshness option: these tokens are known-dead by
construction, so there is nothing to gate.

The following tradeoffs were made:

- The reclaim is a second filesystem pass next to the existing sweep,
scoped to the tokens a purge just dropped. It duplicates the "which
artifact belongs to which token" knowledge that each driver already has,
but keeps the sweep's discovery semantics (and its gate) untouched.

The following alternatives were considered:

1. Shortening or zeroing `FRESHNESS_GATE_MS` when the caller is
`trash.purge`. Rejected: the gate exists because a transcript can be
created before its claiming row commits, so bypassing it globally would
reintroduce the race that deletes a live session's transcript.
2. Letting the sweep discover recently purged sessions (e.g. via a purge
epoch). Rejected: more moving parts and still a discovery window, where
the exact-token approach is deterministic and provably scoped to the
deleted sessions.

Links to places where the discussion took place:
https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/21579

### Breaking changes

None. Trashed and active sessions keep their transcripts, so Restore and
resume are unaffected, and the orphan sweep keeps working as the
backstop.

### Special notes for your reviewer

- Wiring: `AgentLifecycleService` reads `sessionId -> resume tokens`
before the deletion transaction and calls
`reclaimPurgedRuntimeSessions()` after it commits, for the permanent
session purge (`purgeSessions`), the expired-trash purge
(`purgeExpiredSessions`, i.e. the daily run and Empty Archive), and
`deleteActiveAgentPermanently(agentId, true)`. The archive-only path
deliberately does nothing.
- Claude Code layout only: Pi runtime artifacts keep their existing
sweep-based reclamation (out of scope for this issue, and stated as such
in the commit message).
- Tests:
`src/main/services/trash/__tests__/agentPurgedRuntimeSessions.test.ts`
covers all four purge entry points with a transcript touched *now*
(inside the 5-minute gate), the "only archived keeps both files"
invariant, and the live-claimed-token case;
`src/main/ai/runtime/__tests__/orphanSessionReclaim.test.ts` covers the
driver-level contract (only the named token, empty project directory
removal, missing root, empty set).
- Before/after evidence: with the source changes reverted (pre-fix tree
+ the new tests), the four reclaim tests fail with `AssertionError:
expected true to be false` — i.e. the transcript is still on disk, which
is the reported bug; with the fix they pass.
- Verification run locally: `pnpm exec vitest run` over the 14 affected
test files (the new/changed ones plus every `AgentLifecycleService`
consumer) → **14 files / 490 tests passed**; `pnpm typecheck:node` →
clean; `pnpm exec oxlint --deny-warnings` and `pnpm exec eslint` over
the changed files → clean; `pnpm lint` → clean (full run).

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

Hosted macOS development startup could exceed the 60-second readiness
budget. Git Bash stripped `TZ=Asia/Shanghai` before launching the
Windows controller, and `expectVisible` failed in strict mode when a
selector matched several elements.

After this PR:

Both branch and tag modes have a 120-second readiness budget. The
controller restores an absent `TZ` to `Asia/Shanghai` before reporting
and native application launch, preserving explicitly supplied timezones.
`expectVisible` checks the first match, consistent with `expectText`.
The controller README documents these contracts.

Fixes #22069

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made:

- Keep one startup budget without adding a dispatch input.
- Set the missing timezone in the native Node controller: another
workflow environment declaration would still be stripped by Git Bash.
The existing native launch chain passes the environment to the
application; actual application timezones remain measured.
- A hidden first match still fails even when later matches are visible.
Actions and `waitFor` keep their unique-match requirements.

The following alternatives were considered:

A branch-only timeout increase and clearer strict-selector errors were
considered; the requester selected a uniform 120-second budget and
first-match visibility assertions. Changing the runner's
operating-system timezone would unnecessarily broaden the repair.

commits.message:
refactor wave 2: speakers v2, media/noise, cross-device, calls/recaps/actions/vocabulary, MCP read-API correctness (shadow by default) (#23358)

## What and why

Integrate wave 2 of capture, speaker evidence and notes against the
reviewed wave-1 authority. This is a branch-only handoff: no PR, merge
to main, runtime cohort, deployment or production data access. All
implementation commits use the requested co-author trailer.

- Wave 1: merged origin/refactor-integration first (2ca1c676bc7); main
had not absorbed #23335 at intake. Its verified merge f6021c0f9dd landed
at 2026-10-22 20:39:40Z and is now merged here.
- V1 speakers: 4c368cc8ae5. Participant hints and bounded
compatible-cluster reduction, explicit channel/near-field/voice anchors,
ambiguity-preserving people matching and enrollment quality. Applied
speakers-live-name-hook.patch. Reconciled the newer wave-1 abstention
contract: preserve unresolved identity while allowing compatible count
consolidation.
- V2 media/noise: 1519a9a1b2b. Applied media-consumer-integration.patch.
Classify before notes, keep media/noise history with deterministic
minima, suppress memory/task/recap derivation through one shared helper,
and persist terminal intelligence suppression for replay. Explicit
restore/reprocessing clears the exclusion and marker. Shared live/sync
hallucination admission remains cohort-only.
- V3 cross-device: a05a1f823373. Completed-capture shared-speech
reconciliation and exact-key coverage aliases reuse the ledger and
capture-group writer. Originals and audio remain; unique secondary
speech remains visible. Streaming partial-window suppression and
automatic secondary-socket dispatch remain unimplemented.
- M MCP: 34d47d3e84fc. Correct filtered memory candidates, bounded
default lists, fair batch budgets/continuations, whole-window screen
aggregates, truthful counters/stubs, call metadata, provenance and
explicit timezones. Additive read correctness is on by default, as
authorized in lane M. Omitted timezone retains released UTC behavior.
- V4 calls/recaps/actions/vocabulary: d4509d3b4af6.
Completed-local-day/grace-period recaps, durable states and rollback
recovery, positive-evidence call metadata, owner-involved commitments
and bounded Soniox vocabulary. Applied calls-boundary-integration.patch
and calls-prompt-integration.patch, including authenticated agent
identity and cohort-sensitive notes cache identity. Automatic stale task
mutation remains partial: its producer-bound reference and canonical
CAS/reminder adapter do not exist in this lane. Older screen/desktop
producers still need explicit joined-controls evidence.

## Defaults, flags and ramp

SPEAKER_EVIDENCE_MODE, MEDIA_NOISE_MODE, CAPTURE_COVERAGE_MODE,
NOTES_PACKET_V2_MODE, EPISODE_BOUNDARIES_MODE, LIFECYCLE_V2_MODE,
CALLS_RECAP_MODE, ACTION_ITEMS_V2_MODE and STT_VOCAB_MODE remain shadow.
No serve cohort is configured. Existing client flags remain off/unknown.
Costly shadow database writers use refactor_modes.shadow_sampled:
CAPTURE_COVERAGE_MODE_SHADOW_PERCENT,
SPEAKER_EVIDENCE_MODE_SHADOW_PERCENT and
EPISODE_BOUNDARIES_MODE_SHADOW_PERCENT, each default 5.
STT_VOCAB_MODE_SHADOW_PERCENT samples source reads at default 1. Serve
cohorts always write and zero disables sampled writes. All bindings are
declared and the registry regenerated. Invalid percentages keep the
bounded default. V4 phone/calendar boundary publication is serve-only
under CALLS_RECAP_MODE; shadow projects the evidence locally without
authority writes. No CALLS_RECAP_MODE_SHADOW_PERCENT binding is needed
for this serve-only choice. On-demand recaps explicitly bypass scheduled
grace; all scheduling/backfill keeps the completed-day grace.

Owner dazheng, by 2026-10-26: synthetic integrated acceptance, reviewed
runtime digest pilot, then 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%, one full lookback
window per step. Keep modes shadow while configuring sampled serve
cohorts; mode serve is the 100% stage. Align producer/consumer runtime
cohorts (especially speaker/boundary evidence with media and calls) so
sampling does not make serving evidence unavailable. No expansion until
manual/identity violations, false folds, lost unique speech/custody,
false owner-call/media exclusions, genuine-speech drops and duplicate
recap deliveries remain zero. Inspect speaker count/anchor/agreement
metrics, omi_media_noise_shadow_total (especially repeated_sentence
admission receipts), cross-device duplicate/examined lines, coverage
admits/seconds, sync failures/latency and vendor spend. No paid
duplicate generation/transcription in shadow. Rollback modes to off and
clear runtime cohorts; durable lifecycle obligations still reconcile.
Persisted groups/classifications are non-destructive and may need
restore/reprocess after rollback. Budget cohort entry for one
regeneration per fingerprint-less legacy day inside the seven-day
lookback (subject to the existing per-run backfill cap); retained IDs
and delivery receipts prevent duplicate notifications. No serve cohort
was enabled for this work.

## Review disposition

| Review finding | Status | Resolution / reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| V1 #1 nullable speaker | Done | Never project a null cluster speaker
into a numbered segment; production-seam regression. |
| V1 #2 count metrics | Done | Producer and observer share a
voice/channel partition helper; channel splits are not reductions. |
| V1 #3 learning state quality vs stale fence | Skipped | Requires
changing the transactional publication result and learning-state
contract, beyond a mechanical fix. Existing bounded quality counter
distinguishes rejection; track before serve ramp. Enrollment and
unpublished-blob cleanup remain protected. |
| V1 #4 live name-only guard | Done | Supplied patch applied before
text-only lookup/create/map mutation. |
| V1 #5 count cues | Skipped | No threshold change without audited
acceptance data. Acoustic thresholds, cannot-links and abstention
retained; count hints cannot force incompatible voices together. |
| V2 H1 dormant consumers | Done | Patch applied; real
processing/persistence, replay, all four consumer boundaries and
restore/reprocess exercised. |
| V2 M2 genuine foreign repetition | Skipped | No evidence supports
changing the threshold here. Zero serve cohort; pilot must audit
repeated_sentence receipts before expansion. Audio custody remains
intact. |
| V2 M3 shadow reads | Skipped | Production volume validation is outside
the no-prod-reads scope. Reads are bounded; no second paid call or
shadow media-edge write. Sampled speaker/boundary writers bound
mutations; serving pilots need aligned producer coverage. |
| V2 L1 collapsed metric checks | Done | Explicit conversation bucket
and strict unknown-check rejection with regression. |
| V2 L2 admission naming | Skipped | Distinct module namespaces, no
shared caller or behavior collision; avoid unrelated public rename. |
| V2 L3 sync hook size | Done | Existing no-content settlement needs a
small hook, covered by tests and line-count metadata. |
| V2 L4 fixtures | Done | Minimal request-authority and timeline fixture
updates retained. |
| V3 dead distinct_streams return | Done | Removed unreachable duplicate
condition; unknown devices abstain. |
| V3 shadow lane label | Done | Compare accepts explicit lane; V3 does
not emit an L1 fold observation. |
| V3 serve query transaction cost | Skipped | No query semantics change
without runtime evidence. Bounded alias validation reads remain; watch
sync latency/failures before expansion. |
| M P1 default memory failure | Done | Default lists use released-size
bounded reads, return data and explicit incomplete coverage; filtered
incomplete windows still error. |
| M P2 read amplification | Done | Physical-read regression pins bounded
default source batch. |
| M P3.1 aggregate cursor | Done | Ignore stale aggregate cursor and
explain whole-window behavior. |
| M P3.2 timestamps | Done | Released strings retained unless offset
format/timezone is requested. |
| M P3.3 calendar-day stub pagination | Skipped | Intentional
bounded-date contract; an old in-flight cursor may shift across
deployment. No historical rewrite or invented failure cause. |
| M P3.4 retired/private helpers | Done | Dead collector/branch/imports
removed; shared adapters public with migrated callers. |
| M P3.5 duplicate-ID progress | Done | Absolute occurrence cursor with
regression. |
| V4 HIGH boundary authority write | Done | Parent ruling wins: both
phone record and calendar ingest are serve-only under the calls cohort.
Shadow uses local evidence; the regression holds
EPISODE_BOUNDARIES_MODE=serve and proves a non-cohort user produces no
authority write. |
| V4 MEDIUM on-demand grace | Done | Explicit user_initiated plumbing
from generate_daily_summary_on_demand bypasses grace; scheduler/backfill
do not set it. Partial-day and post-midnight grace tests exercise the
actual producer. |
| V4 MEDIUM STT uid | Done | Both legacy initial/reconnect calls and the
managed Soniox leg pass authenticated request uid. Removed get_byok_uid
fallback; real managed config and legacy call seams are tested. |
| V4 MEDIUM vague_social / incident 09 | Done | Named counterpart plus a
concrete place/time retains owner-alias commitments, including catch up
with Matt in NYC. Fourteen incident/negative cases cover missing
feedback, CV review, Deepgram check, invitation/Drive, unrelated customs
purchase and bogus hiking. Promisor/provenance authority remains intact.
|
| V4 LOW legacy-day regeneration cost | Done | Budgeted in the ramp
above; no serve cohort enabled. |
| V4 LOW dead constants | Done | Removed six unused lane constants.
Actual shared cohort bindings now live in and are consumed by
refactor_modes._COHORT_ENVS; no env behavior changes. |
| V4 LOW stripped comments | Done | Restored explanatory shared model,
finalizer, notifications and Soniox comments/docstrings; public recap
docs distinguish legacy order and serving revision/state behavior. |
| V4 LOW inverted / expired parity labels | Done | Found vocabulary
emits agree; absent expired evidence compares the retained durable call
projection. Regression assertions pin both labels. |
| Integrator runtime-image closure | Done | All 19 contracts compared
using third_party_dependency_modules against origin/main; zero added
third-party modules. Incorporated PR #23355 branch and added GPU
closure/shim regressions. |

## Conflicts and shared contracts

Resolved person_pool.py by retaining incoming quality checks and wave-1
type annotation; duplicate_capture.py retains both lifecycle serving and
cross-device imports. Generated artifacts are regenerated from
generators, not resolved by hand. ContentKind has one literal definition
shared by stored/create models and policy; request classification stays
hidden/server-authored. BoundaryKind includes media_playback once.
Participant count and owner anchor live only in SpeakerEvidence. Call
fields are additive optional Conversation metadata; explicit boundary
proof survives canonical normalization and wire round trips. V4
persisted stubs pass through M with null generated_at. Media/noise-only
days report not_generated rather than falsely saying no recordings;
actual empty days keep no_recordings. Both one-shot and agentic prompt
mounts are exercised in off/shadow/serve.

The pipeline guide records integration, sampling, call/recap/prompt
contracts, replay and pending socket semantics. The developer storage
guide explains original-recording retention and unknown/remote metadata
without publishing rollout controls. Dead-code analyzer regenerated its
baseline without new suppressions; the allowlist tool deliberately never
auto-edits allowlists. Existing evaluator-only exceptions remain, and
imported wave-1 contract scaffolds have no stale allowlist entries.

## Runtime image closure audit (fix pass)

Merged fresh origin/main at 81270c66d1dd9b0a6a4ed866f2c8b8ea6c4abfff
after #23355 landed. It merged without conflicts and leaves exactly the
same source tree as fix commit ed2c03440df. Before #23355 landed, also
merged origin/fix-parakeet-policy-closure at
2d3ec7039c6f6a15d040b134c3082d91eeebcc4f; its remote branch was deleted
after merge. No unseen remote integration commits were overwritten.

The audit independently executes each revision's
backend/scripts/runtime_image_contracts.py
third_party_dependency_modules(contract) over every registered contract
(including lazy imports), without importing application code or reading
production. There are **zero added and zero removed third-party probe
targets across all 19 images** against the final main base; no new
lockfile/requirements package is needed.

The earlier comparison against pre-#23355 main
4499deb154ffd811d9e679436d895fa0ca46f4fe had zero additions in all
