fix(app): purge a deleted account's local recordings and stop foreign audio counting as storage pressure (#23351)

## What changed and why

Deleting an account in the app removed only the WAL index files
(`wals.json` and its backup). The live `LocalWalSync` still held that
account's recordings in memory: `clearUserState` retired them, the next
save wrote them back to disk, and the next account to sign in parked
them as foreign-owner records forever. A phone that went through three
account deletions held 1,069 such files. Every index save re-serialized
all of them, and `_pendingDiskWalCount` counted them, so a brand-new
account hit the admission count cap (`storage_at_risk`, cap 720) from
its first minute.

- **On account deletion:** `purgeAccountWals(uid)` deletes the deleted
account's recordings (index entry and file; active, retired and foreign)
before `clearUserState`, while the WAL session still belongs to that
account.
- **Remembered deletions:** the deleted uid is kept in
`deletedAccountUids` (bounded to 20), which survives sign-out and the
deletion wipe.
- **At index load:** foreign-owner records whose owner is in that list
are deleted instead of parked, logging `wal_orphan_purge`. Foreign
records of accounts that were not deleted on this phone are untouched.
- **Storage pressure:** foreign-owner records no longer count toward
`_pendingDiskWalCount`, so another account's audio can never trip this
account's `storage_at_risk`.
- **Cold-start lists:** after a cold start the preference store hands
string lists back as `List<Object?>`.
`SharedPreferencesUtil.getStringList` quarantines that as a type
mismatch and `clearPreferencesForSignOut` silently dropped it, so the
remembered list would not have survived a restart or a sign-out. The
list is read through the plugin's typed getter, and sign-out now keeps
untyped string lists. (Seen on a simulator: `cachedPeople` and
`cachedTranscriptionVocabulary` are quarantined the same way on every
cold start; that broader read bug is not changed here.)

No UI change. Records of the signed-in account, retired records of a
signed-out account, and `legacy` records are not affected.

UI-Evidence: none -- no UI change; local recording index and
storage-pressure behavior only

## Product invariants affected

- INV-CAP-1: preserved. Audio is removed only when the user explicitly
deletes the account that owns it, after the server confirms the
deletion. Capture, uplink and retention of the active account are
unchanged, and audio of any account the user did not delete is kept.

Cloud Run `backend-sync` answered HTTP 500 about 110–215 times per hour on `/v2/sync-jobs/run` and 125–170 per hour on `/v1/conversation-finalization-jobs/run`. Every one was the same Firestore 400: three conversation documents sit at the 1 MiB ceiling, so the write each job needs can never land, and both runners treated that permanent refusal as retryable. - Quiet finalization (`quiet_finalization.run`, reached from the finalization worker for `quiet-` jobs and from the reconciler) now catches `is_document_size_limit_error`, retires the check as `quiet_done` with `last_failure_code=document_size_limit`, and returns a status the handler acks with 200. - The enrichment outbox (`outbox.run`, behind `/v2/sync-jobs/run` `sync_reprocess` on the default `sync_handler` route that prod uses) parks the row dormant with `held_reason=document_size_limit` instead of leaving a leased row the sweep re-wakes. The handler answers 200 `held`; a redelivery reads the dormant row as `stale`. - Both emit a WARNING and `record_fallback(reason=document_size_limit, outcome=exhausted)`. Any other `InvalidArgument` still raises. The conversation documents are not touched. Shrinking them (occasion rollover before the limit) is a separate change. The `enrichment_queue` consumer path (`utils/enrichment/consumer.py`, staging only today) does not get the same terminal in this PR; prod runs `ENRICHMENT_ROUTE` unset, which is `sync_handler`. ## Product invariants affected none ## How it was verified - Prod evidence before the change: `gcloud logging read 'resource.type="cloud_run_revision" AND resource.labels.service_name="backend-sync" AND severity>=ERROR AND textPayload:"exceeds the maximum"'` shows the 400 from `database/firestore_transaction_retry.py` on both endpoints, three conversation ids, 91–372 retries each in a 7-hour window. - Confirmed the live `backend-sync` revision has no `ENRICHMENT_ROUTE`, so the outbox path is the one prod runs. - Unit tests: the 8 test files covering the outbox, quiet checks and finalization (`test_batch_pipeline_serving`, `test_conversation_quiet_finalization`, `test_enrichment_callback_fence`, `test_enrichment_route`, `test_fsr_s2_singleton_loops`, `test_listen_finalization_cloud_tasks`, `test_outbox_firestore`, `test_recording_sessions`): 495 passed, also in reverse file order. - Not verified against prod Firestore: the fix has not been deployed, so the 500 rate drop is unconfirmed until it ships. ## Tests - `test_conversation_quiet_finalization.py`: an oversized conversation retires the quiet check with the failure code instead of raising; other `InvalidArgument` rejections still surface; the worker endpoint acks with 200. - `test_enrichment_route.py`: the outbox row parks dormant with `held_reason` and no successor wake; a redelivery is `stale`; unrelated `InvalidArgument` still raises; the legacy `/v2/sync-jobs/run` handler answers 200 `held`, then 200 `stale`. ## UI evidence UI-Evidence: none -- backend-only change ## Failure class (fixes) Failure-Class: FC-permanent-write-rejection-retried-forever

feat(audio): store BLE Opus as captured by default (P71) (#23325)

## What

Implements David's 2026-10-22 ruling (**P71**): for Omi BLE devices,
durably
store the device's **original Opus frames as captured**, next to the
decoded
PCM16, going forward. Existing PCM stays. Opus is ~60–100× smaller than
PCM16
(today `chunks/*.batch.enc` PCM alone is ~393 GiB/day).

The as-captured container already exists merged-dark from #21528
(raw-live
WAL packs, shared AES-GCM envelope, reader fallbacks, retirement proof).
This
PR turns its fleet phases on by default and gives Phase 2 its own ramp
knob;
it does not invent a new container.

## Changes

- **`backend/config/audio_archive.py`** — `LIVE` (dual-write original
Opus
WAL / lossless FLAC packs under `raw-live/`) and `READ` (readers prefer
  raw, decode PCM16 on read, fall back to stored PCM chunks) become
  **flag-only fleet phases, default on**. Kill switches:
`AUDIO_ARCHIVE_LIVE_ENABLED=false` / `AUDIO_ARCHIVE_READ_ENABLED=false`
(per service). No percent cohort gates them anymore — a percent gate
would
  keep LIVE silently dark wherever `AUDIO_ARCHIVE_PERCENT` is unset.
- **Phase 2 (`STOP_PCM`, stop the PCM write)** — stays default off and
now
  ramps on a dedicated **`AUDIO_ARCHIVE_STOP_PCM_PERCENT`** (default 0),
because `AUDIO_ARCHIVE_PERCENT` is pinned at 100 fleet-wide for
COALESCE.
  The skip still requires READ plus the unchanged `verified_pcm_paths`
  byte-exact coverage+identity proof (16 kHz mono opus/flac, zero gaps,
  whole-pack capture-PCM SHA or byte-identical decode). Multi-channel,
  non-16 kHz, aac/lc3 sources and any coverage hole keep the PCM write.
- **Manifests** — `AUDIO_ARCHIVE_LIVE/READ_ENABLED=true` across the six
  runtime_env services and both listen/pusher charts (dev+prod);
`AUDIO_ARCHIVE_STOP_PCM_PERCENT` declared beside `AUDIO_ARCHIVE_PERCENT`
in every surface (added to the existing workstream B
duplicate-declaration
  allowlist in `scripts/check_feature_flag_registry.py`).
- **Registry** — LIVE/READ rows are now default-on ops_kill kill
switches;
  STOP_PCM_ENABLED/`_PERCENT` rows carry the ramp. Docs updated
(`runbooks/sync-ingest-archive.md`, `docs/listen_pusher_pipeline.mdx`).
- **Tests** — fleet defaults + kill switches; live pack kill switch
(append
with consent writes nothing when LIVE=false); invalid percent fails
closed
  on both knobs; STOP_PCM isolation from the shared percent + cohort
  stability; batch payload still downloaded exactly once under READ.
  Existing tests already pin the round trip (packet-exact + sample-exact
  native-Opus replay through `archive_capture_bytes` → `read_pack`), the
reader fallbacks, the encryption envelope (`[4B BE len][12B
nonce][AES-256-GCM
  ct+tag]`, HKDF per-uid key) and the byte-exact PCM retirement proof —
  unchanged by this PR.

## Codec facts (inventory)

Omi BLE opus devices capture 16 kHz mono (`opus` 8 kB/s wire,
`opus_fs320`
16 kB/s; `opus_fs320` normalizes to `opus` before decode). One websocket
message = one self-describing Opus packet; the raw-live WAL container
prefixes each packet with a uint32le length, so per-frame device framing
is
fully recoverable (`packet_provenance` reads nb_frames from packet
headers).
pcm8/pcm16 are stored losslessly as FLAC in raw-live; aac/lc3 packs are
stored but never serve reads. Non-Opus/lossless or non-16 kHz sources
never
qualify for STOP_PCM.

## Phase 2 ramp plan (lead expands)

1. **0** until the LIVE+READ soak is clean (archive objects/bytes
growing
with intake, `omi_fallback_total{component=pusher,reason=upload_failed}`
   ≈ 0, batch STT success + shadow WER parity flat, playback/audio-merge
   build errors flat).
2. **5%** via `AUDIO_ARCHIVE_STOP_PCM_PERCENT` for ≥12 h.
3. **100%** after the lead reviews the 5% readout.
Metrics: `omi_audio_archive_pcm_writes_avoided_total` tracks the cohort
share; rollback = percent to 0 first, then the ENABLED flag; keep READ
on
   for raw-only history until PCM regeneration is verified.

## Exposure notes

- Storage: raw adds ~1/60–1/100 of PCM volume (~4–7 GiB/day vs 393)
while
  dual-writing; net reduction starts only at Phase 2.
- Reads: READ adds one metadata fetch per legacy spanless chunk read
before
the data fetch; for raw-covered spans it replaces per-chunk data fetches
  with one pack fetch per ~60 s span. Reviewed behavior from #21528,
  unchanged here.
- Per-user consent (`private_cloud_sync_enabled`) still gates every raw
  write; deletion purges `raw-live/` (conversation and account level).

## Verification

- `BACKEND_UNIT_TEST_FILE_LIST=… bash backend/test.sh` (11 files: sync
ingest archive, storage opus encoding, batch upload storage, runtime env
  validator + render, pusher config refs, rollout cohort deploy/parity,
  create_audio_files_from_chunks, round4 reconnect inventory, staging
  mirror): **75 passed**; storage_opus_encoding: 36 passed, 11 skipped.

fix: preserve live held audio through transient staging failures (#23309) ## Problem and behavior A transient GCS timeout/503 burst exhausted the live held-audio upload budget and escaped both the receive/final-flush boundary (1011) and `cap_held_updates`. Keep PCM until an immutable publication or owner-fenced encrypted journal confirms custody, and recover journals with the existing staging sweep. Open for review only; do not merge or deploy. ## Root cause At base `800f812686b`, `backend/utils/sync/live_cap_upload.py:41-42` re-raises after two lifetime attempts. `backend/utils/sync/live_cap_hold.py:87-94` propagated that failure through `flush`; `backend/routers/listen/receiver.py:2545` and `:2583` call `mark_listen_internal_error` (`:189`, 1011). The updater had an unguarded await at `backend/utils/sync/live_cap_hold.py:531`, reached from the WS task spawned at `backend/routers/listen/receiver.py:2407`. ## Retry and custody - Two upload attempts, 1.5-second socket timeout, 4-second per-attempt async wait, 8-second total including exponential backoff with scaled uniform jitter. Retry timeouts, resets, HTTP 408/429 and 5xx. Other 4xx get one attempt and the permanent outcome. Backoff uses `min(0.2 * 2**(n-1), 1.0) * U(0.5, 1.5)` seconds (100–300ms for the one backoff with two attempts). Both encoder passes use the original 20-second subprocess timeout; the 8s upload budget excludes encoding, and the outer 28s shutdown deadline still applies. - Exhausted/permanent uploads hand off encrypted Opus (at most 128KiB plus encrypted metadata) to an immediately eligible, non-expiring staging journal under the existing owner/deletion fence. No new query, index, local durable-file assumption or scheduler. Restore uses immutable fragment provenance and the existing claim ledger; ambiguous original commits count once. Standalone/fragmentation-off journals use the original receipt identity. - PCM stays owned until that handoff succeeds. each discovery page transaction held two 499-ref transactional get_alls plus

- candidates() now catches any discovery exception, logs one payload-free
  WARNING (stage + class, no uids) and records a record_fallback degrade
  (firestore_read/dream_discovery -> queue_only), then still returns the
  already-due dream_due rows; the sweep never 500s on discovery again.

  transactional get_all, commit write count and allowlist bulk read is
  bounded to the 100-ref bulk-get size with ~5x headroom on the old page
  transaction at full eligibility. The cursor advances only with a page's
  final chunk, so failed or budget-stopped pages re-scan from their start;
  replay is idempotent because the transactional dream_due read skips
  owners a concurrent dirty write already enqueued and dirty writes
  overwrite due_at afterwards (mark_dirty/finish are last-writer-wins).

ci-flake: keep native audio apt install off the network when warm (#23308) ## Summary The `apt-native-audio-replay-timeout` flake persisted after #23266 because that fix left three exposure paths on the hot step of `backend-unit-tests.yml` shards, all observed on 2026-10-22: 1. **Runner image rollout empties the cache.** The cache key pins `ImageVersion`; image `20261021.345.10` rolled out on 10-21/22, and with no `restore-keys` every shard of the first runs on the new image went cold into a 62.8 MB download. On throttled `azure.archive.ubuntu.com` runners that cannot finish inside the 5m step budget (observed 10–60s per small package). 2. **The 6-shard save race leaves no entry.** All shards save the same primary key concurrently; the cache service reserves per key, so losing shards log `Unable to reserve cache ... another job may be creating this cache` (run 39790722827 shard 1, 13:53:38Z) and shards whose install timed out never reach the save step at all — main-push run 39791659773 had 5/6 shards fail this way, so nothing repopulated the cache for anyone. 3. **Even a cache hit is not network-free.** Run 39782487842 shard 3 restored the cached `.deb`s at 12:57:16Z and still timed out at 13:02:29Z inside `apt-get update -qq`, which downloads package indexes from the mirror regardless of cached archives. Confirmed occurrences of the 5-minute `Install native audio replay dependencies` timeout: runs 39790722827 (PR #23302, shards 2+3), 39791659773 (main push, shards 1/2/4/5/6), 39782487842 (shards 3/4/5, one of them with a warm cache). The same code passed with a warm old-image cache at 12:15Z (run 39776810910), so this is CI infrastructure flakiness, not a regression. ## Changes (all inside this flake's own step in `.github/workflows/backend-unit-tests.yml`) - `restore-keys` fallback across `ImageVersion` bumps within the same runner OS: the `.deb` set tracks the ubuntu24 distro repos, not the image patch version, so the newest saved image keeps every run warm through rollouts. - Warm installs replay the cached dependency closure with `sudo dpkg -i` — zero network on the hot path. `apt-get` (update + `install -f`, bounded by the existing Acquire retries/timeouts) runs only as repair if the replay fails; the cold path is unchanged and keeps its 5m bounded allowance. - Single-writer cache save (shard 1 only), removing the concurrent same-key save race. A `restore-keys` fallback hit reports `cache-hit: 'false'`, so shard 1 also backfills the exact key for new image versions. `.github` is edited only for this flake's own step and no workflow is added, per the 10-22 CI flake-fix and caching direction. ## Verification - `actionlint` clean on the modified workflow; YAML parse and `bash -n` on the changed run block pass. - `scripts/pr-preflight --suggest`: ci lane, no product-invariant citations, no failure-class declaration required. - The restored-cache-but-still-timed-out shard (39782487842 shard 3) demonstrates the warm path must skip `apt-get update`; `dpkg -i` of the cached 87-`.deb` closure needs no indexes and no mirror. ## Risk - `dpkg -i` replays exactly the saved closure; if a future image bump ever made that replay fail, the apt repair path resolves and downloads only the delta before failing loudly — no silent skips. - Old-image cache entries are reused across image bumps; they come from the same ubuntu24 noble/noble-updates pools the images are built from, and a stale set degrades to the apt repair path, not a hang.

ci-flake: keep native audio apt install off the network when warm

The 2026-10-22 runner image rollout (20261021.345.10) emptied the
native-audio .deb cache for every shard because the cache key pins
ImageVersion and no restore-keys fallback exists; the six shards also
race one another saving the same key ('Unable to reserve cache ...'),
so no entry was written back. Cold 62.8 MB downloads then hit the 5m
step ceiling on throttled mirrors (runs 39790722827 PR #23302 shards
2/3, main-push 39791659773 shards 1/2/4/5/6, 39782487842 shards 3-5).

Even a cache hit stayed exposed: run 39782487842 shard 3 restored the
.debs at 12:57:16Z and still timed out at 13:02:29Z inside
apt-get update -qq, which downloads package indexes from the mirror
regardless of cached archives.

- restore-keys fall back across ImageVersion bumps within the same
  runner OS; the .deb set tracks the ubuntu24 distro repos, not the
  image patch version.
- warm installs replay the cached closure with dpkg -i (no network);
  apt repairs only if that replay fails.
- save runs on shard 1 only, removing the concurrent same-key save
  race; a restore-keys hit reports cache-hit 'false', so shard 1 also
  backfills the exact key for new image versions.

feat: silent backfill and reversible noise close [DO NOT MERGE] (#23260)

**DO NOT MERGE.** This ready PR is for review only; the assignment
explicitly forbids merge, deploy and apply.

## What changed and why

Historical stuck conversations need an explicitly silent recovery path
before an operator can safely backfill them. Add an immutable
`silent_backfill_v1` finalization job policy that persists title/summary
and suppresses derived-work queues and automatic delivery across retries
and completed replays.

Add a snapshot-fenced metadata-only noise close/restore, retaining
transcripts and audio references, plus an operator-only counts
preview/private-plan/apply tool with newest-first ordering, owner scope,
durable owner/global pacing, kill switch, first-error stop and spend
receipts. No scan, admission or backfill starts on shipment. See
`backend/docs/runbooks/stuck-backfill.md` for approval, serving-release
and rollback limits. Forward recovery/disconnect fixes remain separate;
this diff does not touch `recover_stale_in_progress`. The reviewed
Firestore caller fingerprint changes only for new document-read fences;
its serving query shape and index requirements remain unchanged.

## Product invariants affected

- INV-MEM-4: historical summaries preserve capture content and create no
memory mutations.
- INV-TASK-2: silent historical work materializes no tasks/reminders or
task acceptance.

## How it was verified

`omi-heavy`: 417 original focused tests passed, covering existing Cloud
Tasks/lifecycle behavior and silent processing/replay suppression. At

hook passed all 35 preflight checks, zero-error typecheck, all 19
runtime-image contracts and 86 selected unit tests (including both
budget-denial regressions). Integration tests were intentionally

GitHub checks below are the authority for full CI.

`backend/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
backend/tests/integration/test_stuck_backfill_emulator.py -m
integration` through `omi-heavy`: 29 tests passed, exercising real
close/restore, exact revisions, session changes, concurrent close,
immutable job admission, per-owner serialization and transactional
global pacing. Only synthetic fixtures were written.
- Backend typecheck: zero errors. Independent separate-copy GLM review
found a capture-preservation P1, now fixed with an emulator regression.
Final separate-copy GLM follow-up reports no P0/P1. Its nanosecond
comparison P3 is fixed with a pure helper regression; owner dead-letter
and plan-time privacy notes remain fail-safe operational limits.
- No endpoint was added. Existing worker-route contracts are covered by
the 282-test Cloud Tasks suite; the changed DB seams were exercised
against the emulator; a real HTTP worker replay used actual
claim/fanout/completion transactions and a repeated task ACK.
Provider/automatic delivery functions were fail-if-called synthetic

Episodes M3) with a merge commit; the red backend unit shard file
`test_conversation_relevance.py` was reproduced locally through

`test_stuck_backfill.py`, `test_stuck_backfill_operator.py`,

`test_stuck_backfill_emulator.py` and `test_conversation_relevance.py`

UI-Evidence: none -- operator/backend behavior; no UI change.

This PR is not approval to apply a plan or deploy. All queue consumers

fix(stt): preserve funded window finalize on VAD pause (#23265) When an Omi-funded Parakeet window reaches a normal VAD pause, `CapSocket` advertises the window class but rejects its `finalize(vad_pause=True)` call. Python raises `TypeError` before the proxy body or any Parakeet HTTP request; the managed leg records `send_failed`, fails over, and can vote to bench a healthy provider. Forward provider-specific finalize arguments at the shared cap boundary and add bounded local-send phase/exception diagnostics. This shared primitive fixes every cap-wrapped caller; the regression exercises the actual funded admission → cap proxy → window → VAD pause → POST/transcript chain rather than a permissive proxy mock. Existing health classification is preserved. ### Attribution and measured scope The 2026-10-22 p63 report records 1,508 window `send_failed` settlements over its rolling 24-hour window, versus 217 connection losses, 37 provider 5xx and 3 timeouts: `send_failed` is **1,508 / 1,765 = 85.4%** of classified provider failures. In the first complete post-P/Q hour (04:00–05:00Z), about **7 send failures / 112 admissions = 6.3%** remained. Admissions and settlements can cross hour boundaries; these are diagnostic ratios, not randomized session failure estimates. The funded cap cohort was **50% on all 40 listen pods** at the report's ~06:19Z refresh; cap accounting recorded **11,207 seconds** of accepted Parakeet audio over 24 hours. The reproduced signature error deterministically explains the failure of an affected funded window on its first ordinary VAD pause. Historical logs discarded the exception class, so **the fraction of the 1,508 events caused by this exact error is not recoverable**; 50% allocation is not a measured failure share. The new `omi_stt_local_send_failures_total{provider,phase,exception_class}` counter measures the remaining local causes after rollout. Window POST p95 was 0.49–0.84s, with no 24h OOM/fatal-GPU increments; this fix needs no capacity increase. ### Rollback and rollout `STT_CAP_FINALIZE_FORWARD_ENABLED` defaults on. `false`/`0`/`off` selects generic no-argument finalize while retaining the permissive proxy signature, so rollback does not recreate the TypeError. Generic finalize can flush sub-second speech blips earlier. Held providers remain unopened. Allocation, health thresholds, session caps, deadlines and GPU placement are unchanged. The lead owns the next off-peak listen train (22:00–13:00Z), merge and deployment. Compare finalize/TypeError diagnostics, `send_failed` settlements, automatic recovery stages, transcript availability and window POST latency. Preserve the automatic health gate; no forced unbench or cap increase. Production acceptance has not run. ### Verification - Pinned-source baseline reproduction: direct window accepts the keyword; legacy cap proxy raises `TypeError` before HTTP (saved p63 baseline receipt). - Focused four-file suite: **323 passed** (95 cap dispatch, 204 window live, 7 local diagnostics, 17 live failure) at `1e1900e809f`, via `BACKEND_UNIT_TEST_FILE_LIST` and `BACKEND_PYTEST_WORKERS=2`, `OMI_HEAVY_WAIT=1800 /Users/dazheng/workspace/omi/bin/omi-heavy run -- nice -n 19 bash test.sh` from `backend/`. - `OMI_HEAVY_WAIT=1800 BACKEND_PYTEST_WORKERS=2 OMI_PR_BODY_FILE= /Users/dazheng/workspace/omi/bin/omi-heavy run -- nice -n 19 make preflight`: **PASS, all 35 checks**, at `1e1900e809f` (1,808.42s execution; normal gates retained). - Real-chain arms cover forwarded finalize, generic rollback, exact legacy signature failure before HTTP, and capture-setup failure attribution. Proxy units cover held/no-open behavior; diagnostic units check bounded labels and absence of exception-message content. HTTP is fake; this does not claim live serving acceptance. - Separate-copy GLM review: round 1 SHIP; recovered round 2 delta review SHIP (`62d9471c008..9adf2adf2f4`, static review). Parent inspected the subsequent test-only teardown correction: the capture-setup arm now expects the canceled pump's propagated `CancelledError`; its behavior and diagnostic assertions remain intact. ### Product invariants affected none Failure-Class: new New class: `FC-provider-proxy-finalize-signature-drift`. The violated contract is that a class-advertising provider proxy must accept and forward the provider-specific finalize protocol. Durable prevention is the forwarding primitive plus the real funded-window regression and bounded diagnostics, registered with the class's canonical test artifacts.

Episodes M3: one conversation per occasion, salience, and a background day line on Home (#23269) ## What Episodes M3: for episodes users, one conversation per occasion, built at the source, plus a quieter Home. - **Occasion conversations (listen).** A live conversation stays open across lulls and pendant reconnects for 15 minutes, instead of splitting on 2 minutes of silence and stitching the pieces back together later. One occasion gets one transcript and one notes pass, and needs no merge. - **Salience (notes).** The notes pass says whether a conversation is a `highlight` or `background`. - **Background day line (app).** On Home, a day's background conversations fold into one line under the day header ("Also: TV in the background 32m · …"). Tapping the line shows them as rows. Stacked on #23198 (Episodes v1.1). ## Why David labeled four blind rounds on his own week (2026-10-22): - **Boundaries.** Real content up to about 45 minutes apart was almost always one occasion. A fixed 15-minute window matched a topic-aware model judge on a held-out week, at no model cost. - **Noise.** Noise should be dropped, not stitched in. - **Home.** Low-value occasions are worth keeping but not worth a row. He then chose this design from mockups: "Use the one-line recap under the day header for Background, with B built at the source." ## Changes **Listen (`routers/listen`, `config/occasion_conversations.py`)** - **Admission.** `client_gate.occasion_mode(uid)` requires the kill switch, the episodes cohort, and a client that has shown it renders episodes. Any read failure fails closed. Only the mobile app's own capture is admitted; desktop sources and multi-channel (phone-call) sessions keep today's boundaries. - **Silence window.** Admitted sessions use a window of at least 15 minutes (`OCCASION_GAP_SECONDS`). A user's own longer setting still wins. - **Reconnects.** A new recording id inside the window continues the open conversation (`_occasion_attach_target`, logged as `event=occasion_attach`). That requires the same device and source, `in_progress`, not deleted, discarded or locked, under the span cap, and the existing resumable-continuation check. - **Span cap.** At 3 hours (`OCCASION_MAX_SPAN_SECONDS`) the lifecycle loop rolls the conversation over (`event=occasion_span_rollover`), so all-day ambient capture stays under document limits. - **Users not admitted:** no change. The gate is pure CPU outside the cohort. - **Docs:** a new occasion section in `backend/docs/listen_pusher_pipeline.mdx`, and the kill switch in the feature-flag registry. **Notes (`models/structured_extraction.py`, `utils/llm/notes_agent_prompt.py`)** - `RichStructuredExtraction`, `AgentNotesSubmission` and the agent's submit tool gain an optional `salience` field: `highlight` or `background`. - The one-shot `StructuredExtraction` schema is unchanged, so its prompt bytes are stable. The agent's instructions describe salience (`notes-agent-v6`). - An out-of-vocabulary answer is dropped, never the note. - `Structured.salience` is omitted on the wire when unset. OpenAPI, the Dart wire model and the plugin SDK are regenerated. **App** - **`Structured.salience`.** Parsed from the wire and the cache, and round-trips. - **The fold.** `foldsIntoBackgroundLine` takes only completed, unstarred, unlocked conversations. It applies only for episodes users in Home's default view (no search, folder or starred filter, and not in selection mode). - **Placement.** The line sits under the day header, below the live episode row. ## What

These are follow-ups from David's first real use of chat video on
2026-10-22, on an iPhone and on Telegram.

**1. Sent videos show a gray square.**
- Cause: `addMessageLocally` put the clip's file path in the bubble's
image thumbnail, because the server stores a video as stills with
`mime_type: image/jpeg`. The debug log has the matching
`ImageDescriptor.encoded` FlutterError.
- `MessageFile` now keeps `video` (its duration) from the wire model.
- `uploadVideoServer` keeps a copy of the first sampled frame.
- The bubble shows that frame with a play badge and the clip's length.
- Uploads are paired with their own source file, since they finish out
of order.
- The server's thumbnail for a video, used after a reload, is now its
opening frame instead of a shrunken overview grid.

**2. Mobile chat can't be interrupted.**
- Send disappeared while Omi was answering, and there was no Stop.
- Now an empty composer shows **Stop** during a reply.
- Sending a message during a reply stops that reply first and is then
answered. The earlier question stays in the thread, so the model sees
both.
- Text already shown stays. An empty placeholder is removed. A stopped
reply is never marked failed.
- The HTTP request is actually aborted (`cancelSignal` →
`AbortableRequest`), so the server cancels generation.
- Backend: the app turn lease is now released when the stream closes
early. It also waits up to 0.75 s for a just-released lease before
answering 409. Before this, a resend could get 409 until the lease went
stale (300 s).

**3. Telegram and iMessage: a correction replaces a reply nobody has
seen yet.**
- Each inbox row gets content-free `supersedes` and `chat` fields.
- While a turn streams, a side task checks every 2 s for a newer plain
message in the same conversation. It uses the existing
`status`/`created_at` inbox index.
- The turn stops at its next non-terminal frame, but only if:
  - nothing was delivered,
  - no draft was shown,
  - no tool wrote anything.
- A stopped turn sends no apology, completes its row and releases its
lease, so the correction is answered next.
- Commands, button callbacks, link proofs, album parts, reentry turns
and terminal frames never trigger this.
- Otherwise the queue stays first in, first out, exactly as before.

**4. Voice transcription failures were invisible.**
- The client logged only at debug level, so the shared debug log had
nothing during the 2026-10-22 Modulate credit outage, when every request
returned 502.
- Failures now record a content-free `voice_transcription_failed` event
with the HTTP status (or the error type when there is no response). The
response body is not decoded, because the app-client schema inventory
allows response decoding only through generated models.
- When the fault is on the server, the message says "Something went
wrong on our side."

Episodes v1.1: structure at first words, moments that keep up, a live clock that holds (#23198) ## What Episodes v1.1: the live episode now exists from the first words, keeps its notes current during steady talk, and doesn't lose speech when a session moves. The app's live clock no longer drops to 0s. These problems were found on the only real user so far: 3 episodes in about 10 hours, each created 6–34 minutes late with one model update. ## Why it was broken - **The episode existed only after a successful model call.** The first nano call needs a 45 s pause or 600 words. Until then, Home showed "Listening now", its timer fell back to capture state, and fragment conversations sat as separate rows under it. - **A moment ended only when the next batch arrived.** Steady talk produced no updates for minutes. The buffer lives in one pusher process, so a pod move or a reconnect dropped what was buffered. - **The app's running length had three fallbacks.** The last one was a transcript offset that resets with every conversation. With the Omi pendant on iOS, `liveCaptureStartedAt` reads null whenever the ingress health lease lapses, so the label dropped to 0s and back. - **Idle closes were stamped with the time of the lazy read**, up to 8 h after the episode actually ended. ## Changes **Backend (`utils/episodes`)** - **Structure before notes.** `service.attach_conversation` runs at a conversation's first live words. It opens or joins the live episode by the cheap rules, with no model call. - Live splits, short fragments and parallel captures join the episode at once, so Home hides them under one row. - An ambiguous gap (2–30 min) joins provisionally (`pending_boundary`). That conversation's first moment asks Jev, and on a confident "moved on" the conversation is split into the next episode (its link is rewritten and its provisional items are left behind). - **New moment triggers.** - `interval`: after `MOMENT_MAX_SECONDS` (180 s) of steady speech. - Early first moment: the first moment of a live stretch comes at 30 s and 60 words, so the row gets a title within about a minute. - `session_end`: the pusher teardown flushes the buffer. - **Honest idle closes.** `closed_at` is `min(now, last_activity_at + CLOSE_GAP_SECONDS)`. - **Gate cost.** Live capability reads are cached per process for 2 min (`client_seen_cached`), so Redis is read about once per user per process per 2 min instead of once per moment. Live sessions are counted at first speech. - **Metrics that add up.** Every bounded series is exported at zero from process start. Replicas come and go, and a counter born at its first increment made `increase()` miss rare events; the cost counter read about 0. **App** - **`LiveStartAnchor`**, held by `EpisodeProvider` and shared by the Home row, the live page and the device page. - It counts from the server episode start, else from the earliest capture start seen while streaming. - It is sticky across null reads and reconnects, and never falls back to a transcript offset. - It resets when the episode closes or streaming stops. - **Polling.** Every 10 s until a live episode exists, then every 30 s. - **Narrower rebuilds.** The Home row selects only (display state, start, source) instead of watching the whole `CaptureProvider`. The device page selects the start instead of the last segment end. ## Review A GLM-5.3 review per milestone ran in parallel. Both verdicts were SHIP_WITH_FIXES, and the fixes are in the last commit: - the session-end flush is scoped to the ending session's conversation; - provisional joins are keyed per conversation; - a failed notes call after a split keeps a structural episode; - the attach counter remembers several recent conversations per user; - the latency histograms are primed; - the anchor adopts a server start once per episode and keeps the old start across an idle close during a lapsed lease; - quick polling stops after 3 minutes without an episode; - no timer is armed after dispose; - the device page's live length ticks in its own row; - a widget test reproduces the 0s bug. Not fixed: the listen fallback (used only when pusher is unavailable) still relies on finalization for its buffer, as documented in `live.py`. ## Tests - **Backend** (`BACKEND_UNIT_TEST_FILE_LIST` + `./test.sh`): the 6 `test_episodes_*` suites all pass. New cases cover: - the attach opening an episode with no model call, and being idempotent; - fragments and parallel captures joining; - a pending join that Jev splits, and one that Jev keeps; - a long-gap attach; - the idle `closed_at`; - the interval and early first moment; - the session-end flush; - attach and session counting through the gate; - the gate's read cache. - **App:** `live_start_anchor_test` covers a lease lapse, a reconnect re-arm, the episode start winning and then a close, server clock skew, and the adaptive polling. 411 tests across the episode, device, Home and perf suites pass, including `sync_indicator_isolation_test`. UI-Evidence: none -- no layout or copy change; the row, live page and device page render the same, only the running-length source and update timing change (covered by unit tests) ## Product invariants affected - INV-TASK-2: unchanged. Provisional items are still never action items, and a split drops nothing into Tasks. - INV-PERF-1: no frame-rate timers. The row's rebuild scope is narrower, and polling is 10 s only while no live episode exists and a live surface is on screen. - INV-DATA-1: no routing change. Same `/v1/episodes` API and base URL. Failure-Class: none ## Rollout `EPISODES_ENABLED` kill switch, unchanged. Beta channel (TestFlight) only, per David (2026-10-22). fix: preserve pendant finalization across disconnects (#23195)

## Problem and change

Mono pendant/phone capture can disconnect before its quiet deadline,
leaving a content-bearing conversation in progress without a durable
finalization job. A reconnect with a new client identity then strands
the old row.

Arm one durable quiet check per conversation at session setup and on
every mono socket exit. Leave capture ownership unchanged until the
check re-reads the row and recording lease, then admit through the
transactional SERVER_RECOVERY lifecycle. Checks persist on the inline
GKE listen tier even without queue bindings; the Cloud Run reconciler
owns their due wakes on a default 60-second cadence (300 seconds when
disabled). Same-conversation continuation defers the check; a new
identity cannot suppress the old row. Existing desktop
clean-close/multichannel paths and processing-generation fences remain
authoritative. An independent fast sweep selects an indexed
content-bearing due window after five minutes (avoiding ~392k historical
in-progress stubs); the existing two-hour full scan remains always on
with its own cursor and five-minute cadence for markerless content or
unknown leases; new sessions have a direct indexed due item even after
process death. When the fast sweep clips its eligible window, it resumes
after the considered rows rather than the scan tail, preventing refused
unknown-lease rows from starving later expired-lease rows.

## Rollout and kill switch

Ship on: LISTEN_QUIET_FINALIZATION_ENABLED=true (source default and
dev/prod manifest/Helm bindings). Deploy the queue-capable Cloud Run
consumer/reconciler/worker before GKE listen for minute-scale recovery
and metric acceptance. A listen-only producer rollout retains durable
indexed custody; recovery wakes and the metric begin when the consumer
revision serves, so that interval is a partial rollout. Use the existing
durable-finalization queue and worker. Set false on listen and all
API/reconciler/finalization-worker hosts to stop arming, retire
unadmitted quiet checks, and restore the previous 2-hour fallback
threshold. Already-admitted processing jobs finish normally. The
declared due-content collection-group index must be READY before
release; the existing Firestore readiness gate enforces this. This PR
changes source/manifests only: no production write, index application,
conversation redrive, deploy, or PR merge was performed.

Before any future `singleton_loops: 100` graduation, restrict
finalization-loop lease ownership to queue-capable consumers: an inline
GKE leader currently no-ops that existing global lease. This PR does not
change that fleet lever.

Observe an expired-lease disconnect reaching one processing revision;
verify reconnect continuation defers without splitting. Alert on
increase(omi_conversation_orphaned_unfinalized_total[10m]) > 0; no user
labels. Counter counts observations, so retries can repeat a row. Legacy
backlog drain remains subject to rotating scan/admission caps; forward
sessions have per-row due custody.

An outage can leave a small set of durable batch units held, while the
existing paid-redrive CLI scans the owner's lifetime history and
includes old disposition receipts. That blocks a bounded repair for
owners with more than 1,000 jobs and makes a new canary scope include
already spent work.

intersection, paginated owner discovery, and a private immutable cohort
manifest. Dry-run bootstraps the census digest without paid calls or
Firestore writes; apply requires the unchanged manifest and approved
digests. Canary and remainder retain fixed-prefix replay and paid-epoch
fences, and the first non-success stops further units.

Projection/enrichment preserve notes, audio, usage and ledger
convergence while suppressing repair-derived reminders/notifications and
creation webhooks, including pending effects-only work. Later normal
revisions resume normal behavior. Silent bridge cleanup retains its debt
rather than cancelling task reminders. The serving changes must be
deployed before any silent paid apply.

their original tool and approved digests; this version deliberately
refuses to adopt or reset them. The optional unit-ID file and cohort

perf(episodes): memoize the live transcript's per-notify derivations

Every capture notify rebuilt the live transcript's timeline from
scratch: a copy of every segment, a speaker resolver over the whole
conversation, the episode's moment/item decoration scan (moments x
segments), a photo re-sort and re-group — all on the UI isolate, again
and again for as long as the capture ran and the transcript grew.

The state now memoizes the snapshot, resolver, decorations and photo
groups behind one key (transcript version, list identities and lengths,
people identity, episode instance, conversation id), so a notify that
changes none of them rebuilds nothing and a new line costs only its own
row. Session resets that swap the segment list without a version bump
are covered by the list identity in the key.

fix(listen): prevent stale in-progress recovery starvation (#23194)

Old discarded `in_progress` rows occupy the reconnect scanner's
oldest-ten window indefinitely. Finalization refuses those rows, while
the wrapper discards its boolean and the scanner logs an attempt as if
it recovered the row. A newer content-bearing orphan can remain
invisible forever.

Recovery now claims a durable ten-row page, newest eligible first, and
advances a per-user CAS cursor before attempting it. Refusals and
failures cannot pin that cursor. Claims have a shared one-minute
backoff; empty/short tails wrap; each scan reads at most 20 candidate
documents plus cursor/deletion-marker state and a CAS reread. The claim
transaction checks the authoritative account-deletion marker before
writing, so erasure cannot be followed by recreated cursor metadata.
Protected rows remain unchanged. No-op paths log their reasons,
`route=noop` returns false, and
`omi_stale_recovery_outcome_total{outcome}` records truthful per-row
dispositions without UID/content labels. Accepted means handoff/empty
deletion, not worker completion.

Default on. Kill switch: `STALE_IN_PROGRESS_RECOVERY_ENABLED=false`. The
kill switch is declared in canonical runtime configuration and both
listen Helm environments. One new descending Firestore composite is
declared/generated; it must be READY before shipment. No workflow
changes, index application, deploy, production write, redrive, or merge
is part of this PR. This is separate from P53 pendant disconnect
finalization.

fix(stt): require stronger language evidence for short probes (#23176) Six-second synthetic Chinese clips were classified as English at confidence 0.804–0.839, passed the 0.80 permission floor, and produced Latin phonetics through Parakeet. Require 0.90 audio-language confidence for probes shorter than ten seconds. Longer probes keep 0.80, and declared supported languages retain their existing route. The CPU selector/intake and worker share the floor. Probe duration comes from actual decoded frames, not the provider response; the worker checks its validated unit duration so previously admitted short uncertain metadata also fails closed. `STT_PRERECORDED_SHORT_LID_GUARD_ENABLED` defaults on; only `false` restores the previous floor on the affected CPU or worker runtime. This is independent of the existing language guard. No deploy, account mutation, or replay is part of this PR. The regression fixture records five synthetic clip hashes and their frozen LID decisions. Tests replay those decisions through prerecorded selection, intake freezing and the worker adapter, and check duration boundaries, declared/longer routes and rollback. These are deterministic policy regressions, not a new vendor replay or a general LID-accuracy claim. Production cost coverage: the exported counters do not join probe duration and confidence to the selected route. The share of Parakeet-routed units with samples under ten seconds and confidence 0.80–0.90, and the resulting daily cost delta, are unmeasurable from current aggregate telemetry. No numeric cost or production misroute-rate claim is made. The policy change is limited to that short uncertain subset. Validation: 107 focused backend tests passed via `backend/test.sh` (audio-language and language-custody suites), and `make preflight` passed. Production/staging acceptance remains unrun; the next train must include the CPU changes and a separate worker image promotion before qualification. as the app's own login item: Cua Spaces Helper.app inside the app bundle,
registered with SMAppService.agent, signed with the Cua team and a stable
designated requirement. System Settings lists it by name and icon, and its
permissions are kept by bundle id across updates.

  permissions; repairs a helper that launchd lost after the app was replaced.

  `host.service` check in `cua doctor`; `cua host setup` uses the helper when
  the app is installed and never reinstalls the old LaunchAgent over it.
- Packaging: helper bundle, launcher, pinned cua-spacesd (sha256-checked),
  inside-out signing; uninstall.sh removes old and new and resets their
  privacy entries.

The login item now runs the app's own executable (`CuaSpacesMac
--service-helper run`), which starts the bundled cua-spacesd
(Contents/MacOS/cua-spacesd) as its child. macOS holds the app responsible,
so Screen Recording and Accessibility are both asked for and listed under
"Cua Spaces". With a separate helper bundle, macOS filed Accessibility under
"Cua Spaces Helper" but Screen Recording under "Cua Spaces": two names.

commits.message:
fix(llms): keep tests green after the release catalog regen (#15240)

* fix(llms): keep Bedrock Sonnet 4.5 through models.dev deprecation

models.dev now marks Claude Sonnet 4.5 on Bedrock (bare id and all geo
profiles) and Z.AI Coding Plan's glm-5.2 as deprecated, and catalog
normalization drops deprecated models. The next `bun run version` regen
would therefore:

- remove Sonnet 4.5 from the Bedrock catalog, so resolveBedrockModelId
  can no longer confirm a geo profile and sends the bare id, which AWS
  rejects for on-demand use
- leave zai-coding-plan's default model missing from its catalog

Retain the deprecated Sonnet 4.5 Bedrock entries in normalization (used
by both generation and the live catalog refresh) until AWS retires the
model, and move the Z.AI Coding Plan default to glm-5.3.

Also stop pinning ClinePass fallback tests to a specific model the Cline
backend no longer lists; they now check against the generated catalog.

* test(desktop): give the compiled plugin startup test a generous import timeout

Cold Windows runners intermittently take longer than the 4s default to start
the sandbox child, failing sdk-test. The test covers resource loading, not
startup time.

* revert(llms): drop the deprecated Bedrock Sonnet 4.5 retention

Let models.dev deprecations flow through the catalog as before. Point the
Bedrock geo-prefix test at Claude Haiku 4.5, which models.dev still lists, so
it passes after the release catalog regen.

fix(vscode): stop GitHub connection poll from flashing the loading indicator (#15235)

* fix(webview): stop GitHub connection poll from flashing the loading indicator

* refactor(webview): pass named options to GitHub connection load

feat(vscode): hide Plan/Act toggle and auto-approve bar for cloud sessions (#15233)

* feat(vscode): hide Plan/Act toggle for cloud sessions instead of disabling it

* feat(vscode): hide auto-approve bar for cloud sessions

fix(desktop): show a startup screen with Retry and Export diagnostics when the Hub fails (#15130)

* fix(desktop): start the local Hub after the sidecar is reachable

The sidecar ran Hub setup before starting its server. When the Hub failed
or hung, the webview had nothing to connect to, and every action surfaced
as "desktop backend endpoint not ready" or a confusing sign-in/save error.

Start the server and publish the endpoint first, then run the existing Hub
setup (login-shell PATH, bundled CLI `hub ensure`, session manager) in the
background. Its status (starting, ready, failed) is broadcast as
`hub_status` and replayed to each new connection. Setup that has not
finished after 30 seconds reports failure but keeps running, so a slow Hub
still completes. `retry_hub` retries; commands other than the status,
retry, and diagnostics export wait while startup is in progress, as they
previously waited for the transport. Failures are logged and reported to
telemetry; the user-facing message is fixed text.

* feat(desktop): show a startup screen with Retry and diagnostics export

Until the local Hub is ready, show a spinner instead of the app. If Hub
startup fails, show what happened with Retry and an Export diagnostics
button that uses the existing Hub-independent export. If the desktop
backend itself is unreachable for 30 seconds, say so and offer Reload.

The app mounts the first time the Hub is ready and then stays mounted; the
screen covers it again only if a later Hub startup fails. The Hub update
dialog moves outside this gate so the startup mismatch check cannot fire
before it is listening.

* fix(desktop): address startup screen review feedback

- Replace the app with the startup screen when a later Hub startup fails,
  instead of covering it. Dialogs portal outside the inert wrapper, so an
  open one kept trapping focus and disabling clicks behind the screen. The
  screen now sits below dialogs (z-40) so the Hub update prompt stays on top.
- Render the window title bar on the startup screen so frameless Windows
  windows keep their minimize/maximize/close controls and drag region.
- Drop a command that waited for Hub startup if its connection closed in
  the meantime. Close cleanup has already run by then, so work such as a
  browser sign-in started for that connection could not be cancelled.

* fix(desktop): keep open conversations through a Hub startup failure

Unmounting the app when a later Hub startup failed discarded open threads
and the selected session, and Retry remounted it before the Hub was ready.

Keep the app mounted and hide it with React Activity whenever the Hub is
not ready. Hidden Activity content keeps its state but unmounts effects, so
open dialogs and popovers, including portaled ones, are hidden and release
their focus traps and body pointer-events while the startup screen shows.
The hook also resets to "starting" when the transport drops, so a restarted
sidecar's status is never read from the previous one.

* fix(desktop): resume stream flushing and avoid leaking a manager on retry

- Hiding the app with Activity runs useChatSession's effect cleanup, which
  cleared the stream flush timer but left its ref set. Activity keeps refs,
  so after the app was restored schedulePendingStreamFlush saw the stale id
  and never scheduled again, stalling streamed text. Reset the ref (and the
  turn-end reconcile timer ref) in those cleanups.
- initializeSessionManager installs the local binding before its final
  approval-readiness sync. If that sync failed, a retried Hub startup
  created a second manager and overwrote the binding without disposing the
  first. Reuse the installed binding and only re-run the sync.

* fix(desktop): keep the open remote conversation when the app is shown again

Showing the app again after a Hub restart re-runs Activity effects, so the
get_process_context bootstrap selected a fresh draft for the connected SSH
environment and navigated away from the open conversation. Refresh the
remote environment on every load, but bootstrap navigation only after the
first successful one.

Co-authored-by: Saoud Rizwan <saoudrizwan@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(desktop): reset voice input when the app is hidden mid-recording

Hiding the app with Activity runs SpeechInput's unmount cleanup, which
cancels the recording, but keeps its listening/processing state. The
cancelled recording could no longer clear that state, so the composer
stayed read-only after the Hub recovered.

Co-authored-by: Saoud Rizwan <saoudrizwan@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Cursor Agent <cursoragent@cursor.com>
Co-authored-by: Saoud Rizwan <saoudrizwan@users.noreply.github.com>

build(desktop): bump @tauri-apps/cli to 2.12.3 for fast RPM bundling (#15278)

* build(desktop): bump @tauri-apps/cli to 2.12.3 for fast RPM bundling

Tauri CLI <= 2.12.2 bundles rpm-rs 0.16, whose compressed payload
writer takes ~6.5 min locally (~19 min on CI runners) to package our
~440 MB Linux payload. 2.12.3 ships rpm-rs 0.30, which builds the
same RPM in ~8s.

* test(desktop): track NSIS 3.13 pinned by Tauri CLI 2.12.3

Tauri CLI 2.12.3 moves its bundler from NSIS 3.11 to 3.13
(tauri-apps/tauri#16237). Update the installer test's CLI/NSIS pins
and the desktop-test.yml download (SHA1 verified against the bundler's
NSIS_SHA1).
chore: make @saoudrizwan sole code owner of .github/ and README.md (#15279)

feat(telemetry): report per-run stall signals (#15228)

* feat(telemetry): report per-run stall signals

Add task.run_health (one per agent run, every exit path) and task.run_idle
(at most once per run, after 60s with no runtime event) so harness stalls
can be measured from telemetry instead of transcripts.

run_health carries the longest gap between runtime events and what preceded
it, finish reason, final message shape and a text signature of a final
text-only turn. session.input_sent gains agentBusy, msSinceTurnEnd and a
bumpKind label (probe/nudge/greeting) so the user's reaction to a run can be
paired with it; task.cancelled gains msSinceLastEvent. No message text is sent.

* refactor(telemetry): move run stall signals into a core observer

Stall diagnostics now come from a core RunHealthObserver that watches
runtime events, instead of living in the agent loop. Its fields are added
to agent.run-finished / agent.run-failed through a runEndTelemetryProperties
hook, replacing task.run_health and the task.cancelled additions.

Also fixes measurement gaps: tool-argument streaming now emits a
tool-call-delta progress event, the silence before a run ends is counted,
and a turn rejected before reaching history is labelled empty.

* fix(telemetry): tighten run stall signals

Clear finishReason per turn, skip textSignature for media-only replies,
keep stall fields off replayed queued prompts, and document the run
health observer.

* fix(telemetry): identify the run on its run-end stall fields

agent.run-finished / agent.run-failed carry no session, model or provider of
their own, so the stall fields could not be grouped by model or provider,
paired with the user's next message (session.input_sent), or filtered to
root agents. RunHealthObserver now adds sessionId, isSubagent, providerId and
modelId to the run-end properties; undefined values are omitted.

* fix(telemetry): keep stall labels on prompts sent during a queued run

A queued prompt replayed by the drain starts its run unlabelled, but the
session-wide drain flag also stripped the stall fields from new prompts
the user sent while that queued run was busy. Only the replay itself (the
input that starts the run) is unlabelled now.

Tool-argument chunks now report progress at most once a second: each
event copies the whole conversation, and a large file write streams
thousands of chunks.

* fix(telemetry): mark only the replayed queued prompt as a replay

The queue drain now marks the one input it replays, and runTurn consumes
that marker, instead of inferring a replay from the session-wide drain
flag. Fresh user input during a queued run keeps its stall fields
whether the run is busy or just finishing.

---------

Co-authored-by: Max Paulus 🥪 <max@cline.bot>

repos.description: Developer-friendly OSS embedded retrieval library for multimodal AI. Search More; Manage Less.

commits.message:
feat!: return lazy iterators for table and namespace listings (#4599)

Make table and namespace listings consistent with other resource
listings across Rust, Python, and TypeScript. Callers can iterate over
individual names across all pages, with configurable page sizes and
continuation tokens.

In order to avoid breaking existing Python users, this change adds some
compatibility methods to the returned Python iterators. Code such as:
```
for t in db.list_tables().tables:
    print(t)
```
will continue to work as expected because the iterator has a `tables`
field and a `page_token` field, which function as expected to reveal the
first page of results. In other words, it is never necessary to use the
iterator __as an iterator__. It may be used as if it were an old-style
response object. (As the iterator progresses, the `tables` list may
switch to the second, third, etc. page of results.) Similar
compatibility code allows the async python API to keep working as well.

fix(python): keep a renamed Permutation column in its position (#4626) The `Permutation.rename_column` docstring says it "only changes the name of the column that is visible from this permutation". But `permutation.py:868-870` adds the new name at the end of the selection and then deletes the old key, so the renamed column also moves to the last position. Hugging Face `datasets`, which `Permutation` mirrors (#2725), keeps it in place. Positional formats feel it most: `with_format("numpy")` swaps the feature order of every row. Before, on `d97df0c`: ``` $ python repro.py /python/python # lancedb 0.41.0b12 extension, Python sources from the tree ['id', 'value'] ['value', 'row_id'] [{'value': 0, 'row_id': 0}] [[10 1]] ``` After: ``` $ python repro.py /python/python ['id', 'value'] ['row_id', 'value'] [{'row_id': 0, 'value': 0}] [[ 1 10]] ```
repro.py (its first output line, lancedb.__file__, is cut above) ```python import sys; sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1]) import tempfile import lancedb from lancedb.permutation import Permutation print(lancedb.__file__) db = lancedb.connect(tempfile.mkdtemp()) tbl = db.create_table("t", [{"id": i, "value": i * 10} for i in range(3)]) perm = Permutation.identity(tbl) print(perm.column_names) renamed = perm.rename_column("id", "row_id") print(renamed.column_names) print(renamed.__getitems__([0])) print(renamed.with_format("numpy").__getitems__([1])) ```
For comparison, `datasets` 5.1.0 gives `['new_id', 'value']` for `Dataset.from_dict({'id': [1, 2], 'value': [3, 4]}).rename_column('id', 'new_id').column_names`. No issue exists for this. The fix rebuilds the selection dict in order. The cost: code that renamed a column and then read it by position in numpy batches (say `[:, -1]`) gets a different column after this, with no error. `rename_columns` calls `rename_column` once per name, so it gets the fix too. rows.

so it accepts both filter types.

covers `count_rows`, `to_table`, `head` and a projection that excludes

with a `WHERE` clause.

`ruff format --check` pass.

fix(python): keep OpenaiReranker scores on the rows they rate (#4549)

`OpenaiReranker._rerank` asks the chat model for a relevance score per
document. The model can return the documents in any order, for example
sorted by score. The reranker then replaces the `text` column with the
documents in that order and appends the scores in that order. The other
columns keep the input order.

So after a rerank, the `text` and `_relevance_score` of a row belong to
a different row. The `id`, the vector and every other column still
describe the original row. If the model leaves out a document,
`append_column` raises `ArrowInvalid`, because the new column has fewer
rows than the table.

## Fix

`_rerank` keeps the `text` column unchanged, so it also keeps its
position and type. It maps each score back to its row by the document
content. If the model leaves out a document, `_rerank` raises a
`ValueError` that gives the number of documents with no score.

## Tests

`python/python/tests/test_openai_reranker.py` replaces the chat client
with a stub that returns a fixed reply. The tests do not need `openai`
or an API key.

- One test returns the documents sorted by score. It checks that each
`id` keeps its own `text` and score. On `main`, the row with id 1 gets
the text `cats purr`, which belongs to id 2.
- One test returns 2 of 3 documents. It checks for the `ValueError` with
the count of missing documents. On `main`, the call raises
`ArrowInvalid: Added column's length must match table's length`.
- Both tests fail on `main` and pass with the fix.
- `test_rerankers.py`: 16 passed, 13 skipped, on the lancedb 0.40.0
wheel with and without the fix. The skipped tests need real API keys.
- `ruff format --check` and `ruff check` (0.9.9) pass on the changed
files.
- I did not build the native extension. I ran the tests against the
lancedb 0.40.0 wheel with the changed file copied over it. In that
wheel, `rerankers/openai.py` and `rerankers/base.py` are byte-identical
to `main`.

The Node SDK has no OpenAI reranker, so there is no parity change. This
change does not conflict with #4515, which edits `_client` in the same
file.

fix(python): stop retrying permanent embedding errors and cap the backoff delay (#4542)

Permanent embedding errors (HTTP 400/404/422 and other 4xx) were retried
the full `max_retries` times with an
uncapped, multiplicatively jittered backoff, so a typo'd model name
looked like a hang of about an hour
(median 50 min of sleeping with a 404; see the issue for the repro and
numbers).

Changes (`python/python/lancedb/embeddings/utils.py`,
`embeddings/base.py`):
- An HTTP status in 4xx other than 408/409/429 is raised immediately.
The status is read from `status_code`,
`http_status`, `response.status_code`, an integer `code`
(google-api-core, urllib) or a botocore
`response["ResponseMetadata"]["HTTPStatusCode"]`. AWS throttling
reported as 400 stays retryable (matched by
  error code). `AuthenticationError` by name is unchanged.
- Still retried: 408, 409, 429, >=500, and anything without a
recognisable status (connection errors, timeouts,
custom exceptions), so existing custom embedding functions behave as
before.
- New keyword `max_delay=60` (last in the signature, default keeps call
sites working). `delay = min(delay * base,
max_delay)` with equal jitter `delay/2 + random() * delay/2`. With
defaults the waits are [1,2], [2,4], [4,8],
[8,16], [16,32], [30,60], [30,60] s, worst case about 182 s instead of
up to 2.5 h.
- The "Maximum number of retries" exception now has `from e`. The
`max_retries` comment in `base.py` describes the
  rules.

Not changed: `embeddings/openai.py` (it swallows `BadRequestError`; open
#4154/#4005/#3152 cover it), Retry-After
handling (the code never used it), and the "C Data interface error"
wrapping from the native layer (the original
message is now included in it).

Behaviour changes to be aware of: every 4xx except 408/409/429 fails
fast, including 401/403 coming through
`response.status_code` (requests/httpx), which used to be retried; a
provider that signals transient failures with
a 4xx and no AWS-style code is no longer retried; the first retry waits
1-2 s instead of 2-4 s.

Tests (`python/python/tests/test_embeddings.py`): 48 new cases (23 test
functions): permanent errors are not
retried, transient errors are, botocore-style errors, the delay is
capped, exact exponential growth without jitter,
jitter bounds, no float overflow for a large `max_retries`, the original
error is attached, and end to end through
`table.add` and `table.search` with a stub function (one call and no
sleep). On `main` 23 of them fail with the
change stashed; the rest are guards that must not change.
`test_embeddings.py`: 61 passed, 4 skipped.
`ruff format`/`ruff check` are clean on the touched files.

Verification caveat: `main`'s Python layer needs a newer native module
than the 0.40.0 wheel, so the tests were
run with the wheel's native module preloaded through a small shim (the
same shim ran the baseline on `main`); a
wider run of embeddings/pydantic/query/table tests has the same 36
failures before and after (that mismatch).
Not run: real provider APIs (a fake OpenAI-style server was used), Node
or Rust code.

fix(python): write plain Enum fields of a LanceModel as their values (#4357)

Since #3232, `pydantic_to_schema` maps an `Enum` field to the Arrow type
of its values, including enums without a `str`/`int` mixin. Writing such
models still failed: `model_to_dict()` returns `model.model_dump()`,
which keeps the Enum members, and Arrow can only convert members that
are also `str`/`int` instances.

```python
class Color(Enum):
    RED = "red"

class Item(LanceModel):
    color: Color

tbl = db.create_table("items", schema=Item)
tbl.add([Item(color=Color.RED)])
# pyarrow.lib.ArrowTypeError: Expected bytes, got a 'Color' object
```

`create_table(data=[...])` fails the same way, and int-valued enums
raise `ArrowInvalid`.

`model_to_dict()` now replaces Enum members with their values, including
in nested models and lists. Lists of plain scalars (vectors in
particular) are returned without being walked, so the per-row cost stays
about the same as `model_dump()` alone (21.3µs vs 20.3µs for a 1536-dim
model). Reading back is unchanged: Pydantic already validates the stored
value into the Enum member.

Added `test_plain_enum_values_are_written`, which covers str and int
valued enums, `Optional` and `List` fields, and an Enum inside a nested
model, and checks that `to_pydantic` round-trips the rows. It fails with
the `ArrowTypeError` above before the change. `test_pydantic.py`,
`test_embeddings.py`, `test_table.py` and `test_db.py` pass, and `ruff
format --check` / `ruff check` are clean.

fix(python): keep embedding functions registered without an alias readable (#4356)

`EmbeddingFunctionRegistry.register()` documents that the class name is
used when no alias is given, and it does register the class under that
name. But it stored the alias itself (`None`) as
`__embedding_function_registry_alias__`, which is what
`function_to_metadata()` writes into the table schema. A table using
such a function gets `"name": null` in its `embedding_functions`
metadata, and any later read of the functions fails:

```python
@get_registry().register()
class MyEmbed(TextEmbeddingFunction): ...

f = MyEmbed.create()
class Schema(LanceModel):
    text: str = f.SourceField()
    vector: Vector(4) = f.VectorField()

tbl = db.create_table("t", schema=Schema)
tbl.add([{"text": "hi"}])   # KeyError: None
tbl.search("hi")            # KeyError: None
```

This stores the key the class is registered under instead, so the class
name round-trips. For aliased classes the key is the alias, so their
metadata is unchanged. The TypeScript registry already falls back to
`ctor.name` in the same way.

Added `test_embedding_function_registered_without_alias`, which creates
a table with such a function, reopens it, and adds a row. It fails with
`KeyError` before the change. `test_embeddings.py`, `test_pydantic.py`,
`test_table.py` and `test_db.py` pass, and `ruff format --check` / `ruff
check` are clean.

fix(python): return original scores from hybrid search with normalize="rank" (#4343)

## Summary

With `rerank(..., normalize="rank")`, a hybrid query returns ranks (1.0,
2.0, 3.0, ...) in the `_distance` and `_score` columns instead of the
real vector distances and BM25 scores.

`_combine_hybrid_results` converted both result sets to ranks first, and
only then captured `original_distances` / `original_scores`. So the step
that restores the original values after reranking put the ranks back.
With `normalize="score"`, the real values are returned as expected.

Repro (RRFReranker(return_score="all"), vector distances 0 / 25 / 100):

| normalize | `_distance` returned | `_score` returned |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"score"` | 0.0, 25.0, 100.0 | 0.47, 0.67, None |
| `"rank"` (before) | 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 | 1.0, 2.0, None |
| `"rank"` (after) | 0.0, 25.0, 100.0 | 0.47, 0.67, None |

## Changes

- Capture the original `_distance` / `_score` columns before converting
them to ranks, then normalize the ranked column. The reranker input is
unchanged; only the values restored afterwards are fixed.
`AsyncHybridQuery` uses the same function, so both sync and async are
covered.

fix: gate remote job error construction behind the remote feature (#4233)

## Summary

Fixes #4142: `lancedb` failed to compile without the `remote` feature.

`TerminalResult::decode` in `rust/lancedb/src/job.rs` constructed the
`Error::Http` variant unconditionally, but that variant is declared
behind

crate's default feature set is empty, a plain `lancedb = "0.38"`

```
  --> rust/lancedb/src/job.rs:102:40
```

The module itself is not remote-only (it carries local job support), so
instead of gating `pub mod job`, both `Error::Http` constructions now go
through a small `remote_job_error` helper that resolves to `Error::Http`
with the `remote` feature and falls back to `Error::Runtime` without it.
A `request_id` is only ever `Some` for remote jobs, so the fallback is
unreachable in practice without the feature.

fix: table_names should not list loose .lance files as tables (#4203)

`table_names()` enumerates with `read_dir`, which returns files as well

`list_tables()` already applies the correct rule ("Only child
directories can be tables"), and
`test_listing_ignores_non_table_children` documents it, so the two
listing APIs currently disagree.

The practical damage is in `drop_all_tables()`, which is built on
`table_names`: with a loose `.lance` file present it deletes some real
tables, fails on the file with `os error 20 (NotADirectory)`, and then
fails the same way on every retry — the database can never be emptied
through the API, and the partial drop is not recoverable.

`common_prefixes` through the same `table_name` helper `list_tables`
uses; the sort/`start_after`/`limit` handling is unchanged.
`drop_tables` additionally attempts every name before returning, still
reporting the first error unchanged (kept rather than an aggregate error
so the mapped exception types in the bindings stay exactly as they are).

for the drop behavior — all three fail without the fix. Full `cargo test

fix(python): don't crash inferring schema for an all-null vector column (#4034)

Fixes #4033

`create_table(data=...)` without an explicit schema raised `IndexError:
index out of bounds` when a `vector`/`embedding`-named list column was
all-null. `_modal_list_size` infers the dimension with
`pc.mode(pc.list_value_length(arr))[0]`, and pyarrow's `mode` skips
nulls, so an all-null column produces a zero-length result and the `[0]`
subscript blows up.

The sibling `_infer_vector_dim` already guards the identical
`pc.mode(...)` with a `len == 0` check and returns `None`;
`_modal_list_size` just didn't. This makes `_modal_list_size` return
`Optional[int]` and return `None` when every value is null, and the call
site then leaves the column as a variable-length list instead of
inventing a fixed size — the dimension is genuinely unknowable when
there are no non-null rows.

Added a regression test that creates a table from an all-null
`list<float32>` vector column and asserts it succeeds, the column stays
a `list<float32>`, and the rows are queryable. It fails on `main` with
the `IndexError` and passes with this change.

fix(python): accept tuple and Arrow vector queries (#3972)

## Summary

Sync `Table.search()` declares tuple, `pyarrow.Array`, and
`pyarrow.ChunkedArray` query vectors as supported, and the async query
path already accepts them. The sync query builder only classified lists
and NumPy arrays as vectors, however, so these inputs were routed
through embedding/FTS resolution and then rejected. Arrow and tuple
inputs also did not contribute a query dimension when selecting among
multiple vector columns.

This change:

- recognizes the supported tuple and Arrow containers as sync vector
queries for both `auto` and explicit `vector` query types;
- converts them to the existing internal `float32` NumPy representation
at the sync builder boundary;
- infers dimensions from tuple, primitive Arrow, and list-valued Arrow
queries so schemas with differently sized vector columns select the
matching column.

The regression test uses two vector columns with dimensions 2 and 3. It
verifies tuple, Arrow array, and chunked Arrow queries through both sync
query modes and confirms the dimension-2 column is selected.
