package/valgrind: fix build with a libgcc built without optimization

The 64 bit division helpers of libgcc (__divdi3 and friends) are
compiled with -fexceptions -fnon-call-exceptions. Buildroot passes
TARGET_CFLAGS to gcc through CFLAGS_FOR_TARGET, so with BR2_OPTIMIZE_0
libgcc itself is built with -O0. GCC then keeps the (empty) exception
landing pads in those objects, which therefore reference
_Unwind_Resume() and __gcc_personality_v0(), normally provided by
libgcc_eh.a. Valgrind links its tools with -nodefaultlibs, so that
library is not available and the link fails on 32 bit targets:

  ld: libgcc.a(_divdi3.o): in function `__divdi3':
  libgcc2.c:1226: undefined reference to `_Unwind_Resume'
  ld: libgcc.a(_divdi3.o):(.data.rel.local.DW.ref.__gcc_personality_v0[DW.ref.__gcc_personality_v0]+0x0):
      undefined reference to `__gcc_personality_v0'
  collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
  make[4]: *** [Makefile:1180: memcheck-x86-linux] Error 1

Backport the upstream commit providing dummy definitions of both
symbols in libgcc-sup-<platform>.a, which is linked after -lgcc, so
toolchains providing the real symbols are unaffected. They can never be
reached, as Valgrind's core is plain C and never raises an exception.

This issue has been present since commit 0fe633cdff66 ("gcc: explicitly
use C{XX}FLAGS_FOR_TARGET instead of --enable-target-optspace"), which
started building the gcc target libraries with TARGET_CFLAGS, and thus
with -O0 when BR2_OPTIMIZE_0 is enabled, instead of -Os. This is not a
gcc regression: both gcc 11 and gcc 15 emit these landing pads at -O0.
It therefore affects 2015.08 and later, including 2025.02.x and
2026.02.x.

Fixes:
https://autobuild.buildroot.org/results/4a58c34308095e4d8ae91e0a779c94123ee497f6

Fixes: 0fe633cdff66febadc50bab3e0af4b3be53811c8 ("gcc: explicitly use C{XX}FLAGS_FOR_TARGET instead of --enable-target-optspace")

commits.message:
Merge pull request #1520 from twmb/1519-kfake

kfake: answer failed piggybacked share acks as Kafka does

kfake: answer a waiting ShareFetch's failed acks

A ShareFetch that carried a failed piggybacked ack and acquired no
records waited for records, and we dropped the response holding the
ack error. When the wait ended, we answered the acked partition with no
error, so the client read the failed ack as a success. Kafka holds ack
results until the fetch completes and answers them then. A waiting
fetch now keeps its failed acks and answers them when it completes.

The new test fails without the fix.
TestShareFetchAckedPartitionAnsweredOnce faults the request, which
completes the fetch at once, and TestShareGroupFetchMaxWaitBeyondOverhead
acks successfully.

kfake: answer a share partition once when it is acked and fetched

A ShareFetch carrying a piggybacked ack for a partition it also fetches
got two entries for that partition when the ack failed: one with the
ack error, then one with the fetch result. Kafka writes the ack result
into the fetch entry. kgo keeps the first entry it sees for a partition
and drops the rest, so it dropped the fetch result: records acquired
for the member were never delivered and sat until the acquisition lock
timed out, and a fetch error, including NOT_LEADER_OR_FOLLOWER and its
CurrentLeader, was lost.

The new test fails without the fix. TestShareGroupNonRetryableAckError
and TestShareGroupAckRequeue build their responses by hand, so they
cannot test kfake's response builder.

Merge pull request #1518 from spicysharkco/fix/strftime-12-hour-clock

kgo: format midnight and noon as 12 in strftime %I, %l and %r

kgo: format midnight and noon as 12 in strftime %I, %l and %r

The strftime directives %I, %l and %r used the hour modulo 12, which is
0 for midnight and noon. A record stamped 00:05:06 printed
"00  0 00:05:06 AM" for "%I %l %r". The 12-hour clock runs 1 to 12, so
the output is now "12 12 12:05:06 AM". Hours 1 to 11 and 13 to 23 are
unchanged.

commits.message:
test(materials): make the heartbeat-loss extraction scenario deterministic (#1994)

Test-only. The heartbeat-loss scenario failed intermittently on PostgreSQL (expected 2 transactions to be 0) because of three races in the test:

- The stale run read the shared test clock, so after `expire` its heartbeat could renew the lease before the takeover claimed; the run now keeps the time it claimed at.
- The claim skips a row a heartbeat has locked (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED); the takeover is retried, bounded, and asserted.
- A fixed 100 ms sleep assumed a post-takeover heartbeat had returned; the scenario now waits for one that reports the loss.

On failure the scenario releases the gated run before rethrowing, so its heartbeat timer does not outlive teardown.

release: v1.3.0-rc.1 (#1993)

Version 1.3.0-rc.1, the first release candidate for 1.3.0 (knowledge base). CHANGELOG section with breaking changes, release conditions and known issues; README News entries.

feat(workspace): polish knowledge base page layout (#1989)

UI-only polish of the knowledge base page; no data flow, API, persistence or i18n changes.

- The top-level drop ground folds away at rest and opens only while a file in a folder is dragged, so the list card sizes to its rows.
- Usage becomes one panel with the knowledge base allowance and the separately counted file storage side by side, each with a progress bar.
- File rows get type-aware tinted icons, status chips, taller rows with dividers and a hover tint; folders use the accent folder icon and open folders show their files on a sunken ground.
- The empty state is centred with an upload action.

fix(web-fetch): let DeepSeek fetch wait for headers until the request deadline (#1990)

DeepSeek's fetch endpoint sends response headers only after it has fetched the whole page, so the fixed 10s header timeout aborted slow pages that the provider still completed and billed. Use the request deadline (bodyTimeoutMs, default 30s) for the header wait, as the Firecrawl provider already does.

Fixes #1984

fix(whiteboard): make text and code selectable (#1952)

Whiteboard text and code elements can now be selected and copied: only their wrappers get select-text, copied code keeps indentation without line numbers, and the rest of the canvas stays non-selectable. Full-canvas motion wrappers are pointer-events none with only the element subtree receiving events, so earlier elements stay hit-testable, and dragging from shapes or empty canvas still pans. Selection is scoped to the whiteboard via a selectable prop, so slide playback is unchanged. Part of #1945 (step 1).

fix(editor): keep legacy narration markers stable across edits (#1953)

Key the cached legacy-audio evidence in useSceneIssues on the inputs observeLegacySpeechAudio reads (stage, scene id, order, and each speech action's id, text, audioId and audioInvalidated) instead of the scene object, so unrelated immutable edits no longer flash a local-audio-unchecked marker on the thumbnail. Nothing is persisted; real issues still surface. Also aligns the zh-TW sceneHasErrors label.

ci: run CI for the workbench-home integration branch (#1958)

Adds `integration/workbench-home` to the CI `push` and `pull_request` branch lists, following the existing integration branches, so the branch cut from `main` and its sub-PRs run the main CI. Tracked in #1957.

(cleanup) Remove BridgeJSONValue (#983)

Summary:
## Motivation

https://github.com/facebook/idb/issues/982 gave accessibility answers typed models in `FBSimulatorBridgeProtocol`, but the bridge between the host and the in-Simulator guest still had three problems:

- **Untyped data.** `BridgeJSONValue`, a "JSON of any shape" enum, still carried every other service's answers (notification settings, delivered notifications, health, network) and every accessibility request's parameters.
- **Hand-written coders.** Nearly every model in the protocol library wrote its own `init(from:)` and `encode(to:)`: 35 of them. Most existed to spell keys, to flatten a union into one object, or to tolerate shapes no guest of this revision sends.
- **Three wire dialects.** Service commands used Swift's automatic tagged encoding with `_0` wrappers. Accessibility requests were flat objects keyed by `verb`. Accessibility answers were untagged `ok` envelopes that only decoded once the host told the decoder, through `userInfo`, which request they answered.

This PR removes `BridgeJSONValue`, moves the protocol onto Swift-generated `Codable`, and gives every request and answer the same shape: the case's name keyed to what it holds.

## What changes on the wire

| | Before (protocol 4) | After (protocol 5) |
|---|---|---|
| Service command | `{"dns":{"_0":{"set":{"servers":["::1"]}}}}` | `{"dns":{"action":{"set":{"servers":["::1"]}}}}` |
| Accessibility request | `{"accessibility":{"_0":{"verb":"describe","pid":42,"traversal":…}}}` | `{"accessibility":{"action":{"read":{"pid":42,"options":{…}}}}}` |
| Where answers live | `values` (untyped), `accessibility`, `propertyList` | one `answers` list |
| Service answer | `{"values":[{"action":"clear","ok":true,"error":null,…}]}` | `{"answers":[{"health":{"answer":{"action":"clear","ok":true,…}}}]}` |
| Accessibility answer | `{"accessibility":{"ok":true,"tree":…,"pid":42}}`, typed only via the request | `{"answers":[{"accessibility":{"answer":{"tree":{"response":{…}}}}}]}` |

Every frame now decodes on its own, with no request-dependent decoding step.

## What it removes

Across the protocol library, the guest and the host, against `main`:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Hand-written `init(from:)` / `encode(to:)` in `FBSimulatorBridgeProtocol` | 35 | 5 |
| `BridgeJSONValue` (type and uses) | 112-line type, 27 uses | gone |
| `[String: Any]` in `FBSimulatorBridgeProtocol` | 13 | 3 |
| Lines in `FBSimulatorBridgeProtocol` | 2,543 | 2,102 |
| Production lines changed | | +831 / −1,028 |
| Test lines changed | | +1,429 / −902 |

That 2,102 includes the new service-answer models (`BridgeAnswer.swift`, 231 lines). The five coders that remain:

- **`BridgeAXScalar`** (two coders). An attribute's value is whatever the accessibility server answered (a string, a bool or a number), so it is an untyped scalar, not a variant.
- **`BridgeAXIndirect`** (two coders). The property wrapper that lets a node hold an optional node; it codes as the node itself.
- **One private helper** that records why a frame's accessibility request failed to decode, so the guest can answer with the reason.

Per file, in the protocol library: `BridgeAXOutcome.swift` 380 → 172, `BridgeAXRequest.swift` 272 → 162, `BridgeAXRequestDecoding.swift` 255 → 134, `BridgeAXAnswer.swift` 106 → 37, `BridgeAXNode.swift` 232 → 174, `BridgeJSONValue.swift` 112 → 0.

The flat, verb-keyed request form survives only where it is genuinely input: the one-shot command line's flags. Its parser moved, unchanged, from the protocol into the guest (`AccessibilityParameters`), which accounts for most of the guest's growth.

## The commits

Each commit leaves every suite passing, and each change in behaviour is pinned by a test before the code changes.

**Removing `BridgeJSONValue`**

1. **Pin accessibility requests as they travel in a frame.** Coverage only. The request tests now spell each request as frame JSON, and pin the exact bytes and the guest's lenient rules for flags and numbers.
2. **Decode accessibility requests straight from the frame.** `BridgeAXRequest` gets one keyed `Codable` with the same rules. *Removes:* the `[String: BridgeJSONValue]` decode, `payload` dictionaries, and `accessibilityParameters(of:)`.
3. **Pin every service answer as the host reports it.** Coverage only. The host passes a service's answer on as text, so that text is pinned exactly for every service.
4. **Model every other service's answer in the protocol.** Typed models for every service answer, and protocol version 5.
5. **Answer every other service with its typed model.** The guest builds those models. *Removes:* every dictionary the guest built for a service answer.
6. **Remove `BridgeJSONValue`.** *Removes:* the type, `BridgeResult.values`, and `BridgeOutput.write(_:)` for an arbitrary object.

**Generated coders and one wire shape**

7. **Pin every command and each kind of result as a frame carries it.** Coverage only: every command case and each kind of result, as literal frames.
8. **Generate the accessibility structs' coders.** `BridgeAXNode` takes its coding keys from `BridgeAXWire.Node` itself. *Removes:* the struct coders, and the decoding tolerances for shapes no guest of this revision writes.
9. **Name each command's action rather than `_0`.** Per-case coding keys, still generated.
10. **Send accessibility requests as their own cases.** Generated, tagged requests, with `validate()` for what a request means. *Removes:* the flat request coder from the protocol; the flat parser moves to the guest's command line.
11. **Answer every command in one list.** *Removes:* the separate `accessibility` and `propertyList` fields, and the service answers' coders.
12. **Send accessibility answers as their own cases.** *Removes:* every accessibility answer coder, `BridgeAXAnswer.Kind`, the `userInfo` key, `decode(_:as:)` and `answerKind`.

## Behaviour changes

- **The protocol is version 5.** The shared guest's socket directory is named by the version, so hosts and guests from either side of this change never meet.
- **Health reports booleans.** `ok` and record flags read `true`/`false` everywhere; approve, revoke and list used to say `1`/`0`.
- **Missing values are left out, not written as `null`.** Health and notification-settings text no longer contains `"error":null` or `"showsInLockScreen":null`.
- **Network lists travel as a property list.** A network store holds whatever was written to it, so its contents travel as a property list (base64 inside the JSON frame). The host renders the same JSON text from it.
- **Decoding tolerances are gone.** A host only reads its own revision's guest, which writes every answer whole, so it no longer tolerates:
  - a flag as a number;
  - a missing `truncated`, `asserted` or display capability;
  - an unknown error kind;
  - an oversized pid;
  - an unreadable modal.

  Such a frame is refused as an unparseable guest response.
- **Request validation.** A request that means nothing (a pid or display of 0, a client type on a non-semantic traversal, a negative tunable) is refused by the guest however it arrived. A malformed request's error names an unexpected value's JSON type (`null`, `an array`) rather than Foundation's description.
- **The one-shot command line** prints accessibility answers in the tagged shape, and health in the same shape the socket carries.

commits.message:
feat: format the generated files with rustfmt by default (#1785)

Templates rarely produce rustfmt-clean output, and the usual workaround
is a Rhai post hook shelling out to `cargo fmt`. That hook runs against
the temp template dir, which is a UNC path on Windows, so it breaks from
`--git` while working fine from `--path`.

- Formatting is on by default. Opt out with `[template] fmt = false` or
`--no-fmt`.
- Only the files a run actually wrote get formatted, so `--init` into an
existing project leaves the surrounding code untouched.
- `rustfmt` directly rather than `cargo fmt`: the latter's finest
granularity is the package, and handing it a path widens the set instead
of narrowing it. Each file is formatted against the edition of the
package it lands in.
- Formatting can never fail a generation. A missing component or an
unparseable file warns and carries on.
- `post = ["fmt"]` is a built-in identifier rather than a script, and
re-enables formatting for a template that opted out.

Closes https://github.com/cargo-generate/cargo-generate/issues/1776, and
the original request it narrows,
https://github.com/cargo-generate/cargo-generate/issues/884.

Related: https://github.com/cargo-generate/cargo-generate/issues/1435
stays open. Template authors no longer need the `cargo fmt` post hook,
which removes the reason most people hit that bug, but `system::command`
on the git path is unchanged.

fix(window): bring presented window reliably to front at launch

Keyboard-launcher launches (Raycast/Spotlight Enter) left the
LSUIElement app unforegrounded with a missing Dock icon until Mission
Control forced a refresh. Investigation across real-machine rounds
(recorded in the ADR-0017 supplements) pinned three cooperating causes:

- The launch activation retry never started at launch: the workspace
  window's participation events (anchor attach / occlusion / key) could
  all miss the launch moment when content installed before the window
  became visible and the visibility notification fired before the
  anchor attached. A deferred visibility rescan plus re-armable chain

  requires both isActive and menu bar ownership.

  system; forced activation is a three-hop sequence with real settle
  delays (accessory -> 0.1s -> regular -> 0.15s -> activate), which
  re-registers the app with WindowServer/Dock and reclaims the menu
  bar. Each acting attempt also re-asserts makeKeyAndOrderFront and
  orderFrontRegardless as a visible-layer fallback.

Harden no-hash Rust dist regression coverage

Fix crate_link_paths scan for no-hash dep files

The RustInputsPackager scans crate_link_paths for dependency rmeta
and rlib files, extracting the crate name from each filename via
rsplitn(2, '-'). This assumes every file has a -<metadata-hash>
suffix. When a file has no hash (e.g. libcrc_fast.rmeta produced by
a crate with crate-type = ["lib", "cdylib", "staticlib"]),
rsplitn yields a single element and the code hits continue, skipping
the file entirely.

The file is never packaged and sent to the dist worker, which then
fails with E0463: can't find crate for crc_fast.

Extract the crate-name-and-extension logic into a testable helper,
crate_name_and_ext_from_lib_path, that uses file_stem() to strip the
extension before rsplitn, then falls back to the whole stem as the
libname when no - separator is found.

Signed-off-by: KK <pandeykamal13526@gmail.com>
(cherry picked from commit 14b1d48688794b126c287969f1c8dbee4e1eeac5)

Fix parse_rustc_z_ls for deps without -HASH suffix

Modern rustc (1.75+) emits extended metadata per dependency line in
`rustc -Z ls=root` output:

  N libname[-hash] hash HASH host_hash ... kind ... public

Crates built without a content hash suffix (e.g. crc_fast, a
build-script artifact) appear as:

  N crc_fast hash 05bce6... host_hash None kind Unconditional public

parse_rustc_z_ls used splitn(2, ' ') which yields libstring as the
entire trailing metadata ("crc_fast hash 05bce6... host_hash ...").
The subsequent rsplitn(2, '-') finds no '-' and libname becomes the
whole string, so it never matches the bare "crc_fast" parsed from
rmeta filenames during crate_link_paths scanning.

The unmatched dep is silently skipped, its rmeta is not packaged for
the dist worker, and the worker fails with E0463: can't find crate
for `crc_fast`.

Fix: take only the first whitespace-delimited token of libstring
before the existing rsplitn('-') logic runs, so crates with and
without a -HASH suffix both resolve to the bare crate name.

scattered over an earlier unrelated part of the text (opus via "openrouter",
astra via "radius radius/gpt") and the real match ranked last. It now also
scores every contiguous occurrence and keeps the best alignment.

/resume matched one concatenated id/name/messages/cwd string. Scattered
matches in megabytes of message text or in UUIDs were noise, and the
position penalty buried real hits deep in a transcript. Fields are now
matched separately: name and cwd fuzzy, id and messages exact only, with no
position penalty. Ranking is name text, then id/message/cwd text, then
scattered name/cwd matches. Lowercased message text is cached per session.

Knowing how annoying re-logins in corporate environments can be, I think
we can open the browser and copy the code to the clipboard (what the user
asks for) without forcing it upon users (which I assume was the reason
it was removed in 8f0e9251b9265e73cb85e97b8a190db40c96e57c).

This change adds optional browser opening and code copying during
device-code login after an additional confirmation (usually Enter).
It should work for all providers, with an optional opt-out controlled
by the provider author, not user settings.

Updates of pi.dev installer installs run npm ci against a release
lockfile that pins every package, so npm never resolves versions and a
configured min-release-age does not apply. The --min-release-age=0 flag
had no effect, but security scanners that block it stopped the update.

Set up preview packages (#11260)

* feat: publish preview packages to pkg.earendil.com

CI packs every public package after the build, with internal dependencies
pointing at the same commit's builds. A workflow_run job publishes them to
the earendil-pkg worker with the job's GitHub OIDC token, moves main or
pr-<n>, and comments install commands on the PR. Closing a PR deletes its
ref. pi-env is left out because its daemons are only built for releases.

install their previews anyway. Fork PRs are no longer packed or
published, which keeps fork code out of the registry and removes the PR
lookup: the PR number now comes from the workflow_run event. The PR
comment is dropped; the job summary lists the install commands.

  selecting the PR into main; a branch can also have PRs into other
  branches, and the index expression tripped workflow linters.

  were uploaded as push builds.
- Move pr-<number> only while the PR is open into main with this commit
  as its head, checked live, so a late publish cannot recreate the ref of
  a closed PR; otherwise publish without a ref and print a notice.
- Set concurrency per job, so skipped fork runs never wait in a group.

* docs: drop the service rule from the preview-packages.yml header

* docs: name the earendil-works/pkg worker in the preview script

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Keep a complete addon when this launch's download fails

When a download failed, maybe_download_addons removed the addon directory
unconditionally. If another process had finished installing the addon in the
meantime, that deleted its good copy, possibly while its browser was loading
it. The handler now removes the directory only when it has no manifest.json,
in both the Python and TypeScript launchers, each with a regression test.

One window remains: two processes that both find a stale, non-empty partial
directory can still interleave its removal and their renames.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Count plugin-container processes as leftover browsers

leftover_browsers matched only processes running the --binary, but on
Linux Firefox's content processes run plugin-container, which sits
beside it. Those are the processes that keep spinning after a guard
fails to close its browser, so the report never named them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Test the ASCII font names through the packaging step

The test renamed a directory with ascii_file_names directly, so it would
still pass if add_includes_to_package stopped calling it. It now packages
a small font bundle, with 7z and the language packs stubbed out, and
checks the names that would go into the zip. A font file's extension is
always ASCII, so the name keeps it as is.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Keep a complete addon another process installed first

The atomic extraction removed the target before renaming into it. With two
processes downloading at once, the second could delete the first's finished
addon while its browser was loading it. If the first renamed in between, the
second's rename failed on the non-empty directory, and its error handler then
deleted the good copy, so it launched without uBlock Origin.

Rename first. If the target is not empty and already holds a manifest.json,
keep it and drop the temp dir; only an incomplete target is replaced. The
TypeScript port mirrors this and gains the atomic-extraction test, and both
gain a regression test for an addon installed during extraction.

iPhone Duo: the chat list's search field stays on screen in unfolded landscape

With no status bar height, SearchDisplayController starts a list-mode search bar 20pt above the top, which suits the
legacy fields: they are drawn at the bottom of the bar. The glass field is drawn at the top of its frame, in the
navigation bar's search row, already below the status bar, so the offset put it 20pt above the row. In the Duo's
unfolded landscape the list pane has no status bar (the clock is in the detail pane's corner), and the active field
sat at window y -12, half off the screen. A glass bar now starts at the row's top, its bottom where it was, so the
results' inset is unchanged. Any status bar height above 0, the legacy fields and `.navigation` mode lay out as before.

Verified on the Duo simulator, unfolded landscape: the field at window y 8 (was -12, from an lldb frame dump), and the
open animation, captured at 10x slow, settles there without a jump.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Chats tab menu: no trailing divider when there are no folders

The folder list keeps an .allChats entry (the server's dialogFilterDefault)
after the last folder is deleted, so the long-press menu read it as non-empty:
it said "Edit Folders" and appended a separator with no folders after it.
Decide on whether the list holds any folder instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Suspicious peers: hide buttons and emoji status, read nothing until accepted

While a user's chat shows the report/block panel (CachedUserData.isSuspiciousPeer),
their messages were only partly untrusted: plain-text links were stripped, but
buttons, rich-message links, link-preview text and their emoji status were live,
and the chat read their messages on sight. Until the panel is dismissed or the
account sends them a message:

- Reply-markup rows are not shown (bubbles, stickers, round videos). Rich messages go
  through instantPageForSuspiciousSender: links become plain text as in a plain
  message, inline pills and button rows are not shown, block indices are kept for
  rich-quote node ids. A link preview shows no button, opens nothing, and its text
  loses links too (MessageTextEntity.isShownFromSuspiciousPeer, now shared with the
  text bubble).
- The emoji status is hidden in the chat title, the panel's Premium-mark note and
  the profile header (with a collectible status's cover and colours).
- The history reads nothing, also while a non-contact's settings are still unknown.
- Sending a non-scheduled message clears canReport/canBlock locally (Add Contact
  stays), which ends the state.

Verified on the simulator with a temporary hook forcing the state (removed): keyboards
hidden and back live on dismiss, URL buttons likewise, title and profile show the
Premium star instead of the status, read decisions held and applied on dismiss and
on send (gate log; Skip Read History was on, so no read reached the server). Rich
messages are covered by InstantPageSuspiciousSenderTests only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

iPhone Duo: story camera rounds the chat list with the screen's corners

Opening the story camera slides the chat list aside, and a black strip on
its left edge (transitionCornersView) rounds its left corners like the
screen's. It was drawn with the one deviceMetrics.screenCornerRadius (55pt),
while the folded Duo screen's left corners are 8pt (hinge side; 59pt
outside). The strip now takes the screen's top-left and bottom-left radii
from layout.screenCornerRadii and is redrawn when they change (fold,
rotation). Where they are uniform, every other screen included, it is drawn
exactly as before.

Checked on the Duo simulator, folded portrait, with animations slowed 10x:
the sliding chat list's left corners went from 55pt to 8pt.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

iPhone Duo: story camera and editor clear the home indicator

On the folded screen (466x678) the 9:16 preview is 150pt taller than the
screen, so the camera and editor take their compact bottom layout, whose
offsets were tuned for home-button phones (the only other phones whose
preview overflows). Measured from the screen edge they put the camera's
mode selector, gallery and flip buttons, and the editor's bar, on the home
indicator (layout.intrinsicInsets.bottom, 20pt; the Duo's safeInsets.bottom
is 0).

- Camera: the bottom inset is at least the home indicator's (phones only).
  Every other phone has more room than that below the preview, so only the
  Duo changes. The collage reorder hint stays below the preview, as before.
- Editor: the bar sits 62pt above the indicator instead of the edge. The
  drawing screen's bar keeps matching it (rows above move up with it), and
  the sticker frame helper, shared with the cut-out screen, keeps its
  bottom limit in step. Beside the unfolded status island the bar still
  mirrors the top row, which already clears the indicator.

Checked on the Duo simulator, folded portrait: camera bottom row and
shutter 20pt higher, editor and drawing bars end at about 649pt, above the
indicator at about 669pt. Sticker editor not checked on screen.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

iPhone Duo: modal status bar, unfolded stories, column transitions, Edit/Done placement, contacts separators

Modal status bar. On a phone a modal card leaves a dark frame above it, so the navigation controller forces a white
status bar while one is up. On the Duo the status bar is a block in a corner beside the side strip (folded portrait:
84x170, glyphs at y 85-150) that the card covers, so the white glyphs sat over the modal's own, usually light, content;
unfolded landscape took the root's style under a full-screen modal. Where the status bar is a corner block beside a
strip it now takes the style of the topmost card that still overlaps the block (`coversStatusCorner(frame:)`, the
card's frame including an interactive dismiss: `presentedCardFrame`), else the root's, switching with the usual 0.2s
fade once a swipe has moved the card off the block entirely.

Stories on the unfolded screen use the iPad card layout. The viewer chose it by `widthClass == .regular`, which the
Duo's modal host never reports (no floating panels), so the unfolded screen took the phone layout and the story
filled it, cropped. The container now decides `isCardLayout` (regular width, or the Duo's inner screen:
`DeviceMetrics.isIPhoneDuoInnerScreen(size:)`) and hands it to the item set. Portrait keeps the card clear of the
status island; landscape centres it in the band beside the strip with 16pt margins (nothing reserves the top or the
bottom there), 324x637, and gives the input row at least a phone's width (375pt), since that card is narrower than any
phone and Stealth Mode's countdown placeholder (an animated text that never truncates) ran under the share button.

Column transitions. Chats' side column is its story capsule over the compose circle, a chat's its back circle over
the avatar capsule, at the same two places; shapes paired by role, so the story capsule travelled to the avatar's
place while compose faded out under it and back faded in. Column shapes now pair by index from the column's top
(`Role.column(n)`), as the row's right platters pair by index from the edge: each stays in place and swaps its items.

Edit/Done. Beside the strip the bar moves icon buttons into the column and an accent one into its trailing circle,
while text stays in the row, so on every Edit/Done screen Done jumped from the row into the strip. A button can now be
marked to stay in the row (`UIBarButtonItem.staysInRow`, `NavigationBarComponent.Button.staysInRow`,
`ItemListNavigationButton(staysInRow:)`), and every Edit/Done toggle's Done is: Chat Folders, Devices, Blocked
Users, privacy exceptions, Stickers, Archived Stickers, the proxy list, notification exceptions, channel admins,
members and removed users, the language list, chat backgrounds, Calls and the profile. Calls' Done is the accent
checkmark on every path (its empty-state paths, and the language list's and backgrounds' theme paths, made bold text);
chat backgrounds' toggle animates. The side column's glass now materializes through `isVisible` instead of alpha,
which native glass ignores, so an accent circle there no longer pops in.

Contacts. Invite Friends' separator ends 16pt short of the edge as the contact rows' do, and the standalone access
notice draws no separator above itself (every device).

Rules and helpers recorded in docs/iphone-duo-layout.md. Tests: DisplayTests (corner coverage, inner screen),
NavigationBarComponentTests (column pairing, row placement). Verified on the Duo simulator (folded portrait; unfolded
landscape and portrait stories) and the iPhone 18 Pro simulator.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

MtProtoKit: Cancel the backup address lookup when a context is cleaned up

MTContext's cleanup disposed every pending action except the backup
address discovery. A context freed while a lookup was in flight (the login
screen's network on macOS) hit the DEBUG leaked-disposable assert, and in
release the lookup kept running after the context was gone.

commits.message:
feat: iOS game data in the app's Documents, installed once; .app output, app icon and the name TOTK; faster iOS packaging

build_app.py --ios-game-data documents leaves the 17 GB RomFS image out of
the app; install_device.py --game-data copies it into Documents/GameData in
1 GiB parts with a SHA-256 marker and skips it when the device already has
it, so later installs take minutes. The app reads it through
TOTK_ROMFS_DATA, keeps it out of backups, and shows a line on screen
instead of starting when the data is missing or incomplete.

The iOS build can write an unsigned .app (install_device.py installs it
by APFS clone), carries the game's own icon (from the player's files, as on
the Mac) and is named TOTK on the home screen. The seed is cloned as one
folder, its manifest hashes reused, and compiled shader libraries cached by
source: 13-17 min -> 6-8.5 min. The build makes the contribution folder and
points the iPhone / iPad watcher at it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf: iPhone / iPad warm the shared list's render pipelines and draw while new ones are prepared; shader and pipeline counts shown

iPhone 14, the same play from app start: frames over 100 ms 73 -> 31,
pipelines built on the submit thread 1,221 -> 80, pipeline building inside
long frames 24.9 s -> 1.6 s. The warm-up also reads shader-seed/pso_list.tsv
(the shared list's pipelines, shipped by the iOS build). Draws whose pipeline
is not ready are skipped on iOS by default as on the Mac
(TOTK_ASYNC_PIPELINES=0 turns it off); work that writes memory still waits.
The shader box shows the new-shader and new-pipeline line on iOS too, on by
default on every platform.

fix(gfx): resolve indirect draws on the GPU timeline; Bayonetta 3 no longer drops objects while the camera moves

Bayonetta 3's colour pass is one MultiDrawElementsIndirectCount per object, counted by a visibility word the depth
pre-pass of the same submission writes. The replay read those counts on the CPU while encoding, where memory holds the
last completed frame's words, so objects coming into view were not drawn: holes, trails and see-through characters
whenever the camera moved. Now one compute dispatch per run of indirect records resolves their Metal indirect
arguments in GPU order, and the draws read them with indirectBuffer. TOTK_GPU_INDIRECT=0 keeps the old CPU read.

Measurement knobs used to find it: DM_EXP_EQ_SER / DM_EXP_EQ_FUNC (another compare for EQUAL depth draws into one
target) and DM_EXP_VIS_FILL (an inline update of that size writes 0xffff words).

fix: Breath of the Wild no longer drops to 30 fps in game after the map's Hero's Path playback

The dirty-page tracker gave no range to a pool that shared a 16 KB host page with a tracked pool, and destroying such a
pool looked its address up and dropped the other pool's range. The map's Hero's Path playback creates and destroys many
of these pools; afterwards every texture of the affected pools was uploaded again at every submission (about 350 uploads,
130 MB a frame, 33 ms of submit CPU): 24-30 fps in game after closing the map.

Now (GAME_BOTW only, nvn_dirty.c): a pool that overlaps live ranges gets one range for each run of its own pages, so
ranges never share a page and the fault handler still finds at most one range per page; a texture across a range border
is checked, protected and written by the GPU range by range; a pool removes only the ranges it owns; a range under
removal is flagged first, so a neighbour's texture cannot leave a shared page read-only in it; the removal moves the
write generation on and a re-upload reads "tracked" again (BOTW_REUP_TRACKED, nvn_obj.h; empty for TOTK). The
dirty-race probe gains 12 BOTW checks (-DGAME_BOTW=1: 26 of 26). TOTK preprocesses the same (v0, v112, v121, v143).

Game run (player save copy, Hero's Path on the minimap, map playback, back to the game, 120 Hz display): 80 fps in game
after closing the map, as before opening it (frame p50 12.1 ms, submit CPU 7.2 ms at about 3,450 draws); 12 texture
re-uploads in the whole run instead of about 350 a frame.

perf: shaders that draws further on cannot go without are prepared at once, in parallel

A draw that cannot be skipped (it stores, writes depth inside an occlusion count, ...) needs its variant and Metal library
before it is drawn. Its job was usually queued in the background already (the planning scans meet programs first), behind
the jobs of draws that can be skipped, so the submit thread took it back and translated and compiled it itself, one after
another: flying into Lookout Landing took 157 libraries in 13 frames, 6.3 s compiling and 1.6 s translating.

The first time a submission meets a shader that is not ready, the rest of it is scanned (state replayed, nothing drawn,
like pso_predict_rest). The jobs of the draws that will not be skippable run at once on urgent translator services of
their own (totk_rt_variant may_defer 2; TOTK_RT_URGENT_WORKERS, 4), and the background line starts no new job meanwhile
(TOTK_RT_URGENT_FIRST=0 lets it run on). Programs met for the first time are made with every stage in the background;
other new variants are queued as before. A scan that ends on its budget may go on from the next miss, up to 16 per
submission (TOTK_SHADER_PREDICT_SCAN / _US; TOTK_SHADER_PREDICT=0 turns it off). The background translators go from 2 to 4
(TOTK_RT_BG_WORKERS): with 2, jobs waited 13-15 s in line and what they draw appeared that late; 4 halved the skipped draws.

Measured (Mac M4, 1.4.3, empty cache, cold Metal cache, prebuilt libraries, main = 30a1b93 built clean):
- no seed, two runs each: in-world frames over 16.7 ms 9.3 / 9.4 s -> 2.4 / 2.5 s, worst frame 2.1-2.5 s -> 0.18-0.26 s;
- with the seed (a new player), three runs each: worst frame flying into Lookout Landing 131 / 684 / 203 -> 117 / 128 / 125 ms.
More draws are skipped the first time something is met (with the seed 14 -> about 580), so it appears a few frames later.
Played by hand without the seed: worst in-world frame 252 ms, 1,670 variants translated.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf: draws in an occlusion count may be skipped while their shader is prepared; a count they leave at 0 reports 1

Async shaders (Mac) skip a draw whose new shader or pipeline is not ready, but never one inside an occlusion count: two
thirds of the variants still translated on the submit thread were those (2026-10-21). Such a draw is now skipped too
when it writes neither depth nor stencil and does not store. Its count is then the only other thing it makes, so the
occlusion range (reset to report) remembers the skip and a report that comes to 0 with a skipped draw in it is raised to
1: the game culls on zero / non-zero, one bounding-sphere proxy per object, so at worst an occluded object is drawn for a
frame. The same mark covers draws iOS skips for a variant not translated yet, which used to report 0 and cull the object.
TOTK_OCCL_SKIP=0 makes those draws wait as before; TOTK_ASYNC_WHY splits the remaining counted ones by reason.

Measured (Mac M4, 1.4.3, empty cache, no seed, cold Metal cache, grass -> Lookout Landing -> shrine, two runs each):
flying into Lookout Landing 31.2 / 28.8 s of frames over 16.7 ms -> 8.4 / 8.1 s, worst frame 13.8 / 13.2 s -> 2.5 / 2.0 s.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: audio voices play on past an end-of-stream wave buffer

An end-of-stream wave buffer stopped the voice for the rest of the render
frame. Breath of the Wild marks every streamed music buffer (14,336
samples, 0.3 s) as end of stream, so each music channel lost up to 5 ms
at every join: a steady stutter on every output device. End of stream
now only restarts the played-sample count and the voice continues into
the next queued buffer in the same frame, as Ryujinx's
MarkEndOfBufferWaveBufferProcessing does. probe-audio gains a check for
it (fails on the old code).

[Jobs] Fix completed-task logs while a job group is active (#10826)

* [Jobs] Fix completed-task logs while a job group is active

With a task filter, `sky jobs logs JOB TASK` (and the dashboard's per-task
log view) chose between a finished task's saved log and a live tail of its
cluster by the whole job's status. While another task kept the job RUNNING,
a finished task was tailed from its cluster, which may be gone: a pipeline
tears it down, and a job group keeps its record until the group ends while
the cluster's idle autodown deletes it. The request then never returned,
waiting on a missing handle or retrying the deleted cluster with "The job
cluster is preempted or failed."

Decide by the filtered task's own status on every status read, so a task
that finishes during a live tail also stops it. Without a log reader, wait
for the controller to record the saved log path of a task that just
SUCCEEDED, as the follow path already does. Messages that name a status say
whether it is the task's or the job's, and the exit code is the task's.

* [Tests] Cover completed-task logs in an active pipeline

[Core] Don't fail reads on a read-only workspace when its enabled-clouds cache is cold (#11162)

* [Core] Don't fail reads on a read-only workspace when its enabled-clouds cache is cold

Refreshing a cold enabled-clouds cache goes through check_capabilities,
which only accepts workspaces the caller can write because the refresh
rewrites the workspace's cached rows. A user who can only read the active
workspace therefore failed read-level requests (validate, optimize,
list_accelerators) with "Workspace 'X' not found in SkyPilot
configuration" whenever that cache was cold.

Such a caller now gets a freshly probed answer that is not stored, probed
once per request. The optimizer's re-check of a pinned cloud follows the
same rule, so a reader pinned to a disabled cloud gets "requires X which
is not enabled". Writers keep refreshing and storing as before.

The error now names the user, says when the workspace is read-only for
them and lists the workspaces they can write; a workspace they cannot
read is still reported as not found or not accessible. A reader with no
enabled cloud is told to ask a member or an admin to run `sky check`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Key a reader's unstored cloud probe on the request config

The probe reads the request's merged config (for example Kubernetes
allowed contexts), and in the API server process concurrent /validate
requests share the request-scoped cache. Key it on a digest of that
config so two requests with different settings never share an answer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Test] Stub recheck_clouds in the enable_all_clouds fixture

The fixture stubs check.check_capability with a function that returns

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Keep a reader's cloud re-check for the whole request

The re-check result a read-only caller cannot store lived in a 60 s TTL
cache, so a long optimization could drop it and later reads fell back to
the stored rows without the re-checked cloud. Use a request-scoped LRU
cache instead; it is still cleared at the start of every request.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(sqlserver): stop reading the result stream after the row limit (#13101)

* fix(sqlserver): stop reading after the result row limit

The SQL Server driver kept consuming the whole TDS result stream after the
requested row limit was reached and only flagged the surplus rows as
truncated. A query whose full result set is large therefore spent seconds
draining rows that the caller had already discarded: on a 1.29M-row result
a row-limited execution took 12.8s while the same bounded SQL returned in
about 60ms. Other clients look fast because they stop at the first page.

Stop the stream as soon as the limit is hit, send a best-effort ATTENTION
and mark the connection as abandoned so the pool replaces it instead of
reusing a client that still has unread tokens on the wire. Only executions
that asked for a row limit and are not session-pinned take this path;
multi-statement batches, transactions and pinned sessions keep draining so
later statements and session state stay intact.

* fix(sqlserver): limit stream abandonment to parsed read queries

fix(windows): 区分 WebView2 运行时问题与安全软件拦截，新增有界兼容启动阶梯 (#13036)

* fix(windows): diagnose WebView2 runtime failures and recover startup

On Windows the "main window never appears" failure has three very different
causes that used to share one misleading "enterprise compatibility mode"
retry: WebView2 runtime missing, WebView2 runtime registered but damaged, and
a security product blocking WebView2. This change separates them before Tauri
creates a window and turns the single retry into a bounded recovery ladder.

- webview2_preflight: three-state runtime health (available / missing /
  registered_but_damaged), runtime version and install kind, installed security
  products, msedgewebview2 process count, Zone.Identifier and integrity level,
  plus an STA environment-creation probe with a hard timeout and HRESULT capture
- startup_recovery: 11-profile bounded compatibility ladder (isolated user data,
  sandbox/GPU off, RendererCodeIntegrity off for old runtimes, in-process GPU,
  temp data, scan delay, warm-up child, AppCompat Windows 8 layer, elevated
  relaunch, relocated copy, single-process experiment) with per-profile user data
  folders, fast-fail window probing, chain handoff through environment variables,
  bounded watchdog and silent auto-remembering of the winning profile
- startup_messages: native-dialog i18n catalog (zh-CN / zh-TW / en, English
  fallback); runtime problems point at the Windows 10 offline package that
  bundles WebView2, support codes stay in startup.log, success stays silent
- windows_appcompat: reversible per-user AppCompat Windows 8 layer used by a
  late profile
- wry: make WEBVIEW2_USER_DATA_FOLDER / WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS
  effective at runtime (union --disable-features lists) and honor

fix(mysql): honor the configured budget for remaining infrastructure timeouts (#13100)

* fix(mysql): derive remaining driver timeouts from the pool checkout budget

#12924 moved MySQL metadata/DDL checkouts onto MySqlPool::checkout_timeout,
but query cancellation and the auxiliary MySQL profiles still used the
compile-time 5 s budget:

- kill_query_with_opts opens a fresh physical connection for KILL QUERY;
  pass the caller's DbOperationBudget checkout budget through the query,
  SQL-file import and result export paths.
- Dolt, StarRocks, MySQL-compatible and OceanBase-MySQL metadata helpers
  and mysql_object_source now use pool.checkout_timeout().

On a slow link those paths failed after 5 s even with a 300 s connect budget.

The metadata gate waited a fixed 5 s, so on slow links queued metadata
requests reported "DBX metadata pool is busy" while the permitted ones were
still progressing. Derive the wait budget from the connection's configured
connect timeout, keeping the old 5 s floor and the 300 s config cap.

The MySQL stale-pool probe also started a new physical connection when the
pool had no idle connections, then abandoned it after 500 ms. Skip the probe
in that case: there is nothing idle to validate, and the real checkout will
surface failures.

Adds unit tests for both rules.

gateway: a model slow to start again and again rests on its account (小八)

小八 on Discord (2026-10-23): a WorkBuddy plugin account answered magpie's
own 504 "no first token in 30s" 58 times on kimi-k3-1 and glm-5.3 (the
vendor's per-model token limit, which it never names, it just stalls).
The group went on each time, then asked the same account first on the
next request: 15 slow starts in 17 minutes in one session.

Cause: gateway.go's hw.slow branch (the group's FirstToken let a member
go) never rested anything, by design ("a long prompt being slow to start
anywhere"), and nothing counted slow starts. So every request waited out
the whole FirstToken on the stalled member before falling back.

Now restSlow (routing.go) counts slow starts per restID (provider,
account or key, model). Once rests nothing, as before. The second in a
row, within slowForget (30m) of the last, rests that model on that
account: 1 minute, doubling each time after, capped by the provider's
RestCapOr(longestRetry), never for a provider whose rest cap is off. An
answer clears the count (servedCandidate). A client-cancelled request
never reaches the slow branch, so it counts nothing. A longer rest
already there is kept. The rest carries Rest.Model, so the Routing page
shows it on that model's rows only. The Routing story of a rested slow
try says so, and the group editor's slow-to-start hint no longer says
"It doesn't rest" (en, zh, zh-TW, ja, de).

in between restarts the count; twice: the model rests on k1 with Key
a#k1/m, Model m, under a minute; k1's whole key and k2/m don't rest; the
next request asks k2/m first; a/n still goes to k1; a third slow start
backs off longer; an answer ends it). TestCanceledSlowStartRestsNothing
(three client cancels during the first-token wait: no rest, no count).
routing-went-on.test.cjs gains a rested slow try in five languages;
group-first-token.test.cjs's i18n list has the new strings.

catalog sets m.Context. A per-model entry already won and still does.

m.Output and the catalog, on old and new (checked "*"=128000). Anthropic-
and Responses-type custom providers read the same WindowOf and are fixed

routing, usage: an account renamed in magpie reads by its new name (magpie-community/plugins#310, molvqingtai)

molvqingtai renamed a Kiro (plugin) account from "example@gmail.com (foo)"
to "example@gmail.com (bar)", and the Routing page kept saying "(foo)" on
every request made after. Cause: the Routing page never looked up the
user's name at all. A trace's `who` is the vendor's account name
(Weighed.Who), and plugins/routing/client.js showed it as it was. Usage
records (ProviderAccount) keep the vendor's name the same way, and the
Usage page's Accounts, the request log's Account filter, `magpie usage`,
a gateway key's accounts (AccountNames, /api/caller-keys) and Routing's
"Several accounts" pools (onOf) all showed it raw too. This affected
built-in and plugin providers alike.

Records still keep the vendor's name. It is the key the user's name is
stored under (providers.json AccountNames, in lower case), so it stays
the identity: Routing still groups and ranks by `who`. The name is looked
up when it is shown: provider.AccountShown / AccountShownOf /
AccountRef.Shown in Go, and userShown (accountNameOf over /api/providers'
accountNames) on the Routing page. So requests from before the rename
read by the current name too, and a cleared name goes back to the
vendor's. A key's name and an unnamed account read as before.
Already right before this change: quota cards and the menu bar (Alias),
`magpie accounts`, and the editor's account row.

davsync: a GitHub backup too large for the Contents API goes up as a blob (Zhang-Wei, Discord)

Zhang-Wei (Discord, v0.1.1318, 102 skills) saw every sync fail with
"GitHub sync: HTTP 422: Sorry, the file is too large to be processed"
on magpie/magpie.magpie-backup; the last backup that went up was about
19 MB. The Contents API's PUT refuses files well under the 100 MB a blob
can hold.

A repository with commits is now written through the Git Data API:
the ref's head, the file's version at that head (it must still be the one
sync read, or errChanged), a base64 blob, a tree on the head's tree, a
commit with the head as its parent, and a ref update without force. Still
one commit per write or removal, and the version is the blob SHA as
before. A ref update that is not a fast-forward is built again on the new
head (the blob is kept), up to three times, then errChanged; if the new
head changed the backup it is errChanged at once, so another computer's
backup goes through the normal merge. A branch deleted meanwhile is an
error, not created. Usage files and their removal take the same path.

An empty repository has no head to build on, so its first write still
goes through the Contents API (one commit, unchanged). If that is refused
as too large (422 "too large" or 413), a short README.md in magpie's
folder makes the first commit and the backup follows as the second.

Reading was already right for large files: the object media type gives
encoding "none" over 1 MB and bytes() downloads by blob SHA; the new
test covers it at 21 MB.

The fixture now serves the Git Data API (blobs, commits, trees, a
fast-forward-only ref update) and refuses a Contents PUT over
contentsLimit with GitHub's 422 text. docs/subsystems/sync-backup.md says
how writes go and names the new tests.

agent: a reasoning effort picked in VS Code's Copilot Chat survives magpie's sync (chim3744 on Discord)

chim3744 (magpie 0.1.1318) picked "max" for a magpie model in Copilot
Chat's model picker, and requests went out at "low".

Cause: VS Code 1.142 keeps that pick inside the provider group, as
settings["<model id>"].reasoningEffort (languageModels.ts
setModelConfiguration). magpie's setGroup built its group with
vscodeGroupJSON, which has no settings key, compared the whole object
with sameJSON, and edit.SetJSONItem replaced the whole group. Every Sync
(catalog.Changed on start, a vendor list fetch, a provider edit) and
every magpie model pick in VS Code wiped the pick, and Copilot Chat fell
back to the model's first level ("low" of [low, high, max]).

Fix: vscodeGroupKept lays magpie's group over the one in the file with
mergeTheirs, as theirsKept does for the other agents (#2030). Every key
magpie doesn't write stays: settings, and anything else VS Code or the
user puts there, such as an apiKey reference. The models list stays
magpie's whole, so a model gone from the catalog still leaves it. The
settings of a model magpie no longer lists are kept, since they are the
user's values. When nothing magpie owns changed, the compare is a no-op
and the file is not written. This covers VS Code, VS Code Insiders and
VSCodium (customendpoint and customoai), every profile, since all go
through setGroup. agent-wiring.md lists what is kept.

Siblings checked:
- chatLanguageModels.json is written only by vscode.go. Cursor
  (cursorlocal.go) writes nothing of Cursor's. magpie writes no
  language-model groups for Windsurf, Trae or Kiro IDE.
- Every other syncJSON caller in internal/agent already merges through
  theirsKept, piBlockKept, openCodeKept, mothxBlockKept, qoderKept or
  t3Merged (2eee900dc, #2030's siblings). That covers Pi, Crush, Ante,
  Aside, MothX, StepCode, OpenCode, Qoder, Cline, Command Code, Pencil
  and T3 Code. The exception is Zed's available_models. That is
  magpie's model list, an array, and Zed keeps the model the user picked

dsh: maxTokens leaves dsh half its window, or a quarter for output where that is more (#3298 item 3)

822f2b304 (#2823) held the maxTokens magpie lists for dsh to a quarter
of the window, because dsh reserves it, plus 65536 of headroom, before
it compacts (compaction-basic's resolveCompactSpec: threshold = min(0.8W,
W - maxTokens - 65536)). On a large window the quarter cut more than
compaction needs: DeepSeek's own deepseek-flash, 1000000/393216, was
listed at 250000, though all 393216 leaves dsh 541248 (54%).

Now the cap is max(W/4, W/2 - 65536): the output may take what leaves
dsh half the window to compact in, or a quarter of the window where that
is more (every window under 262144, where there is no half to spare
beside the headroom). A Max output the user set is still written as set
(outputOr), and contextWindow and /v1/models don't change.

dsh 0.2.0-rc.2's own resolveCompactSpec, run on the installed
compaction-basic over each figure (threshold tokens):

| window / output | vendor | quarter (main) | now |
| 524288 / 524288 | no message budget | 131072 -> 327680 | 196608 -> 262144 |
| 500000 / 393216 (#2823) | 41248 | 125000 -> 309464 | 184464 -> 250000 |
| 131072 / 65536 | no pressure budget | 32768 -> 32768 | 32768 -> 32768 |
| 1000000 / 393216 | 541248 | 250000 -> 684464 | 393216 -> 541248 |
| 400000 / 128000 | 206464 | 100000 -> 234464 | 128000 -> 206464 |
| 200000 / 393216 | no message budget | 50000 -> 84464 | 50000 -> 84464 |
| 128000 / 393216 | no message budget | 32000 -> 30464 | 32000 -> 30464 |

#2823's case stays fixed: 250000 is half its 500000 window (its
reporter's own plan A), against 41248 before 822f2b304; it is lower than
the quarter's 309464, which is the trade. The 128K and 200K windows
#3298 names don't change: any output above the quarter there takes it
straight out of what dsh compacts at, and a user who wants more sets Max
output.

gateway: a safety refusal said in a stream is a refusal for a client answered whole too, and rests nobody (#3274, CartethyiaQwQ)

CartethyiaQwQ (#3274): Codex's "safety filter: cyber_policy" refusal
(the Daybreak note) set healthy accounts aside; two such turns benched a
five-account pool for about 17 minutes.

Cause: the HTTP 400 cyber_policy is already a refusal (policyRefusal reads
its code: next account asked, nobody rests), and so is one said in a
stream relayed as a stream. A Codex account is always streamed upstream,
so a stream:false Responses, Chat or Messages request is answered from
that stream whole. There, a response.failed or error event whose error
has a code (cyber_policy) but no invalid_request_error type got no status
from the decoder, and the whole path answered it 502 api_error: retried
on the same account, then every account asked, each one but the last
resting by backoff. A refusal after a few words went to the client as a
finished 200 turn, and the failure after it rested the account.

Fix, at the decoders and the whole path:
- filterRefused (fallback.go): a stream error event refusedCode reads as
  the safety filter's gets status 400 and Said {"error":{type
  invalid_request_error, code}}. Used by every decoder that set
  Code: refusedCode -- Responses (both error sites, after requestRefused),
  Chat, Anthropic and carriedError.
- The whole path (gateway.go) answers a reply the filter cut part way as
  the refusal, not its words so far, and notes it in refusedHeader, since
  Anthropic's error shape drops the code that settle reads.
- restAfterMarked: a 400 whose error object policyRefusal reads as a
  refusal rests nobody and counts no failure (By "off", Why refused), as
  the ZDR refusal does, for any route that reaches it.
- docs/subsystems/gateway-routing.md says so.

Review of the submitted patch (dc6c695db, not taken as is): it matched
`safety filter|cyber_policy|Daybreak access` anywhere in a 400's words,
so a 400 that echoes the user's prompt in its message skipped the rest
too; its fixture was magpie's own refusedError text, which restAfter is
never handed for a 400; and it gated on status 400, while the path that
rested (above) answered 502, so it would not have stopped the rests.
Its restAfter unit tests' shape is kept in TestRestAfterPolicyRefusal.

library: a standalone Windows rtk gets rtk's own upgrade action (#2006, Edward4226; LoKi)

An rtk.exe that no package manager installed (rtk's own Windows release
unzipped into %USERPROFILE%\.local\bin, say) had no upgrader, so the
Library page showed RTK's update with no usable Upgrade. LoKi
(lokic7123-star) hit it on v0.1.1285 and again on 0.1.1320; Edward4226
reproduced it and wrote this patch (his bc2056804, author kept).

rtkUpgrader now gives such an rtk.exe the rtk-windows-release action
(shown as "rtk's own Windows release"): on amd64, when winget's folders,
cargo's folder and winget's own records/winget list didn't claim it.
UpgradeRTK then takes RTKLatest's version, downloads checksums.txt and
rtk-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip from rtk-ai/rtk's release through
source.DoOfficial, checks the zip's SHA-256 against checksums.txt, takes
rtk.exe out of it, writes it beside the old one and swaps it in with
steady.Rename, putting the old one back if the swap fails.

Changed from Edward's patch in review:
- The action no longer names a version: it read rtkLatest under the lock
  RTKLatest holds while it asks GitHub (up to ~16s), so ReadRTK, a page
  draw, would wait on it. UpgradeRTK already falls back to the last known
  version through RTKLatest.
- A winget that couldn't say whether it owns the rtk (timed out, failed,
  couldn't run) is no answer, not "not winget's": askWingetOwns now
  returns (yes, known); only winget missing, exit 0 without rtk-ai.rtk,
  or 0x8A150014 (no package) count as known-no. The winget arm above is
  unchanged (yes only when winget listed it). Without this, a winget
  timeout handed a possibly winget-owned rtk to the standalone path.
- Only a zip member named rtk.exe is taken (no "any .exe" fallback, which
  could pick rtk-proxy's), and an oversized one is refused rather than
  cut short.
- An aside (rtk.exe.old-<pid>) an earlier upgrade couldn't remove, because
  an agent was running that rtk, is removed on the next upgrade.
- The arch is a var (rtkArch) so the upgrader test runs on arm64 hosts
  instead of skipping; the redundant winget/cargo folder checks are gone
  (the switch's earlier cases already return for those).
- Two of the patch's tests failed as written on macOS (ReplacesBinary
  counted VERSION as a leftover; UpgradeRunsTheInstall compared the
  script rtkPath finds there with rtk.exe's text); both fixed.
- New tests: TestRTKWindowsStandaloneAsksWinget (no winget / unlisted /
  listed / failed / hung), TestRTKWindowsReleaseZipNeedsRTKExe, the
  arm64 case, and a stale aside in TestRTKWindowsReleaseSwapsTheFile.

agent: Codex's config never names magpie's model list once it is gone (zwaydot on X)

opened: "ChatGPT configuration could not be loaded … No such file or

CLI and the app both.

Cause: dropList removed ~/.codex/magpie-models.json whatever Codex's
provider was (Unwire calls it unconditionally at its end), while
model_catalog_json was taken out of config.toml only by dropProvider,
and only while model_provider was still "magpie". A config whose
provider was moved off magpie (taken out, or set to another provider by
the app, another tool or a hand edit) while it still named magpie's
list was left, after Disconnect or Unwire, naming the removed file.
Separately, Disconnect put back the user's own model_catalog_json from
before magpie without checking its file was still there.

Now:
- dropList takes model_catalog_json out wherever it names magpie's list
  and the list is gone (known gone: a Stat that fails otherwise is not
  taken for it);
- a model_catalog_json of the user's own is put back only while its file
  is there (not judged in a WSL distro, whose spelling this side can't
  look at);
- Sync (run at every start through SyncCatalog, connected or not) mends a
  config already in this state: magpie's list written again while magpie
  is the provider, else the key taken out. Users already hit by this are
  fixed by updating and starting magpie, with no reconnect.

The workaround given on X (delete model_catalog_json, and
model_provider = "magpie" if it is there, from ~/.codex/config.toml) is
right: it is what this does by hand.

gateway: a name a fake-IP resolver answers is fetched through its TUN or a local proxy (#2593)

With Clash's TUN fake-ip (Clash Verge Rev on Windows, TomXPRIME), Surge's
enhanced mode (h4rk8s) or Loon on, the system resolver answers every name
in 198.18.0.0/15, which the download guard (image_fetch_guard.go) listed
as special. So web_fetch, a caller's image (fetchPicture), a vendor's
image or video by URL and generate_image's download (imagemcp) refused
every URL as "a private address". All of them go through publicTransport;
nothing else uses it.

What changed:
- The address rule moved into internal/netguard (Public, FakeIP,
  LoonPaired), shared by the gateway's guard and a provider's icon
  (icon.go's publicIP is now netguard.Public or FakeIP, as #252 meant).
  The icon guard gets the gateway's stricter list with it (Teredo, 240/4,
  NAT64 and 6to4 forms of a private address are refused there too).
- publicTransport: a name (never an address literal) whose every answer
  is in 198.18.0.0/15 is fetched. With no proxy (pure TUN) the fake
  address is pinned and dialled, and the dial guard lets that one address
  in, no other. Through a proxy on this computer (loopback or localhost)
  the proxy is given the name, never the fake address: h4rk8s showed a
  real Surge CONNECT by name works and by the 198.18 address doesn't. A
  plain http:// request's Host to that proxy is the checked name, never
  the caller's own Host. Through a proxy elsewhere it is refused.
- An answer with any other address beside the fake ones (private or
  public) is judged as before, so fake + 192.168.x is refused; loopback,
  RFC 1918, link-local with 169.254.169.254, CGNAT, unspecified,
  multicast and documentation stay refused; every non-fake answer is
  still pinned; redirects are re-checked as before.
- Loon's synthesized AAAA (fd27:712::/96 holding an A answer of the same
  reply) is left out and the A answer judged in its place, as icon.go
  already did, so a Loon answer isn't refused as fc00::/7.
- docs/subsystems/gateway-routing.md says all of this, and the trust it
  asks for: where a fake-IP name really goes is decided by the fake-IP
  resolver, which magpie can't see, so a name pointing at the user's
  network is reached if that resolver's rules send it there. The icon
  path already accepted this (#252).

Credit: ggbdpq found the cause and wrote both patches on the issue
(hunt/2593-webfetch-fakeip, then hunt51-a-fakeip-proxy: the fake-only,
loopback-proxy, name-not-literal predicate and its test shapes, which
this follows); h4rk8s's real Surge comparison showed the pin had to go
for a proxy; TomXPRIME's Windows report showed pure TUN needs the direct
dial.

agent, gateway: a Claude model magpie can only ask translated no longer keeps auto mode's server review on (nexnull on Discord)

nexnull (Claude Code 2.1.308, magpie v0.1.1318, DeepSeek 4.1 flash) saw
Claude Code's notice that auto mode's classifier "isn't eligible because
your requests go through 127.0.0.1:3425". The wiring leaves
CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER unset while any model Claude Code can reach
through magpie is reviewed (claudeReviewed), and it judged that by
AutoModeReviewed, which counts a Claude model by its name. A relay that
lists claude-* beside DeepSeek with only a Chat (or Responses) URL, or a
Claude model the user pinned to chat, is asked translated: a probe showed
such a request goes to /v1/chat/completions with no safeguards and no
safeguard_results. So the review stayed on and the notice showed.

AutoModeReviewable (gateway/automode.go) is AutoModeReviewed on a route
that reaches the Messages API: the Claude subscription, or a provider
with an Anthropic URL whose APIs for the model (a user pin first) include
Anthropic. claudeReviewed asks it for the provider and each fallback, so
Claude Code and T3 Code get CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=0 there. It is
still magpie's own stashed value (claude.auto_mode_server): a user's own
value is left alone, and disconnect or restore takes magpie's off.
serverReview, already on the Messages route, keeps AutoModeReviewed.

Chosen on purpose: any reachable model that is really reviewed keeps the
review on. Writing 0 by mistake would lose server review on Claude
silently, while leaving it on by mistake costs the notice, which Enter
dismisses for 24h. A relay with an Anthropic URL (OpenRouter, AiHubMix)
still counts as reviewable, since some pass the field through. No
client mimicry and no prompt or identity text changes.

sessions: a path listed twice in one read is read once, so the start's warm-up no longer quits magpie (#2932)

Since c381e4cd1 (#2776) each file a refresh reads has an
entry in parsing, closed and deleted when its parse is published.
refresh checked parsing[f.path] while picking the files to read but set
the entry only later, while building the jobs, so a path listed twice
in one want passed the check twice: two jobs on one entry, and the
second publish closed a nil channel. The start's warm-up
(warmSessions -> StatsAndNative -> refresh) took magpie down a few
seconds after every start, in the GUI, `magpie web` and --gateway alike.

Tsuki-hash, on Windows and macOS.

Two sources of the duplicate were found in the thread:
- CODEBUDDY_CONFIG_DIR on WorkBuddy's folder (TimWongUp's .zshrc;
  on Windows WorkBuddy's installer, or its IDE host for its children,
  sets both variables to one .workbuddy): codebuddyFiles and
  workbuddyFiles listed each .jsonl once each.

  (nativeas): both scan to one string, one <db>#<id> path.

changes:
- refresh marks a file in parsing as it takes it, so a second listing
  of the path is left out (or waited on). This is the guard: whatever
  list repeats a path, no refresh reads it twice.
- allFiles and callSources keep each path once (distinctPaths), so a
  path is not counted twice either. OpenCode's list doubles the same
  TEXT/BLOB rows (tested); ZCode's and Alma's would too.
- hermesFiles keeps one file a session id, as late as its later row.
- codebuddyFiles lists nothing when CodeBuddy Code's folder is
  WorkBuddy's (os.SameFile: a link or Windows' case rules count too),
  so those sessions are WorkBuddy's on the Sessions page and in usage;
  Dirs names such a folder once. A session the CodeBuddy CLI wrote
  there shows as WorkBuddy's (agreed by TimWongUp on the issue).

commits.message:
terminal: continuations must restart at C1 sequence introducers (#14814)

A stream continuation that ended after an 8-bit C1 introducer had
aborted an APC could not be exported. For example, `ESC _ data 0x9B`
ends the APC and starts a CSI, but the tracker only treats ESC as the
start of a new sequence, so it kept the aborted APC. Replaying that
would end the APC a second time, and validation rejected it.

Export now starts at the last C1 introducer that moved the parser into a
new sequence and writes it in its 7-bit ESC form.

build: add -Dinstalled-exe-path for the Linux launcher files (#14806)

The Zig 0.17 port replaced the absolute path to the executable in the
desktop file, D-Bus services and systemd user service with a bare
`ghostty`, since the install prefix is no longer known while the build
is configured. systemd resolves a bare ExecStart= name against a fixed
search path rather than PATH: /usr/bin and /usr/local/bin on most
systems, and only systemd's own directory on NixOS. So the service
failed to start for any install outside those directories, including
every Nix one.
    
-Dinstalled-exe-path gives the absolute path to write into those files.
Without it they still name the executable alone, which is right for
packages installing to /usr. The Nix package passes its output path, and
the Flatpak manifests pass /app/bin/ghostty, which is what they produced
before the port.

Fixes #14805

AI disclosure: Claude Code was used in the preparation of this PR.

aborted an APC could not be exported. For example, `ESC _ data 0x9B`
ends the APC and starts a CSI, but the tracker only treats ESC as the
start of a new sequence, so it kept the aborted APC. Replaying that
would end the APC a second time, and validation rejected it.

Export now starts at the last C1 introducer that moved the parser into
a new sequence and writes it in its 7-bit ESC form.

terminal: discard cancelled or aborted APC commands (#14812)

ECMA-48 says a control string that is cancelled or aborted is thrown
away. xterm only dispatches a control string on ST, and Kitty only ends
an APC on ST or BEL, so neither runs the command.


https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-48/

kitty graphics: non-chunk continuations end the chunked transmission (#14811)

While a chunked Kitty graphics load was in progress, every transmit or
animation frame command was treated as its next chunk, regardless of its
transmission medium. A file (`t=f`), temporary file (`t=t`), or shared
memory (`t=s`) command arriving mid-load had its encoded path appended
to the partial image as pixel data.

This diverged from Kitty. The spec only defines chunking for direct
data, and continuation chunks must carry only the `m` and `q` keys, so a
command with another medium can never be a continuation. Kitty abandons
the in-progress load and handles the command as a new transmission, for
both image and animation frame loads. A client that interrupts a load
this way now gets the image or frame it asked for instead of a corrupted
or failed one.

`execute` now destroys the in-progress load before dispatching any
non-direct transmit or frame command, so the command is handled as a
fresh transmission, including its own `q` setting.

This diverged from Kitty. The spec only defines chunking for direct
data, and continuation chunks must carry only the `m` and `q` keys, so
a command with another medium can never be a continuation. Kitty
abandons the in-progress load and handles the command as a new
transmission, for both image and animation frame loads. A client that
interrupts a load this way now gets the image or frame it asked for
instead of a corrupted or failed one.

`execute` now destroys the in-progress load before dispatching any
non-direct transmit or frame command, so the command is handled as a
fresh transmission, including its own `q` setting.

nix: check that the launcher files name the installed executable

Run `systemd-analyze verify` on the systemd user service, and check that
every Exec= and TryExec= in the D-Bus service and desktop file is an
absolute path to an executable, so a build that stops passing
-Dinstalled-exe-path fails instead of shipping a service systemd can't
start.

The verifier starts a user manager, which needs a writable runtime
directory that the sandbox doesn't have, so it gets one under $TMPDIR.

build: add -Dinstalled-exe-path for the Linux launcher files

The Zig 0.17 port replaced the absolute path to the executable in the
desktop file, D-Bus services and systemd user service with a bare
`ghostty`, since the install prefix is no longer known while the build
is configured. systemd resolves a bare ExecStart= name against a fixed
search path rather than PATH: /usr/bin and /usr/local/bin on most
systems, and only systemd's own directory on NixOS. So the service
failed to start for any install outside those directories, including
every Nix one.

-Dinstalled-exe-path gives the absolute path to write into those files.
Without it they still name the executable alone, which is right for
packages installing to /usr. The Nix package passes its output path, and
the Flatpak manifests pass /app/bin/ghostty, which is what they produced
before the port.
