Fix contradicting guide bounds in the macro, integer bound decoding, and system-tool usage (#367)

* Keep the later of contradicting guide bounds in the Generable macro

* Decode whole-number integer schema bounds as Int

* Keep the usage of system-model tools out of the response that called them

* Treat a timeout that overflows in addition as no limit

* Check for cancellation before collecting a single-snapshot response

Send partial snapshots of structured streams (#364)

* Send partial snapshots of structured streams

Build each structured stream snapshot from the content's partial form,
so a snapshot arrives before every required property has, and a usage
update sends one too. A stopped tool round still uses the response
text only when it decodes as the complete content.

* Decode partial snapshots in a generic function for Swift 6.3

Document reasoning replay, tool-round limits, and response start timeouts (#365)

Name Ollama and Chat Completions among the providers that keep and replay
reasoning, say which models don't apply maximumToolRounds to every
response, and list the new extensions under Differences from Foundation
Models.

Fix contradicting guide bounds and the reasoning past the tool-round limit (#366)

* Keep the later bound of contradicting number guides

Guides such as .minimum(10) with .maximum(5) stopped with a precondition
since number bounds became typed. Build the schema again, with the later
guide's bound replacing the earlier one it contradicts.

* Leave the reasoning of the round past the limit out of ToolRoundLimitExceeded

Ollama and Anthropic added that round's reasoning to the entries before
recording the round, so the error's transcript entries could end with it.
Record the round with only the rounds that ran, as the other providers do.

* Call the nonisolated(nonsending) TaskLocal.withValue

Swift 6.4 deprecates the overload that takes an isolation. Declaring
RequestUsageChannel.outside and its operation nonisolated(nonsending)
selects the new overload on 6.4 and the old one on 6.3.

Document HTTP transports in the README (#363)

* Document HTTP transports in the README

* Use the baseURL label in the README's Ollama example

Give Chat Completions reasoning back in each tool round and on replay (#358)

* Give Chat Completions reasoning back in each tool round and on replay

Thinking models served through Chat Completions return their reasoning in
`reasoning_content` (DeepSeek) or `reasoning` and `reasoning_details`
(OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway). The provider dropped it, so a model lost its
plan between tool rounds, and DeepSeek, which requires it back whenever a
request has tools, failed with a 400.

The reasoning is now kept in the transcript as a reasoning entry before the
tool calls or response of the message it came with, and sent back on that
message as received. The tool loop and replay both build the message from the
entry, so the two requests stay the same and prompt caching keeps working.
Other providers' reasoning entries are still left out.

Fixes #326

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01B4WBsc1Jp8fGufe89MhQFB

* Send Chat Completions reasoning back only to the host that wrote it

Hosts that serve Chat Completions don't agree on the reasoning fields: Groq
rejects `reasoning` on an assistant message and Mistral rejects
`reasoning_content`. A reasoning entry now records the host of the API that
wrote it, and its fields go back only on requests to that host; a transcript
carried to another host replays its messages without them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01B4WBsc1Jp8fGufe89MhQFB

* Record Chat Completions reasoning with a typed origin

* Test that a failed turn's Chat Completions reasoning isn't sent

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: mattt <mattt@me.com>

Add configurable response start timeout (#300)

* Add configurable response start timeout

* Test the response start timeout through each transport

* Make the response start timeout optional, and whole seconds on Linux

- responseStartTimeout is nil by default: the transport decides, as with
  send's optional timeout. A URL session waits as its configuration says,
  as in 1.0, and AsyncHTTPClient up to 180 seconds. When it's set, both
  transports use it as it is.
- On Linux, a URL session's timeout is rounded up to whole seconds, as
  FoundationNetworking keeps only whole seconds of timeoutInterval: half a
  second was none.
- The deprecated session initializers are renamed to the initializers
  without responseStartTimeout, so their fix-its write code that builds.

The timeout tests use the loopback server, and run with the other tests
that send through a URL session, as on Linux they share one request gate.

* Test that a huge response start timeout doesn't trap on Linux

A streamed response's start timeout reaches the URL session transport as the request's timeout,
which is now clamped below Dispatch's limit, so a timeout too long to wait for at all is no limit
to speak of rather than a crash.

* Format, and expect the decoding error a huge timeout's request ends with

Count a response's requests as each one completes (#357)

* Count a response's requests as each one completes

As in Foundation Models, whose executor sends each request's usage to the
session while the session runs the tool loop, a response that isn't
streamed now counts each request in session.usage as it completes, through
an internal channel. A response that throws, from a tool, the tool-round
limit, an answer that doesn't decode, or cancelling, keeps the usage of the
requests it made. 1.0 counted a response's usage only once it returned.

- RequestsUsage.add, where the providers that loop add each request, and
  the single requests of Ollama and Anthropic report to the channel.
- The session sets the channel around a response, and once it returns
  counts only what wasn't reported, so a model that doesn't report, such
  as one outside the package, is still counted once.
- What a tool or a stream asks of a model runs with no channel: a stream
  counts its usage from its snapshots, as before.

No public API changes.

* Test a wrapped built-in model's usage, and say which tasks inherit the channel

A model of another library that wraps a built-in one and calls it through respond has the built-in
model's requests counted for the response, once, and kept when the wrapper throws after it.

RequestUsageChannel's doc comment says a Task {} made within a response inherits it, and
Task.detached doesn't.

* Format with swift-format

---------

Co-authored-by: Mattt Zmuda <mattt@me.com>

Give Ollama's reasoning back to it in each tool round (#341)

* Give Ollama's reasoning back to it in each tool round

Ollama's provider read no thinking from responses, so a reasoning model such as DeepSeek began again after every tool call. Its thinking is now kept as a reasoning entry and sent back as the message's `thinking`, in the tool loop and from the transcript. Reasoning carries a typed `Origin`, which Anthropic's provider uses too: each provider gives back only its own.

* Don't send reasoning a failed turn left with the next answer

Reasoning that no assistant message followed, as a turn that failed or was
cancelled leaves it with .preserveTranscript, is dropped at the next prompt
or instructions, instead of going back as the next answer's thinking.

Throw CancellationError when collecting a cancelled response (#362)

* Throw CancellationError when collecting a cancelled response

A streamed response's iterator ends without an error when its task is
cancelled, so collect() returned the snapshots so far as the whole
response, or threw noSnapshots when there were none. It now checks for
cancellation once the stream ends, as the session's streaming task does.

* Break the cancellation comment at its clause boundary

Co-authored-by: Mattt Zmuda <mattt@me.com>

commits.message:
Update appSpecific.cpp

This PR refactors the updateAppStatus function to improve reliability and execution speed. Key changes include replacing unsafe and slow atoi/atof(implicit double) with std::from_chars/strtof(float), and substituting the linear if-else mispredicted chain with an O(1) compile-time MurmurHash3 switch statement to reduce CPU cycles and instruction cache pressure(the nuance is that the parameter label strings must no longer be identical to avoid collisions; they must differ by at least one character, or you need to incorporate extra `strcmp`). Now, settings should be applied significantly faster, and the web interface as a whole during changes should become more responsive. Additionally, this update adds critical safety guards: null pointer checks, explicit array bounds validation, guaranteed buffer null-termination, and strict static_cast type conversions. Overall, my goal was to speed up the switching of parameters in the web interface, as this process would sometimes be excessively slow and cause the system to lag—for no apparent reason. The core logic has been kept as it was; a quick button, toggle and input fields check showed that everything was working.

Update mjpeg2sd.cpp

Fix for line 485 - implemented configurable 5 sec rate limiting to avoid cluttering the log and lowered to LOG_VRB level.

Update streamServer.cpp

rtsp fix (connected with mjpeg2sd.cpp - 485 line) It appears that sometime after version 10.9.5, RTSP broke, and the worker ended up without a slot from which data could be read.

The VLM heading rule can keep a source depth of 6 at section level 6.
docling-core before 2.103.1 exports that level as seven "#" in Markdown,
which is not a heading. 2.103.1 caps the Markdown heading at six "#", as

Signed-off-by: Christoph Auer <cau@zurich.ibm.com>

fix(vlm): keep every markup heading depth distinct across VLM mappers

The layout label alone decides title versus section header. Each mapper
now stores the raw markup depth of a section header: "#" x N or <hN>
gives level N. A section header without markup gets depth 2, like "##".

The new normalize_section_header_levels() then runs once per document.
If no section header has depth 1, all levels go up one step, so every
heading exports with its source depth. Otherwise the levels stay, so two
source depths never share one level.

Depth 1 does not become a title. Models use depth-1 section headers for
chapter and part headings, and often use depth 1 and depth 2 on the same
page. The old "max(1, N - 1)" rule merged those two depths into one level.

The rule is per document, not per page. The VLM pipeline maps pages with
normalize_heading_levels=False and normalizes the joined document once.
So one depth gets the same level on all pages. Standalone mapper calls
normalize their single page by default.

Changes in output versus origin/main:
- dots, Nemotron Parse 3.5, DeepSeek-OCR, Unlimited-OCR, PaddleOCR-VL:
  pages with depth 1 keep "#" and "##" distinct (before: both became
  level 1). Pages without depth 1 do not change.
- Chandra and Nemotron Parse 2.0: pages without depth 1 now export the
  source depth (before: one "#" too deep). A section header without
  markup now sorts with "##" (before: level 1 next to "#").
- Shared HTML fragment helper: it now only records raw depth; the
  calling mapper normalizes.

Signed-off-by: Christoph Auer <cau@zurich.ibm.com>

fix(vlm): share the Nemotron 3.5 formula delimiter normalizer

and ended with it. For formulas with several segments it left unbalanced

"$a$ + $b$" became "a$ + $b".

The Nemotron 3.5 mapper already handles these cases. Move its normalizer
to vlm_utils as strip_math_delimiters, so the Nemotron Parse 2.0 and 3.5
mappers use the same function. It removes every \( and \), keeps \\, and
then removes outer \[...\], $$...$$ or $...$ pairs that enclose the
whole text.

docs: fix arithmetic update-assignment equivalence (#3682)

The manual said `a op= b` is equivalent to `a |= . op b`. It is actually
equivalent to `(b as $b | a |= . op $b)`: the right-hand side gets `.`
as input, not the value being updated, and each value it outputs gives a
separate result.

This updates the description and adds two examples, `.a += .b` and `.a
+= (1,2)`. `tests/man.test` and `jq.1.prebuilt` are regenerated.

[megatron, ci] fix: honor module ignore patterns in ModelOpt QAT (#8329) ### What does this PR do? Fix ModelOpt QAT module ignore patterns so that they disable the module's child quantizers. For example, `*self_attention.linear_proj` currently matches neither `...linear_proj.input_quantizer` nor `...linear_proj.weight_quantizer`. Training therefore still applies fake quantization even when rollout explicitly keeps the corresponding `o_proj` in BF16. Keep the existing direct-quantizer rule and append a `pattern.*` rule. This preserves explicit quantizer selection and Megatron aliases, while respecting the module-name boundary (`in_proj_a` does not disable `in_proj_ab`). Duplicate check: [open ModelOpt/ignore PRs](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+ModelOpt+ignore), [open ignore_patterns PRs](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+ignore_patterns). The related rollout matching work (#7918) and TE FP8 audit work (#8132) do not fix this ModelOpt module-to-child-quantizer matching path. No equivalent open fix was found. This addresses one concrete mismatch relevant to #8186, not that entire roadmap. ### Checklist Before Starting - [x] Search for similar PRs (queries above). - [x] Title format: `[megatron, ci] fix: honor module ignore patterns in ModelOpt QAT`. ### Test - `python -m pytest -q tests/utils/test_modelopt_mxfp8_on_gpu.py`: **34 passed** with ModelOpt 0.44.0/compressed-tensors 0.17.0, and **34 passed** with compressed-tensors 0.18.0. Tests exercise actual `mtq.quantize`, sibling isolation, direct quantizer patterns, aliases, unchanged presets, and exact BF16 forward/backward behavior. - Before the file rename, new tests applied to the unmodified baseline, `python -m pytest -q tests/utils/test_modelopt_mxfp8_on_cpu.py -k ignore`: **6 failed, 11 passed, 17 deselected**. - `pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=always`: **all 14 hooks passed**. `git diff --check` passed. - **Actual H100 end-to-end experiment:** baseline and fixed Qwen3-0.6B each completed **10 GRPO optimizer updates** with Megatron/ModelOpt FP8 QAT and vLLM FP8_BLOCK rollout, using the same configuration and seed. One H100 80GB; TP/PP/CP/EP=1; 8 prompts × 2 samples; learning rate 1e-5; entropy coefficient 0.001. Packed inputs use an explicit causal attention override (`use_arbitrary_attention_mask=False`). | Instrumented check | Baseline | Fixed | | --- | --- | --- | | Enabled input/weight quantizers in 28 ignored output projections | 56/56 | 0/56 | | First ignored projection maximum QDQ error at every step | 0.0859375 | 0 | | Updates with changed first-projection weights | 10/10 | 10/10 | | BF16 exported weight exactly equals actual vLLM loaded weight | 11/11 | 11/11 | The refit check covers the first output-projection tensor at initialization and after every update. Baseline refit equality already holds; the fix removes unintended actor-side fake quantization. Both runs have finite nonzero gradients and actual parameter updates throughout, including batches whose GRPO advantages are zero. [Reproduction commands, exact environment, raw scalar/event records, and refit checks](https://github.com/LZC-BELIEVER/verl/tree/1a6bb8a727d27c00af3fbd0c4cc9b68e9a057d7e). Commands used are provided there: `run_training.py --arm baseline|fixed --steps 10 --tag run`, `verify_refits.py ... --steps 10`, and `plot_results.py --tag run`. These are single-seed arithmetic correctness runs. Mean reward was 0.7375 (baseline) versus 0.39375 (fixed); mean sampled K3 KL was 0.0115391 versus 0.0119434. The trajectories differ, so the curves do not demonstrate reward or whole-model KL improvement. Multi-GPU, MXFP8 end-to-end, and Qwen3.5/GDN experiments were not run. GitHub CI has not yet been requested. The renamed test module was revalidated: **34 passed** with each compressed-tensors version (0.17.0 and 0.18.0), **34 tests collected** using the GPU workflow exclusion rules, and all 14 pre-commit hooks passed. This review revision changes test discovery only; the H100 curves above were produced by the original fix. ### API and Usage Example No API change. Existing module patterns now take effect: ```yaml actor_rollout_ref: actor: megatron: qat: enable: true mode: fp8 ignore_patterns: ["lm_head", "*mlp.gate", "*self_attention.linear_proj"] rollout: quantization: linear: FP8_BLOCK moe: FP8_BLOCK ignore: ['re:.*self_attn\.o_proj$'] ``` Actor ModelOpt patterns use globs; rollout patterns shown here use the explicit regex prefix. Backend-specific names still need to correspond to the same layer. ### Design & Code Changes - Expand module ignores to child quantizers, retaining the original direct pattern. - Replace the string-only regression assertion with behavioral quantization checks and cover FP8/MXFP8 and BF16 gradient preservation. - Rename the test file to `test_modelopt_mxfp8_on_gpu.py` so the existing GPU unit-test command discovers it automatically in an environment with ModelOpt/compressed-tensors. No separate workflow step is needed. AI assistance (Codex) was used for the implementation, tests, experiment instrumentation, and description. [megatron, trainer] fix: pack the teacher's top-k tensors with the student's CP split (#8332)

### What does this PR do?

Follow-up to #8325, from a finding in its review
([comment](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8325#discussion_r4344130772)).

`compute_forward_kl_topk` packs the teacher's top-k tensors itself.
#8325 gave it the student's low-precision padding but not the student's
CP split, so on THD the teacher rows could match `student_logits` in
shape and still belong to other tokens:

- **CP layout**: `dsv4_hybrid` splits the student's rows contiguously,
while the teacher's were split zigzag, the default. With CP=2, MXFP8 and
16 sequences of 17 tokens, rank 0 holds 256 rows on both sides, and 128
of its 136 valid student tokens get the teacher values of another token
or of a padding row (all 136 on rank 1). With 32-token sequences, 248 of
256 rows differ on rank 0 and all 256 on rank 1, and that was already
the case before #8325. #8325 turned the 17-token case from a failed
shape assertion into the same silent misalignment.
- **Dynamic CP** (not reachable end to end today): the engine rejects
dynamic CP with distillation (`Dynamic CP does not support
distillation`). The micro-batch's `local_cp_size` is still passed down,
so the teacher's tensors would be split over the same group as the
student's if that combination is enabled; the unit tests cover the
packing.

`forward_step` now passes the `cp_layout` and `local_cp_size` it gives
the model forward to the logits processor, which forwards them with
`quant_align_size` through `distillation_ppo_loss` and
`compute_topk_loss` to the Megatron loss. The teacher tensors are packed
with the same THD arguments as the student inputs. Other strategies get
no extra arguments. The BSHD path is unchanged: `preprocess_bshd_engine`
always splits zigzag over the static CP group, for the student and the
teacher alike. `pad_to_length` is already rejected with top-k
distillation.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [cp_layout
distillation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+cp_layout+distillation),
[forward_kl_topk](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+forward_kl_topk).
No open PR passes the CP split to the teacher packing. #8061 fixes the
BSHD `forced_max_seqlen` mismatch; the two PRs touch neighbouring lines
of `compute_forward_kl_topk` and `compute_topk_loss`, so whichever lands
second needs a small rebase.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

```bash
pytest -q tests/utils/test_megatron_fp8_padding_on_cpu.py tests/workers/test_megatron_distillation_only_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/test_megatron_value_head_cp_layout_on_cpu.py
# 49 passed
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
# passed
```

The new tests give every token its own number and compare, row by row,
what the KL receives with the student's rows (CP state stubbed):

| test | cases |
|---|---|
| static CP=2 | both layouts × both CP ranks × no / 16 / 32-token
alignment × 17- and 32-token sequences (24) |
| dynamic CP | a group of 2 within CP 4, both layouts × both ranks in
the group (4) |
| the failure mode | student contiguous, teacher zigzag: equal shapes,
128 of 136 tokens misaligned |
| `forward_step` | a `dsv4_hybrid` model's layout and the micro-batch's
`local_cp_size` reach the top-k loss |

With the teacher packing reverted to ignore the CP split, the 12
contiguous and the 4 dynamic-CP cases fail. The logits processor and
`compute_topk_loss` tests check that the arguments reach the Megatron
loss and no other backend. The other CPU tests of the distillation,
padding, router replay and CP-layout code pass as on main. Not run on
GPUs.

### API and Usage Example

No config or API change. `compute_forward_kl_topk`, `compute_topk_loss`,
`distillation_ppo_loss` and
`MegatronEngineWithLMHead._lm_head_logits_processor` take two more
optional arguments, `cp_layout` (default `"zigzag"`) and `local_cp_size`
(default `None`); the defaults keep the previous behaviour.

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/workers/engine/megatron/transformer_impl.py`: `forward_step`
hands the logits processor the `cp_layout` and `local_cp_size` of the
student forward; `_lm_head_logits_processor` passes them to the top-k
loss.
- `verl/trainer/distillation/losses.py`: `distillation_ppo_loss` and
`compute_topk_loss` forward them to the Megatron loss only.
- `verl/trainer/distillation/megatron/losses.py`:
`compute_forward_kl_topk` packs the teacher's THD tensors with
`quant_align_size`, `local_cp_size` and `cp_layout`, as the model
forward packs the student's.
- Tests: `tests/utils/test_megatron_fp8_padding_on_cpu.py`,
`tests/workers/test_megatron_distillation_only_on_cpu.py`.

### What does this PR do?

VeOmni already supports node-local BF16 gradient transport with FP32
accumulation and output, but verl does not expose its configuration. Add
the default-off `low_precision_reduce_scatter_comm` option and forward
it directly to the pinned VeOmni model builder.

Implements the [assigned low-precision communication
scope](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/8186#issuecomment-6332111088)
in #8186 using [VeOmni
#1167](https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/VeOmni/pull/1167), which is
already included in the pinned dependency.

AI assistance was used for implementation, review, test execution, and
PR preparation.

#8186](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+8186+in%3Abody),
[VeOmni low-precision
PRs](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+veomni+low+precision),
and [the exact option
name](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+low_precision_reduce_scatter_comm).
No open PR implements this configuration wiring; the upstream VeOmni PR
provides the transport being exposed here.
- [x] Title follows `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

Local validation of the final implementation:

```bash
uv run --no-sync python -m pytest -q tests/workers/test_veomni_parallel_init_on_cpu.py
# 8 passed

uv run --no-sync pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=never
# all hooks passed

git diff --cached --check
# passed
```

Historical two-GPU correctness acceptance was run on one host with 2 ×
H200 NVL, using the real verl VeOmni engine and a locally generated tiny
Qwen3 checkpoint. The [acceptance script from the earlier
revision](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/250427376b35304a1425a0ddc45fd5be20ecc0c1/tests/special_distributed/test_veomni_low_precision_comm.py)
and its CI step have been removed from this PR per
[review](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8330#discussion_r4345373421),
since transport unit tests belong in VeOmni. The original validation
command was:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node=2 tests/special_distributed/test_veomni_low_precision_comm.py
# PASS
```

The baseline observed 12 native FP32 ReduceScatter calls; the enabled
run observed 12 low-precision hooks and 12 BF16 all-to-all calls. Across
two optimizer updates with two microbatches per rank, gradient and
parameter-update relative L2 and maximum absolute differences were zero.

A separate actor-update benchmark used a 428M-parameter dense Qwen3,
sequence length 512, per-rank batch 4 / microbatch 2, eager attention,
and no activation checkpointing or compilation. Four independent runs
used the same checkpoint and inputs in native–low–low–native order, with
5 warmup and 10 measured steps each. Timing includes zero-grad,
forward/backward, optimizer and scheduler steps, with CUDA
synchronization; each sample uses the maximum time across ranks.

| Run | Median ms/step | IQR ms | Peak allocated GiB | Peak reserved GiB
|
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| native-1 | 117.023 | 1.116 | 5.927 | 6.318 |
| low-1 | 130.853 | 3.218 | 5.927 | 6.416 |
| low-2 | 119.163 | 0.762 | 5.927 | 6.416 |
| native-2 | 118.891 | 2.209 | 5.927 | 6.318 |

This workload showed no speedup. The low-precision runs had higher
reserved memory and substantial run-to-run timing variation; no
bottleneck or stable slowdown percentage is claimed.

GPU environment: PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, runtime NCCL 2.29.7, Transformers
5.16.1, and VeOmni commit `10a26aca258f91a7af3e698cc0db8c6c51705989`.
The isolated environment reused the image's PyTorch/CUDA libraries, so
this was not a clean frozen-install validation. GPU results were
collected on the earlier implementation, before removing compatibility
checks and the forward-only guard. The final tree passed the existing
CPU regression tests and hooks; CUDA was not rerun, and forward-only
inference was not tested on GPU. The standalone performance harness and
raw logs are supporting validation artifacts, not added repository
files.

### API and Usage Example

Add these overrides to a VeOmni training command:

```bash
model_engine=veomni \
actor_rollout_ref.actor.veomni.mixed_precision=true \
actor_rollout_ref.actor.veomni.low_precision_reduce_scatter_comm=true
```

precision. The hook only performs gradient communication during
backward, so forward-only inference does not execute it. VeOmni retains

and HSDP replica AllReduce are unchanged.

validates the configuration and selects eligible shard groups.

[megatron, trainer] fix: recipe-agnostic THD padding and FP8 padding of top-k distillation tensors (#8325)

### What does this PR do?

Follow-up to #8127, for two of its review threads.

1. **Recipe-agnostic THD padding**
([review](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8127#discussion_r4336382125)).
`preprocess_packed_seqs` and `preprocess_thd_engine` took two
FP8-specific arguments, `use_fp8_padding` and `fp8_recipe`. They now
take one integer, `quant_align_size`: the token alignment each packed
sequence needs for the model's low-precision GEMMs (`None`: no
low-precision padding). `get_thd_quant_align_size(config)` derives it
from the `TransformerConfig`, for FP8 recipes through Megatron-Core's
`get_fp8_align_size` (32 for MXFP8, 16 otherwise), so a new format such
as NVFP4 or MXFP4 (#7971) adds a branch there instead of another
parameter. The model forward, the fused forward and router replay all
call it. The padding itself is unchanged.
2. **Top-k distillation under FP8**
([review](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8127#discussion_r4337984910)).
`compute_forward_kl_topk` packs the teacher's top-k tensors itself and
asserts they match the student logits, but it packed them without the
student's FP8 padding, so Megatron top-k distillation failed that
assertion under any FP8 recipe; the gap predates MXFP8. The engine now
passes `quant_align_size` to the Megatron loss, which packs the teacher
tensors with it on THD and with `use_fp8_padding` derived from it on
BSHD.

Left out: on BSHD, `pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max` (on by default) pads the
student micro-batch to the mini-batch max (`forced_max_seqlen`) while
the teacher tensors are not padded to match. That fails the same

Adds three raw log-prob metrics next to the existing

[megatron] feat: MXFP8 training recipe and end-to-end example (#8127)

### What does this PR do?

Adds the **MXFP8 training recipe** (`fp8_recipe: mxfp8`, Blackwell) to
verl's Megatron path, an end-to-end example and its documentation,
`docs/low_precision/mxfp8.md`. Together with what main already has,
#8287 (the trainer quantizes the rollout weights with
compressed-tensors) and #8306 (SGLang MXFP8 refit), this gives an MXFP8
RL recipe: MXFP8 GEMMs in training through Transformer Engine (TE), and
an MXFP8 rollout on vLLM or SGLang.

- **Training.** `fp8_recipe: mxfp8` already flows through
`override_transformer_config`. The one functional gap was THD sequence
padding:
- TE's MXFP8 quantizer needs both GEMM dimensions divisible by 32, and
the wgrad scale blocks run along the token dimension.
- So packed sequences are padded to `lcm(32, align)` per sequence under
MXFP8, using Megatron-Core's own `get_fp8_align_size` (the mapping it
applies to its MoE FP8 padding).
  - Every other recipe keeps its previous alignment (`lcm(16, align)`).
- **QAT combined with a TE FP8 recipe is rejected** at engine init: QAT
fake-quantizes weights inside BF16 GEMMs, while an FP8 recipe switches
the GEMMs themselves to FP8.
- **Examples**, each with `PRECISION=mxfp8` (MXFP8 end to end) or
`PRECISION=bf16` (the same job as the BF16 baseline):
- `examples/mxfp8/run_qwen3_8b_megatron.sh`: GRPO on Qwen3-8B with
GSM8K; the defaults fit one B200.
- `examples/mxfp8/run_qwen3_30b_a3b_megatron.sh`: GRPO on Qwen3-30B-A3B
(MoE) with DAPO-Math-17k on one 4×B200 node, experts included.
- **Docs.** `docs/low_precision/mxfp8.md` (new, in the Low Precision
toctree): the configuration, which kernels the vLLM and SGLang rollouts
use, the examples with their results, and earlier runs on DAPO-Math-17k.

Nothing changes unless an FP8 recipe is configured.

This was part 1 of #7519's split; as the maintainers asked, it now
stands alone (the consolidated #8314 was closed in favor of it). Making
the THD packing helpers recipe-agnostic, as suggested in the review,
follows in a separate PR.

commits.message:
Merge pull request #2105 from kevinwwillis/bugfix/tunneld-windows-selector-loop

tunneld: Serve on the selector loop on Windows

Merge pull request #2107 from kevinwwillis/bugfix/tunneld-start-tunnel-usbmux-fallthrough

tunneld: Try the other connection types for a device not on usbmux

Merge pull request #2108 from kevinwwillis/bugfix/tests-mark-start-tunnel-device

tests: Mark test_start_tunnel as a device test

tests: Mark test_start_tunnel as a device test

test_start_tunnel discovers real devices itself (usbmux, and Bonjour on the
local network) and builds a tunnel to the first one found. It uses no
device-backed fixture, so the conftest auto-marking never tags it, and
`pytest -m "not device"` runs it: on a host whose network has a paired device,
the device-free run creates a real tunnel interface to that device.

tunneld: Try the other connection types for a device not on usbmux

/start-tunnel without a connection_type tries usbmux first. For a device
usbmux does not list (e.g. one reachable only over Wi-Fi), create_using_usbmux
raises DeviceNotFoundError, which the usbmux branch did not catch, so the
request failed with HTTP 501 before the USB and Wi-Fi branches ran. Catch it
like the other usbmux failures so the request falls through.

tunneld: Serve on the selector loop on Windows

uvicorn's "asyncio" loop factory always builds a ProactorEventLoop on win32,
bypassing the WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy pymobiledevice3 sets for #1217
(and #1811). On the proactor loop the Wi-Fi monitor's bonjour browse gets no
answers, so tunneld never creates a Wi-Fi tunnel on Windows. Pass loop="none"
there so uvicorn leaves the loop to the active policy.

Fixes #2051

Merge pull request #2104 from doronz88/bugfix/dtx-cancelled-channel-replies

dtx: Fail the requests on a channel the device cancels

tests: Skip DVT location simulation where the device lacks it

iOS 13 doesn't offer com.apple.instruments.server.services.LocationSimulation
(it simulates location through com.apple.dt.simulatelocation), so the
tests now skip unless the device advertises the service.

dtx: Fail the requests on a channel the device cancels

A DTX service the device cannot create is still granted its channel,
then cancelled instead of answering: iOS 13's DTServiceHub logs "Could
not create service named ...LocationSimulation" and sends
_channelCanceled:. The channel shut down, but the reply futures are
kept per connection, so the call waiting on it hung forever
(`developer dvt simulate-location set` on iOS 13). A channel now fails
the requests still awaiting its reply when it shuts down.

Merge pull request #2103 from doronz88/tests/hygiene-gaps

tests: Close the gaps in socket_hygiene

tests: Run device tests under socket_hygiene

Their fixtures are function-scoped, so the whole device connection,
tunnel included, now has to be closed by the end of each test.

tests: Select the test device with --udid

The device fixtures always took the first USB device, so with several
connected only that one could be tested.

tests: Check module- and session-scoped fixtures for leaked sockets

socket_hygiene starts after the wider-scoped fixtures, so a socket one
of them opens and never closes was never caught. Each one now records
what it opens from its setup, and its teardown fails if any of it is
still open. Each socket is recorded by the innermost recording active
when it is created, and a reported fd is marked as accounted for in the
fixtures around it, so a leak is reported once, by whoever opened it.

tests: Track every socket a test creates in socket_hygiene

The transport and selector checks only see the test's own loop, and
where fds can't be listed (Windows) nothing caught a socket the test
left open without a transport. Every socket object created during the
test is now recorded, from socket.socket.__init__ (Windows raises no
socket.__new__ audit event for one made from an existing fd, such as an
accepted socket), and one still open at teardown fails the test, on
every platform and whichever loop it was on. An unclosed loop is caught
the same way, by its self-pipe sockets.

The selector check now skips a proactor loop, which calls its proactor
_selector but has no selector map.

Merge pull request #2102 from doronz88/ci/remove-codeql

ci: Remove the CodeQL workflow

ci: Remove the CodeQL workflow

Its findings on this repository have all been false positives: the
device protocols require what it flags (legacy TLS versions for old
lockdownd, and similar), so every alert so far has been dismissed.

Merge pull request #2100 from doronz88/docs/userspace-tunnel-read-shutdown

userspace_tunnel: Say how the tunnel's read task really ends

Merge pull request #2101 from doronz88/tests/fd-kind-no-dup

tests: Inspect sockets in socket_hygiene without opening an fd

tests: Inspect sockets in socket_hygiene without opening an fd

_fd_kind() duplicated each socket fd to read its addresses. For a family
socket() can't describe (AF_ROUTE, AF_SYSTEM) the constructor raised
without taking the duplicate, so it stayed open, read as a new leak and
kept the settle loop duplicating until the process ran out of fds; the
macOS CI runner holds such a socket and every test failed. Wrap the fd
itself and detach it instead.

Merge pull request #2099 from doronz88/bugfix/mounter-legacy-devices

mounter: Fix image mounting and listing on pre-iOS 14 devices

Merge pull request #2098 from doronz88/maintenance/create-task-over-ensure-future

maintenance: Start tasks with asyncio.create_task(), not ensure_future()

Merge pull request #2097 from doronz88/tests/socket-hygiene-everywhere

tests: Run every device-free test under socket_hygiene

service_connection: Close a TCP dial that completes as its caller is cancelled

wait_for() drops a result that completes in the iteration its wait is
cancelled or times out (Python 3.12+), so a dial finishing as its
caller was cancelled left the connection open, holding the fd and the
device's service until garbage collection. The dial now runs shielded;
when the wait ends without it, it is cancelled, and a connection it
completed anyway is closed.

tests: Run every device-free test under socket_hygiene

The fixture was opted into by the ServiceConnection, TLS and FDR tests
only; the other raw-socket users (usbmux, the userspace tunnel's relay,
screen_stream's RTP socket, the FDR proxy) and whatever comes next were
unchecked. Collection now applies it to every device-free test, placed
after the wider-scoped fixtures (whose sockets outlive a test by design)
and before the function-scoped ones, so it checks after they are torn
down. It also:

- waits up to a second for an fd a server or portal thread closes just
  after the test returns, so only a socket still open counts as leaked;
- names a leaked socket's addresses, and ignores the system resolver's
  persistent mDNSResponder connection;
- yields to the loop without asyncio.sleep, which tests monkeypatch.

The CDP asset-server helper served from daemon threads that
server_close() does not join, leaking the accepted connection's socket.

Merge pull request #2096 from doronz88/refactor/strip-ssl-over-streams

service_connection: Do the pre-iOS 14 TLS strip over the bound streams

service_connection: Wait for the close when the TLS strip fails

On Windows the proactor transport releases the socket only once its
pending read is cancelled, so the socket was still open when the
failure was raised.

Merge pull request #2095 from doronz88/refactor/service-connection-bind-on-create

service_connection: Bind on creation and negotiate TLS there

userspace_tunnel: Say how the tunnel's read task really ends

async_read() and async_read_batch() said closing the socketpair raises
OSError and so ends tun_read_task. Closing a socket under a pending
sock_recv() does not wake it (the kernel drops the fd's registration);
the task ends because stop_tunnel() cancels it before close().

doctor: Give up on an image mounter that does not answer

The developer-image check waited forever on a mounter held by another
client (before iOS 14 it serves one at a time), blocking doctor and its
host test. It now gives up after 10 s and reports the check as unknown,
saying why.

mounter: Fix image mounting and listing on pre-iOS 14 devices

Before iOS 14, mobile_storage_proxy serves one host connection at a
time: a second one is not answered until the first closes (observed on
iOS 13.3 in its syslog). auto_mount_developer(), auto_mount_personalized()
and every mounter CLI command left their connection open, so on such a
device the next mounter command in the process (doctor's check, a
lookup after auto-mount) hung. Each now closes its connection.

Also:
- `mounter list` falls back to LookupImage where CopyDevices is unknown
  (the proxy hangs up after refusing it); the Developer image, the only
  one before iOS 14, is listed with the fields CopyDevices gives it.
- auto_mount_developer() downloads a missing image into the per-user
  cache rather than into an installed Xcode bundle, which belongs to its
  installer (root, typically) and made the download fail; an explicit
  --xcode is still used and written to.
- `auto-mount --xcode` accepts the Xcode.app directory; it was declared
  a file, so it rejected every Xcode bundle.

maintenance: Start tasks with asyncio.create_task(), not ensure_future()

Every call site passes a coroutine from a running loop, which is all
create_task() takes; ensure_future() only adds accepting other
awaitables, and the package already starts its other tasks with
create_task(). Each task is now named, for debugging, and
CDPTarget._spawn() is typed to take a coroutine (naming its task after
it).

service_connection: Do the pre-iOS 14 TLS strip over the bound streams

The strip handshake (TLS, then plaintext) was a blocking wrap_socket()
on the raw socket before binding it, so the socket would not be read by
a transport mid-handshake (#1810). That blocked the event loop for up
to the 10 s handshake timeout, relied on SSLSocket's private _sslobj /
detach() dance, and needed a socket that is not yet bound, so it could
not work over TCP.

The handshake now runs in an ssl.MemoryBIO over the bound streams, fed
one whole TLS record at a time so nothing past the handshake is
consumed; the stream transport stays the only reader of the socket. A
peer that answers with something other than TLS records fails at once
instead of after the timeout. Stripped TLS now works over TCP too.

tests: Fail socket tests that leave an fd, transport or loop watch behind

A socket_hygiene fixture checks, after each test, that the test closed
every fd it opened, left no transport open, and left the loop watching
no fd but its own wake-up pipe. A stale watch is the use-after-free that
wakes nothing once the fd number is reused. It collects garbage first so
an unclosed object's ResourceWarning lands in the test that leaked it.
Applied to the ServiceConnection, TLS-at-creation and FDR tests.

dtx: Remove the unused DTXConnection.from_socket

It had no callers, and a failure before asyncio's transport took the
socket left it open; DTX connections are built from the streams of an
already-bound connection.

service_connection: Bind on creation and negotiate TLS there

A ServiceConnection used to hold a raw socket and bind it to the event
loop lazily, so the fd had two holders until start() ran: the race the
previous commits fix came from close() picking the wrong one. The
connection is now always created bound, from (reader, writer), and
nothing but its stream transport owns the fd:

- usbmux sockets go through from_socket(), which binds them with TLS
  (or the pre-iOS 14 strip handshake) before the connection exists,
  and closes them if that fails;
- TCP dials streams and upgrades them in place, as before, also before
  the connection exists;
- create_service_connection() takes the ssl_context/strip_ssl choice,
  so start_lockdown_service() and the DTX opener no longer bind first
  and upgrade after (the DTX non-strip path used to upgrade in place).

Removed with the raw socket: start(), setblocking(), the sync API
(recv_sync, sendall_sync, recvall_sync, recv_prefixed_sync,
recv_plist_sync, ssl_start_sync, read/write/tell) and ssl_start();
create_ssl_context() is now a module function and start_tls() the
mid-session upgrade lockdownd's StartSession uses. fdr's GeneratorExit
path, which cannot await, closes the connection's writer directly
instead of closing a socket the transport owns.

Merge pull request #2094 from doronz88/bugfix/service-connection-close-during-start

service_connection: Fix a close during start leaving a live transport on a reused fd

lockdown, dtx: Close a service connection whose SSL start fails

start_lockdown_service() and the DTX opener dropped the new connection
without closing it when the handshake (or reading the pair record for
it) raised, leaking its socket until garbage collection.

service_connection: Cancel an in-flight start on close instead of closing its fd

open_connection() registers its transport for the socket's fd before it
returns. A close() that ran in that window saw no writer yet and closed
the bare socket, leaving a live transport on an fd number the OS then
handed to the next socket; asyncio refuses sock_* calls on it ("File
descriptor N is used by transport"), so every later usbmux connection
on that loop failed. start() then also stored the streams close() had
just cleared, bringing the closed connection back.

close() now cancels the open (which closes its transport and the socket
with it), or closes the streams of one that already finished, and the
opener raises ConnectionTerminatedError instead of keeping them.

perf(runtime-shared-lib): don't attach an empty OTel context to every operator output (#3906)

The send-output closure inserted an `open_telemetry_context` parameter
on every output, but every operator API passes an empty string there
(Rust: a TODO, C: zero-initialized). The key carries nothing, since
Metadata::open_telemetry_context() reads a missing key as "", yet it
cost two String allocations and a BTreeMap insert per output, an extra
metadata entry on the wire for every receiver to decode, and its mere
presence kept DoraNode::send_output from attaching the current tracing
context. Insert it only when non-empty.

feat(arrow-convert): read `Vec<bool>` and `Vec<String>` back from a DoraArray (#3810)

* feat(arrow-convert): read `Vec<bool>` and `Vec<String>` back from a DoraArray

`IntoArrow` is implemented for `Vec<bool>` and `Vec<String>`, and its
docs point to the `TryFrom<&DoraArray>` impls for the reverse direction,
but there were none for these two types. On the default feature set
(`default = []`, so no raw Arrow access) a node therefore had no way to
read such a payload as Rust values: `Vec<String>` did not compile, and
`String`/`&str`/`bool` reject anything longer than one element.

Add both, with the same contract as the primitive `Vec<T>` impls: any
length, no nulls. `Vec<String>` accepts `Utf8`, `LargeUtf8` and
`Utf8View`, like the scalar string impls, since pyarrow and Polars
senders commonly produce the latter two. The `DoraArray` doctest and
`docs/api-rust.md` now show the round trip.

perf(node-api): give daemon-path outputs heap samples instead of SHM ones (#3832)

SampleAllocator::allocate picked a zenoh SHM buffer for every payload at
or above the zero-copy threshold, whatever path the output takes. An
output pinned to the daemon path (a backpressure or cross-machine
consumer, or a handshake frozen at init) then copied each SHM sample out
into a DataMessage::Vec: an SHM allocation (with GC), a zero-filled heap
buffer and a full copy per message, while also taking pool space from
the outputs that publish directly.

send_output and send_output_raw now allocate for the output's known
path: SHM only when it is direct-ready, a heap buffer otherwise, which
the daemon path sends without a copy. Readiness is final once init
returns (an output is then ready or frozen), so the choice cannot go
stale. The remaining SHM -> Vec fallback copy (a failed direct publish)
uses AVec::from_slice and no longer zero-fills first.

The scalar path rejects a `string<=N>` longer than N bytes and a

paths dropped the bound and published over-bound strings. Share one

fix(tensor-pool): sweep machine-qualified orphan segments at dataflow spawn (#3867)

A daemon with a machine id passes DORA_MACHINE_ID to every node it
spawns, and the node then names its pool segments
`dora_pool_{machine_id}_{dataflow_id}_{node_id}_{counter}`. The
per-dataflow orphan sweep only matched the unqualified
`dora_pool_{dataflow_id}_` prefix, so on any machine-id deployment a
node that crashed before registering its pool left the segment in
/dev/shm for good (the startup sweep only runs in cross-machine mode).

Thread the daemon's machine id into the sweep and match both forms,
keeping the counter check and the local-node filter.

fix(cli): strip send_stdout_as/send_logs_as from a replayed node (#3904)

fix(ros2-bridge-node): accept namespaced topic, service and action names on DDS (#3892)

* fix(ros2-bridge-node): accept namespaced topic, service and action names on DDS

The standalone bridge built every DDS name with
`Name::new("/", name.trim_start_matches('/'))`, passing the whole name
as the base name. `ros2_client::Name::new` rejects a `/` in the base
name, so any name with more than one segment failed with
`BadChar('/')` and the bridge exited at startup: `/turtle1/cmd_vel`
(used by examples/ros2-bridge/yaml-bridge), `/camera/image_raw`, any
namespaced service or action. Only single-segment names worked.

Parse the name with `Name::parse` instead, which puts every segment
but the last into the namespace and keeps the name absolute, at all
four call sites (topic, service client/server, action).

fix(daemon): let a stop succeed for a dataflow that just finished here (#3903)

* fix(daemon): let a stop succeed for a dataflow that just finished here

The coordinator sends StopDataflow to a dataflow's daemons one after
another. Stopping a node on an earlier daemon closes the inputs of the
nodes on a later one, which can then finish the dataflow before its own
stop arrives. That daemon answered "no running dataflow", failing
`dora stop` and `dora cluster restart` (nightly cluster-e2e).

Reply Ok while the dataflow's finish report is still held (pending or
unconfirmed): the stop is already done.

Fixes #3888

commits.message: Remove root sdkconfig.defaults and CMakeLists.txt and ignore them (#25174)

TuyaMCU: pace outgoing frames so the MCU is never written to back-to-back (#25151)

\#Description:
TuyaSendCmd() doesn't have any sort of pacing, so two back-to-back
commands can land within milliseconds of eachother.

In my specific devices and likely many other Tuya based devices, this
can cause the MCU to crash. This is compounded by the fact that Tasmota
(unnecessarily) writes the local-time every 60s, and the heartbeat every
11s. So roughly every 660s, they coincide, and then several times a day
the MCU will crash.

The end result is that my lights would randomly turn-off, or in the
case of my 3-way lights, they would even turn on randomly in the middle
of the night.

This patches the Tuya MCU driver to queue outgoing frames and release them from FUNC_LOOP once the following four spacing rules pass:

  byte_counter  must not be part way through receiving a frame
  tx_ack_wait   still waiting on a reply, given up after
                TUYA_TX_ACK_TIMEOUT_MS
  tx_last_ms    minimum gap, for commands that don't receive a response
  rx_last_ms    silence since the last byte in

TUYA_TX_MAX_HOLD_MS limits the ack and quiet wait time.

Behaviour changes for existing users:

  - datapoint writes are paced, so a fade or slider drag (might) emit fewer
    intermediate values. The queue insertion order is such though that
    values are never lost, and this is quite the edge-case.
  - a command can be delayed by the minimum gap plus the hold ceiling
  - a full queue with nothing collapsible drops its oldest frame

\#Testing:
I wrote a stress test that could crash the MCU at-will by spamming lots
of writes heartbeat writes.
With this applied, the same test does not crash the MCU

I have also been using this for over a month on all of my lights with 0
issues.

WifiManager: name the setup AP as it is turned on (#25169)

WifiManagerBegin() turned the AP on with WifiSetMode() and named it with
WiFi.softAP() only after WifiSetMode()'s delay(100): for that time the AP
beaconed under the SDK's default name, ESP_ and the AP MAC, which a phone
or computer then lists beside the real name, often for a minute after.

WiFi.softAP() turns the AP on and names it at once, so it now comes first;

commits.message:
Accept built-in UV tokens without a PIN in MakeCredential/GetAssertion (#822)

* Accept built-in UV tokens without a PIN in MakeCredential/GetAssertion

With the fingerprint feature, getPinUvAuthTokenUsingUvWithPermissions
issues a pinUvAuthToken through built-in UV without any PIN set. But
MakeCredential and GetAssertion reject every pinUvAuthParam with
CTAP2_ERR_PIN_NOT_SET when no PIN is set (CTAP 2.0 logic), so that
token can never be used.

Platforms prefer the token path whenever pinUvAuthToken is advertised,
so an authenticator with built-in UV and no PIN fails every UV-required
request (e.g. Chrome: "operation timed out or not allowed").

Keep the 2.0 check, but only reject when no form of user verification
is configured: neither a PIN nor an enrolled built-in UV method.

* Apply the user verification check to all "protected by some form of UV" steps

Move has_user_verification to storage and use it wherever CTAP 2.1
says "protected by some form of user verification" but OpenSK only
checked for a PIN: the discoverable-credential check in MakeCredential
(makeCredUvNotRqd), authenticatorLargeBlobs set, and
authenticatorConfig.

The remaining pin_hash checks are PIN-specific by the spec: clientPin
in getInfo, the zero-length pinUvAuthParam response, setPin/changePin,
forceChangePin, and blocking built-in UV when the PIN is blocked.

* Update comments for the user verification check

CTAP2.1 does cover a pinUvAuthParam on an authenticator without any form
of user verification, and the rk check now depends on any form of user
verification, not only a PIN.

Prepares publishing OpenSK to crates.io (#823)

Adds a script that helps us upload the crates.

Changes OpenSK's version number to 0.1.0 as it should, since we are not
stable yet. This is not to be confused with the CTAP specification and
branch names we use.

Copies the LICENSE file to the OpenSK library.

Reject Relying Party IDs that are empty or longer than 253 bytes (#805)

WebAuthn requires the RP ID to be a valid domain string: non-empty, and
capped at 253 bytes in presentation format by RFC 1035, so browsers
never send anything else.

Nothing enforces that for software that talks CTAP directly over USB
HID. A MakeCredential request with rk=true and an empty or longer RP ID
runs the whole ceremony, including the user presence check and the key
generation, and only fails at the very end when storing the
discoverable credential, because the oversized RP ID pushes the
serialized credential past the maximum value size of the persistent
store.

Reject the RP ID upfront instead, right after parsing.

Rebased on develop and reuses MAX_RP_ID_LENGTH from data_formats (now
pub(crate)), which was introduced for the setMinPINLength RP IDs.

commits.message:
Merge pull request #666 from gpolak/view_tree_back_dispatcher_owner

Set the view tree OnBackPressedDispatcherOwner in CoreAppCompatActivity

Set the view tree OnBackPressedDispatcherOwner in CoreAppCompatActivity

RibActivity attaches its root view to android.R.id.content without calling
setContentView, so ComponentActivity.initializeViewTreeOwners() never runs.
initViewTreeOwners() fills in the lifecycle, ViewModel store and saved-state
owners, but not the OnBackPressedDispatcherOwner. findViewTreeOnBackPressed-
DispatcherOwner() therefore returns null for every view in a RIB activity.

View-based components that register back callbacks through the view tree
(for example a bottom sheet that dismisses on back) silently skip
registration. Under predictive back the key-event fallback never fires, so
back reaches RibActivity's callback and the router navigates away instead
of the component handling it.

Add an explicit androidx.activity dependency to rib-android-core. That
pulls in a newer lifecycle, where the ViewTreeLifecycleOwner and
ViewTreeViewModelStoreOwner classes are no longer callable from Kotlin, so
switch to the equivalent extension functions; the compiled calls are the
same.

fix(session): append the rebuild boundary after the newest message (#2702)

* fix(session): end the rebuild tail at the newest message and read turn state through it

An automatic rebuild passed a window read before the current step, so the
step that triggered it fell between the digest range and the appended
boundary and reached neither the model nor the writer. The runLoop also
took the boundary as the turn's user message, asking the model to answer
it after a finished turn and dropping the turn's own settings.

* fix(session): carry unanswered users on the rebuild boundary and keep boundaries out of resume

Unanswered user messages at the end of a rebuild tail were cut to the
verbatim quote cap and lost their attachments; they are now copied onto
the boundary in full. Queued inputs the inbox has not delivered stay out
of the tail so they arrive once, as their own messages. Recovery and
resume treated the boundary as a later user turn, and a finished turn
left a stop reminder in front of the user's next prompt.

* fix(session): bring back queued inputs a rebuild skipped once they end undelivered

A queued input left out of a rebuild tail and then cancelled stayed in
the session and was offered for resume, but no window held it any more.
Recovery also offered interrupted assistants from inside a rebuild tail,
whose context the window no longer has.

* fix(session): bring back only the queued inputs a rebuild actually skipped

Receipt state cannot tell an input the rebuild left out apart from one
that had already ended and was represented on the boundary, so the
boundary now records the inputs it skipped.

* fix(session): carry still-queued inputs forward to the next rebuild boundary

Only the newest boundary's deferred inputs are consulted, so one still
queued when a second rebuild ran was dropped from the record. Every
undelivered input is now recorded, read once per insert.

* docs(compose): report the rebuild boundary placement work in lossless-session-db spec

* test(session): check the memory paths reminder on the rebuild boundary

main replaced the per-message recall reminder with one memory paths
reminder per context window; after a rebuild that window starts at the
boundary.

* test(checkpoint): wait for the writer before the rebuild-tail test tears down

The fork:false case timed out once in CI after its assertions passed,
with the writer still in flight when the instance was disposed. Also

commits.message:
Mutate the logger's handler in place on metadata writes (#529)

Give `Logger.handler` a `_modify` accessor and replace its `get` with
`_read`, so metadata writes update the stored handler instead of a copy.

### Motivation:

`Logger.handler` only has `get` and `set`. A write such as
`logger[metadataKey: "k"] = "v"` gets a copy of the handler, writes to
it while the stored handler still shares the metadata dictionary, and
sets it back. So every write copies the whole dictionary, and
`withLogger(mergingMetadata:)` does that once per key.

### Modifications:

- Give `Logger.handler` `_read`, `set` and `_modify` accessors. `_read`
yields the stored handler. `_modify` keeps the existing uniqueness check
on the storage and then yields the stored handler, so metadata and log
level writes change it in place. `set` keeps the same check for plain
`logger.handler = newHandler` assignments, which are cheaper through a
setter than through `_modify`.
- Add a test handler that counts copies of its metadata, with tests for
direct writes and for `withLogger(mergingMetadata:)`. Without the change
they report 10 copies instead of 0, and 5 instead of 1.

### Result:

A metadata write on a logger that owns its storage no longer copies the
dictionary. A copied logger still copies once on its first write, so
value semantics are unchanged.

1,000 metadata writes with a handler that keeps metadata in a plain
dictionary, debug build, three runs each:

| Keys on the logger | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | 7.2 to 8.1 ms | 0.46 to 0.50 ms |
| 1,000 | 20.2 to 20.6 ms | 0.46 to 0.55 ms |
| 10,000 | 134.0 to 134.4 ms | 0.47 to 0.50 ms |
| 100,000 | 1.29 to 1.30 s | 0.32 to 0.35 ms |

`withLogger(mergingMetadata:)` with 10,000 keys went from 0.64 to 0.65 s
down to 2.9 to 3.1 ms. `StreamLogHandler` still rebuilds its pretty
metadata string on every write; this change does not touch that.

All 176 tests pass on macOS with Swift 6.4, and `swift format lint
--strict` and `swift package diagnose-api-breaking-changes` are clean.
Once yielding accessors land, `_read` and `_modify` can become `yielding
borrow` and `yielding mutate`.

Fixes #526.

commits.message:
RED-213286: test that BLESS NO-EVICT survives module writes, reloads and eviction (#1082)

* RED-213286: test that BLESS NO-EVICT survives module writes, reloads and eviction

Redis 8.12 adds BLESS, which marks a key NO-EVICT. The flag lives outside the
module value, so every module path that writes, replaces, saves or reloads a
value must keep it. RED-220725 (fixed in redis/redis#15995) was such a path:
TDIGEST.MERGE into an existing key replaced the value and dropped the flag.

tests/flow/test_bless.py:
- every write command in test_replication.ROWS keeps NO-EVICT when it runs
  on a blessed key, plus TDIGEST.MERGE ... OVERRIDE
- a blessed key of each type keeps the flag through DEBUG RELOAD and an AOF
  rewrite without the RDB preamble (the types' own aof_rewrite callbacks)
- blessed keys of each type are not evicted under allkeys-lru

Skipped on cluster and on servers without BLESS.

commits.message:
testing: runtest.py improvements ported from OpenImageIO (#2189)

Port the parts of OIIO PR 5465 and 5476 that apply to OSL's
runtest.py:

* run_app() takes a failureok parameter. If the first word of the
  command names an OSL app (oslc, oslinfo, testshade, testrender,
  testoptix) or an OIIO app (oiiotool, maketx, etc.), it is replaced
  with the full path to the built app.
* New run_commands() takes a multi-line string of shell commands, one
  per line, and runs each through run_app(). Blank lines and `#`
  comments are skipped. So a run.py can list commands exactly as they
  would be typed, and docs can include them by reference.
* The oslc, oslinfo, oiiotool, maketx, oiiodiff, testshade, testrender,
  and testoptix helpers are now thin wrappers around run_app().
  oiiotool() also gained failureok and concat parameters.
* text_diff ignores trailing whitespace differences, which can vary by
  platform (e.g. cmd.exe's echo).
* redirect_push and redirect_pop to let a test redirect a portion of
  output to a different file.

Assisted-by: Claude Code / Claude Opus 5.5

Signed-off-by: Larry Gritz <lg@larrygritz.com>

ci: testshade --buildinfo, and show it in the GHA summary (#2186)

Add read-only ShadingSystem attributes describing how OSL was built,
so any app linking liboslexec can retrieve them. These are modeled on
OIIO's attributes of the same names:

* `build:platform` -- e.g. "MacOS/ARM"
* `build:compiler` -- e.g. "gcc 11.2"
* `build:simd` -- synonym for `osl:simd`
* `build:dependencies` -- semicolon-separated "name version" for every
  dependency the build looked for (from CMake, via a configured private
  header, buildopts.h)
* `build:batched` -- batched SIMD targets compiled in
* `hw:batched` -- the subset of those this hardware can run

Add `testshade --buildinfo`, which prints those attributes plus the
running hardware (and GPU, for OptiX builds). It mirrors
`oiiotool --buildinfo`. For example:

```
OSL 1.16.0.0dev | Linux/x86_64
    Build compiler: gcc 11.2 | C++17/201703
    HW features enabled at build: sse2,sse3,ssse3,sse41,sse42,avx,avx2,f16c
    Back ends: x86_64 single, batched b8_AVX2
    Dependencies: ZLIB 1.2.11, Imath 3.1.9, OpenImageIO 3.0.11.0, pugixml 1.16, LLVM 15.0.7, partio, Python3 3.10.11, pybind11 2.9.0, Qt6 NONE, Qt5 5.15.9, Robinmap, BISON 3.0.4, FLEX 2.6.1
    Running on: 4 cores, 15.6 GB, SIMD sse2,sse3,ssse3,sse41,sse42,avx,avx2,avx512f,avx512dq,avx512ifma,avx512cd,avx512bw,avx512vl,fma,f16c,popcnt,rdrand
```

ci-test.bash appends this to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, as OIIO does (OIIO
PR 5453), so each CI job's toolchain and dependencies are visible at a
glance on the workflow summary page.

Also fix bugs in ShadingSystem::getattribute:
* "hw:simd" queried the nonexistent OIIO attribute "hw:string".
* "osl:simd" never reported neon.
* "osl:cuda_version" and "osl:optix_version" returned a raw char*
  rather than a ustring's chars, so retrieving them as a ustring gave
  garbage.

Assisted-by: Claude Code / Claude Opus 5.5

Signed-off-by: Larry Gritz <lg@larrygritz.com>
